workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, and set up default trading fees.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions

steps.title: Register Broker ID with Orderly Team
steps.description: Provide your unique Broker ID (a string identifier), Broker Name, Default Taker Fee, Default Maker Fee, and initial Broker tier/level (e.g., 'public') to the Orderly team for backend configuration.
steps.important: Broker tiers can increase based on trading volume, which reduces Orderly's base taker fee. Default fees are typically configured at setup (e.g., 6 bps taker, 3 bps maker).

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature. Registration must be done separately for testnet and mainnet.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. For example, if a broker sets a 0.05% taker fee, they earn 0.05% - 0.03% = 0.02% per trade. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates. The Orderly team can share an internal script for periodic fee maintenance if needed.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account. Check the balance by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet or using the private Get Current Holding endpoint.

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity. After the change, the attacker can only potentially modify the DEX itself and the broker ID. Orderly support will also update the Orderly One login wallet. Monitor the DEX closely during the transition.

commonIssues.issue: Custom fees below standard tier not applying.
commonIssues.solution: Custom trading fees below the standard tier require the builder to be in the Diamond tier of the Builder Staking Programme. Additionally, the DEX must be 'graduated' (not using a shared broker ID). If not graduated, fees cannot be modified. Contact the Orderly team to request trial periods for custom fee structures.

workflows.name: Tracking User Holdings, Volume, and Leaderboards via Orderly APIs
workflows.description: Monitor user deposits, collateral holdings, per-user and broker-level trading volume, and leaderboard data using Orderly's Builder APIs, dashboard indexer, Dune analytics, and React SDK to power rewards programs, trading competitions, and platform analytics.
prerequisites: Active Orderly-powered DEX with a broker ID
API authentication credentials (orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id)
Understanding of keccak256 hashing for token identification
Backend system for processing volume data (for rewards/points programs)
Understanding of date-based vs. timestamp-based queries

steps.title: Fetch User List and Leaderboard via Builder API
steps.description: Get a list of users and aggregate volume data across all users for your broker using the Builder's Leaderboard API.

steps.title: Track Individual User Volumes
steps.description: Use the private endpoint to fetch per-user volume data per date for your broker. Connect this data to your own points or rewards system.
steps.important: This endpoint returns volume data per date, not by arbitrary timestamp range. The trading volume display uses a 7-day rolling window. User-level volume statistics are settled once daily using the previous day's complete data (updated around 00:00 UTC).

steps.title: Retrieve Broker Daily Volume via REST API
steps.description: Use the get-broker-daily-volume endpoint to retrieve volume data for all accounts under your broker. Authenticate with your admin account's headers.
steps.important: Register an account under your broker_id (or use your admin account) to authenticate this request.

steps.title: Query Granular Trade Data via Dashboard Indexer
steps.description: For more granular or custom queries by timestamp range, use the Orderly Dashboard indexer API.
steps.code: GET https://orderly-dashboard-query-service.orderly.network/events?address={wallet}&broker_id={broker_id}&event_type=PERPTRADE&from_time={unix}&to_time={unix}
steps.important: The dashboard source code is open source at https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/orderly-dashboard.

steps.title: Fetch User Deposits via Events API
steps.description: Retrieve deposit events for users using the events API. Use the 'token_hash' parameter (keccak256 hash of the token) to filter by specific tokens.

steps.title: Get Exact Holdings via Read-Only Key
steps.description: For exact holdings, users can create a read-only Orderly key and share it with the builder to query via the get-current-holding endpoint.
steps.important: Orderly uses cross margin, meaning the user's entire holdings are taken into account. There is no exact public way to get specific token holdings or track which collateral is used for specific positions.

steps.title: Query Market Maker Trade History
steps.description: Market makers can query their trade history programmatically using the REST API.
steps.important: MM transaction orders can be queried for 4 days, and non-transaction orders for 8 hours. Ordinary users' orders are kept for the last 30 days (up to 2,000 orders; excess is archived).

steps.title: Retrieve Real-Time Market Data via React SDK
steps.description: Use React SDK hooks for real-time market data including index price, open interest, volume, and funding rate.
steps.important: Historical open interest data is not tracked by Orderly.

steps.title: Retrieve Historical Data via REST API
steps.description: Use REST API endpoints for historical volume and funding fee data.

steps.title: Access Built-in Leaderboard and Configure Point Campaigns
steps.description: Orderly DEXs include a built-in leaderboard at the /leaderboard path. Use point campaigns to configure custom leaderboards based on metrics like trading volume or PnL.
steps.important: Point campaigns allow flexible leaderboard configurations for trading competitions and community engagement.

steps.title: Query Top Traded Tokens and Platform Data via Dune
steps.description: Use the Dune dashboard to query top traded tokens by volume and access platform-specific trading data in the 'Builders Data' section.
steps.important: Orderly also provides an API for updated trading data if you need programmatic access.

steps.title: Retrieve All Brokers Programmatically
steps.description: Use the public REST API to retrieve all registered brokers with their broker_id and broker_name.

steps.title: Find User Account IDs for Reward Distribution
steps.description: If the Orderly dashboard leaderboard wallet links are unresponsive, use the Builder's Leaderboard API as an alternative to retrieve account IDs for reward distribution.
steps.important: Clicking wallet addresses on the dashboard leaderboard (https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/) has experienced known issues. Contact Orderly support if the API alternative is insufficient.

steps.title: Request Daily Trading Report (Market Makers)
steps.description: Orderly can send a daily trading report via email showing trading volume and market share average.
steps.code:
// Provide your email to the Orderly team
// Reports sent from: mmreports@orderly.network

commonIssues.issue: Cannot track which collateral is used for specific positions.
commonIssues.solution: This is by design due to cross margin. The user's entire holdings are considered as collateral. For exact per-token holdings, users must share a read-only Orderly key.

commonIssues.issue: WebSocket balance does not match DEX display.
commonIssues.solution: The WebSocket balance endpoint only triggers on collateral changes and does not include unrealized PnL. The DEX total value includes USDC holdings, non-USDC holdings at index price, and unsettled PnL.

commonIssues.issue: token_hash parameter not matching.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the correct keccak256 hash of the token string. Refer to the reference implementation at the orderly-dashboard repository.

commonIssues.issue: Need volume data for a specific timestamp range, not just dates.
commonIssues.solution: Use the Orderly Dashboard indexer API instead of the /v1/builders/users/volumes endpoint, which only returns per-date data.

commonIssues.issue: Old trade history not available via API.
commonIssues.solution: MM transaction orders are available for 4 days, non-transaction orders for 8 hours. Ordinary users' orders are kept for 30 days (up to 2,000). Older data is archived and may require direct on-chain queries.

commonIssues.issue: Broker daily volume endpoint returns empty data.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are authenticating with an account registered under your broker_id. The timestamp must be current UTC time in milliseconds.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot track affiliate-specific volume.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly does not provide built-in affiliate tracking. Brokers must build their own affiliate/referral tracking system on top of Orderly's APIs.

commonIssues.issue: Historical open interest data needed.
commonIssues.solution: Historical open interest data is not tracked by Orderly. You will need to capture and store this data independently using the real-time useTickerStream hook.

commonIssues.issue: Displayed volume decreases unexpectedly.
commonIssues.solution: This is normal behavior with the 7-day rolling window. Large older transactions falling out of the window while smaller new ones enter cause the displayed total to decrease.

commonIssues.issue: Dashboard leaderboard wallet links unresponsive.
commonIssues.solution: This is a known issue addressed via bug fixes. Use the Builder's Leaderboard API (GET /v1/builder/leaderboard) as an alternative or contact Orderly support.

commonIssues.issue: Leaderboard not showing at /leaderboard path.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your DEX is properly deployed and the URL routing is configured correctly. The leaderboard is a built-in feature of Orderly-powered DEXs.

commonIssues.issue: Dune dashboard data seems outdated.
commonIssues.solution: Dune queries may have a slight delay. For real-time data, use the Orderly API or admin WebSocket streams.

workflows.name: Customizing Orderly SDK Theme, UI, and Branding
workflows.description: Customize the theme, colors, UI elements, and branding of your Orderly-based DEX using CSS variables, the Theme Builder (Storybook), the Orderly One editor, and SDK configuration options including RTL support, custom asset categories, and mobile navigation.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK integrated (v2.12.0+ for custom asset categories, v3.1.0+ for RTL support) or Orderly One DEX created
Brand colors and design assets prepared
Access to your application's CSS/theme files
Access to Storybook for live preview

steps.title: Use the Orderly Theme Builder (Storybook)
steps.description: Open the Orderly Theme Builder (Storybook) to visually select colors, fonts, and other style options, preview and test theme customizations in real time, then copy the generated CSS code.

steps.title: Override CSS Variables in Your Project
steps.description: Apply custom theme by overriding CSS variables. In SDK v1, variables use the '--orderly' prefix; in SDK v2.8+, the prefix changed to '--oui'. For Orderly One, paste CSS variables into the Theme Customization section.
steps.important: To create a light theme, mainly tweak the base/foreground variables. Full light theme support is not officially available; additional CSS overrides with !important may be needed. You may need to clear localStorage for theme changes to take effect.

steps.title: Apply Targeted CSS Overrides
steps.description: Use targeted CSS overrides with !important rules to customize SDK components that don't respond to CSS variable changes alone.
steps.important: Some minor issues (e.g., text in SVGs) may not be fully fixable via CSS overrides.

steps.title: Change Section Colors in Orderly One
steps.description: For Orderly One DEXs, click 'Edit Desktop' and then click directly on the different sections of the page to change their colors using the color picker.
steps.important: You do not need to go into the 'Themes' menu to change colors; the color picker is available directly from the section editing screen.

steps.title: Change Specific UI Element Colors
steps.description: The leverage indicator and similar UI elements use the 'Primary' color setting. Update the Primary color in your Orderly One configuration to change them.
steps.important: The Primary color also affects the links at the top of the page, which use a gradient between 'Primary' and 'Primary Light'. The leverage indicator specifically uses just the 'Primary' color. If you removed sync from primary colors but the element still appears in the old color, ensure you are modifying the correct Primary color field.

steps.title: Hide 'Powered by Orderly' Footer
steps.description: Add custom CSS to hide the 'Powered by Orderly' footer text. There is no obligation to keep the label.

steps.title: Hide Orderly Exchange Name in TradingView Charts
steps.description: Hide the exchange title in TradingView charts using CSS.
steps.important: As of the latest update, built-in CSS customization via the platform is temporarily unavailable. Builders must fork the DEX template, apply CSS modifications manually, and self-host.

steps.title: Configure Logo Display
steps.description: To make your logo blend seamlessly into the top navigation bar, remove the logo's background (make it transparent) or set the logo background to the same color as your DEX background.
steps.code:
/* Logo requirements:
   - Transparent background (alpha channel)
   - Dimensions: 600x120
   - Icon on the left, text on the right
*/
steps.important: Use a light-colored logo for best results against a dark navigation bar. Use image editing tools to remove the background before uploading.

steps.title: Configure Mobile Logo Display
steps.description: On mobile, the DEX defaults to showing the secondary logo. If the uploaded secondary logo does not include text (e.g., only shows an icon), you can change this behavior.
steps.important: To fix mobile logo display, either update the code to select the main logo for mobile display, or upload a different secondary logo that includes the desired text. This customization requires modifying the frontend code of your DEX.

steps.title: Fix Button Text Visibility
steps.description: If button text (e.g., 'Create Account' or 'Deposit') is not visible, adjust the Primary Contrast color.
steps.important: CSS validation is built in to prevent malformed entries. Avoid manually pasting extra characters at the end of the theme config.

steps.title: Change Default Trading Pair
steps.description: Modify the default trading symbol displayed on your DEX by updating the configuration in your codebase.

steps.title: Configure Custom Asset Categories
steps.description: From SDK v2.12.0 onward, builders can configure custom asset categories for their UI. No categories are set by default — builders choose which categories to display for their users.
steps.important: SDK v3.1.3 added a dedicated Crypto category across market discovery experiences including the Market Selector, Market Search, Market Sidebar, and Markets page.

steps.title: Add Bottom Navigation Tabs on Mobile
steps.description: Include the `bottomNavProps` property in the Scaffold component to add bottom navigation tabs on mobile view.
steps.code:
// Refer to SDK documentation:
// https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/react/components/scaffold#5-bottomnavprops-optional

steps.title: Enable RTL Language Support
steps.description: SDK v3.1.0 introduced RTL language support for Arabic, Persian, and Hebrew. Layouts, typography, and components mirror correctly for RTL locales.
steps.code: "@orderly.network/react": "^3.1.0"
steps.important: RTL support is automatic based on the user's locale setting. No additional configuration is required beyond upgrading to v3.1.0+.

steps.title: Fork Repository for Deeper Customization
steps.description: For deeper customization beyond the no-code template, fork the generated GitHub repository and modify the code directly.
steps.important: When using your own repository, you will not receive automatic SDK updates but will be notified of available updates.

steps.title: Enable QR Code Feature
steps.description: The QR code allows users to scan from their laptop to switch to mobile trading and create a Progressive Web App (PWA) on their phone.
steps.important: The QR code feature only works after a customized URL has been set for the DEX. It will not work with generic URLs.

commonIssues.issue: Theme/CSS changes not taking effect.
commonIssues.solution: Clear browser cache and localStorage for theme changes to take effect. Ensure CSS selectors are specific enough to override default styles. Use !important if necessary. Ensure CSS overrides are loaded after the SDK's default styles. For Orderly One, ensure you click 'Update DEX configuration' after applying CSS changes.

commonIssues.issue: Light mode does not work properly.
commonIssues.solution: Full light theme support is not officially available. Use CSS overrides with !important rules targeting specific classes. Some elements like SVG text may not be fully customizable.

commonIssues.issue: Brand gradient and button colors not editable in Orderly One.
commonIssues.solution: There is a known bug where the brand gradient and button colors do not sync with the primary color setting. As a workaround, set these colors by editing the CSS directly.

commonIssues.issue: CSS variable prefix mismatch after SDK upgrade.
commonIssues.solution: In SDK v1, variables use the '--orderly' prefix; in SDK v2.8+, the prefix changed to '--oui'. Update all CSS variable references when upgrading.

commonIssues.issue: Button text is invisible after theme change.
commonIssues.solution: Adjust the Primary Contrast color (--oui-color-primary-contrast) in the theme config to black or white depending on your button background color.

commonIssues.issue: Leverage indicator color not changing.
commonIssues.solution: The leverage indicator uses the 'Primary' color setting. Ensure you are modifying the correct Primary color field. It uses just the 'Primary' color, not the gradient.

commonIssues.issue: Built-in CSS customization unavailable on Orderly One.
commonIssues.solution: Built-in CSS customization via the platform is temporarily unavailable (expected to return in 2–4 weeks). Fork the DEX template, apply CSS modifications manually, and self-host in the meantime.

commonIssues.issue: RTL layout not mirroring correctly.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using SDK v3.1.0 or later. Verify the user's locale is set to an RTL language (Arabic, Persian, or Hebrew).

commonIssues.issue: Mobile logo shows icon only without text.
commonIssues.solution: Upload a secondary logo that includes the desired text, or modify the frontend code to use the main logo for mobile display.

commonIssues.issue: QR code not appearing on the trading page.
commonIssues.solution: Set a customized URL for your DEX. The QR code feature does not work with generic/default URLs.

workflows.name: Configuring Custom Domain and SSL for Orderly DEX
workflows.description: Configure DNS settings to host your Orderly-powered DEX on a custom domain or subdomain, including handling occupied main domains, non-standard domain extensions, and SSL/HTTPS enforcement.
prerequisites: Orderly One DEX created and configured (or active custom DEX deployment)
Access to your DNS provider (e.g., GoDaddy, Cloudflare)

steps.title: Choose Subdomain if Main Domain is Occupied or Uses Non-Standard TLD
steps.description: If your main domain (e.g., www.yourdomain.com) is already assigned to another service via a CNAME record, you cannot assign a second CNAME with the same name. Similarly, non-standard TLDs (e.g., .trading) may have DNS propagation or SSL certificate issues when used as apex domains. Use a subdomain for your DEX (e.g., app.yourdomain.com or dex.yourdomain.trading).
steps.code:
// Instead of: yourdomain.trading
// Use: dex.yourdomain.trading
steps.important: You do not need to purchase a new domain. A subdomain works perfectly for hosting your DEX alongside other services and is more reliable for non-standard TLDs.

steps.title: Add CNAME Record in DNS Provider
steps.description: In your DNS provider (e.g., GoDaddy, Cloudflare), add a new CNAME record pointing your subdomain to Orderly's hosting endpoint.
steps.important: Ensure no conflicting A or CNAME records exist for the same subdomain name.

steps.title: Set Domain in Orderly One DEX Profile
steps.description: In the Orderly One dashboard, navigate to your DEX profile custom domain settings. Enter your desired domain name (e.g., app.yourdomain.com) and redeploy the DEX.
steps.code:
// DEX management page:
https://dex.orderly.network/dex
steps.important: The domain must be properly registered and configured in the broker profile.

steps.title: Wait for DNS Propagation
steps.description: After updating the DNS and Orderly One settings, allow time for DNS propagation.
steps.important: DNS changes may take anywhere from 15 minutes to 48 hours to fully propagate.

steps.title: Enable HTTPS Enforcement
steps.description: Contact the Orderly team to manually enable HTTPS enforcement for your custom domain. This step is required to avoid 'Not Secure' browser warnings.
steps.important: HTTPS enforcement may need to be manually enabled by the Orderly team after DNS propagation completes.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot assign CNAME to main domain.
commonIssues.solution: If the main domain already has a CNAME record for another service, use a subdomain instead. You cannot have two CNAME records with the same name.

commonIssues.issue: SSL certificate not provisioning for custom domain.
commonIssues.solution: Try using a subdomain format (e.g., dex.yourdomain.trading) instead of the apex domain, especially for non-standard TLDs. Ensure the CNAME record has fully propagated before requesting HTTPS enforcement.

commonIssues.issue: DEX not loading on custom domain after DNS setup.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the CNAME record points to orderlynetworkcreator.github.io, ensure the domain is correctly set in Orderly One, confirm no conflicting records exist, and allow time for DNS propagation (up to 48 hours).

commonIssues.issue: 'Not Secure' browser warning after configuring custom domain.
commonIssues.solution: Contact the Orderly team to turn on enforcing HTTPS for the site. This is a manual step that must be done after DNS configuration.

workflows.name: Customizing DEX UI: Asset Categories, Chart Branding, and Trading Features
workflows.description: Configure custom asset categories, header navigation, TradingView chart colors and branding, sound notifications, bulk close, TP/SL offsets, and other UI customization options in the Orderly SDK.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.12.0 or later (v3.1.3+ recommended for asset categories)
Orderly SDK v2.5.1 or later (for header navigation)
Access to DEX source code or Orderly One theme editor

steps.title: Configure Custom Asset Categories
steps.description: Starting from SDK v2.12.0, builders can configure custom asset categories for their UI. No categories are set by default — builders choose which categories to display for their users. SDK v3.1.3 added a dedicated Crypto market category across market discovery experiences including the Market Selector, Market Search, Market Sidebar, and Markets page.
steps.important: No categories are set by default. Builders must explicitly configure which categories to display. This gives builders full control over how assets are grouped and presented to users.

steps.title: Customize Header Navigation
steps.description: SDK v2.5.1 introduced customizable header navigation items, allowing brokers to tailor the interface to their needs.
steps.important: Custom navigation items allow brokers to add links to external pages, custom features, or reorganize the default navigation structure. Configure header navigation items through the SDK configuration to match your DEX's branding and feature set.

steps.title: Hide Orderly Branding from TradingView Chart
steps.description: In the open-source UI template, use the tradingViewConfig object in config.tsx to hide the exchange name displayed on the chart.
steps.important: This removes the 'Orderly' label that appears as the data source on the TradingView chart, allowing your DEX branding to take precedence.

steps.title: Customize TradingView Chart Candle Colors
steps.description: Use the overrides property in the tradingViewOrderlyConfig object to customize candle colors.
steps.code:
overrides: {
  "mainSeriesProperties.candleStyle.borderDownColor": "#DC2140",
  "mainSeriesProperties.candleStyle.borderUpColor": "#1F8040",
  "mainSeriesProperties.candleStyle.downColor": "#DC2140",
  "mainSeriesProperties.candleStyle.upColor": "#1F8040",
  "mainSeriesProperties.candleStyle.wickDownColor": "#DC2140",
  "mainSeriesProperties.candleStyle.wickUpColor": "#1F8040",
}
steps.important: If changes don't appear, clear localStorage to force the chart to reload with new settings.

steps.title: Configure Sound Notifications
steps.description: SDK v2.10.2 introduced configurable sound alerts for trading events. SDK v2.12.3 fixes a bug in Safari, Firefox, and Edge where queued trade sound notifications would trigger simultaneously upon returning to an inactive trading tab.
steps.code:
// Upgrade to v2.12.3 for sound notification fixes:
"@orderly.network/react": "^2.12.3"
steps.important: Sound notifications are configurable for various trading events such as order fills and position changes.

steps.title: Enable Bulk Close by Profitability
steps.description: SDK v2.10.2 introduced bulk close by profitability, allowing users to close all profitable or losing positions at once.
steps.important: This feature enhances the user experience for active traders managing multiple positions.

steps.title: Configure TP/SL with Mark Price Offset
steps.description: SDK v2.12.3 allows users to set Offset and Offset% values for Take Profit and Stop Loss specifically calculated from the Mark Price. SDK v2.12.2 improved TP/SL logic on TradingView so that chart-dragging interactions use mark price instead of entry price.
steps.important: This enables 'lock-profit' stop-loss scenarios for existing profitable positions.

steps.title: Preview UI Colors with Storybook
steps.description: Use the Orderly Storybook to preview color settings and UI components before deploying changes.
steps.code:
// Storybook:
https://storybook.orderly.network/?path=/story/package-trading-tradingpage--page
steps.important: Storybook is faster than the Orderly One preview feature for checking individual component colors. There is no published mapping list of which color settings correspond to which UI elements.

commonIssues.issue: No asset categories appearing in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: No categories are set by default. You must explicitly configure which categories to display in your SDK configuration. Ensure you are using SDK v2.12.0 or later.

commonIssues.issue: 'Orderly' label still visible on TradingView chart.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the tradingViewConfig object in config.tsx is properly configured to hide the exchange name. Clear browser cache after making changes.

commonIssues.issue: TradingView chart color changes not appearing.
commonIssues.solution: Clear localStorage to force the chart to reload with new override settings.

commonIssues.issue: Sound notifications trigger simultaneously when returning to inactive tab.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v2.12.3 or later, which fixes this bug in Safari, Firefox, and Edge.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot determine which color setting maps to which UI element.
commonIssues.solution: Use the Orderly Storybook to preview components and their colors. There is no published mapping list, so visual inspection via Storybook is the recommended approach.

workflows.name: Creating Bracket Orders with Take Profit and Stop Loss via API
workflows.description: Open trading positions with nested Take Profit (TP) and Stop Loss (SL) child orders using the Orderly Create Algo Order API endpoint for automated position management.
prerequisites: Orderly API credentials (orderly-key, orderly-secret) with trading permissions
Understanding of algo order types and nested order structures
Active Orderly account with sufficient margin

steps.title: Review Algo Order Documentation
steps.description: Review the algorithmic order documentation and examples to understand TP/SL and bracket order configurations.
steps.code:
// Algo order samples and documentation:
// https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/algo-order-samples

steps.title: Understand Bracket Order Structure
steps.description: Bracket orders use `algo_type: 'BRACKET'` on the parent order with nested `child_orders` arrays. Stop orders do not support TP/SL directly — only Limit/Market parent orders do.
steps.important: The TP/SL side must be opposite to the position side. Set `reduce_only: true` on all child orders.

steps.title: Construct the Bracket Order Payload
steps.description: Build the JSON payload with the parent order and nested TP/SL child orders using the Create Algo Order endpoint. Authenticate with orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, and orderly-account-id headers.
steps.important: Algorithmic orders including TP/SL configurations are handled through a dedicated endpoint, separate from standard market/limit orders. The `trigger_price_type` can be set at the child_orders level to specify whether the trigger uses mark price, index price, or last traded price. For a BUY parent order, TP/SL child orders must have side 'SELL'. For a SELL parent order, they must have side 'BUY'.

steps.title: Submit and Verify the Order
steps.description: Send the bracket order to the Create Algo Order endpoint and verify it was placed correctly by checking the response and querying active algo orders. Monitor the order status through the API or WebSocket to confirm TP and SL levels are active.
steps.code:
// Verify active algo orders:
GET /v1/algo/orders?symbol=PERP_ETH_USDC&algo_type=BRACKET

commonIssues.issue: Child orders rejected with validation error.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure `reduce_only: true` is set on all child orders and that the TP/SL side is opposite to the parent order side.

commonIssues.issue: Trying to add TP/SL to a Stop order.
commonIssues.solution: Stop orders do not support TP/SL directly. Only Limit or Market parent orders can have bracket child orders.

commonIssues.issue: Trigger price not activating as expected.
commonIssues.solution: Check the `trigger_price_type` setting. By default, it may use mark price. Ensure the trigger price value is realistic relative to the current market price.

commonIssues.issue: TP/SL orders not triggering at expected prices.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the TP and SL price parameters are correctly formatted and within valid ranges. Check the algo order documentation for exact parameter requirements.

commonIssues.issue: Algo order request returns authentication error.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure all required headers (orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id) are correctly set and the signature is valid for the request body.

workflows.name: Fixing Python SDK _dispatch_request Function
workflows.description: Fix the _dispatch_request function in the official Orderly Python SDK to properly handle headers and request bodies for POST/PUT and GET/DELETE requests.

steps.title: Locate the _dispatch_request Function
steps.description: Open the orderly_evm_connector/api.py file and find the _dispatch_request function.
steps.code:
// File: orderly_evm_connector/api.py
// Function: _dispatch_request

steps.title: Replace the Function Implementation
steps.description: Replace the existing _dispatch_request function with the corrected version that properly handles Content-Type headers for different HTTP methods.
steps.important: The fix ensures POST/PUT requests send JSON bodies with the correct Content-Type header, while GET/DELETE requests use form-urlencoded.

steps.title: Test API Calls
steps.description: After applying the fix, test both GET and POST API calls to verify they work correctly with the proper headers.
steps.important: Verify that POST requests now send JSON bodies and GET requests use form-urlencoded format.

commonIssues.issue: POST requests failing with 400 or 415 errors.
commonIssues.solution: This is the exact issue the fix addresses. The original function does not set the correct Content-Type header for POST/PUT requests. Apply the replacement function.

commonIssues.issue: GET requests failing after applying the fix.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the else branch correctly sets 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=utf-8' for GET and DELETE requests.

workflows.name: Configuring the Multilevel Referral Program
workflows.description: Enable and configure the Orderly DEX Multilevel Referral Program to scale growth and incentivize communities through multi-tier referral rewards.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.9.0 or later (or latest Orderly One version)
Access to Admin Tool or Orderly One dashboard

steps.title: Upgrade SDK
steps.description: Ensure your DEX is running SDK version 2.9.0 or later. For Orderly One DEXs, ensure you are on the latest version available on the platform.
steps.important: As of SDK v2.12.4, users can bind a referral code to their existing account at any time post-registration, rather than being required to provide a code during registration.

steps.title: Activate the Referral Program
steps.description: Enable or upgrade the referral program via the Admin Tool or through the Orderly One dashboard.
steps.code:
// Admin Portal:
https://admin.orderly.network/login

steps.title: Configure Referral Code Parameters
steps.description: When creating a referral code, configure the rebate rates. All values are expressed as absolute decimals (e.g., 0.5 means 50% of fees).
steps.important: The owner of the referral code can adjust the split between referrer and referee at any time. Referral rebates are settled in USDC regardless of the collateral asset used, and are sent to users once per day.

steps.title: Use order_tag for Per-Order Referral Tracking
steps.description: Attach a referral code at the order level using the `order_tag` field in the create order API. This overrides any account-level referral binding.
steps.code:

Body: {
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "order_type": "MARKET",

  "side": "BUY",

}

steps.important: The Multilevel Referral Program supports multi-tier referral structures, allowing brokers to incentivize communities at scale.

commonIssues.issue: Rebates not appearing for users.
commonIssues.solution: Rebates are settled once per day in USDC. Ensure the referral code is correctly bound to the user's account and that the rebate rates are properly configured.

commonIssues.issue: Users unable to bind referral code after registration.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your SDK is updated to v2.12.4 or later, which enables binding referral codes to existing accounts at any time post-registration.

steps.important: Permissionless listings allow builders to list any asset not currently on Orderly. As the market owner, the builder earns 100% of liquidation fees plus 50% of Orderly's base fee on that market.

commonIssues.issue: Chart requests fail or cause instability for newly listed markets.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.3+ which optimizes K-line history loading to stop requesting unavailable historical data before a market's listing time, improving page stability.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot use Cross Margin on permissionless markets.
commonIssues.solution: This is by design. Permissionlessly listed markets only support Isolated Margin to limit risk exposure.

workflows.name: Setting Default Language Based on User Location
workflows.description: Configure your Orderly DEX to automatically set the default language based on the user's geographic location using geo IP detection.
prerequisites: Access to a geo IP API service
Ability to modify DEX frontend code or server configuration

steps.title: Choose Detection Approach
steps.description: Decide between client-side or server-side geo IP detection. Client-side is simpler but may cause a brief flash of the default language. Server-side provides a cleaner experience.
steps.important: Server-side rendering with Node.js allows changing the default language before sending static assets. The default static Nginx setup does not support pre-render location detection.

steps.title: Implement Geo IP Detection
steps.description: Use a geo IP API to determine the user's location and map it to the appropriate language code.

steps.title: Apply Language Setting
steps.description: Set the detected language as the default for the DEX interface before rendering the trading components.
steps.important: The language toggle button can also be re-enabled in the UI for manual switching by users who prefer a different language.

commonIssues.issue: Brief flash of default language before geo-detected language loads.
commonIssues.solution: Use server-side rendering with Node.js to detect location and set the language before sending static assets to the client.

commonIssues.issue: Geo IP API returns incorrect location.
commonIssues.solution: Use a reliable geo IP service and provide a manual language toggle as a fallback for users.

workflows.name: Querying Trading Data, Analytics, and Campaigns via API
workflows.description: Retrieve user and broker trading volumes, PnL, fees, referral stats, leaderboard rankings, campaign data, and account health using Orderly's REST API, WebSocket streams, SDK hooks, and dashboards. Also covers setting up and managing trading competitions and campaigns.
prerequisites: Active Orderly-powered DEX with registered broker ID
Orderly API credentials configured (orderly-key, orderly-secret, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id headers)
Admin wallet registered for broker-level and referral endpoints
Orderly SDK v2.0.0+ (optional, for SDK hooks)
Campaign requirements defined if running competitions (time, tasks, thresholds)

steps.title: Set Up Campaign with Orderly Team
steps.description: Provide campaign details to the Orderly team: campaign name, start/end dates, and trading task details (e.g., volume-based leaderboard). You will receive a campaign_id. For custom response formats (e.g., Gate Wallet, Layer3), provide requirements well in advance.
steps.important: For Perps Competitions, configure season-based parameters (season_id, start_at, trading_end_at, claim_start_at, claim_end_at, base_prize_pool, alpha/beta coefficients, etc.) via the backend before the competition starts. For Orderly One DEXs, launch permissionless competitions via Fuul integration with no coding required.

steps.title: Query Campaign Rankings and Leaderboard Data
steps.description: Use the public campaign ranking endpoint to fetch leaderboard data for trading competitions. Rankings are based on users' wallet addresses.
steps.important: Campaign PnL = Account Value (end) - Account Value (start) - total deposit value + total withdrawal value. This is account-level PnL, not per-symbol. Volume data updates every few minutes; other stats update hourly. Campaign data is archived 6 months after campaign ends (from Campaign 75+). Export data before the deadline.

steps.title: Integrate with Quest Platforms (Galxe, Layer3)
steps.description: For Galxe integrations, use a JavaScript expression to evaluate task completion from the standard API response.
steps.important: Standard campaign API response wraps data in a `data` object (e.g., {"success": true, "data": {"volume": 1000}}). Custom formats require dedicated development by the Orderly team.

steps.title: Retrieve User Trading Volume and Statistics
steps.description: Use REST API endpoints and SDK hooks to retrieve daily volume, user volume statistics, and overall user stats.
steps.important: 'ltd' means 'life to date', not 'last trading day'. For account UID, use the useAccountInstance hook and access account#keyStore.

steps.title: Fetch Broker and Per-User Volume Data
steps.description: Use private and public endpoints to get broker-level trading volume, per-user volumes, and aggregate analytics.
steps.important: Brokers can only access data for users under their own broker ID. The builder users volumes endpoint does not distinguish volume between specific trading pairs. Orderly does not provide a direct API for number of trades.

steps.title: Query Builder Leaderboard for Volume, PnL, and Fees
steps.description: Use the broker leaderboard endpoint for volume, PnL, and fee data within a 90-day window.
steps.important: The broker_fee field reflects fees before referral rebates are deducted. The endpoint requires authentication and date range must be within 90 days.

steps.title: Retrieve Referral and Funding Fee History
steps.description: Use dedicated endpoints for referral statistics, rebate data, and funding fee history.
steps.important: The admin wallet has exclusive access to referral code and fee rebate APIs. Do not rely on users pasting their account ID (UID) — implement proper wallet verification.

steps.title: Retrieve Deposit, Withdrawal, and Position History
steps.description: Fetch asset history, liquidation data, and position records for users.
steps.important: Withdrawal transaction hashes may take time to appear due to block confirmations (~500 blocks on Polygon). The position_notional field represents the total for the entire liquidation event, not per individual row.

steps.title: Subscribe to Real-Time Account Health via WebSocket
steps.description: Subscribe to WebSocket topics for real-time account health, balance, and position data.
steps.important: Implement reconnection logic with exponential backoff. Orderly does not offer hourly broker volume REST endpoints or webhooks — use WebSocket for sub-daily granularity.

steps.title: Query User Balance and Portfolio Performance
steps.description: Retrieve user balances, historical PnL, and construct performance charts.
steps.important: Real-time PnL must be calculated from position data, current price, and collateral. Account balance = Sum(holding token × current price) - Unsettled PnL.

steps.title: Access User Data via Admin API and Dashboard
steps.description: Use admin endpoints and the Orderly dashboard for broker-level user data access.
steps.important: Admin API endpoints are in Beta. The events_v2 endpoint only supports filtering per specific user (account_id). Granular trade data is stored for 90 days via standard API; use dashboard endpoints for older data.

steps.title: Fetch Vault APY and Track Partner Volume
steps.description: Retrieve vault APY values and track partner-specific volume using order tags.
steps.important: Assign a unique referral code as the order_tag value for all orders from a specific partner.

steps.title: Get User Points and Trading Rewards
steps.description: Use the public points endpoint for historical Merits data, or the current epoch estimate endpoint for active Trading Rewards.
steps.important: The Merits campaign has ended and been replaced by Trading Rewards. Use the current epoch estimate endpoint for active reward data.

steps.title: Build Custom Leaderboard UI
steps.description: Use the Orderly broker template on GitHub for ready-made leaderboard page examples, or build your own using the campaign ranking and volume APIs.
steps.important: Orderly does not provide a ready-made leaderboard UI — builders must implement their own. Implement periodic polling (every 30-60 seconds) to keep leaderboards updated. Reward distribution must be handled by the organizer.

commonIssues.issue: Campaign data no longer accessible.
commonIssues.solution: Campaign data is archived after the campaign ends (6 months for campaigns after ID 75, 1 month for campaigns before ID 75). Export data before the archiving deadline.

commonIssues.issue: PnL calculation seems incorrect for individual symbols.
commonIssues.solution: Campaign PnL is account-level, not per-symbol. The /v1/public/campaign/ranking endpoint includes unrealized PnL (UPnL), while /v1/broker/leaderboard/daily reflects only realized PnL.

commonIssues.issue: Errors when saving or publishing a points campaign on Orderly One.
commonIssues.solution: Clear your browser's local storage to force the creation of a new Orderly key, then retry. You must connect using the EOA wallet that was originally used to create the DEX.

commonIssues.issue: WebSocket connection drops frequently.
commonIssues.solution: Implement reconnection logic with exponential backoff. Ensure your WebSocket client handles reconnection gracefully.

commonIssues.issue: Volume data seems inconsistent or empty.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the correct endpoint and authenticating with the correct admin wallet registered under your broker ID. Brokers can only access data for users under their own broker ID. Paginate through all results.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal transaction hash not appearing in history.
commonIssues.solution: Wait for sufficient block confirmations (~500 blocks on Polygon). The hash will appear once the transaction is confirmed on-chain.

commonIssues.issue: Deposit status not updating in real time.
commonIssues.solution: Use useDepositStatusScript hook for reactive updates, or subscribe to the wallet WebSocket topic.

commonIssues.issue: Points endpoint returns empty data.
commonIssues.solution: The Merits campaign has ended. Use the current epoch estimate endpoint for active Trading Rewards data instead.

commonIssues.issue: Real-time PnL is not available via a single API call.
commonIssues.solution: Calculate real-time PnL from position data, current price, and collateral using WebSocket balance stream combined with position and price endpoints.

commonIssues.issue: Leaderboard endpoint returns empty data.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the date range is within the 90-day window and that broker_id and address parameters are correct. The endpoint requires authentication.

commonIssues.issue: Admin API endpoints return 403 Forbidden.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using properly authenticated admin API credentials. These endpoints are in Beta and may require additional setup with the Orderly team.

commonIssues.issue: broker_fee values seem higher than expected.
commonIssues.solution: The broker_fee value reflects fees before referral rebates are deducted. Check the referral rebate summary endpoint for net amounts.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot get lifetime volume for a specific wallet.
commonIssues.solution: There is no single endpoint for lifetime volume. Use dashboard endpoints to aggregate all trades. Granular trade data is only stored for 90 days via standard API.

commonIssues.issue: Campaign ranking API returns empty results on testnet.
commonIssues.solution: Use the testnet-specific endpoint (https://testnet-api.orderly.org/v1/public/campaign/ranking). The mainnet UI is hardcoded to mainnet.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot aggregate trades by broker, user, and market simultaneously.
commonIssues.solution: This is a current API limitation. The events_v2 endpoint only supports filtering per specific user (account_id). Use the Builder's Leaderboard API for aggregated volume data.

commonIssues.issue: Broker API key rejected on testnet.
commonIssues.solution: Broker keys must be registered separately for testnet at https://github-dev.orderly.network/broker-registration/ (select a testnet chain when registering).

commonIssues.issue: Referral code verification returns false positives.
commonIssues.solution: Never trust user-provided UIDs. Always verify through actual wallet login and use the check-referral-code endpoint with authenticated data.

commonIssues.issue: Fee revenue endpoint shows zero.
commonIssues.solution: Builder-level revenue is settled daily. Ensure your admin wallet is properly registered and that trading activity has occurred.

workflows.name: Adding Custom Chains to Orderly SDK
workflows.description: Add support for new chains like Story, Solana, or Sei to your Orderly-powered DEX using the chainFilter prop in OrderlyAppProvider.
prerequisites: Chain ID of the target network
Broker ID registered on the target chain (if applicable)

steps.title: Import Chain Types
steps.description: Import the necessary chain types from @orderly.network/types for built-in chains.
steps.code: import { Arbitrum, Optimism } from "@orderly.network/types";

steps.title: Configure chainFilter Prop
steps.description: Use the chainFilter prop on OrderlyAppProvider to specify which chains to enable, including custom chains by their ID.
steps.code:
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  brokerName="Your Broker"
  networkId="mainnet"
  chainFilter={{
    mainnet: [
      Arbitrum,
      Optimism,
      { id: 90009090 }, // Solana
      { id: 1514 },     // Story
    ],
  }}
>
  {children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
steps.important: Chain IDs can be found at chainlist.org. For Solana, use ID 90009090. For Story, use ID 1514.

steps.title: Add Testnet Chains (Optional)
steps.description: To add testnet chains like Monad Testnet, use the testnet key in chainFilter with full chain configuration.
steps.important: Your broker_id must be registered on testnet as well. If testnets are not visible, ensure `showTestnet` is not set to `false` in overrides.

steps.title: Handle Network Switching
steps.description: The `networkId` cannot change during runtime. Use a page refresh or separate domain when switching between testnet and mainnet.
steps.important: For Solana support, ensure you are using SDK v2.0.0+ (Hooks SDK) and have applied the Solana Multi-DVN security upgrade (v2.12.3+).

commonIssues.issue: Chain does not appear in the chain selector.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the chain ID is correct and that the chainFilter prop is properly structured. For testnets, ensure `showTestnet` is not set to false.

commonIssues.issue: Solana deposits/withdrawals fail.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you have upgraded to SDK v2.12.3+ for the mandatory Solana Multi-DVN security upgrade.

workflows.name: Listing a New Token on Orderly Network

Market maker integrated with Orderly (or willingness to bring your own)

steps.title: Verify Price Index Availability
steps.description: Ensure your token has price index availability with at least 3 price feed sources from Tier 1 & 2 CEXs and on-chain oracles.
steps.important: Without sufficient price feed sources, the token cannot be listed as a reliable index/mark price is required for perpetual trading.

steps.title: Secure Market Maker Integration
steps.description: Ensure a market maker that has integrated with Orderly is available for your token. Projects can bring their own market maker or use Orderly's existing MM integrations.
steps.important: Orderly's liquidity is provided by 50+ professional market makers including Sellini, Wintermute, Kronos, and RiverSide Hedge.

steps.title: Meet Liquidity Requirements
steps.description: Ensure the token meets Orderly's minimum liquidity requirements for listing.
steps.important: These requirements ensure sufficient market depth and tight spreads for a good trading experience.

steps.title: Submit Listing Proposal

steps.important: Builders can also use the Permissionless Listing framework to list tokens without the standard listing process, or use Custom Oracles to push prices for non-standard assets.

commonIssues.issue: Token does not meet minimum FDV requirement.
commonIssues.solution: The minimum FDV/market cap is $20M+. Consider using the Permissionless Listing framework as an alternative path.

commonIssues.issue: Insufficient price feed sources.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the token is listed on at least 3 Tier 1 or Tier 2 CEXs, or supplement with on-chain oracle price feeds. Custom Oracles can also be used to push prices directly.

commonIssues.issue: No market maker available.

workflows.name: Accessing Builder Analytics and Trader Data
workflows.description: Access trading volume, user data, wallet information, and on-chain transaction details for your Orderly-powered DEX using the Builder Data API, Orderly Dashboard, and Dune analytics.
prerequisites: Active Orderly-powered DEX with a broker ID

steps.title: Query Builder Volume and User Data via API
steps.description: Use the Builder Data API endpoint to access trading volume and user data for your DEX.
steps.important: This endpoint provides volume and user-level data specific to your broker ID.

steps.title: View Wallet and Trader Data via Orderly Dashboard
steps.description: Access the Orderly Dashboard to view wallet data and trader information, filtering by your broker ID.
steps.important: Brokers can filter by their broker ID to see all traders and their associated wallets.

steps.title: View On-Chain Transaction Details
steps.description: View processed, human-readable trade details on the Orderly dashboard. After a trade is matched off-chain, the backend submits transaction details to the chain as a ledger entry.
steps.important: Orderly uses an off-chain matching, on-chain settlement model. Trades are matched off-chain for speed, then settled on-chain as ledger entries.

steps.title: Use Dune Analytics for Trending Tokens and Broader Analytics
steps.description: For trending tokens and broader analytics that are not available via API, use Orderly's Dune dashboard.
steps.code:
// Dune Dashboard:
https://dune.com/orderly_network/orderly-dashboard
steps.important: There is no dedicated trending tokens API. Dune provides the most comprehensive analytics for the Orderly ecosystem.

commonIssues.issue: Builder Data API returns empty results.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are authenticating correctly with your broker admin credentials and that your broker ID is properly associated with the request.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot find specific trade on the dashboard.

workflows.name: Enabling and Trading with Isolated Margin Mode
workflows.description: Enable isolated margin mode at the broker and SDK level, configure symbol-level leverage, and execute isolated margin trades via the Orderly REST API, including managing margin, closing positions, and handling TradingView chart integrations.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.11.2 or later (mandatory for isolated margin infrastructure; v3.1.3+ recommended for all fixes)
Active broker ID and DEX deployment
Registered Orderly account with a Trading Key (scope: 'trading') for API trading
Sufficient collateral deposited in the Orderly account
Communication channel with Orderly team for broker-level enablement

steps.title: Request Isolated Margin Enablement from Orderly Team
steps.description: Contact the Orderly team to request Isolated Margin Mode enablement for your broker ID. This must be enabled separately for testnet and mainnet and goes through production environment testing.
steps.important: After the Orderly team enables the feature, there may be a ~20 minute delay before it becomes active. Plan for this activation delay when scheduling the feature rollout.

steps.title: Upgrade SDK to Required Version
steps.description: Upgrade to SDK v2.11.2 or higher, which is a mandatory update for isolated margin infrastructure. SDK v2.12.0+ adds ISO/Cross margin labels on orders, positions, and TradingView chart position lines. SDK v3.1.3 is recommended for all bug fixes.
steps.important: Isolated margin mode assigns a defined margin per position, meaning profits from one position cannot offset losses in another. The feature is rolled out gradually across all Orderly DEXs.

steps.title: Configure Symbol-Level Leverage (Optional)
steps.description: Starting from SDK v2.7.3, brokers can configure leverage per symbol instead of account-wide leverage, giving traders greater flexibility and control over margin settings for individual markets.
steps.code: "@orderly.network/react": "^2.7.3"
steps.important: Symbol-level leverage allows traders to set different leverage limits for different trading pairs. SDK v2.2.0+ unlocks 100x leverage on BTC, ETH, and SOL perpetual pairs.

steps.title: Set Leverage for Isolated Margin via API
steps.description: Configure the leverage for a specific symbol under Isolated Margin mode using the REST API. Each symbol maintains independent leverage settings per margin mode.
steps.important: Higher leverage means less margin is allocated per position and a tighter liquidation price. Each symbol can have different leverage under Cross vs Isolated mode independently (e.g., 10x Cross and 20x Isolated for the same symbol).

steps.title: Place Orders with Isolated Margin
steps.description: Submit an order with margin_mode set to 'ISOLATED' in the request body.
steps.code:
POST /v1/order
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "order_type": "LIMIT",
  "side": "BUY",
  "order_price": 2500,
  "order_quantity": 1,
  "margin_mode": "ISOLATED"
}
steps.important: If margin_mode is omitted, the symbol's default margin mode is used. You can change the default display mode via POST /v1/client/margin_mode, but this is primarily for frontend display and does not restrict which mode you can trade in.

steps.title: Add or Reduce Margin on an Existing Position
steps.description: Adjust the margin allocated to an isolated position to manage liquidation risk.
steps.important: ADD transfers margin from available balance to the isolated position. REDUCE transfers margin from the isolated position back to available balance.

steps.title: Query Isolated Margin Positions
steps.description: Retrieve the current state of an isolated position including margin, leverage, liquidation price, and PnL.
steps.important: For real-time position updates, subscribe to the private 'position' WebSocket topic instead of polling the REST endpoint.

steps.title: Enable Advanced TP/SL with Mark Price Offset
steps.description: From SDK v2.12.3 onward, advanced TP/SL options allow users to set Offset and Offset% values specifically calculated from the Mark Price.
steps.important: This gives traders more precise control over take-profit and stop-loss levels relative to the Mark Price rather than the entry price.

steps.title: Verify TradingView Chart Integration
steps.description: SDK v2.12.0+ displays cross/isolated margin mode labels on TradingView chart position lines along with leverage. SDK v3.1.3 fixed an issue when closing isolated margin positions from TradingView position lines by sending the correct margin mode to prevent reduce-only validation errors.
steps.important: Ensure your TradingView integration is up to date to display margin mode labels correctly and allow seamless chart-based position closing.

steps.title: Handle Permissionless Markets
steps.description: Permissionless listing markets may be configured as 'isolated only'. Ensure your frontend correctly defaults to isolated margin mode for these markets.
steps.important: Permissionlessly listed markets are Isolated-only to limit risk exposure. They do not support cross margin.

steps.title: Batch Leverage Update (Optional)
steps.description: Update leverage for multiple symbols at once by omitting the symbol parameter. Behavior differs between Cross and Isolated modes.
steps.important: For Cross mode: all cross-margin symbols update atomically (all succeed or none do). For Isolated mode: the update only applies to symbols with no active isolated positions or pending orders; eligible symbols always update.

commonIssues.issue: Isolated margin mode not available in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your SDK is at least v2.11.2 (mandatory infrastructure update). Wait ~20 minutes after the Orderly team confirms enablement. Ensure the feature was enabled for the correct environment (testnet vs mainnet). The feature is being rolled out gradually across all Orderly DEXs.

commonIssues.issue: 'Margin will be insufficient after' error when using 100% slider on isolated margin market orders.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.0 or later, which reserves a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula.

commonIssues.issue: Reduce-only validation error when closing isolated margin positions from TradingView.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.3 or later, which sends the correct margin mode when closing positions from chart position lines.

commonIssues.issue: Cross margin still available on permissionless markets.
commonIssues.solution: Permissionless markets should default to isolated margin only. Check that your frontend correctly handles the _arthur suffix and forces isolated margin mode.

commonIssues.issue: Maximum leverage lower than expected.
commonIssues.solution: Check existing open positions and available margin. The effective maximum leverage depends on the initial margin ratio calculation which accounts for all open positions.

commonIssues.issue: Margin labels not showing on TradingView chart.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v2.12.0+ which adds position lines with cross/isolated margin mode labels and leverage display on the TradingView chart.

commonIssues.issue: Order rejected due to insufficient margin.
commonIssues.solution: In Isolated Margin, each position requires dedicated margin. Ensure you have enough available balance to cover the initial margin requirement (IMR) for the new position at the configured leverage.

commonIssues.issue: Batch leverage update does not apply to some Isolated symbols.
commonIssues.solution: In Isolated mode, batch leverage updates skip symbols that have active isolated positions or pending orders. Update those symbols individually after closing positions or canceling orders.

commonIssues.issue: Liquidation occurs unexpectedly.
commonIssues.solution: Isolated Margin caps losses at the margin assigned to that position. If the position's margin falls below the maintenance margin ratio (MMR), only that single position is liquidated. Add margin proactively using POST /v1/position_margin with type 'ADD'.

steps.title: Stake $ORDER Tokens
steps.description: Stake $ORDER tokens to gain voting power in governance proposals. Stakers receive esORDER with vesting.
steps.important: Staking $ORDER is required to participate in governance votes, including the Vote to Retain process for token delistings.

steps.title: Vote on Governance Proposals
steps.description: Participate in governance proposals that can redirect up to 60% of Orderly fees into $ORDER buybacks.

steps.title: Participate in Vote to Retain
steps.description: When tokens are identified for potential delisting, vote to retain them. More than 3% (or 5% in some cases) of total staked $ORDER must vote AGAINST delisting within a 5-day voting period.
steps.important: Tokens without sufficient votes are delisted. The index/mark price is fixed at the average price of the last hour before delisting time.

commonIssues.issue: Unsure how esORDER vesting works.
commonIssues.solution: esORDER has a 3-month vesting period. During vesting, tokens cannot be transferred but can be used for governance voting and fee tier qualification.

commonIssues.issue: Vote to Retain threshold unclear.
commonIssues.solution: The threshold is typically >3% or >5% of total staked $ORDER, depending on the specific proposal. Check the governance proposal details for the exact threshold.

steps.description: Design your volume-based fee tiers. By default, all users have the same fees unless you implement a tier system.

steps.title: Run Script on Schedule

steps.important: The script queries user volumes and calls the Orderly API to update individual fee rates for users who qualify for different tiers.

steps.title: Alternative: Fixed Fee for All Users
steps.description: If you prefer a simple approach without volume tiers, set the default fee to your desired rate and all users will trade at that rate.

commonIssues.solution: Ensure the script is running with the correct admin wallet credentials and that the API calls are properly signed. Check the Orderly API response for errors.

commonIssues.issue: Users complain about unexpected fee changes.
commonIssues.solution: Communicate your fee tier structure clearly on your DEX. Consider notifying users when they move between tiers.

workflows.description: Integrate on-chain staking of ORDER tokens via the proxy contract, including LayerZero fee handling for cross-chain staking operations.

steps.title: Approve ORDER Token for Proxy Contract
steps.description: Before staking, the user must approve the proxy contract to spend their ORDER tokens.
steps.important: The approval must be completed before calling the stakeOrder function.

steps.title: Fetch LayerZero Fee
steps.description: Call the quoteStakeOrder view function on the proxy contract to get the required LayerZero bridging fee.
steps.important: The Orderly app multiplies the quoted fee by 1.1, though the exact reason is undocumented. This buffer helps prevent transaction failures due to fee fluctuations.

steps.title: Call stakeOrder Function
steps.description: Execute the staking transaction by calling stakeOrder with the ORDER amount and attaching the LayerZero fee as msg.value.
steps.important: Attach the adjusted LZ fee as the `value` parameter. Insufficient value will cause the transaction to revert.

steps.title: Handle Unstaking
steps.description: To unstake, users can press the down arrow in the staking interface to reveal the unstake button, or call the unstake function on the proxy contract.
steps.important: See tokenomics addresses for all relevant contract addresses: https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/tokenomics/addresses

commonIssues.issue: Staking transaction reverts with insufficient value.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are attaching the LayerZero fee (multiplied by 1.1) as msg.value. Call quoteStakeOrder first to get the current fee estimate.

commonIssues.issue: Approval transaction succeeds but staking fails.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the approved amount is sufficient and that the user has enough native token (ETH) to cover the LayerZero fee.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot find unstake option in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Press the down arrow in the staking interface to reveal the unstake button.

prerequisites: Backend server capable of secure key storage

steps.title: Create Orderly Key in Browser
steps.description: Generate an Orderly key locally in the user's browser with trade and asset scope (read scope is also useful). This key pair is used for API authentication without requiring wallet signatures for every request.
steps.important: The ORDERLY_SECRET is not provided by Orderly — you must generate it yourself. It is used for generating request signatures as part of API authentication.

steps.title: Send Key to Backend for Storage
steps.description: Transmit the generated Orderly key to your backend server for secure storage. The backend will use this key to sign API requests on behalf of the user.
steps.important: Store the key securely on your backend. Never expose the secret in client-side code or logs.

steps.title: Route Trades Through Backend
steps.description: When a user initiates a trade, route the request through your backend. Your backend uses the stored Orderly key to create trades via the Orderly API.

steps.title: Deduct Fees via Internal Transfer
steps.description: After trade execution, deduct insurance or service fees by creating an internal transfer from the user's Orderly account to your broker's Orderly account.
steps.important: After internal transfer to your Orderly account, you can withdraw the accumulated fees. Withdrawing to another address may require whitelisting your smart contract address.

commonIssues.issue: API requests fail with authentication errors.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the orderly-key is correctly registered and that signatures are properly generated using the orderly-secret. Check timestamp synchronization — timestamps must be within the allowed window.

commonIssues.issue: Internal transfer fails.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the user has sufficient balance and that the transfer amount does not exceed available funds after accounting for open position margins.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal to external address fails.
commonIssues.solution: Withdrawing to another address may require whitelisting your smart contract address with the Orderly team.

workflows.name: Generating and Managing Orderly API Credentials
workflows.description: Generate ed25519 keypairs for Orderly API authentication, register them with Orderly, manage key lifecycle including expiration and deletion, derive public keys from private keys, create read-only monitoring keys, and store credentials for automated trading.
prerequisites: Registered Orderly account (wallet registered with a broker ID)
Access to broker registration tool or Orderly SDK
Understanding of ed25519 keypair generation and Orderly API authentication

steps.title: Understand API Authentication Model
steps.description: Orderly uses ed25519 keypairs for API authentication. When a user creates an account and enables trading (both requiring a Web3 wallet signature), an ed25519 keypair is generated locally and the public key is registered with Orderly. All subsequent API calls use this keypair — no wallet signature needed per call.
steps.important: A user may create multiple keypairs for the same account. Every user needs their own API key per account. A broker cannot use a single API key for all users.

steps.title: Generate Orderly Key and Secret Pair
steps.description: The Orderly Key (public) and Secret (private) are generated permissionlessly by signing an EIP-712 message with an EVM wallet (or using the Solana equivalent). The private key generated during this process serves as the ORDERLY_SECRET. Keys are stored in browser local storage after generation.
steps.important: The secret key is shown only once when creating an Orderly key. Store it securely. The private key is never exposed to Orderly or any server. You only need a registered account to generate a key.

steps.title: Set Custom Key Expiration
steps.description: By default, Orderly keys expire after 30 days. Set a custom expiration period during key creation to avoid frequent key rotation.
steps.important: If no expiry date is explicitly set, the key expires after 30 days by default. On the DEX UI, expiration time cannot be set at the moment, but there is a delete button available.

steps.title: Register Key with Orderly
steps.description: After generating the key pair, register it with Orderly to associate it with your account via the public endpoint or through the DEX UI portfolio/API key page.
steps.important: Base URL is api.orderly.org (api-evm.orderly.org is deprecated but still works).

steps.title: Retrieve API Key from Browser Local Storage
steps.description: The Orderly API key and secret are stored in browser local storage after connecting the wallet. Look for a key like 'orderly_mainnet_[number]' containing accountId and orderlyKey.
steps.important: The public key (API key) must be derived from the private key stored in local storage.

steps.title: Derive Public Key from Private Key Manually
steps.description: The Orderly public key can be derived from the 64-byte private key by taking the last 32 bytes and Base58 encoding them.
steps.important: The private key is 64 bytes. Only the last 32 bytes are used for the public key derivation.

steps.title: Create Read-Only Monitoring Key
steps.description: Create a separate, independent Orderly API key with read-only scope for monitoring services to avoid affecting trading API rate limits.
steps.important: Rate limiting is enforced per account, but monitoring rate limits do not affect trading API keys since trading endpoints have additional, separate rate limit configurations.

steps.title: Use Credentials for API Authentication
steps.description: Use the generated credentials to authenticate API requests by including the required headers.
steps.important: Withdrawals always require a wallet signature from the user, regardless of API key authentication. This is a security requirement.

steps.title: Store Keys for Automated Trading (Bots)
steps.description: For trading bots that trade on behalf of users, the application must store the user's Orderly Key securely since automated products cannot rely on users generating keys in their browser at trade execution time.
steps.important: It is recommended to have at least a UI where users can register and store their Orderly Key in the application's infrastructure so that bots can trade on their behalf, as well as handle deposits and withdrawals.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot find orderly-account-id or orderly-key.
commonIssues.solution: Obtain these from your DEX under Portfolio -> API Keys, or from the broker registration page at https://github-dev.orderly.network/broker-registration/.

commonIssues.issue: Signature verification fails on API requests.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the signing message format is exactly {timestamp}{method}{path}{body}, the signature is base64url-encoded, and the timestamp is in milliseconds. The secret is shown only once during key creation — if lost, generate a new key pair.

commonIssues.issue: Trading bot cannot execute trades.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the bot has access to the user's stored Orderly Key. The infrastructure must control and store these keys securely for automated trading.

commonIssues.issue: API key expires unexpectedly.
commonIssues.solution: Set a custom expiration period during key creation. Default expiration is 30 days. Expired keys must be replaced by generating new ones.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot find API key in local storage.
commonIssues.solution: Look for a key like 'orderly_mainnet_[number]'. Ensure the wallet was properly connected and the account was registered before key generation.

commonIssues.issue: Monitoring service hits rate limits that affect trading.
commonIssues.solution: Create a separate read-only API key for monitoring. Trading and monitoring rate limits are configured independently.

commonIssues.issue: Need to revoke a compromised API key.
commonIssues.solution: Use DELETE /v1/client/orderly-key to remove the key, or use the delete button in the DEX UI portfolio page.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawals fail even with valid API key.
commonIssues.solution: Withdrawals always require a wallet signature from the user, regardless of API key authentication. This is a security requirement.

workflows.description: Implement the Delegate Signer feature to support Account Abstraction (smart contract) wallets and fix EIP-712 signature verification errors when using delegate withdrawals.
prerequisites: AA wallet or delegate signer wallet setup

steps.title: Understand the AA Wallet Limitation
steps.description: Orderly Network requires EIP-712 signatures, which smart contract wallets (AA wallets) cannot natively sign. Implement the Delegate Signer feature to allow a designated EOA to sign on behalf of the AA wallet.
steps.code:
// Delegate Signer documentation:
// https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-evm/user-flows/delegate-signer
steps.important: Alternatively, AA wallets can manage user liquidity between chains while an EOA handles Orderly-specific signing.

steps.title: Configure EIP-712 Typed Data for Delegate Withdrawals
steps.description: When constructing the EIP-712 typed data for delegate withdrawals, ensure the delegateContract field type is set to 'address'.
steps.important: Using the wrong type for delegateContract is a common cause of signature verification failures.

steps.title: Sign with the Correct Key
steps.description: The EIP-712 signature must be produced by the delegated signer's wallet private key, not the Orderly secret key.
steps.important: The Orderly secret key is only used for the 'orderly-signature' header authentication, not for EIP-712 delegate signing.

commonIssues.issue: EIP-712 signature verification error on delegate withdrawal.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the delegateContract field type is 'address' (not 'string') and that the signature is produced by the delegated signer's wallet private key, not the Orderly secret key.

commonIssues.issue: AA wallet cannot sign Orderly transactions.
commonIssues.solution: Implement the Delegate Signer feature to designate an EOA to sign on behalf of the AA wallet. Reference: https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/delegate-signer

workflows.name: Customizing SDK Trading Interface Theme and Charts
workflows.description: Customize the Orderly SDK trading interface including light/dark themes, CSS variables, TradingView chart colors, PnL card sharing, and component-level styling.

steps.title: Override CSS Variables for Theming
steps.description: The Orderly SDK uses CSS variables prefixed with '--oui-' for theming. Override these variables in your CSS to create custom themes.
steps.important: Be cautious with overrides like '.oui-text-transparent { color: inherit !important; }' as they can cause text visibility issues in certain themes.
