steps.important: Some studies_overrides (like volume colors) may only work in paid TradingView versions. SDK v1.3.2+ includes fixes for TradingView override configuration support.

steps.title: Configure PnL Card Sharing
steps.description: Configure PnL card sharing via the shareOptions prop on OrderlyAppProvider with custom colors, background images, and layout.
steps.code:
<OrderlyAppProvider
  shareOptions={{
    pnl: {
      profitColor: 'green',
      lossColor: 'red',
      backgroundImages: [
        '/images/poster_bg_1.png',
        '/images/poster_bg_2.png',
      ],
      layout: {
        message: {
          width: 100,
          height: 25,
          fontSize: 16,
          position: { left: 300, top: 150 }
        }
      }
    }
  }}
>
  {children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>

// For per-position poster data, use the usePoster hook
// with position data from usePositionStream
steps.important: Use profitColor and lossColor (not fontColor or color) to set PnL text colors. Referral codes are displayed on PnL cards by default if a referral code belongs to the account.

steps.title: Add Custom Component IDs for CSS Targeting
steps.description: SDK v1.3.2+ adds component IDs to the orderbook and trades modules, enabling brokers to customize these modules via CSS.
steps.important: Upgrade to SDK v1.3.2 or later to access component IDs for the orderbook and trades modules.

commonIssues.issue: Chart color changes only appear on desktop but not mobile.
commonIssues.solution: Clear localStorage as the SDK may cache chart settings. A known SDK bug affecting mobile chart color configuration was addressed in subsequent SDK updates.

commonIssues.issue: TradingView overrides not applying.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using SDK v1.3.2+ which includes fixes for TradingView override configuration. Clear browser cache when testing, as local cache can override default settings.

commonIssues.issue: Text visibility issues after theme customization.
commonIssues.solution: Avoid overly broad CSS overrides like '.oui-text-transparent { color: inherit !important; }'. Test your theme in both light and dark modes.

commonIssues.issue: colorConfig property doesn't change candlestick colors.
commonIssues.solution: The colorConfig property (downColor, upColor, etc.) applies to on-chart trading elements only. Use TradingView chart overrides for actual K-line/candlestick colors.

workflows.name: Troubleshooting Withdrawal and Order Placement Errors
workflows.description: Resolve common API errors when withdrawing funds and placing orders, including amount errors, price filter violations, and PnL settlement requirements.
prerequisites: Understanding of Orderly trading and withdrawal flows

steps.title: Fix 'Amount Error' (Code 5) on Withdrawals
steps.description: The 'Amount error' occurs when the withdrawal amount is less than the withdrawal fee. Ensure the amount exceeds the fee and is specified with correct decimal precision.
steps.important: The withdrawal fee is dynamic and varies by chain. Always check the /v1/public/token endpoint for current fees.

steps.title: Settle Unsettled PnL Before Withdrawing
steps.description: All PnL must be settled before withdrawing. Unsettled PnL inflates total_collateral_value but is not reflected in the withdrawable holding balance.
steps.important: Use the PnL settlement endpoint if withdrawal fails due to unsettled PnL.

steps.title: Fix 'Price Filter Requirement' Error (Code -1104)
steps.description: This error occurs when order price or quantity does not conform to the symbol's tick size or lot size filters.
steps.important: Check the symbol's trading rules from the available symbols endpoint for exact precision requirements.

steps.title: Understand Withdrawal Processing Times
steps.description: Withdrawal processing time depends on the destination chain, typically ranging from a few minutes to around 30 minutes.
steps.important: A withdrawal fee is charged (deducted from the withdrawal amount) to cover cross-chain messaging costs. The fee varies by chain.

steps.title: Retrieve Available Trading Symbols
steps.description: Use the public REST API to get all supported trading pairs and their precision requirements.
steps.important: Use this endpoint to verify precision requirements before placing orders to avoid filter errors.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal fails with 'Amount error' (code 5).
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the withdrawal amount exceeds the dynamic withdrawal fee and is specified with 6 decimal places. Settle all PnL before withdrawing.

commonIssues.issue: Order rejected with 'price filter requirement' error (code -1104).
commonIssues.solution: Verify that order_price follows quote_tick increments and order_quantity respects base_tick decimal precision. Use order_quantity (not order_amount) for futures/perpetual orders.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal takes longer than expected.
commonIssues.solution: Processing time varies by chain (few minutes to ~30 minutes). During high network congestion, withdrawals may take longer. Check the destination chain's status.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal to specific chain fails with error code 28.
commonIssues.solution: That chain may not be enabled for your broker. Some chains have exclusivity arrangements. Contact Orderly support to enable additional chains.

workflows.name: Configuring SEO and Brand Metadata for Orderly One DEX
workflows.description: Customize SEO metadata, Open Graph tags, and social media link previews for your Orderly One-based perpetual DEX so that your brand appears instead of 'Orderly Network'.
prerequisites: Hosting on a platform like Vercel (recommended)

steps.title: Move Configuration to Build-Time Environment Variables
steps.description: The default Orderly One setup loads config dynamically from /public/config.js at runtime, causing social media crawlers to capture the default 'Orderly Network' name. Move configuration to .env build-time variables.
steps.code:
# .env file
VITE_APP_NAME=YourBrand
VITE_APP_DESCRIPTION="Your description"
VITE_SEO_SITE_NAME="YourBrand Perps"
VITE_SEO_SITE_DESCRIPTION="Your description"
VITE_SEO_SITE_URL=https://yourdomain.com
VITE_SEO_SITE_LANGUAGE=en
VITE_SEO_SITE_LOCALE=en_US
VITE_SEO_THEME_COLOR=#000000
VITE_SEO_KEYWORDS="dex, perps, crypto"
steps.important: Social media crawlers do not execute JavaScript, so runtime-loaded config will not be captured. Build-time variables ensure crawlers see your brand.

steps.title: Configure Additional Build-Time Variables
steps.description: Set other useful build-time variables for broker configuration and UI customization.
steps.code:
# Additional .env variables
VITE_ORDERLY_BROKER_ID=your_broker_id
VITE_ORDERLY_BROKER_NAME="Your Brand"
VITE_DEFAULT_CHAIN=1
VITE_ORDERLY_MAINNET_CHAINS=1,42161,10
VITE_PRIVY_APP_ID=your_privy_id
VITE_ENABLED_MENUS=trade,vaults
VITE_TRADING_VIEW_COLOR_CONFIG={...}
steps.important: These variables are embedded at build time and will be available to crawlers and in the initial HTML response.

steps.title: Deploy and Verify
steps.description: Deploy your DEX with the new environment variables and verify that social media link previews show your brand.
steps.important: A native Open Graph feature that works without moving config to .env is on the Orderly team's backlog but has no confirmed release timeline.

commonIssues.issue: Social media previews still show 'Orderly Network'.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure configuration is set as build-time environment variables (.env), not runtime config (/public/config.js). Crawlers do not execute JavaScript.

commonIssues.issue: Environment variables not being picked up after deployment.
commonIssues.solution: Rebuild the application after changing .env variables. Vite embeds VITE_* variables at build time, so a new build is required for changes to take effect.

prerequisites: Contact with Orderly team for onboarding

steps.title: Contact Orderly Team for Onboarding
steps.description: The Ceffu integration onboarding process involves multiple steps handled by Orderly. Contact the Orderly team to initiate the process and receive onboarding documentation.
steps.important: The onboarding includes linking the Orderly DEX wallet (account_id) to a Ceffu account.

steps.title: Use Orderly-Wrapped Ceffu Endpoints
steps.description: Endpoints for delegation and venue rebalancing are wrapped by Orderly and belong to the Orderly API, not the Ceffu API directly.
steps.important: These are Orderly API endpoints that wrap Ceffu functionality. Do not call Ceffu API directly for these operations.

steps.title: Track Rebalance Operations
steps.description: Use the venue_rebalance_request_id returned in the rebalance response to track the status of operations.
steps.important: Assets remain in Ceffu custody throughout the trading process.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot find Ceffu-specific API documentation.
commonIssues.solution: Contact the Orderly team for the onboarding documentation. Ceffu endpoints are wrapped by Orderly and documented separately from the standard API.

commonIssues.issue: Venue rebalance operation stuck.
commonIssues.solution: Use the venue_rebalance_request_id to check the operation status via the history endpoint. Contact Orderly support if the operation remains pending.

workflows.name: Understanding and Optimizing Builder Staking Tiers and Fees
workflows.description: Understand Orderly's fee structure and Builder Tier System, qualify for higher tiers via 30-day trading volume or ORDER token staking, reduce base taker fees, and leverage tier benefits including maker fee rebates, marketing support, and listing campaigns.
prerequisites: Active Orderly-powered DEX with broker ID
ORDER tokens for staking (optional) or sufficient trading volume
Understanding of current trading volume metrics and fee structure

steps.title: Review Base Fee Structure
steps.description: Orderly charges a base 3 bps (0.03%) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Brokers set their own fees on top; the custom fee portion (above base fee) goes 100% to the broker. Maker fee rebates range from -0.5 bps to 0, and brokers can retain the rebate as revenue or pass it to users.
steps.important: Fees can be changed later by the broker once the admin wallet is set up. Funding rate fees are charged continuously while positions remain open and are separate from trading fees.

steps.title: Review Builder Tier Classifications and Requirements
steps.description: The Builder Tier System categorizes brokers into Public, Silver, Gold, Platinum, and Diamond tiers based on 30-day average trading volume or ORDER tokens staked. Higher tiers unlock reduced base taker fees, marketing support, and listing campaigns.
steps.important: Builders can qualify through EITHER trading volume OR ORDER token staking — whichever threshold is met first. RWA pair fees are also tier-based.

steps.title: Calculate Potential Fee Savings
steps.description: Model your potential savings by comparing your current base fee against the reduced rate at higher tiers based on your trading volume.
steps.important: For high-volume DEXs, the fee reduction from Diamond tier (1 bp) can significantly outweigh staking costs.

steps.title: Upgrade Tier via Trading Volume
steps.description: Increase your 30-day average trading volume to qualify for higher tiers automatically. Volume is calculated as a 30-day rolling average across all trading activity under your broker ID.
steps.important: Tier upgrades based on volume use a 30-day rolling average, so changes may take time to reflect. Contact the Orderly team to confirm your tier upgrade.

steps.title: Upgrade Tier via ORDER Token Staking
steps.description: Stake ORDER tokens through the staking portal or proxy contract to qualify for higher tiers without meeting volume requirements.
steps.important: Staking is an alternative to meeting volume thresholds. For example, staking 2M ORDER qualifies for Platinum tier (2 bps) without needing $1B in 30-day volume.

steps.title: Understand the Booster Distributor Program
steps.description: The Booster Distributor Program provides direct access to the Platinum tier. Distributors can grant other builders (including their own DEX) Platinum tier status, allowing them to skip staking/volume requirements.
steps.important: DEX owners are generally not turned into distributors to prevent gaming the system. Boosted Distributors are gated and only provided to verified users. Distributors must generate enough volume and revenue within 2 months to maintain the tier.

steps.title: Monitor Tier Status and Revenue
steps.description: Track your 30-day volume, staking amounts, and accumulated revenue to maintain or improve your tier classification.
steps.important: Accumulated revenue is collected in your Orderly account and must be withdrawn to your admin wallet. Losing tier status will increase your base taker fee.

steps.title: Implement Custom Fee Tiers for Users (Optional)
steps.description: Use the Custom Fees feature to set different fees per user based on their volume, or collect fees normally and send rebates manually/off-chain.
steps.important: Orderly provides scripts to automatically move users into different fee tiers based on volume.

commonIssues.issue: Unsure which tier my broker qualifies for.
commonIssues.solution: Check your 30-day average trading volume on the Dune dashboard or admin portal. Compare against tier thresholds: Platinum requires ≥$1B volume or 2M ORDER staked; Diamond requires ≥$10B volume or 7M ORDER staked. Contact the Orderly team for tier verification.

commonIssues.issue: Tier not updating after reaching volume threshold or staking.
commonIssues.solution: Tier calculations are based on 30-day average trading volume and may take time to process. Ensure your staking wallet address was correctly provided during broker ID registration. Contact Orderly support if the tier does not update.

commonIssues.issue: Staking transaction fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you have approved the ORDER token for the proxy contract and that you are attaching sufficient LayerZero fee (quote the fee via quoteStakeOrder and multiply by 1.1 for safety margin).

commonIssues.issue: Unsure whether to stake ORDER or increase volume.
commonIssues.solution: Both paths lead to the same tier benefits. Compare the cost of staking ORDER tokens versus the revenue impact of reduced base fees. Staking provides a more predictable path if volume fluctuates.

commonIssues.issue: Confusion about total fee charged to users.
commonIssues.solution: Total user fee = Orderly base fee + Builder fee on top. The builder keeps everything above the base fee. Check your tier level to know your base fee.

commonIssues.issue: Revenue not appearing in admin wallet.
commonIssues.solution: Revenue is collected in the Orderly account, not directly in the wallet. You must withdraw accumulated revenue from the Orderly account to your admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Custom fee tiers not applying to users.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the Custom Fees feature correctly and that user volume data is being tracked via the Get Builder's Users Volumes endpoint.

commonIssues.issue: Distributor status revoked.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure sufficient volume and revenue are generated within the 2-month window. Contact the Orderly team if you believe the revocation was in error.

workflows.name: Managing Order Execution and Position Lifecycle
workflows.description: Create, manage, and close positions using the Orderly SDK hooks and REST API, including market/limit orders, TP/SL orders, and position margin calculations.
prerequisites: User wallet connected and Orderly account registered
Basic understanding of perpetual futures trading

steps.title: Create Orders Using useOrderEntry Hook
steps.description: Use the useOrderEntry hook to manage order state reactively. Bind input changes to setValue() and submit via onSubmit().
steps.important: Do not maintain separate order state with useState — use the hook's setValue exclusively. The formattedOrder object represents the current order state and is what gets validated and submitted.

steps.title: Close a Long Position
steps.description: To close a long position, send a SELL order with reduce_only: true. For a market close, omit order_price and set order_type to MARKET.
steps.important: Position quantity is positive for long and negative for short positions. Always use reduce_only: true when closing to avoid accidentally opening a new position.

steps.title: Create TP/SL Orders
steps.description: TP/SL orders are stop orders with reduce_only enabled. Submit two separate orders for TP and SL. Use the useTPSLOrder hook for TP/SL-specific operations.
steps.important: When creating TP/SL for an entire position, quantity may show as 0, which represents the full position. Offset percentage inputs use decimal format (0.1 = 10%).

steps.title: Calculate Position Margin and Liquidation Price
steps.description: Position margin is calculated as: margin = Math.abs(positionSize) * markPrice * mmr. Use useOrderEntry for real-time estimated liquidation price before entering a position.
steps.important: Use the absolute value of position size since it can be positive (long) or negative (short). MMR details: https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/perpetual-futures/formulas-definitions#maintenance-margin-ratio

steps.title: Subscribe to Order Execution Events
steps.description: Subscribe to the executionreport WebSocket topic to track fills, cancellations, and rejections in real time.
steps.important: The useOrderStream and usePositionStream hooks also auto-update when orders are filled or positions change, though there may be a slight delay in WebSocket push updates.

commonIssues.issue: useOrderEntry validation fails unexpectedly.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using setValue() exclusively to update order state rather than maintaining separate useState variables. The helper.validate() function validates the in-memory formattedOrder state.

commonIssues.issue: TP/SL orders not cancelling properly.
commonIssues.solution: Use cancelAlgoOrder() instead of cancelOrder() for TP/SL and algorithmic orders. The standard cancelOrder function does not work for algo orders.

commonIssues.issue: Filled orders show unexpected entry price.
commonIssues.solution: For filled orders, use the average_executed_price field (not the price field). The price field is only populated for limit orders and represents the limit price set by the user.

workflows.name: Managing Account Collateral, Leverage, and PnL Settlement
workflows.description: Monitor account health metrics including collateral, leverage, margin ratio, and PnL, and programmatically settle PnL before withdrawals.
prerequisites: User wallet connected and Orderly account registered

steps.title: Get Account Collateral and Value
steps.description: Use the useCollateral hook to retrieve total collateral, free collateral, total account value, available balance, and unsettled PnL.
steps.important: Definitions available at: https://orderly.network/docs/trade-on-orderly/perpetual-futures/formulas-definitions

steps.title: Get and Adjust Account Leverage
steps.description: Use useMarginRatio() for current leverage and margin ratio, and useLeverage() to get and update maximum account leverage.
steps.important: Leverage is account-wide, not per-trade. Changing leverage affects all positions.

steps.title: Calculate Unrealized PnL
steps.description: Use the formula pnl = qty * (markPrice - openPrice) or the SDK helper function to calculate unrealized PnL for a position.
steps.important: For unrealized ROI percentage, use totalUnrealizedROI from the account data and multiply by 100.

steps.title: Settle PnL Programmatically
steps.description: Call account.settle() to settle unrealized PnL into withdrawable balance. This must be done explicitly — it is not automatic.
steps.important: Settling only changes withdrawable balance if PnL is positive. Only call settle when unsettledPnL !== 0. Settling applies to the entire account's PnL, not individual positions.

steps.title: Settle PnL via REST API
steps.description: To settle PnL via the REST API, first obtain the settle PnL nonce, then call the Request PnL Settlement endpoint.
steps.important: Users cannot withdraw the full amount of their profits unless PnL is settled first.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal fails with insufficient balance despite visible profits.
commonIssues.solution: Call account.settle() before attempting withdrawal. Unrealized PnL must be explicitly settled to become withdrawable.

commonIssues.issue: Leverage update does not take effect.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the update function from useLeverage() hook and waiting for the mutation to complete. Leverage is account-wide and affects all positions.

commonIssues.issue: Unsettled PnL shows as 0 but account value seems incorrect.
commonIssues.solution: Check useCollateral() for all balance components. If unsettledPnL is 0, all PnL has already been settled. Verify totalValue and availableBalance separately.

workflows.name: Integrating Custom Wallet Providers with Orderly SDK
workflows.description: Connect custom wallet providers (Privy, Coinbase, RainbowKit/Wagmi, Magic Link, Solana wallets, or custodial solutions) to the Orderly SDK using the WalletConnectorContext, wallet adapter pattern, or web3-onboard configuration.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.2.0+ installed (v2.11.2+ recommended for Privy Solana fixes)
Wallet provider SDK installed (e.g., Privy, Wagmi, Reown, Coinbase, Magic Link)
React application with OrderlyAppProvider or OrderlyConfigProvider
For Solana: Solana wallet adapter packages and custom Solana RPC URL (recommended)
For JS SDK demo: web3-onboard wallet module for the target wallet
Custom wallet provider must support EIP-712 message signing for Orderly authentication

steps.title: Set Up Orderly Provider with Wallet Adapter
steps.description: For SDK v2, use OrderlyConfigProvider (hooks-only) or OrderlyAppProvider (with UI components). Pass the wallet adapter via the walletAdapters prop.
steps.important: The main change from v1 to v2 is the walletAdapters prop on the config provider. Migration guide: https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/migrate

steps.title: Implement Custom Wallet Connector Context
steps.description: For fully custom wallet integrations (RainbowKit, Wagmi, Magic Link, etc.), provide a WalletConnectorContext.Provider that wraps the Orderly provider. Ensure your connector passes the connected wallet address and EIP-712 signing capabilities to the Orderly SDK.
steps.important: The wallet connector context allows you to bridge any wallet SDK (Reown/AppKit, Wagmi, etc.) to Orderly's internal wallet interface. All Orderly components and hooks use this context.

steps.title: Integrate Privy as Wallet Provider
steps.description: For Privy integration (SDK v2.2+), implement a custom PrivyProvider by replacing the default EthersProvider in the OrderlyProvider wrapper.
steps.important: SDK v2.8.13 fixed network switching issues with Privy login. SDK v2.11.2 fixed a bug causing duplicate Solana addresses via Privy.

steps.title: Add Wallet via web3-onboard (JS SDK Demo)
steps.description: For the Orderly JS SDK demo application, install and register the web3-onboard module for the target wallet provider (e.g., Coinbase Wallet).
steps.important: The Orderly JS SDK demo uses web3-onboard for wallet connections. Each wallet provider has its own web3-onboard module. Ensure required API keys or app IDs are configured.

steps.title: Configure Solana Network Settings
steps.description: When networkId is 'mainnet', explicitly set the Solana network and provide a custom RPC URL in the WalletConnectorProvider.
steps.important: The default public RPC (wss://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com/) may fail or be rate-limited. Always provide your own RPC URL for production use.

steps.title: Configure Network and Chain Switching
steps.description: Set the networkId to 'mainnet' or 'testnet' on the provider. Use account.switchChainId() to switch the active chain for data hooks at runtime.
steps.important: Trading data like orders and positions are not chain-specific — they are aggregated across all chains. The networkId cannot change during runtime; use a page refresh when switching between testnet and mainnet.

steps.title: Implement Custodial Deposit and Withdrawal Flows (Optional)
steps.description: For centralized/custodial wallets, create an EOA for the user, sign EIP-712 to register Orderly keys, then use a master wallet for on-chain deposits and withdrawals — eliminating the need for users to hold gas tokens.
steps.important: This avoids needing to fund each user EOA with gas tokens for multiple transactions.

commonIssues.issue: ethers v6 TypeScript build error with Next.js: 'Type Buffer<ArrayBufferLike> is not assignable to type Buffer<ArrayBuffer>'.
commonIssues.solution: Update @types/node and add webpack fallback configuration to next.config.ts: config.resolve.fallback = { ...config.resolve.fallback, fs: false, net: false, tls: false }. Additionally, ethers v6 ships raw TypeScript source files that may break webpack — a postinstall script to delete them may be needed.

commonIssues.issue: Privy login causes network switching failures.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v2.8.13 or later, which fixed network switching issues with Privy login.

commonIssues.issue: Duplicate Solana addresses appearing with Privy.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v2.11.2 or later, which fixed a bug causing duplicate Solana addresses via Privy.

commonIssues.issue: Custom wallet provider fails to sign Orderly messages.
commonIssues.solution: Verify that the wallet provider fully supports EIP-712 message signing. Some wallet abstraction solutions may not implement this standard correctly.

commonIssues.issue: Wallet provider not appearing in the connection modal.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the module is correctly imported and added to the wallets array in the web3-onboard configuration. Check for any initialization errors in the browser console.

commonIssues.issue: Coinbase Wallet connection fails on mobile.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the Coinbase Wallet module is configured with the correct app ID and that deep linking is properly set up for mobile browsers.

commonIssues.issue: Custom wallet connector breaks Orderly authentication.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your wallet connector implementation correctly passes the connected wallet address and signing capabilities to the Orderly SDK. Follow the Web3Modal example closely.

commonIssues.issue: Solana wallet connections fail on mainnet.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you have explicitly set the Solana network to Mainnet in WalletConnectorProvider and provided a reliable custom RPC URL.

commonIssues.issue: Custodial deposits fail to credit user accounts.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the EIP-712 registration was completed successfully and that the depositTo function is called with the correct user Orderly account ID derived from their EOA address and broker ID.

workflows.name: Authenticating and Subscribing to Orderly WebSocket and REST APIs
workflows.description: Generate valid Ed25519 signatures for REST API authentication, connect to private WebSocket streams, and subscribe to real-time data topics including execution reports, wallet events, and market data.
prerequisites: Orderly API key and secret (Ed25519 keypair)
Understanding of WebSocket and REST API authentication patterns

steps.title: Generate REST API Signature in Python
steps.description: Construct the signing message as {timestamp}{method}{path}{query}{json_body} and sign using Ed25519 with your private key.
steps.code:
# Construct message string:
# {timestamp}{method}{path}{query}{json_body}
# - timestamp: milliseconds since epoch
# - method: uppercase HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.)
# - path: endpoint path (e.g., /v1/order)
# - query: includes '?' prefix if present
# - json_body: compact JSON string (no spaces, sorted keys)

# Sign with Ed25519 and base64url-encode the result

# Required headers:
# orderly-timestamp: <timestamp_ms>
# orderly-account-id: <account_id>
# orderly-key: ed25519:<api_key>
# orderly-signature: <base64url_signature>
steps.important: When sending POST/PUT requests, ensure the exact same JSON string used for signing is sent as the request body. Any difference will cause signature verification to fail.

steps.title: Authenticate with Private WebSocket
steps.description: Connect to the private WebSocket endpoint and authenticate using an Ed25519 signature of the current timestamp.
steps.important: Generate a fresh Ed25519 signature of the current timestamp (milliseconds) for each WebSocket authentication attempt.

steps.title: Subscribe to Execution Report Topic
steps.description: After authentication, subscribe to the executionreport topic to receive real-time order fills, cancellations, and rejections.
steps.important: Broker admins can also receive execution reports for specific accounts via wss://ws-broker.orderly.org/ws/stream/{account_id}.

steps.title: Subscribe to Wallet Events
steps.description: Subscribe to the wallet topic to receive real-time deposit and withdrawal event notifications.
steps.important: Wallet events include both deposits and withdrawals. Use this to update UI in real time when funds move.

steps.title: Retrieve Trade Data Beyond REST API Limits
steps.description: The /v1/public/market_trades REST endpoint has a limit of 500 transactions per request. Use WebSocket for real-time trades or kline endpoints for aggregated volume.
steps.code:
# REST endpoint (500 tx limit):
GET https://api-evm.orderly.org/v1/public/market_trades

# For aggregated volume over time buckets (24h, 7d):
# Use kline endpoints
# Note: kline data does not include buy/sell direction

# For real-time trades beyond 500 limit:
# Subscribe to market trades WebSocket topic
steps.important: For aggregated volume calculations over time buckets, kline endpoints are recommended, though they do not include buy/sell (long/short) direction information.

commonIssues.issue: REST API returns 401 Unauthorized despite correct API key.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the JSON body used for signing is exactly the same as the request body (compact, no spaces, sorted keys). Verify timestamp is within acceptable range and headers are correctly formatted.

commonIssues.issue: WebSocket connection drops frequently.
commonIssues.solution: Set ping_interval=10 and ping_timeout=5 to maintain the connection. Implement reconnection logic with exponential backoff.

commonIssues.issue: Market trades endpoint returns fewer results than expected.
commonIssues.solution: The /v1/public/market_trades endpoint has a hard limit of 500 transactions per request. Subscribe to the WebSocket market trades topic for real-time data beyond this limit.

workflows.name: Registering a New Broker on Orderly
workflows.description: End-to-end process for registering a new broker on Orderly, including providing broker details, setting up the admin wallet, and linking to Orderly One if applicable.
prerequisites: Defined broker ID, broker name, and fee structure
Contact with Orderly team for confirmation

steps.title: Provide Broker Details to Orderly
steps.description: Submit the following details to the Orderly team for confirmation and profile configuration.
steps.important: The entire registration process typically takes 2–3 days.

steps.title: Wait for Orderly to Configure Broker Profile
steps.description: After confirmation, Orderly configures the broker profile on their backend. You will be notified when setup is complete.
steps.important: Admin access will be available at https://admin.orderly.network/login once configured.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register your admin wallet using the broker registration app with your broker ID on both mainnet and testnet.
steps.important: You can use different wallets for mainnet and testnet. A multisig like Safe is common for mainnet. After registration, share the address with the Orderly team to complete setup.

steps.title: Register Orderly Account Linked to Broker
steps.description: Create an Orderly account linked to your broker ID by connecting your admin wallet and signing the EIP-712 key registration message.
steps.important: The admin wallet is responsible for collecting fees and has exclusive access to APIs such as referral codes and fee rebates.

steps.title: Link Broker ID to Orderly One (If Applicable)
steps.description: If your DEX was created using the Orderly One no-code solution, provide the broker ID and DEX URL to Orderly support for manual linkage.
steps.important: This step is only needed if using Orderly One. Custom SDK integrations are automatically linked via the brokerId prop.

commonIssues.issue: Broker ID already exists.
commonIssues.solution: Broker IDs must be unique. Choose a different identifier or contact Orderly support if you believe there's a conflict.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet not recognized after registration.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you shared the registered wallet address with the Orderly team and they have enabled it on the backend. Registration on the portal alone is not sufficient.

commonIssues.issue: Orderly One DEX not reflecting broker fees.
commonIssues.solution: The Orderly team must manually link the broker ID to the Orderly One DEX. Contact support with your broker ID and DEX URL.

workflows.name: Building Copy Trading Features
workflows.description: Implement copy trading functionality on your Orderly-powered DEX using admin query APIs, WebSocket streams, subaccounts, and the Order enum feature for per-order fee customization.
prerequisites: Active broker account with admin wallet and API access
Backend infrastructure for managing lead trader signals
Understanding of copy trading mechanics and Orderly subaccount/internal transfer APIs

steps.title: Design Copy Trading Architecture
steps.description: Plan your copy trading system. Orderly does not natively provide real-time trade signals or order details of other users. Common approaches include: (1) Lead traders set up read-only API keys, (2) Monitor order placement via frontend API requests, (3) Listen to trade notifications.
steps.important: Copy trading typically tracks position changes rather than individual order details. Position history is available on-chain.

steps.title: Access Admin Query APIs
steps.description: Use the admin query REST APIs to access transaction information for your own users. User trading data is not publicly exposed—only the DEX admin can access trades for users within their own DEX.
steps.important: All admin API requests must be signed with your admin wallet's Orderly API credentials.

steps.title: Subscribe to Real-Time WebSocket Updates
steps.description: For real-time updates without rate limiting, subscribe to WebSocket topics using your admin account ID.
steps.important: Replace {account_id} with your admin account ID. This provides real-time trade and position updates for all users on your DEX.

steps.title: Set Up Subaccounts for Fund Isolation
steps.description: Use subaccounts to isolate copy trading funds from users' main accounts.
steps.important: Subaccounts allow you to separate copy trading capital and manage risk independently.

steps.title: Implement Lead Trader Signal Capture
steps.description: Set up a mechanism to capture lead trader orders. Options include having lead traders provide read-only API keys or monitoring their order placement through your frontend.
steps.important: Order information is private on Orderly. You cannot access other users' order details without their explicit API key sharing.

steps.title: Configure Custom Fees with Order Enum
steps.description: Use the order enum feature to apply custom additional fees per order, useful for copy trading fee structures where copiers pay a premium.
steps.important: Order enum is particularly useful for copy trading or automated trading strategies where extra fees need to be charged.

steps.title: Execute Copy Trades via API
steps.description: When a lead trader's signal is captured, programmatically place matching orders for all copiers using the Orderly API.
steps.important: Consider slippage and timing differences when copying trades across multiple accounts.

steps.title: Build Leader/Follower UI
steps.description: Create a user interface that displays leader traders' performance metrics and allows followers to automatically copy their trades.
steps.important: Use the admin APIs to calculate leader PnL, win rates, and other performance metrics. Note that account_id values are EVM-formatted even for Solana users because settlement happens on the EVM-based L2.

commonIssues.issue: Admin WebSocket connection fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the correct admin account ID in the WebSocket URL. The account ID must be associated with your broker's admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot identify which chain a user deposited from.
commonIssues.solution: Trading on Orderly is chain-agnostic (settlement on L2), so there is no chain field on trades. Use the public API endpoints that power the Orderly dashboard (inspect network tab at https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/) to get deposit chain information.

commonIssues.issue: Per-order fees not applying correctly.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your integration follows the order enum integration guide exactly. Contact Orderly support if fees are not being applied as expected.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot access lead trader's order details in real-time.
commonIssues.solution: Have lead traders set up read-only API keys for your copy trading system, or monitor order placement through frontend API requests.

commonIssues.issue: Copy trades experience significant slippage.
commonIssues.solution: Implement batch order execution and consider using limit orders instead of market orders to reduce slippage for copiers.

commonIssues.issue: Users interfere with copy trading bot orders.
commonIssues.solution: Use subaccounts to isolate copy trading funds. Communicate clearly to users that they should not manually trade on subaccounts managed by the copy trading system.

workflows.name: Building a Custom Trading UI with Orderly SDK
workflows.description: Build a fully custom trading interface using Orderly's SDK hooks and APIs, including advanced features like TP/SL bracket orders, position history, market filtering, and leverage calculations.
prerequisites: React application with wallet provider integration

steps.title: Install and Configure SDK
steps.description: Install the headless hooks package for full UI control, or use the pre-built React components. Wrap your root element with the appropriate providers.
steps.important: Use @orderly.network/hooks directly instead of @orderly.network/react for full UI control. The hooks SDK is headless (no styling). The OrderlyConfigProvider must be above OrderlyProvider in the component tree.

steps.title: Synchronize Wallet State
steps.description: Pass the wallet's signer to useAccount().setAddress() whenever the wallet connects or switches chains.
steps.important: The SDK does not connect to the blockchain directly — it wraps your wallet provider. Failing to synchronize wallet changes will result in broken UI states and transaction failures.

steps.title: Build Custom Components with Hooks
steps.description: Use hooks like useAccount(), useOrderbook(symbol), and useOrderEntry() to build your custom trading components.
steps.important: The hooks leverage Orderly's reactive SWR-based state management for real-time data updates.

steps.title: Create TP/SL (Bracket) Orders
steps.description: Use the setValues function from useOrderEntry to set take-profit and stop-loss trigger prices along with base order parameters.
steps.important: TP/SL orders trigger when the mark price hits the target price, not the last traded price. In high volatility or low liquidity, the position may settle at a price different from the trigger price.

steps.title: Retrieve User Position History
steps.description: Use the usePositionHistoryScript hook to access full position history including PnL, status, and position IDs.

steps.title: Calculate Total Funding Paid on a Position
steps.description: There is no single field for cumulative funding. Aggregate the funding fee history using the REST API.
steps.important: You must aggregate the funding fee history manually. There is no single field that returns cumulative funding on a position.

steps.title: Filter Markets in the Market Selector
steps.description: Pass a dataAdapter function to OrderlyAppProvider to filter which symbols appear in the Market Selector.
steps.important: Markets disabled in Orderly One settings are NOT automatically filtered in custom SDK integrations. You must implement filtering manually via the data adapter.

steps.title: Understand 24h Price Change and Leverage Calculations
steps.description: The 24h price change is based on the last traded price, not the mark price. Display position-size-dependent leverage limits rather than a single maximum leverage figure.
steps.important: The 24h price change uses last traded price, not mark price. There is no API for historical mark price K-line data. Frontends should display position-size-dependent leverage limits. The effective leverage limit for a given position size should be calculated as 1 / IMR.

steps.title: Check User's Orderly Key Status
steps.description: Verify if a user's Orderly Key is valid and active.

commonIssues.issue: UI does not update when wallet switches chains.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you call useAccount().setAddress() whenever the wallet connects or switches chains. The SDK does not auto-detect wallet changes.

commonIssues.issue: Order submission fails silently.
commonIssues.solution: Check that the wallet signer is properly synchronized and that the OrderlyProvider is correctly wrapping your components. Verify the order parameters match the expected format.

commonIssues.issue: Orderbook data is stale or not updating.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the OrderlyProvider is mounted and the symbol parameter is correct. The hooks use SWR for caching — data refreshes automatically but may have a brief cache window.

commonIssues.issue: TP/SL order triggers at unexpected price.
commonIssues.solution: TP/SL orders trigger based on mark price, not last traded price. In high volatility or low liquidity, the execution price may differ from the trigger price.

commonIssues.issue: Position history shows incomplete data.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure enableSortingStorage is set to true and that the user is properly authenticated. The hook returns all symbols when symbol is set to undefined.

commonIssues.issue: Filtered markets still appear in the selector.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the dataAdapter function is correctly passed to OrderlyAppProvider. Markets disabled in Orderly One are not auto-filtered in custom SDK builds.

commonIssues.issue: Leverage displayed does not match expected maximum.
commonIssues.solution: Maximum leverage decreases as position notional size increases beyond the Small_Notional_Limit threshold. Calculate effective leverage as 1 / IMR for the specific position size.

workflows.name: Configuring TradingView Advanced Charts on Your Orderly DEX
workflows.description: Obtain a TradingView Advanced Charts license and integrate the Orderly trading-view library to display charting data on your custom DEX domain.
prerequisites: Custom domain secured and configured for your DEX

steps.title: Secure Your Custom Domain First
steps.description: Before applying for a TradingView license, ensure your custom domain is finalized. The TradingView team can take around a week to respond, and you want to avoid back-and-forth on URL changes.
steps.important: Orderly's redistribution license is only valid for the dex.orderly.network subdomain. If hosting your own DEX, you must apply for your own license.

steps.title: Create a GitHub Profile
steps.description: TradingView requires a GitHub profile as part of the application process. Create one if you don't already have one.

steps.title: Submit the TradingView License Application
steps.description: Apply for the TradingView Advanced Charts license at the official application page. A registered company is NOT required. You can indicate that you have your own data feed when filling out the application.
steps.code:
// Apply at:
https://www.tradingview.com/advanced-charts/
steps.important: This is a mandatory prerequisite. The Orderly @orderly.network/trading-view library will not work without a valid TradingView license.

steps.title: Wait for Approval
steps.description: The TradingView team typically takes around a week to review and respond to applications.

steps.title: Configure the TradingView Library in Your DEX
steps.description: Once approved, integrate the Orderly trading-view library with your TradingView license in your DEX application. Follow the TradingView documentation for proper library initialization and configuration.
steps.important: Orderly's SDK v3 template includes TradingView files in ./public/tradingview, but the redistribution license only covers dex.orderly.network.

steps.title: Fetch TradingView-Compatible Chart Data
steps.description: Use the Orderly REST API endpoint for TradingView history bars to provide chart data to your chart component.
steps.code:
// TradingView history bars endpoint:
// https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-evm/evm-api/restful-api/public/get-tradingview-history-bars
steps.important: Orderly charts are not directly integrated into TradingView—you use the REST API endpoint to feed data into your TradingView chart component.

steps.title: Alternative: Use lightweight-charts
steps.description: If you need an immediate solution or want to avoid licensing, use TradingView's free open-source lightweight-charts library, which supports candles, lines, and volume without licensing restrictions.

commonIssues.issue: Chart component does not render.
commonIssues.solution: Verify that you have a valid TradingView Advanced Charting library license. The Orderly wrapper requires this license to function.

commonIssues.issue: Chart not rendering on custom domain after SDK v3 integration.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly's SDK v3 template includes TradingView files in ./public/tradingview, but the redistribution license only covers dex.orderly.network. Apply for your own license or switch to lightweight-charts.

commonIssues.issue: TradingView license application rejected or delayed.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your domain is finalized before applying. Double-check that all fields are filled correctly. The lightweight-charts library is a viable fallback.

commonIssues.issue: Chart data not loading for new permissionless markets.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.3+ which optimizes K-line history loading to stop requesting unavailable historical data before a market's listing time.

workflows.name: Troubleshooting Mobile Wallet, SDK Build, and Connector Issues
workflows.description: Resolve common mobile-specific issues (WalletConnect redirect loops, MetaMask infinite popups, Telegram Mini App OAuth errors, input mode overrides), build errors, and wallet connector integration issues when using the Orderly SDK with Next.js and third-party wallet providers.
prerequisites: Understanding of mobile browser and wallet behavior

steps.title: Fix WalletConnect/MetaMask Infinite Redirect Loops on iOS Safari
steps.description: On iOS Safari, WalletConnect WebSocket connections are terminated when the app enters the background. Upon returning, the SDK may fail to re-bind to the existing session topic, causing repeated deep link attempts that Safari blocks as popups.
steps.important: Mitigation steps: (1) Use the wallet's built-in in-app browser (MetaMask browser, etc.) which bypasses these compatibility issues entirely. (2) Ensure you are using the latest MetaMask Mobile version. (3) Close the DApp and generate a new WalletConnect session. (4) Open the DApp in Chrome or Safari instead of in-app browsers (Telegram, KakaoTalk, etc.). The Orderly team is working on SDK-level fixes for automatic reconnection and topic re-subscription.

steps.title: Fix Mobile Deposit Flow Infinite MetaMask Redirect Popup
steps.description: The infinite redirect popup on iOS Safari during deposit is caused by wallet-read polling (balance/allowance checks every 3000ms) triggering deep links before the WalletConnect session is fully settled.
steps.important: To fix: (1) Disable wallet reads on page mount by forcing walletReadsEnabled/depositReadsEnabled to false initially. (2) Start wallet reads only after explicit user intent (e.g., clicking deposit). (3) Reduce polling frequency on mobile. (4) Avoid wallet-provider reads until the wallet session is fully stable. (5) Implement a 'readiness gate' to block balance/allowance reads until wallet/account/chain states stabilize.

steps.title: Resolve Google OAuth '403: disallowed_useragent' in Telegram Mini Apps
steps.description: Google's policy blocks OAuth requests from embedded WebViews. The Orderly SDK (v2.12.3 and later) detects window.Telegram?.WebApp and routes OAuth requests through the external browser via Telegram.WebApp.openLink() to ensure a secure sign-in experience.
steps.code:
// Upgrade to SDK v2.12.3+ to get this fix:
"@orderly.network/react": "^2.12.3"
steps.important: This fix is automatic once you upgrade to SDK v2.12.3 or later.

steps.title: Handle inputmode='decimal' Override Issue
steps.description: When upstream Orderly SDK updates overwrite custom inputmode='decimal' modifications in input components, the numeric keypad on mobile reverts to a standard text keyboard. Affected files include price inputs, quantity inputs, trigger price inputs, and TPSL dialog components.
steps.important: Report this to the Orderly team for inclusion in the base SDK. The team has acknowledged this and is considering adding different input modes in upcoming releases. Use the useInputMode hook consistently for implementation.

steps.title: Fix Solana Mobile Wallet Adapter Build Error
steps.description: Resolve the @solana-mobile/mobile-wallet-adapter-protocol-web3js build error in Next.js 15 caused by a breaking change in a transitive dependency.
steps.important: This is caused by @solana-mobile/wallet-adapter-mobile 2.1 being incompatible with @solana-mobile/mobile-wallet-adapter-protocol-web3js. The Orderly SDK team has been working on a permanent fix.

steps.title: Fix Privy Wallet Connector SDKError
steps.description: Resolve the 'Please provide a wallet connector provider' SDKError when using the Privy wallet connector with OrderlyAppProvider.
steps.important: Ensure the wallet connector provider is correctly set up when integrating the Privy wallet connector with the Orderly React SDK (e.g., using TradingPage component).

steps.title: Register Orderly Key on Solana
steps.description: Solana uses the same API endpoint as EVM for adding Orderly keys. Use the TypeScript example for reference.
steps.important: The wallet must have an existing Orderly account before registering an Orderly key on Solana.

commonIssues.issue: WalletConnect session lost when iOS app enters background.
commonIssues.solution: Use the wallet's built-in in-app browser or open the DApp in Chrome/Safari directly. The Orderly team is working on SDK-level fixes for automatic reconnection.

commonIssues.issue: Infinite MetaMask popup during deposit on mobile.
commonIssues.solution: Implement a 'readiness gate' to block balance/allowance reads until wallet/account/chain states stabilize. Disable wallet reads on page mount and start them only after explicit user intent.

commonIssues.issue: Google OAuth fails in Telegram Mini App WebView.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to Orderly SDK v2.12.3 or later, which automatically routes OAuth requests through the external browser for Telegram Mini Apps.

commonIssues.issue: Numeric keypad reverts to text keyboard after SDK update.
commonIssues.solution: Use the useInputMode hook consistently and report the issue to the Orderly team for inclusion in the base SDK.

commonIssues.issue: Next.js 15 build fails with Solana mobile wallet adapter error.
commonIssues.solution: Add a resolutions (Yarn) or overrides (npm) entry in package.json to pin @solana-mobile/wallet-adapter-mobile to version 2.1.4. Alternatively, use a webpack alias to mock the module.

commonIssues.issue: 'Please provide a wallet connector provider' error with Privy.
commonIssues.solution: Follow the working reference implementation at the GitHub link above. Ensure the Privy connector is properly initialized and passed to OrderlyAppProvider.

commonIssues.issue: 'Account not found' error (-1607) when registering Solana Orderly key.
commonIssues.solution: The wallet address must first register an account on Orderly before adding an Orderly key. Ensure the account registration step is completed first.

workflows.name: Querying Market, Trade, and Account Data via Orderly APIs
workflows.description: Retrieve market summaries, orderbook snapshots, candle data, trade execution history, asset deposits/withdrawals, account balances, and admin-level trade data using the Orderly REST API, Public Info API, and Hooks SDK.
prerequisites: Orderly API access or Hooks SDK integrated
HTTP client capable of sending POST requests with JSON bodies (for Public Info API)
Target wallet address (for public account queries)

steps.title: Query Market Summary, Orderbook, and Candle Data (Public Info API)
steps.description: Use the Public Info API to retrieve market summaries, orderbook snapshots, and OHLCV candle data without authentication.

steps.title: Query Account State and Trade Fills (Public Info API)
steps.description: Retrieve full account snapshots and executed trade fills for any wallet address without authentication.
steps.important: No authentication is required — any wallet can be inspected for positions, orders, fills, and PnL.

steps.title: Check Rate Limit Status (Public Info API)
steps.description: Monitor your current API rate limit usage. This query costs 0 weight and never consumes quota.
steps.important: Safe to poll on every loop iteration since it costs 0 weight.

steps.title: Get Trade Execution History via REST API (Private)
steps.description: Use the private trades endpoint to retrieve individual trade fills (not orders) for authenticated users or admin-level access.
steps.important: The admin trades endpoint excludes funding fees from realized PnL; use GET /v1/admin/funding-fee-history separately.

steps.title: Access Archived Trade Data for High-Volume Users
steps.description: For high-volume traders, older trade data may be archived and unavailable through the admin trades endpoint. Use the Orderly Dashboard indexing service for complete historical data.
steps.code:
// Dashboard: https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/
// Query API: https://orderly-dashboard-query-service.orderly.network/swagger-ui/#/

steps.title: Fetch Deposit and Withdrawal History
steps.description: Use the asset history endpoint or Hooks SDK to retrieve deposit and withdrawal data.

steps.title: Get Account Balance, Equity, and Margin Information
steps.description: Use the following hooks to retrieve comprehensive account financial data.

steps.title: Retrieve User IP Address for Compliance
steps.description: Orderly provides a public endpoint for frontend use to retrieve the user's IP address for compliance or anti-wash-trading purposes.
steps.code:
GET /v1/public/ip-info
// Documentation: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/restful-api/public/get-ip-info#get-ip-info
steps.important: Orderly does not store user IP addresses by default. Call this endpoint from your frontend and store the IP in your own systems.

steps.title: Handle Authentication Headers in Hooks SDK
steps.description: When using the Hooks SDK, use usePrivateQuery for authenticated (private) API endpoints — it automatically handles authentication headers. For public endpoints, use useQuery.
steps.important: usePrivateQuery automatically handles orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id, orderly-key, and orderly-signature headers.

commonIssues.issue: ADDRESS_NOT_FOUND (HTTP 404) when querying account data via Public Info API.
commonIssues.solution: The wallet address has no registered Orderly accounts. Verify the address is correct. You can narrow the scope with broker_id and account_id parameters.

commonIssues.issue: Rate limit exceeded (error code -1003, HTTP 429).
commonIssues.solution: Implement backoff logic and reduce request frequency. Use the rateLimitStatus query (0 weight) to monitor remaining quota. Each query type has a different weight cost.

commonIssues.issue: Pagination cursor not working.
commonIssues.solution: Treat cursors as opaque strings — do not parse or modify them. Pass the 'next_cursor' value from the response directly as the 'cursor' parameter in the next request. A null next_cursor indicates the last page.

commonIssues.issue: Candle data returns stale results.
commonIssues.solution: Candle responses are cached for 60 seconds. If you need fresh data, wait for the cache to expire or adjust the time-range parameters to create a different cache key.

commonIssues.issue: Trade data missing for high-volume users in admin endpoint.
commonIssues.solution: Older trade data may be archived. Use the Orderly Dashboard indexing service (https://orderly-dashboard-query-service.orderly.network/swagger-ui/#/) for complete historical data.

commonIssues.issue: Funding fees not included in realized PnL from trades endpoint.
commonIssues.solution: The admin trades endpoint excludes funding fees from realized PnL. Use GET /v1/admin/funding-fee-history separately to retrieve funding fee data.

commonIssues.issue: IP detection returns incorrect geo-blocking results.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly uses an IP detection database that is periodically updated. Report specific cases to the Orderly support team with the user's IP and region for investigation.

commonIssues.issue: Authentication headers not applied in custom API calls.
commonIssues.solution: Use usePrivateQuery instead of useQuery for private endpoints. usePrivateQuery automatically handles all required authentication headers.

workflows.name: Managing System Maintenance and Token Delistings
workflows.description: Handle scheduled system maintenance windows, token delisting processes, and the community Vote to Retain governance mechanism on your Orderly-powered DEX.
prerequisites: Access to Orderly System Updates Telegram channel
SDK v2.8.11 or later for governance UI support

steps.title: Monitor Maintenance Announcements
steps.description: Join the Orderly System Updates Telegram channel for maintenance notifications. During scheduled system maintenance, users are unable to place or cancel orders. Algorithmic orders will not trigger, and withdrawals are suspended.
steps.code:
// Join the notification channel:
https://t.me/+VnpoOvYpJXA2ZTc1
steps.important: Maintenance is used to deploy product updates such as order enum updates, tick size adjustments, custom trading fees per order, and permissionless vault features. Builders should inform users and plan accordingly.

steps.title: Configure Auto-Cancel for Pending Orders
steps.description: By default, pending orders are NOT automatically cancelled during maintenance. Users or brokers must explicitly enable this via the maintenance config API.
steps.important: Without this configuration, pending orders will remain in the order book and may execute when trading resumes after maintenance.

steps.title: Monitor Delisting Announcements
steps.description: Orderly periodically reviews listed tokens and opens a community 'Vote to Retain' process. Delistings can also occur due to project rebranding (e.g., $TON), token swaps (e.g., $IP), or market disruptions (e.g., $H).
steps.important: Brokers should actively monitor Orderly communications for upcoming delisting reviews.

steps.title: Enable Governance UI Support
steps.description: Ensure your SDK supports the 'Community Vote' announcement message type for proper governance communication in the UI.
steps.code:
// SDK v2.8.11+ supports the 'Community Vote' announcement message type
"@orderly.network/react": "^2.8.11"
steps.important: Without SDK v2.8.11+, governance announcements may not display properly in your DEX interface.

steps.title: Participate in Vote to Retain
steps.description: To retain a token under review, more than 3% of staked $ORDER must vote AGAINST delisting. The voting period typically lasts 5 days. Only staked $ORDER tokens have voting power.
steps.important: Brokers are encouraged to inform and encourage their communities to stake $ORDER and participate in governance.

steps.title: Handle Delisted Token Settlement
steps.description: When a token is delisted, the index price is fixed at the average price of the last hour before the delisting time. Open positions are settled at this fixed price.
steps.important: Builders should prepare in advance and notify users so they can close or manage open positions before delisting takes effect.

steps.title: Sync Frontend Configuration
steps.description: Remove or update the delisted token from your DEX's frontend configuration and notify users accordingly.
steps.important: Builders are advised to sync their frontend configurations promptly after delisting announcements.

steps.title: Track Delayed Cross-Chain Withdrawals
steps.description: If a user's cross-chain withdrawal hasn't arrived, search for the transaction on the Orderly dashboard and track it via LayerZero.
steps.important: Cross-chain withdrawals may experience delays during security upgrades or LayerZero DVN migrations.

steps.title: Revoke Compromised or Unused API Keys
steps.description: Remove Orderly Keys (API keys) using the Remove Orderly Key endpoint when they are no longer needed or if compromised.
steps.important: Regularly audit and revoke unused API keys as a security best practice.

commonIssues.issue: Orders fail during maintenance window.
commonIssues.solution: This is expected behavior. Inform users in advance that order placement, cancellation, and withdrawals are suspended during maintenance.

commonIssues.issue: Users complain about pending orders executing after maintenance.
commonIssues.solution: Inform users to enable auto-cancel via the maintenance config API, or implement this as a default setting in your DEX. Communicate clearly that pending orders remain active by default.

commonIssues.issue: Users confused about position settlement after delisting.
commonIssues.solution: Communicate clearly that the index price is fixed at the average price of the last hour before delisting. All open positions are settled at this price.

commonIssues.issue: Token still showing in UI after delisting.
commonIssues.solution: Update your frontend configuration to remove the delisted token. For SDK builders, ensure your symbol list is synced with Orderly's current listings.

commonIssues.issue: Community Vote announcement not showing in DEX UI.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v2.8.11 or later which supports the 'Community Vote' announcement message type for proper governance communication.

commonIssues.issue: Users don't know how to vote.
commonIssues.solution: Direct users to stake $ORDER tokens and participate in governance through the Orderly platform. Only staked $ORDER has voting power.

commonIssues.issue: Cross-chain withdrawal stuck for extended period.
commonIssues.solution: Track the transaction on LayerZero scan. Delays can occur during DVN migrations or security upgrades. If the transaction shows as completed on LayerZero but funds haven't arrived, contact Orderly support.

workflows.name: Tracking Real-Time Trading Events and Building Leaderboards
workflows.description: Set up systems to track on-chain trading events, build user leaderboards, monitor broker volume, and manage campaign data using Orderly's APIs and open-source indexer.
prerequisites: Node.js or Python environment for API integration
Campaign set up with Orderly team (with campaign_id) for real-time campaign tracking
WebSocket client library or REST API client

steps.title: Choose Your Tracking Method
steps.description: Select from multiple options for tracking trading events: (1) Pull Trading Events API v2, (2) Builders Leaderboard API, (3) dedicated campaign endpoints for real-time data, (4) the open-source Orderly Dashboard indexer, or (5) WebSocket/REST for order book depth.
steps.important: Orders are off-chain, but matched trades are on-chain on Orderly L2. There is currently no WebSocket subscription for new trades; you can only filter by account ID/address via the pull API. Standard volume endpoints update hourly or daily; for real-time tracking, use dedicated campaign endpoints (updated ~every 30 seconds).

steps.title: Use the Pull Trading Events API v2
steps.description: Query on-chain trade events filtered by account ID or address. This is the most flexible option for custom tracking.

steps.title: Use the Builders Leaderboard API
steps.description: Access pre-built leaderboard data that updates every 5 minutes with a 15-20 minute delay.

steps.title: Set Up a Dedicated Campaign for Real-Time Tracking
steps.description: Contact the Orderly team to set up a dedicated trading campaign with a campaign_id. This enables real-time volume tracking for the campaign duration.
steps.important: Campaign data is archived after the campaign ends. Starting from Campaign 75, the archiving window is 6 months.

steps.title: Query Campaign Rankings and User Data
steps.description: Use campaign endpoints to rank users by volume or PnL in real-time, get per-user info, and verify campaign criteria.

steps.title: Run the Orderly Dashboard Indexer
steps.description: Clone and run the open-source indexer to continuously listen for on-chain trade events and store them in your own database.
steps.important: The indexer requires a PostgreSQL database configured via the DATABASE_URL in the .env file.

steps.title: Configure Indexer Start Point
steps.description: Control where indexing starts using contract_deploy_height and contract_deploy_timestamp parameters. To skip historical data and only index recent trades, set contract_deploy_height to a recent block number.
steps.important: Once historical sync completes, the indexer will continuously listen for new blocks.

steps.title: Retrieve Broker Trading Volume
steps.description: Monitor your broker's trading volume via the API or Dune dashboard.
steps.important: Volume is not currently available in the admin console. Use the API or Dune dashboard instead.

steps.title: Map Trading Addresses to Wallet Addresses
steps.description: The address shown on the Orderly leaderboard is the internal trading account address, not the user's actual wallet address. Request address mapping from the Orderly team before distributing rewards.
steps.important: The Orderly technical team can map trading addresses to actual wallet addresses (e.g., Abstract Global Wallet) for campaign reward distribution.

steps.title: Fetch Order Book Depth via REST or WebSocket
steps.description: Access real-time order book depth data via WebSocket for live updates, or fetch order book snapshots via REST API for point-in-time liquidity assessment.
steps.important: WebSocket is recommended for applications requiring real-time order book updates, such as trading bots or live UI displays. WebSocket provides incremental updates, which is more efficient than polling the REST API.

commonIssues.issue: Leaderboard data seems outdated.
commonIssues.solution: The Builders Leaderboard API updates every 5 minutes with a 15-20 minute delay. For real-time needs, use the Pull Trading Events API, dedicated campaign endpoints, or run your own indexer.

commonIssues.issue: Indexer not picking up new trades.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the PostgreSQL database is properly configured and accessible. Check that the indexer process is running and that contract_deploy_height is set correctly.

commonIssues.issue: Need custom scoring/leaderboard based on referrals.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly provides volume data APIs but brokers need to build their own logic on top for custom scoring/leaderboard systems based on referrals.

commonIssues.issue: Campaign data no longer accessible after campaign ends.
commonIssues.solution: Campaign data is archived after the campaign ends (6 months for campaigns after ID 75). Export all needed data before the archiving deadline.

commonIssues.issue: Leaderboard shows internal trading addresses instead of wallet addresses.
commonIssues.solution: Request address mapping from the Orderly technical team before distributing rewards. The leaderboard shows internal Orderly account addresses, not user wallet addresses.

commonIssues.issue: Volume data not updating in real-time.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the dedicated campaign endpoints (get-campaign-ranking, get-campaign-user-info) rather than the standard volume endpoints which update hourly/daily.

commonIssues.issue: REST API returns stale order book data.
commonIssues.solution: REST API provides a point-in-time snapshot. For real-time data, switch to the WebSocket endpoint which provides live order book updates.

commonIssues.issue: WebSocket connection drops frequently.
commonIssues.solution: Implement reconnection logic with exponential backoff. Ensure your WebSocket client handles disconnections gracefully and resubscribes to streams upon reconnection.

workflows.name: Handling Embedded WebView Wallet Integration
workflows.description: Integrate Orderly SDK with embedded WebView wallets (e.g., mobile app wallets), including proper chain ID detection and deposit transaction decoding.
prerequisites: Understanding of postMessage communication between WebView and native layer

steps.title: Track Chain ID in React State
steps.description: You cannot reliably detect the chain from the token contract address alone, as the same address may exist on multiple chains. The chainId is not included in the standardized eth_sendTransaction message. Track the chain ID in your React state instead.
steps.important: Do not attempt to derive chain ID from contract addresses — the same address may exist on multiple chains.

steps.title: Include Chain ID in postMessage Payload
steps.description: Pass the current chain ID along when posting messages from the WebView so the native wallet layer can route to the correct RPC.
steps.important: The native wallet layer needs the chain ID to route the transaction to the correct RPC endpoint.

steps.title: Decode Deposit Transaction Data Fields
steps.description: When processing deposit transactions sent to the Orderly vault contract, decode the data field to extract deposit parameters.
steps.important: The Token Hash is the Keccak-256 hash of the token symbol string (e.g., 'USDT'), not the token contract address.

commonIssues.issue: Transactions sent to wrong chain in WebView.
commonIssues.solution: Always include the chainId in your postMessage payload. Do not rely on contract addresses to determine the chain. Use useAppContext() to get the current chain ID.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot identify token from deposit data field.
commonIssues.solution: Compute the Keccak-256 hash of known token symbol strings and match against Argument 3 in the data field. Remember it's the hash of the symbol string, not the address.

commonIssues.issue: Chain ID changes not detected.
commonIssues.solution: Listen for wallet_switchEthereumChain events and update your React state accordingly. Ensure the currentChainId from useAppContext() is always current.

workflows.name: Understanding Liquidation Mechanics and Margin Configuration
workflows.description: Understand how Orderly's liquidation engine works, configure isolated vs cross margin modes, manage symbol-level leverage settings, and understand how liquidation interacts with stop-loss orders.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.11.0+ for isolated margin support

steps.title: Understand Liquidation Triggers
steps.description: Liquidation is triggered when the Mark Price movement causes the user's Total Collateral Value to drop below the Maintenance Margin Requirement (MMR) — not the bankruptcy price where margin reaches zero. For BTC/ETH, the current MMR threshold is 0.6%.
steps.important: Liquidation tiers categorize positions as either High Risk or Low Risk depending on the trading pair. A liquidator takes over a position based on the risk tier category. This condition is evaluated independently of any stop-loss orders — if the liquidation trigger price is reached before the stop-loss trigger price, the position will be liquidated and the stop-loss order will not execute.

steps.title: Understand Liquidation Amount Calculation
steps.description: The system liquidates enough of the position so that after liquidation, the Margin Ratio returns to IMR + 5%. For example, if IMR = 2%, the post-liquidation target is ~7%. For BTC/ETH, the system now defaults to full liquidation when MR falls below the 0.6% MMR threshold.
steps.important: Stop-loss orders are trigger orders, not guaranteed executions. Setting a stop-loss very close to the estimated liquidation price carries the risk that liquidation triggers first.

steps.title: Calculate Maximum Leverage
steps.description: Maximum leverage is calculated as 1 / base_imr, where base_imr is returned by the public info endpoint. Note that an IMR factor kicks in for larger notionals, reducing effective leverage.
steps.important: An IMR factor kicks in for larger notionals, reducing effective leverage below the theoretical maximum.

steps.title: Configure Isolated Margin Mode
steps.description: Isolated margin mode (SDK v2.11.0+) allows configuring leverage and margin per position rather than account-wide. This limits losses to only the margin assigned to that position.
steps.important: SDK v3.1.0 fixed an issue where maxing out an isolated margin market order at 100% slider was rejected — the SDK now reserves a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula.

steps.title: Configure Symbol-Level Leverage
steps.description: Starting from SDK v2.7.3, leverage can be configured per symbol instead of account-wide, providing greater flexibility and control over individual positions.
steps.important: Note: In the create-order API, there is no leverage field. Users set the margin they want to use for a trade, and the system displays an estimated leverage. The leverage API/hooks refer to the maximum allowed account leverage.

steps.title: Review Liquidation Details
steps.description: Liquidation details including position size before/after, mark price at liquidation, and margin ratio can be reviewed in the Liquidation tab or by requesting a full record from Orderly support with the account address.
steps.important: The estimated liquidation price displayed on the frontend is an estimate that depends on multiple factors across all positions and can fluctuate.

commonIssues.issue: Position liquidated before expected bankruptcy price.
commonIssues.solution: This is by design. Liquidation occurs when collateral drops below the Maintenance Margin Requirement (e.g., 0.6% for BTC), which is always above zero. The bankruptcy price (where margin = 0) is never reached.

commonIssues.issue: Position liquidated before stop-loss triggered.
commonIssues.solution: This is by design — liquidation and stop-loss are evaluated independently. Set stop-loss orders with sufficient distance from the estimated liquidation price to ensure they trigger first.

commonIssues.issue: Isolated margin market order rejected at 100% slider.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.0+ which reserves a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula, preventing 'margin will be insufficient after' errors.

commonIssues.issue: Closing isolated margin position from TradingView fails.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.3+ which sends the correct margin mode to prevent reduce-only validation errors when closing positions from TradingView position lines.

commonIssues.issue: Effective leverage lower than expected for large positions.
commonIssues.solution: An IMR factor kicks in for larger notionals, reducing effective leverage. Check the formulas documentation for details on how position size affects margin requirements.

commonIssues.issue: Full position liquidated instead of partial.
commonIssues.solution: For BTC/ETH, the system defaults to full liquidation when MR falls below the 0.6% MMR threshold. This is expected behavior for these high-liquidity pairs.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot find liquidation details.
commonIssues.solution: Check the Liquidation tab in the DEX UI, or request a full liquidation record from Orderly support by providing the account address.

steps.description: Choose between customizing existing SDK components (limited customization, shows 'powered by Orderly') or building your own components using the Orderly hooks SDK (full customization).
steps.important: The DEX can be hosted on your own domain or subdomain (e.g., perps.yourdomain.com).

steps.title: Change the Broker ID in the SDK

steps.important: You must reset frontend state and re-register the wallet after changing broker ID, as fees and accounts are broker-specific.

steps.title: Hide the Risk Notice Bar for Permissionless Symbols
steps.description: Add a CSS rule to your theme.css file to hide the risk notice bar that appears for permissionless-listed symbols.

steps.title: Enable Testnet Support
steps.description: Testnet is enabled by default in the Orderly SDK unless explicitly excluded using the chainFilter configuration. Ensure chainFilter does not filter testnets out.

commonIssues.issue: Testnet chains not showing in the UI.

commonIssues.issue: Confusion about why different brokers show different chains.
commonIssues.solution: All brokers share the same liquidity/orderbook and run on the same chains. Individual brokers may choose which chains to display or support in their UI, but the underlying infrastructure is shared.
