workflows.name: Troubleshooting LayerZero Cross-Chain Message Failures
workflows.description: Diagnose and resolve common LayerZero cross-chain message failures including NotEnoughNative errors, InvalidInboundNonce on Solana, Unauthorized errors, and manual message retry procedures.
prerequisites: cast CLI tool installed (for manual retries)
RPC URLs for source and destination chains

steps.title: Check Message Status Programmatically
steps.description: If the LayerZero Scan UI is delayed, use the LayerZero Scan API to check message delivery status programmatically for real-time updates.
steps.important: The web UI can experience indexing delays on testnets or during high-load periods. The API is more reliable for programmatic status checks.

steps.title: Resolve NotEnoughNative Errors
steps.description: The NotEnoughNative error occurs when the relay or executor contract on the destination chain lacks sufficient native gas tokens to execute the message. Top up the relay contract with native tokens on the destination chain.
steps.important: After refueling the relay contract with native tokens (e.g., ETH, SEI), retry the message manually or request the LayerZero team to re-execute pending messages.

steps.title: Manually Retry Failed Messages on EVM
steps.description: If the LayerZero Scan 'Execute' button is unavailable or fails (common on testnets), manually retry by calling lzReceive directly on the destination Endpoint V2 contract.
steps.code:
cast send \
  --rpc-url <DEST_RPC> \
  --private-key $pk \
  <ENDPOINT_V2_ADDRESS> \
  "lzReceive((uint32,bytes32,uint64),address,bytes32,bytes,bytes)" \
  "(<SRC_EID>,<SENDER_BYTES32>,<NONCE>)" \
  <OAPP_ADDRESS> \
  <MESSAGE_HASH> \
  <PAYLOAD_BYTES> \
  0x \
  --value 0
steps.important: Ensure the gas limit is sufficient for execution. If you receive LZ_PayloadHashNotFound, the message has already been cleared/executed.

steps.title: Resolve InvalidInboundNonce on Solana
steps.description: InvalidInboundNonce (Error 6007) occurs when messages are delivered out of order on an ordered execution pathway. If a previous message fails and is not retried successfully before subsequent messages are processed, the nonce sequence breaks.
steps.important: Implement a retry system that processes failed messages in nonce order, and ensure the nextNonce function is correctly implemented in your OApp to support ordered delivery.

steps.title: Resolve Unauthorized Errors on Solana Endpoint
steps.description: The Unauthorized error (Error Code 6010) occurs when the signer does not match the OApp delegate registered in the oapp_registry. Ensure the transaction is signed by the correct delegate address.
steps.important: If you transferred the delegate role, verify the on-chain oapp_registry state reflects the new delegate and that the signer in your instruction matches it exactly (e.g., your multisig PDA).

steps.title: Find Testnet Contract Addresses
steps.description: Testnet contract addresses and DVN configurations can be found in the LayerZero SDK config files or by requesting them from the LayerZero team.
steps.important: Sei devnet faucets may be limited. Request tokens directly from the Sei team or use third-party services like gas.zip. For large-scale testing, coordinate with LayerZero or Sei teams for 1,000+ SEI.

commonIssues.issue: LayerZero Scan 'Execute' button unavailable on testnet.
commonIssues.solution: Use the cast CLI to manually call lzReceive on the destination Endpoint V2 contract. Ensure you have the correct message parameters (source EID, sender, nonce, payload).

commonIssues.issue: LZ_PayloadHashNotFound when retrying.
commonIssues.solution: This means the message has already been cleared/executed. No further action is needed.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot obtain testnet native tokens for relay funding.
commonIssues.solution: Sei devnet faucets may be limited. Request tokens directly from the Sei team, use gas.zip, or coordinate with LayerZero/Sei teams for bulk devnet tokens.

commonIssues.issue: Messages stuck due to nonce ordering on Solana.
commonIssues.solution: Process failed messages in strict nonce order. Implement a retry queue that respects nonce sequencing before attempting to deliver subsequent messages.

git clone https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/orderly-mcp
cd orderly-mcp

steps.description: Configure the MCP server with your broker ID so AI agents trade specifically on your DEX. Each broker can launch their own MCP instance, enabling AI agents to interact with their specific DEX configuration.
steps.important: The MCP server acts as a bridge between AI agents and your Orderly-powered DEX, providing the agent with the context it needs to trade. This enables AI-powered trading agents (e.g., built with Starchild) to connect to Orderly APIs and execute strategies on your platform.

commonIssues.issue: Build fails with missing dependencies.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using Yarn (not npm) and that all dependencies are installed. Try deleting node_modules and yarn.lock, then run yarn install again.

commonIssues.issue: MCP server fails to start.
commonIssues.solution: Verify Node.js version compatibility and ensure all dependencies are installed. Check the GitHub repository for setup instructions.

commonIssues.issue: AI agent cannot connect to MCP server.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the MCP URL is accessible and properly configured. Ensure the path to ./dist/index.js is correct relative to your agent's working directory. Ensure CORS headers are set correctly if the agent is making requests from a different origin.

commonIssues.issue: Agent trades are rejected.
commonIssues.solution: Check that the API key, secret, and account ID are correctly configured. Ensure the account has sufficient balance and the broker ID matches your DEX.

commonIssues.issue: AI agent cannot authenticate.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the ed25519 keypair is properly generated and registered. Verify the signing message format: {timestamp}{method}{path}{body}.

commonIssues.issue: Rate limiting on API calls.
commonIssues.solution: Standard rate limits apply. For higher limits, consider setting up a Market Maker account at dmm.orderly.network (50 calls/sec).

workflows.name: Building Trading Bots with CCXT
workflows.description: Build automated trading bots for an Orderly-powered DEX using the CCXT library via the woofipro exchange class.
prerequisites: Orderly API key, secret, and account ID
Broker ID for your Orderly-powered DEX

steps.title: Install CCXT
steps.description: Install the CCXT library in your Python environment.
steps.code: pip install ccxt

steps.title: Retrieve Your Broker ID
steps.description: If you don't know your broker ID, use the get builder list API endpoint with the broker_id parameter left blank to retrieve all registered brokers.

steps.title: Initialize the Exchange Connection
steps.description: Connect to your Orderly-powered DEX using the `woofipro` exchange class with your API credentials.
steps.code:
import ccxt

exchange = ccxt.woofipro({
    'apiKey': 'ed25519:YOUR_API_KEY',
    'secret': 'ed25519:YOUR_SECRET',
    'accountId': 'YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID'
})

# Load available markets
exchange.load_markets()

# Fetch account balance
balance = exchange.fetch_balance()
print(balance)
steps.important: All Orderly brokers share the same underlying API; only the `brokerId` differs. There is no separate v3 API — use the standard Orderly REST endpoints.

steps.title: Execute Trades
steps.description: Use standard CCXT methods to place orders, fetch positions, and manage your trading bot logic.
steps.code:
# Place a market buy order
order = exchange.create_market_buy_order('PERP_ETH_USDC', 0.01)

# Place a limit sell order
order = exchange.create_limit_sell_order('PERP_ETH_USDC', 0.01, 4000)

# Fetch open positions
positions = exchange.fetch_positions()
print(positions)

steps.title: Implement Risk Management
steps.description: Add stop-loss, take-profit, and position sizing logic to your bot. Be aware of Orderly's stop-loss trigger timing behavior.
steps.important: Stop-Loss orders are triggered by the mark price, which updates approximately every 1 second. In high-volatility conditions, the mark price may move past the SL trigger price between updates.

commonIssues.issue: Authentication errors when connecting.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your API key and secret are prefixed with 'ed25519:' and that your accountId is correct. API keys can be generated from the admin wallet at https://www.cryptotraders.exchange/portfolio/api-key.

commonIssues.issue: Markets not loading.
commonIssues.solution: Verify your broker ID is correct and that the DEX is operational. All Orderly brokers share the same underlying API endpoints.

commonIssues.issue: Stop-loss executing at worse price than expected.
commonIssues.solution: This can happen in high-volatility conditions when the mark price moves past the SL trigger between 1-second updates. Consider setting SL further from liquidation price to avoid liquidation occurring before SL triggers.

steps.description: Build the JSON payload with the token symbol and a receiver_list array containing account_id and amount for each recipient, then POST to the transfer endpoint.
steps.important: You can include multiple recipients in the receiver_list array for batch transfers. Internal transfers are instant and do not require on-chain transactions or gas fees.

// Docs:

workflows.name: Understanding and Managing Account Transfers, Sub-Accounts, and Liquidations
workflows.description: Handle account operations including device transfers, sub-account fund management, partial vs full liquidations, and key management best practices.

steps.title: Transfer Orderly Account to a New Device
steps.description: Transfer account credentials via QR code or export. The Orderly key is bound to the device where it was created — generating a new key on a new device creates a separate key, not a migration.
steps.important: If using biometric authentication, the key is tied to the original device's biometric profile. You must export/transfer credentials rather than regenerate them.

steps.title: Manage Sub-Account Fund Transfers
steps.description: Only the main account can make deposits and withdrawals. Sub-accounts only support internal fund transfers between the main account and the sub-account.
steps.important: Funds deposited always go to the main account first, and withdrawals also originate from the main account. Sub-accounts and main accounts share the same credentials, so there is no way to differentiate them outside of Orderly for direct on-chain deposits/withdrawals.

steps.title: Understand Partial vs Full Liquidation
steps.description: Partial liquidation occurs when the margin ratio falls below a threshold but is not critically low — only a portion of the position is liquidated. Full liquidation closes the entire position when the margin ratio is critically low, total notional value falls below minimum, or margin ratio equals the target ratio.
steps.important: The outcome depends on the liquidator, the position's notional value, and the symbol. Isolated margin mode (in development) will allow users to separate risk across positions.

steps.title: Configure Isolated Margin Mode
steps.description: Isolated margin mode (SDK v2.11.0+) allows users to allocate specific collateral to individual positions. Users can hold positions in both cross and isolated margin modes simultaneously.
steps.important: When maxing out an isolated margin market order, the SDK reserves a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula to prevent 'margin will be insufficient' rejections.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot deposit directly to a sub-account.
commonIssues.solution: This is by design. All deposits go to the main account first. Use internal fund transfers to move funds from the main account to sub-accounts.

commonIssues.issue: Orderly key lost when switching devices.
commonIssues.solution: Export/transfer credentials before switching devices. Generating a new key on a new device creates a separate key and does not migrate the existing one.

commonIssues.issue: Position liquidated unexpectedly.
commonIssues.solution: Check if partial liquidation thresholds were breached. For isolated margin positions, ensure sufficient collateral is allocated to the specific position.

workflows.name: Troubleshooting SDK TypeScript and Dependency Conflicts
workflows.description: Resolve common TypeScript compilation errors and dependency conflicts when building with Orderly SDK v2, including ethers v5/v6 conflicts and hook usage issues.

steps.title: Resolve ethers v5/v6 Type Conflicts
steps.description: The error 'Type BytesLike is not assignable to type string' in abi-coder.ts is caused by multiple ethers versions. Orderly SDK v2 depends on ethers v6.
steps.code:
# Delete node_modules and lock file, then regenerate:
rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json
npm install

# If using yarn, force ethers v6 via resolutions:
# package.json:
"resolutions": {
  "ethers": "^6.0.0"
}
steps.important: Check that ./node_modules/@orderly.network/core/node_modules/ethers resolves to v6.

steps.title: Debug useCollateral and useOrderEntry Hooks
steps.description: If useCollateral shows holdings but useOrderEntry returns maxQty = 0, the issue is typically with order type or form validation, not the collateral balance.
steps.important: It is strongly recommended to deploy the reference Orderly UI alongside your integration for debugging purposes to compare behavior.

steps.title: Set Leverage Programmatically with useSymbolLeverage
steps.description: Use the useSymbolLeverage hook to set leverage for a symbol. The leverageLevers array from useCollateral is for UI display only.
steps.important: The leverageLevers array (e.g., [1, 25, 50, 75, 100]) returned by useCollateral is for UI display only and can be ignored when setting leverage programmatically.

steps.title: Enable Isolated Margin Mode
steps.description: Isolated margin mode must be manually enabled by the Orderly team for each broker ID. Contact the Orderly team with your broker ID to request activation.
steps.important: It is recommended to first enable and test isolated margin in the staging environment, as the feature may be in beta.

commonIssues.issue: Type 'BytesLike' is not assignable to type 'string' in abi-coder.ts.
commonIssues.solution: Delete node_modules and lock file, then regenerate. If your project uses ethers v5, use yarn resolutions to force ethers v6 or isolate the dependency.

commonIssues.issue: maxQty is 0 despite having collateral balance.
commonIssues.solution: Check order parameters (type, side, symbol) in useOrderEntry. Deploy the reference Orderly UI for comparison debugging.

commonIssues.issue: Isolated margin mode not available.

- Silver/Gold: Reduced fees at higher thresholds
- Platinum: 2 bps taker fee (≥ $1B 30d volume OR 2M ORDER staked)

steps.important: Unstaking ORDER requires a 7-day waiting period. esORDER requires a 90-day conversion period to ORDER with no yield during conversion.

workflows.name: Managing RWA Perpetual Markets on Orderly
workflows.description: Understand and manage Real World Asset (RWA) perpetual trading on Orderly, including weekend trading mechanics, price bands, and fee structures.

steps.title: Understand RWA Market Types
steps.description: Orderly supports RWA perpetuals including US stocks (NVDA, TSLA, GOOGL, etc.), commodities (gold, silver via CME), and forex pairs (JPY/USD, EUR/USD). These use USDC collateral with no actual token or on-chain settlement.
steps.important: RWA perps are purely perpetual contracts — there is no actual token settlement. Liquidity for commodities comes from CME via market makers.

steps.title: Handle Weekend and Off-Hour Trading
steps.description: RWA markets use price bands during weekends and off-hours when traditional markets are closed. Orderly applies mark price ±1% bands to protect against manipulation during thin liquidity periods.
steps.important: Trading can continue during CME closures (weekends) with MM-provided quotes and static index prices. When markets reopen, bands are removed and price discovery normalizes.

steps.title: Understand RWA Fee Structure
steps.description: RWA taker fees are tier-based and aligned with crypto pair fees (1-3 bps depending on your builder tier).
steps.important: RWA pair fees are now aligned with crypto pair fees. Your builder tier determines the exact rate.

steps.title: Monitor Oracle Sources
steps.description: Orderly uses multiple oracles for RWA pricing: Finage, Tradermade, Pragma, Pyth, Stork, and Chainlink.
steps.important: Multiple oracle sources ensure robust pricing even during off-hours.

steps.title: Communicate Weekend Risks to Users
steps.description: Inform users that liquidity can be thin during weekends, which may result in wider spreads and the ±1% price band limiting price movement.
steps.important: Users should be aware that weekend RWA trading carries additional spread and liquidity risks.

commonIssues.issue: RWA prices seem stuck during weekends.
commonIssues.solution: This is expected behavior. Orderly applies ±1% price bands during off-hours to protect against manipulation. Prices normalize when traditional markets reopen.

commonIssues.issue: Wide spreads on RWA pairs during weekends.
commonIssues.solution: Liquidity is naturally thinner during weekends when CME and traditional markets are closed. Market makers provide quotes but spreads may be wider.

commonIssues.issue: Users confused about RWA settlement.
commonIssues.solution: Clearly communicate that RWA perps use USDC collateral and are purely perpetual contracts — there is no actual stock, commodity, or forex token settlement.

workflows.name: Understanding Orderly Margin, Leverage, and Position Mechanics
workflows.description: Understand how cross margin, isolated margin, leverage, and position tracking work on Orderly to build accurate trading UIs and handle user queries.
prerequisites: Understanding of perpetual futures trading concepts

steps.title: Understand Cross Margin vs Isolated Margin
steps.description: Orderly supports both cross margin (account-level) and isolated margin (position-level, SDK v2.11.0+). Cross margin shares collateral across all positions, while isolated margin dedicates specific collateral to individual positions.
steps.important: Isolated margin mode is supported starting from SDK v2.11.0 and is rolled out gradually across all Orderly DEXs. SDK v2.12.0 adds UI labels on TradingView chart position lines displaying cross/isolated margin mode labels along with leverage.

steps.title: Handle Account-Level Leverage
steps.description: Leverage on Orderly is account-level (cross margin), not per-order. The configured max account leverage is a cap that prevents creating positions with excessive leverage.
steps.important: Opening a position does not deduct USDC from the displayed balance in cross margin mode. The system tracks margin usage via the margin ratio.

steps.title: Display Available Trading Capacity
steps.description: To show users their available trading capacity, display free collateral and estimated leverage based on input parameters. The Hooks SDK provides hooks that calculate these values automatically.

steps.title: Determine Long vs Short from Position API
steps.description: Check the quantity field in the position response to determine position direction.

steps.title: Handle Isolated Margin Max Order Bug Fix
steps.description: SDK v3.1.0 fixes an issue where maxing out an isolated margin market order at 100% was incorrectly rejected. The SDK now reserves a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula.
steps.important: Ensure you are on SDK v3.1.0+ to avoid false rejections when users max out isolated margin positions.

steps.title: Understand Price Tick Rules
steps.description: Order prices must satisfy the tick rule: (price - quote_min) % quote_tick == 0. The price must be evenly divisible by the quote_tick.

commonIssues.issue: USDC balance does not decrease when opening a position.
commonIssues.solution: This is expected behavior with cross margin. Opening a position does not deduct USDC from the displayed balance. Instead, the system tracks margin usage via the margin ratio. Display free collateral to show available capacity.

commonIssues.issue: Isolated margin market order at 100% is rejected.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.0+ which fixes this issue by reserving a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot cancel individual TP or SL from a Position_TP_SL trigger order.
commonIssues.solution: You cannot cancel an individual child order (TP or SL) from a Position_TP_SL trigger. You must cancel the entire parent order and recreate it with only the desired child order(s).

commonIssues.issue: Order price rejected by tick rule.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the order price satisfies (price - quote_min) % quote_tick == 0. The price must be evenly divisible by the quote_tick value for that symbol.

workflows.name: Calculating and Querying Broker Fees from Indexer Database
workflows.description: Calculate broker fees, differentiate trade types, and query executed trades using the Orderly dashboard indexer database and Builder Leaderboard API.
prerequisites: Access to Orderly dashboard indexer database
Broker ID configured in the analyzer

steps.title: Understand Fee Data Limitations in Indexer
steps.description: The Orderly dashboard indexer database does not index whether a trade is maker or taker, and this information is not published to the blockchain.
steps.important: The side field in the partitioned_executed_trades table indicates trade direction (true = sell/short, false = buy/long), NOT maker/taker status.

steps.title: Use Builder Leaderboard API for Fee Calculation
steps.description: To calculate fees with maker/taker differentiation, use the Builder Leaderboard API endpoint which returns total_fee and broker_fee per user per day.
steps.important: Broker fees are aggregated and distributed daily, not per individual trade.

steps.title: Query Executed Trades by Transaction ID
steps.description: Join partitioned_executed_trades with serial_batches on block_number and transaction_index to query trades by transaction_id.
steps.important: Do not use log_index for joining as it differs between the two tables. Use block_number and transaction_index.

steps.title: Run the Dashboard Analyzer
steps.description: Use the orderly-dashboard-analyzer to process indexed blockchain data into a queryable database for your broker.
steps.code:

commonIssues.issue: Cannot determine if a trade was maker or taker from the indexer.
commonIssues.solution: The indexer does not track maker/taker status. Use the Builder Leaderboard API which provides total_fee and broker_fee breakdowns per user per day.

commonIssues.issue: Analyzer shows missing data for certain blocks.
commonIssues.solution: Delete the analyzer database and re-run from the desired start block. The analyzer only processes blocks after the last indexed block, so it won't re-process already indexed data.

commonIssues.issue: Join on log_index returns incorrect results.
commonIssues.solution: Do not use log_index to join partitioned_executed_trades with serial_batches as they differ between tables. Use block_number and transaction_index instead.

commonIssues.issue: Analyzer data lags behind the indexer.
commonIssues.solution: The analyzer may have processing delays relative to the indexer due to asynchronous execution. Allow time for the analyzer to catch up.

workflows.name: Handling Cross-Chain Address Mapping and Withdrawal Fees
workflows.description: Understand how Orderly handles address mapping between EVM and Solana chains, and manage withdrawal fees across different networks.
prerequisites: Active Orderly-powered DEX with multi-chain support
Understanding of EVM and Solana address formats

steps.title: Understand EVM-Solana Address Mapping
steps.description: For deposits and withdrawals, Orderly saves the original Solana user address as bytes32 in the ledger. For staking and claiming rewards, the Solana address is converted into an EVM address.
steps.important: The Solana address is converted by keccak256 hashing and truncating to 20 bytes, with the mapping saved when the user first claims a reward. EVM and Solana users are included in the same Merkle tree using EVM addresses.

steps.title: Handle Address Collision Risk
steps.description: The collision risk of truncating to 20 bytes is considered acceptable since EVM addresses themselves are derived from a bytes32 hash (e.g., via CREATE2 or EOA generation).
steps.important: No special handling is required for address collisions in normal operation.

steps.title: Check Withdrawal Fees Per Chain
steps.description: Withdrawal fees are charged to cover gas fees incurred by Orderly when processing withdrawals. Fees differ per chain.

steps.title: Handle Minimum Withdrawal Amounts
steps.description: Some chains have minimum withdrawal amounts due to high transaction fees. For example, ETH withdrawals require amounts larger than 10 USDC equivalent.
steps.important: Upgrade to SDK version 2.7.4 or later to get improved withdrawal error messaging that clearly communicates minimum thresholds instead of generic 'Amount error' messages.

steps.title: Understand Cross-Chain Order Routing
steps.description: All orders placed on an integrated platform are automatically routed to Orderly's orderbook. Post-trade transactions are recorded on Orderly Chain via LayerZero cross-chain messaging.
steps.important: Multi-chain support is handled automatically by the SDK. Builders do not need to implement cross-chain messaging themselves.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal shows 'Amount error' without descriptive message.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK version 2.7.4 or later. Earlier versions show a generic 'Amount error' toast when the withdrawal amount is below the minimum threshold. The updated SDK provides clear error messaging.

commonIssues.issue: Solana user cannot claim staking rewards.
commonIssues.solution: The Solana address must be mapped to an EVM address first. This mapping is saved when the user first claims a reward. Ensure the user has initiated at least one claim to establish the mapping.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal fees seem too high.
commonIssues.solution: Withdrawal fees cover actual gas costs on each chain and vary by network. Check the Get Supported Collateral Info API for current fee rates per chain.

workflows.name: Implementing Gasless Deposits and Internal Transfers
workflows.description: Build one-click or gasless deposit flows using master wallet approaches, smart contract depositTo functions, and internal transfer features.
prerequisites: Smart contract development capability (for gasless flows)
Understanding of Orderly Vault contract architecture

steps.title: Master Wallet Approach for Gasless Deposits
steps.description: Use a master wallet to transfer funds directly to the user's Orderly account off-chain, bypassing the standard deposit workflow.
steps.important: The master wallet transfers funds directly to the user's Orderly account off-chain. This approach requires careful security considerations for the master wallet.

steps.title: Use depositTo for Third-Party Deposits
steps.description: The depositTo function in the vault smart contract allows depositing on behalf of another user, unlike deposit which only deposits to the caller's own account.
steps.important: Cross-chain deposits require msg.value to cover LayerZero fees, which cannot be easily sponsored via standard gas sponsorship.

steps.title: Build Smart Contract Wrapper for Gas Sponsorship
steps.description: For cross-chain gasless deposits, create a smart contract wrapper that maintains a balance of native gas tokens to handle msg.value on behalf of users.
steps.important: Standard gas sponsorship cannot cover msg.value for LayerZero cross-chain fees. A wrapper contract with pre-funded native gas tokens is needed.

steps.title: Implement Internal Transfers for Rewards
steps.description: Use the internal transfer feature to send USDC/USDT to specific user accounts for rewards or giveaways.
steps.important: Internal transfers may need to be enabled by the Orderly team for your broker. Contact support to request enablement.

steps.title: Handle Smart Contract Account (SCA) Deposits
steps.description: When using a Smart Contract Account instead of an EOA signer, the EOA must still be used for Orderly account creation and signing. The SCA calls approval and deposit functions on the Orderly Vault.
steps.important: For SCA withdrawals, ensure the destination address is the SCA. Withdrawing to an address different from the signer requires the broker to be whitelisted by the Orderly team.

commonIssues.issue: Cross-chain gasless deposit fails due to LayerZero fees.
commonIssues.solution: Standard gas sponsorship cannot cover msg.value for LayerZero fees. Implement a smart contract wrapper that maintains a balance of native gas tokens to handle msg.value on behalf of users.

commonIssues.issue: Internal transfer option not available in UI.
commonIssues.solution: Internal transfers may need to be enabled by the Orderly team for your broker. Contact support to request enablement, or use the internal transfer API directly.

commonIssues.issue: SCA deposit fails with approval error.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the SCA properly calls the approval function on the token contract before calling deposit on the Orderly Vault. Reference useDeposit.ts in the hooks package for the correct flow.

workflows.name: Customizing PnL Card and Understanding PnL Settlement
workflows.description: Configure PnL (profit and loss) card/poster settings including text layout and font, and understand how PnL settlement works on Orderly.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK integrated or Orderly One DEX

steps.title: Configure PnL Card Settings
steps.description: PnL card settings can be configured in the app/utils/config.tsx file of your SDK project.
steps.important: The PnL card allows customization of text layout, font, and visual appearance for shareable profit/loss posters.

steps.title: Understand PnL Settlement Mechanics
steps.description: PnL settlement is for on-chain settlement. Before settlement, actual funds in the on-chain vault are not affected to cover realized gain/loss.
steps.important: The settlement process transfers one trader's losses to another trader's gains at the vault level. A trader can only withdraw funds after settling unrealized PnL.

steps.title: Understand Referral Revenue Share Calculation
steps.description: Referral revenue share is calculated on the broker's portion of the fee, not the total trading fee.
steps.important: Brokers cannot charge a performance fee on realized PnL. Revenue comes from the maker/taker fee split only.

commonIssues.issue: PnL card customization not taking effect.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the configuration is in the correct file (app/utils/config.tsx) and reference the sample configuration gist for proper syntax.

commonIssues.issue: Users unable to withdraw after profitable trades.
commonIssues.solution: Traders can only withdraw funds after unrealized PnL is settled on-chain. This is by design for the on-chain settlement mechanism.

commonIssues.issue: Referral commission seems lower than expected.
commonIssues.solution: Referral revenue share is calculated on the broker fee only (after deducting the Orderly base fee), not the total trading fee. Verify the fee breakdown.

workflows.name: Resolving Withdrawal and Margin Errors
workflows.description: Diagnose and resolve the 'Withdrawal Pre Margin Check Failed' error (error code 20) and handle unsettled PnL that blocks withdrawals.
prerequisites: Active Orderly trading account with open positions or pending orders
API access or DEX UI access

steps.title: Identify the Error
steps.description: Error code 20 ('Withdrawal Pre Margin Check Failed') means withdrawing the specified amount would leave the account undercollateralized given current open positions and orders.
steps.important: This is a safety mechanism to prevent accounts from becoming insolvent.

steps.title: Free Up Margin
steps.description: Close or reduce open positions and/or cancel pending orders to free up margin for withdrawal.

steps.title: Check for Unsettled PnL
steps.description: After closing positions, PnL may remain 'unsettled' in the free collateral calculation, still blocking withdrawals.

steps.title: Settle PnL
steps.description: Call the settle PnL endpoint to finalize unrealized PnL from closed positions.
steps.code:
POST /v1/settle_pnl

// After settling, retry the withdrawal.

steps.title: Retry Withdrawal
steps.description: After freeing margin and settling PnL, retry the withdrawal request.
steps.important: If the error persists, verify that sufficient free collateral exists by checking the account summary endpoint.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal still fails after closing all positions.
commonIssues.solution: Check for unsettled PnL via GET /v1/private/get-all-positions-info and call POST /v1/settle_pnl before retrying.

commonIssues.issue: Pending orders are blocking withdrawal.
commonIssues.solution: Cancel all pending orders to free up reserved margin. Open orders lock margin even if they haven't been filled.

commonIssues.issue: Collateral value fluctuation affecting available margin.
commonIssues.solution: When depositing volatile assets (e.g., SOL) as collateral, the account's USDC-denominated value fluctuates with market price. Free collateral uses the collateral's weight factor (e.g., SOL weight = 0.8). To avoid fluctuations, deposit stablecoins like USDC instead.

workflows.name: Resolving SWR Dependency Conflicts in Next.js
workflows.description: Fix SWR version conflicts and React Server Component issues when using the Orderly Hooks SDK with Next.js.
prerequisites: Next.js project with Orderly Hooks SDK

steps.title: Identify the Conflict
steps.description: SWR version conflicts can cause errors like 'export default (reexported as useSWR) was not found in swr'.
steps.important: This typically occurs when different Orderly packages depend on different SWR versions.

steps.title: Install Specific Package Versions
steps.description: Install compatible versions of the Orderly packages to resolve SWR conflicts.
steps.code: npm install @orderly.network/react@internal @orderly.network/hooks @orderly.network/core
steps.important: Using @internal tag for the react package may resolve version mismatch issues.

steps.title: Add 'use client' Directive
steps.description: In Next.js React Server Components environments, add the 'use client' directive at the top of modules where SWR is imported.
steps.important: SWR hooks must run in client components, not server components.

steps.title: Prepare Minimal Reproduction (If Issues Persist)
steps.description: If issues persist after trying the above steps, prepare a minimal reproduction repo for the DevRel team.
steps.important: Share the reproduction repo with the Orderly DevRel team for further investigation.

commonIssues.issue: Error: 'export default (reexported as useSWR) was not found in swr'.
commonIssues.solution: Install specific compatible versions: npm install @orderly.network/react@internal @orderly.network/hooks @orderly.network/core

commonIssues.issue: Hooks not working in Next.js App Router.
commonIssues.solution: Add 'use client' directive at the top of any module that imports SWR or Orderly hooks. These cannot run in React Server Components.

commonIssues.issue: Version conflicts persist after reinstalling.
commonIssues.solution: Delete node_modules and package-lock.json, then reinstall. If issues persist, prepare a minimal reproduction repo for the DevRel team.

workflows.description: Fork, customize, and deploy an Orderly DEX frontend independently, including HTTPS enforcement and custom domain setup.
prerequisites: Hosting platform (Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, etc.)

steps.description: Fork the Orderly DEX repository and host it on your own platform.

https://github.com/OrderlyNetworkDexCreator/apollo-7970
steps.important: Do not rely on Orderly One to manage custom code changes, as it is a centralized system that will overwrite modifications.

steps.title: Enforce HTTPS
steps.description: Ensure the site is served over HTTPS to avoid 404 errors and 'Embedded wallet only available over HTTPS' issues.
steps.important: All Orderly API endpoints are public and accessible over HTTPS. The embedded wallet feature requires HTTPS.

steps.title: Configure Custom Domain
steps.description: Set up a custom domain for your DEX by configuring DNS records.
steps.important: SSL certificate propagation can take 1-2 days after configuration. The default URL (e.g., salsadex-9009) is intended for testing.

steps.title: Enable Email and Social Login (Optional)
steps.description: Configure Privy for email and social login support.
steps.important: OAuth setup for social logins is considered advanced configuration.

commonIssues.issue: 'Embedded wallet only available over HTTPS' error.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the site is served over HTTPS. Enforce via Cloudflare or DNS settings.

commonIssues.issue: 404 errors on page refresh.
commonIssues.solution: Configure your hosting platform to redirect all routes to index.html for SPA routing. Ensure HTTPS is properly configured.

commonIssues.issue: Custom domain not resolving.
commonIssues.solution: Verify CNAME points to orderlynetworkdexcreator.github.io (with a dot). SSL propagation can take 1-2 days. For apex domains, consider using Cloudflare.

commonIssues.issue: Phantom wallet in-app browser connection issues on Android.
commonIssues.solution: Clear cache and browsing history, reset the device, and ensure the DEX site is served over HTTPS with proper DNS configuration. Collect OS version, browser type, location, and console logs if issues persist.

workflows.name: Understanding Cross-Chain Deposits, Trading, and Withdrawals
workflows.description: Understand how Orderly handles omnichain operations including deposits to chain-specific vaults, off-chain trading, and cross-chain withdrawals via LayerZero.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of Orderly's omnichain architecture

steps.title: Understand Deposit Flow
steps.description: Users deposit into asset manager vaults on their native chain (e.g., Solana vault for Solana users, OP vault for Optimism users).
steps.important: Each chain has its own vault contract. Deposits are chain-specific.

steps.title: Understand Trading Flow
steps.description: Trading happens off-chain via a centralized matching engine with one-click trading — no per-trade signatures required.
steps.important: After initial account setup and trading enablement (which require wallet signatures), all trades are executed using the ed25519 API key without additional wallet signatures.

steps.title: Understand Cross-Chain Rebalancing
steps.description: Orderly rebalances funds between chain vaults using LayerZero. Withdrawals are typically instantaneous because vaults are pre-funded.
steps.important: Cross-margin is used across all positions. The overall margin is calculated globally regardless of which chain the deposit came from.

steps.title: Handle Collateral Value Fluctuations
steps.description: When depositing volatile assets (e.g., SOL), the account's USDC-denominated value fluctuates with the asset's market price.
steps.important: To avoid balance fluctuations from collateral price changes, deposit stablecoins like USDC instead of volatile assets.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal takes longer than expected.
commonIssues.solution: If the destination chain vault needs rebalancing, withdrawal may take ~1-2 minutes. Users can alternatively withdraw from another chain with available liquidity for instant processing.

commonIssues.issue: Account balance fluctuates without trading.
commonIssues.solution: This occurs when volatile assets (e.g., SOL) are used as collateral. The USDC-denominated value changes with market price. Use stablecoins to avoid this.

commonIssues.issue: Isolated margin vs cross margin confusion.
commonIssues.solution: Isolated margin (SDK v2.11.0+) allocates specific margin to individual positions. Cross margin shares margin across all positions. SDK v3.1.0 fixed an issue where maxing out isolated margin market orders at 100% would be rejected — the SDK now reserves a taker fee buffer.

workflows.name: Configuring EIP-712 Signing for Orderly Account Registration
workflows.description: Set up EIP-712 domain separator configuration and implement typed data signing for Orderly account registration and API authentication on EVM chains, including native mobile implementations.
prerequisites: EVM wallet integration (web or native mobile)
Understanding of EIP-712 typed data signing
For native apps: web3j (Android) or web3swift (iOS) library

steps.title: Configure the Off-Chain EIP-712 Domain
steps.description: Use hardcoded values for the off-chain domain separator regardless of the connected chain. The verifyingContract is a placeholder — no real smart contract verifies it.
steps.important: The name is always 'Orderly' and the verifyingContract is always the hardcoded placeholder address.

steps.title: Configure the On-Chain EIP-712 Domain
steps.description: For on-chain operations, use the Ledger contract address on Orderly L2 as the verifyingContract.
steps.code:
// Refer to supported chains documentation for contract addresses:
// https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-evm/addresses
steps.important: The on-chain domain uses actual deployed contract addresses, unlike the off-chain placeholder.

steps.title: Implement EIP-712 Signing in Native Android (Kotlin)
steps.description: Use the web3j library for EIP-712 signing in native Android applications.
steps.important: Do not manually hash data before passing to the signing function. Ensure proper ABI encoding and Keccak256 hashing (not standard SHA-3).

steps.title: Implement EIP-712 Signing in Native iOS (Swift)
steps.description: Use the web3swift library for EIP-712 signing in native iOS applications.
steps.important: The signing must happen client-side; never transmit the private key to a backend server.

steps.title: Consider Alternative Approaches for Mobile
steps.description: If native EIP-712 implementation is not feasible, consider alternatives for mobile wallet integration.
steps.important: For Solana Seeker or similar devices, ensure compatibility with the Seed Vault native wallet and consider adding WalletConnect support.

commonIssues.issue: EIP-712 signature verification fails on Orderly backend.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using Keccak256 hashing (not standard SHA-3) and that the domain separator matches exactly. The chainId must match the user's connected chain.

commonIssues.issue: Native mobile app cannot sign Orderly transactions.
commonIssues.solution: Verify that the signing happens client-side and that the private key is never transmitted. If native implementation is too complex, use an embedded WebView or WalletConnect bridge.

commonIssues.issue: Signature format mismatch between web and native implementations.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure both implementations produce the same signature format (r, s, v components). Test with known test vectors from the Orderly examples repository.

steps.title: Fetch Historical Trading Events

commonIssues.issue: Historical events query returns empty results.

workflows.name: Requesting Higher API Rate Limits for Copy-Trading and Bot Backends
workflows.description: Request elevated API rate limits from Orderly for backend systems that fan out orders to many sub-accounts, such as copy-trading platforms and AI trading agents.
prerequisites: Defined target request rate and endpoint list

steps.title: Identify Rate-Limited Endpoints
steps.description: Determine which specific endpoints are hitting rate limits in your backend system.
steps.important: Per-endpoint rate limits for GET requests cannot be modified on the backend. For high-frequency data needs, use WebSocket subscriptions instead.

steps.title: Prepare Request Information
steps.description: Gather the required information to submit to the Orderly team for rate limit elevation.

steps.title: Submit Rate Limit Request to Orderly Team
steps.description: Contact the Orderly team with your prepared information. They will whitelist your IP to lift gateway-level limits.
steps.important: The Orderly team can whitelist specific IPs to bypass gateway-level rate limits for POST endpoints.

steps.title: Use WebSocket for High-Frequency Data
steps.description: For real-time market data needs, switch from REST API polling to WebSocket subscriptions.
steps.important: There is no restriction limiting WebSocket to 10 connections per IP. WebSocket is the recommended approach for high-frequency data.

steps.title: Track AI Agent Volume with order_tag
steps.description: Use the order_tag parameter when placing orders to track volume generated specifically by your bots or AI agents.
steps.important: Currently, the order_tag must be a valid referral code belonging to the same broker ID. Orderly is introducing order_tag enums for more flexible tagging.

commonIssues.issue: GET endpoint rate limits still apply after IP whitelisting.
commonIssues.solution: IP whitelisting only lifts gateway-level limits for POST endpoints. GET endpoint rate limits cannot be modified. Switch to WebSocket subscriptions for high-frequency data retrieval.

commonIssues.issue: WebSocket connection drops frequently.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your WebSocket client properly handles ping/pong frames and implements reconnection logic. Verify the URL is composed correctly per documentation.

commonIssues.issue: Public WebSocket does not respond to ping/pong.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the WebSocket URL is correctly formatted. Even public streams may require an account-id parameter for DDoS prevention.

workflows.name: Setting Up Delegate Signers for Smart Contract Accounts
workflows.description: Configure delegate signers to allow smart contracts (multisigs, LP vaults, or deposit/withdrawal contracts) to interact with Orderly by delegating an EOA to produce signatures on their behalf, enabling deposits, withdrawals, and trading without requiring direct user or multisig signatures for each operation.
prerequisites: Smart contract deployed (multisig, LP vault, or deposit/withdrawal management contract)
An EOA (Externally Owned Account) to act as delegate signer
Access to broker registration portal and multisig signing capabilities
Understanding of Orderly account registration flow

steps.title: Review Delegate Signer Documentation
steps.description: Understand the delegate signer mechanism and its requirements for smart contract accounts on Orderly. Smart contract accounts (e.g., multisig wallets) cannot directly sign Orderly messages and must delegate an EOA to produce signatures on their behalf.
steps.code:
// Documentation:
// https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/user-flows/delegate-signer
steps.important: Smart contract accounts cannot directly sign Orderly messages. They must delegate an EOA to produce signatures on their behalf.

steps.title: Register Delegate Signer via Broker Portal
steps.description: Establish the delegate signer link between your smart contract and the Orderly account through the broker registration UI. Use the multisig or admin wallet to authorize an EOA as the delegate signer.
steps.important: The delegate signer link must be established before the smart contract can interact with Orderly's deposit, withdrawal, and trading flows. The delegated EOA can sign messages and transactions without requiring multiple multisig signers for each operation.

steps.title: Use Delegate Signer for Orderly Operations
steps.description: Once delegated, use the EOA's credentials to interact with Orderly APIs, log into the admin portal, and perform operations (deposits, withdrawals, trading) on behalf of the smart contract account.
steps.important: Many brokers use a multisig on mainnet via the delegate signer feature for enhanced security of admin operations and fee collection.

steps.title: Implement Deposit and Withdrawal Flows
steps.description: The smart contract can execute deposits and withdrawals on behalf of users using the delegate signer authorization. Deposits are performed via on-chain transactions to Orderly smart contracts, not REST API calls.
steps.important: Withdrawals require EIP-712 wallet signing. The delegate signer feature allows the smart contract to handle this without requiring the user to sign each transaction directly.

steps.title: Implement Trade Execution Logic (Optional)
steps.description: Build the smart contract logic to execute trades on Orderly using the delegate signer authentication for hedging or LP vault strategies.
steps.important: Fully automated on-chain execution is not possible — the delegate signer or EOA must interact with Orderly's off-chain matching engine via API. Funding rate direction determines whether hedging is cost-effective.

steps.title: Test on Testnet
steps.description: Test the full deposit, withdrawal, and trading flow on testnet before deploying to production.
steps.important: For Solana testnet, admin wallet registration via the standard UI is not yet supported. Use your own trading UI with the broker ID configured.

commonIssues.issue: Smart contract cannot sign Orderly API requests.
commonIssues.solution: This is expected behavior. Smart contract accounts must delegate an EOA to produce signatures. Ensure the delegate signer is properly registered and that the contract implements the required EIP-712 signing interface.

commonIssues.issue: Delegate signer permissions not working.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the delegation transaction was successfully executed and confirmed. Verify the EOA is correctly registered as the delegate signer for the smart contract account.

commonIssues.issue: Smart contract deposit transactions fail.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the delegate signer link is properly established in the broker registration portal. Ensure the smart contract address matches exactly.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal transactions revert on-chain.
commonIssues.solution: Check that the EIP-712 signature is correctly generated by the smart contract. Ensure the delegate signer authorization is active and not expired.

commonIssues.issue: Hedging costs are higher than expected.
commonIssues.solution: Check the funding rate direction before executing hedge trades. If the pool is net long and you're shorting, only proceed when the funding rate is positive to avoid paying extra fees.

workflows.name: Running an Orderly Network L2 RPC Node
workflows.description: Set up and operate an Orderly Network L2 RPC node built on the OP Stack with Celestia for data availability (Alt-DA), using op-reth and Conduit's external node infrastructure.
prerequisites: Server with sufficient storage and compute resources
GCP project for snapshot access (requester-pays bucket)
Understanding of OP Stack node architecture

steps.title: Clone the External Node Repository
steps.description: Use Conduit's external node repository which contains the compatible versions and flags for running an Orderly L2 node.
steps.important: Orderly Network migrated from op-geth to op-reth (completed by June 2026). Node operators must use op-reth, not op-geth.

steps.title: Configure Celestia Alt-DA Parameters
steps.description: Set up the Celestia namespace and Alt-DA configuration in your node setup. The op-alt-da service is required.
steps.important: The op-node must be vanilla (not Celestia's fork). The Celestia op-alt-da component is still required after the op-reth migration.

steps.title: Download a Snapshot
steps.description: Syncing from genesis is not recommended due to complexity around the Alt-DA migration block height. Use a snapshot instead from the requester-pays Google Cloud Storage bucket.
steps.important: There are no free public snapshots available. You need to configure a GCP project following the Conduit guide. Genesis sync requires running the Celestia fork first and then switching to vanilla op-node around the Alt-DA migration block height.

steps.title: Start the Node
steps.description: Launch the node using docker-compose with the Celestia configuration. The node uses op-reth, op-node (vanilla), and op-alt-da service.
steps.important: Syncing is supported via consensus-layer (CL) peers using snapshots rather than from genesis.

steps.title: Monitor Node Health
steps.description: Verify the node is syncing correctly and serving RPC requests. Monitor logs for any Alt-DA or Celestia-related errors.
steps.important: Ensure the L1 beacon URL is configured for fallback to Ethereum blobs in case Celestia data availability is temporarily unavailable.

commonIssues.issue: Node fails to sync from genesis.
commonIssues.solution: Do not sync from genesis. Use a snapshot from the GCS bucket instead. Genesis sync involves significant complexity around the Alt-DA migration block height.

commonIssues.issue: op-geth errors after migration.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly Network has migrated from op-geth to op-reth. Ensure you are using op-reth as documented in the Conduit external node repository.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot access snapshot bucket.
commonIssues.solution: The snapshot bucket is requester-pays. You must configure a GCP project and enable billing to access the snapshots. Follow the Conduit guide for setup.

commonIssues.issue: Celestia data availability errors.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the Celestia namespace is correctly configured (0000000000000000000000000000000000000000000584cb53884b3945) and the op-alt-da service is running. Configure an L1 beacon URL as fallback.

workflows.name: Setting Up Orderly Webhooks for Order Notifications
workflows.description: Configure webhook endpoints to receive real-time order status change notifications (NEW, FILLED, PARTIAL_FILLED, CANCELLED, REJECTED) from Orderly with HMAC SHA-256 authentication.
prerequisites: Ability to verify HMAC SHA-256 signatures

steps.title: Request Webhook Setup
steps.description: Contact the Orderly team to configure a webhook endpoint for your broker_id. Orderly will generate a keypair and provide you with the public key for verification.
steps.important: Orderly sends POST requests to a single webhook endpoint whenever an order associated with your broker_id reaches a final state (FILLED, CANCELLED, REJECTED).

steps.title: Implement Webhook Handler
steps.description: Create an endpoint that receives POST requests with full order details and verifies the HMAC SHA-256 signature using the public key provided by Orderly.
steps.important: If your endpoint returns a status code outside 200–299, Orderly will retry the delivery.

steps.title: Use REST API as Golden Source
steps.description: While webhooks provide real-time notifications, always use the REST API as the golden source for order state recovery and reconciliation.
steps.important: Webhooks are supplementary — implement REST API polling as a fallback for critical order state tracking.

steps.title: Supplement with WebSocket Streams
steps.description: For frontend applications, use the WebSocket executionreport stream to listen for order status updates in real time.

commonIssues.issue: Webhook deliveries are being retried.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your endpoint returns a 2xx status code within the timeout period. Check server logs for processing errors that may cause non-2xx responses.

commonIssues.issue: HMAC signature verification fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the correct public key provided by Orderly and that the signature verification follows the HMAC SHA-256 standard exactly.

commonIssues.issue: Missed webhook notifications.
commonIssues.solution: Always use the REST API as the golden source for order state. Implement periodic reconciliation via REST API to catch any missed webhook deliveries.

steps.title: Hide Testnet and Filter Mainnet Chains
steps.description: Use the `chainFilter` prop on `OrderlyAppProvider` with an empty `testnet` array to hide testnet chains and specify which mainnet chains to show.
steps.code:
<OrderlyAppProvider
  chainFilter={{
    mainnet: [Arbitrum],
    testnet: [],
  }}
>
  {props.children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
steps.important: There is no built-in default chain setting. To default to a specific chain like Base, prompt the user's wallet provider to switch chains on connection.

steps.description: Include custom chain IDs in the chainFilter to add support for new networks.
steps.important: Look up chain IDs at chainlist.org. If using the Components SDK, new supported chains may appear automatically.

steps.title: Configure Testnet-Only Mode
steps.description: To support only testnet networks (e.g., Monad testnet) and exclude mainnet, set the testnet array with chain info and leave mainnet empty.
steps.code:
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="orderly"
  brokerName="Orderly"
  networkId="mainnet"
  chainFilter={{
    testnet: [{
      id: 10143,
      chainInfo: {
        name: "Monad Testnet",
        public_rpc_url: "https://testnet-rpc.monad.xyz",
        chainId: 10143,
        currency_symbol: "MON",
        explorer_base_url: "",
        vault_address: "",
      },
    }],
    mainnet: []
  }}
>
  {props.children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
steps.important: Use `chainFilter` to explicitly exclude chains you don't want (e.g., BNB Chain) if you prefer not to upgrade to a version that includes them.

steps.title: Fix English (en) Localization Bug
steps.description: There is a known bug where changing the English locale JSON file does not update default text in the UI. Fix it by removing a specific code block.
steps.important: Other languages work correctly. Only the English (en) locale is affected by this bug.

commonIssues.issue: Arb Sepolia still appears after hiding testnet.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using a compatible SDK version. Some versions like 2.0.0 introduced config changes that may affect chain filtering behavior.

commonIssues.issue: English locale changes not reflected in UI.

workflows.name: Understanding Orderly Withdrawal Security and Mechanisms
workflows.description: Understand how Orderly handles withdrawals, the security mechanisms in place, and what brokers can implement for additional security layers.

steps.title: Understand Withdrawal Verification
steps.description: All withdrawals are verified against a private key signature — there is no way to forge a withdrawal without the user's private key. Orderly API keys (access keys) do not have withdrawal permissions.
steps.important: This means even if an API key is compromised, an attacker cannot initiate withdrawals. Only the user's private key can authorize fund movements.

steps.title: Configure Withdrawal Receiver Addresses
steps.description: Withdrawals can be sent to any specified receiver address via the API. The user controls the destination address through their signed withdrawal request.
steps.important: Orderly does not restrict withdrawal destinations at the protocol level.

steps.title: Implement Broker-Level Security (Optional)
steps.description: While Orderly does not currently support time-locked withdrawals or IP-based restrictions at the protocol level, brokers can implement their own security layers.
steps.important: These security measures are implemented at the broker/frontend level, not at the Orderly protocol level.

commonIssues.issue: Users requesting time-locked withdrawals.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly does not support time-locked withdrawals at the protocol level. Implement this at the broker level using smart contracts or custom withdrawal approval workflows.

commonIssues.issue: Users requesting IP-based withdrawal restrictions.
commonIssues.solution: Implement IP restrictions on your broker's servers or frontend. Orderly does not enforce IP-based restrictions on withdrawal requests at the protocol level.

workflows.name: Tracking TVL and On-Chain Activity
workflows.description: Calculate Total Value Locked (TVL) and track deposits/withdrawals on Orderly contracts for analytics and monitoring.
prerequisites: Access to blockchain indexer (Dune, custom indexer, etc.)
Knowledge of Orderly contract addresses on target chains

steps.title: Index Deposit Events
steps.description: Track deposit events from Orderly contracts. The user wallet address is found in `args.userAddress` for both deposit event types.
steps.important: Both deposit event types use args.userAddress for the user's wallet address.

steps.title: Index Withdrawal Events
steps.description: Track withdrawal events. Note that the user wallet address is in `args.receiver` (NOT `args.sender`), and the fee is already deducted from the amount field.
steps.important: A common mistake is using args.sender instead of args.receiver for withdrawal tracking. The receiver is the actual user.

steps.title: Calculate TVL
steps.description: Compute TVL as the sum of all deposits minus the sum of all withdrawals.
steps.important: Ensure consistent decimal handling across chains. For example, USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain but Orderly only supports 6 decimals for deposits/withdrawals.

steps.title: Handle Decimal Precision Differences
steps.description: Always refer to the `decimals` field in the `chain_details` returned by the Public Token API before processing on-chain transactions.
steps.important: Mismatched decimal precision is a common source of errors in TVL calculations and on-chain transaction processing.

commonIssues.issue: TVL calculation is significantly off.
commonIssues.solution: Check decimal precision handling across chains. USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain but Orderly uses 6. Always reference the Public Token API's chain_details.decimals field.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal tracking shows wrong user addresses.
commonIssues.solution: Use args.receiver (not args.sender) for the AccountWithdraw event. The sender may be the contract, while the receiver is the actual user.

steps.title: Upgrade SDK to v2.12.3+
steps.description: Update your Orderly SDK to version 2.12.3 or later. This version facilitates the migration to the new multi-verifier framework for the Solana Vault contract.
steps.important: This is a critical security upgrade following a LayerZero exploit. DEXs that do not upgrade may experience failures with Solana deposits and withdrawals.

steps.title: Verify Solana Wallet Connection Fixes
steps.description: SDK v2.12.3 also includes Google OAuth login support within Telegram Mini Apps and fixes for Solana wallet connection issues. SDK v2.11.2 fixes a bug where Privy Wallet generated duplicate Solana addresses.
steps.important: Ensure all Solana wallet connection flows are tested after the upgrade.

steps.title: Verify Solana Deposit/Withdrawal Functionality
steps.description: After upgrading, test Solana deposits and withdrawals on testnet to ensure smooth operations under the new 3-of-3 consensus model.
steps.important: The upgrade eliminates a single point of dependency by using three independent Decentralized Verifier Networks (DVNs).

steps.title: Deploy to Production
steps.description: Once verified on testnet, deploy the updated SDK to your production environment.
steps.important: All builders supporting Solana must upgrade to ensure continued operation.

commonIssues.issue: Solana deposits or withdrawals fail after upgrade.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure all SDK packages are updated to v2.12.3 or later. Check that no conflicting older versions remain in your dependency tree.

commonIssues.issue: Cross-chain messages stuck in verification.
commonIssues.solution: The 3-of-3 model requires all three DVNs to verify. If one DVN is experiencing delays, messages may take longer. Monitor LayerZero explorer for message status.

commonIssues.issue: Privy Wallet generates duplicate Solana addresses.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v2.11.2 or later, which fixes this specific bug.

workflows.name: Debugging Orderly API Requests and Resolving SDK Errors
workflows.description: Troubleshoot Orderly API request payloads, resolve common SDK errors, and handle module resolution issues during upgrades.
prerequisites: Access to a partner DEX for comparison (e.g., WooFi)

steps.title: Compare API Payloads with Partner DEX
steps.description: Open a partner DEX (e.g., WooFi) that uses Orderly, perform the same operation (deposit, withdrawal, trade), and inspect the network request in the browser's developer console. Compare the payload structure, parameter types (string vs. number), and values against your own request to identify discrepancies.
steps.important: This is the recommended debugging approach for identifying API request issues.

steps.title: Resolve 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading get)' Error
steps.description: This error typically occurs when mixing SDK v1 and v2 components in the same project. Use SDK v2 exclusively and follow the official templates.
steps.important: Never mix SDK v1 and v2 components in the same project.

steps.title: Resolve Module Resolution Errors in Create React App
steps.description: When upgrading the SDK in a CRA-based project, you may encounter strict ESM module resolution errors (e.g., related to node-stdlib-browser/cjs/proxy/process or @binance/w3w-utils). Modify your Craco configuration to handle polyfills and module resolution properly.
steps.important: Ensure you are using node-polyfill-webpack-plugin and configure Craco's webpack settings to resolve fully specified ESM paths.

steps.title: Handle USDC Decimals on BNB Chain
steps.description: USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain, but Orderly only supports 6 decimals for deposits and withdrawals. Always refer to the decimals field in the chain_details returned by the Public Token API before processing on-chain transactions.
steps.important: SDK v2.3.0 or higher is required for BNB Chain integration. If you prefer not to upgrade, use chainFilter to explicitly exclude BNB Chain from your configuration.

commonIssues.issue: 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading get)' error in TradingPage.
commonIssues.solution: This occurs when mixing SDK v1 and v2 components. Use SDK v2 exclusively and follow the official Next.js template. Configure a custom wallet connection provider for your existing wallet setup.

commonIssues.issue: 'Can't resolve process' or similar ESM module errors after SDK upgrade in CRA.
commonIssues.solution: Install node-polyfill-webpack-plugin and configure Craco's webpack settings to handle polyfills and resolve fully specified ESM paths.

commonIssues.issue: Deposit/withdrawal precision mismatch on BNB Chain.
commonIssues.solution: USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain but Orderly supports only 6. Always check the decimals field in chain_details from the Public Token API. Use SDK v2.3.0+ or exclude BNB Chain via chainFilter.

commonIssues.issue: API request returns unexpected error.
commonIssues.solution: Compare your request payload with the same operation on a partner DEX like WooFi using browser developer tools. Check parameter types (string vs. number) and values.

workflows.name: Understanding the Orderly Key Authentication Flow
workflows.description: Understand and implement the Orderly key (ed25519) registration and authentication flow for API integrations.

steps.title: Generate ed25519 Key Pair Client-Side
steps.description: The Orderly key is an ed25519 private key generated client-side and registered with the backend, functioning similarly to a JWT for sessions. The Orderly key (public key) and Orderly secret (private key) are generated together.
steps.important: Key generation and storage happens on the client side (localStorage). The key is passed into the signing function provided by write functions.

steps.title: Sign EIP-712 Message for Registration
steps.description: The setup/authentication flow requires the user to sign an EIP-712 message before trading. This binds the ed25519 key to the user's wallet address.
steps.important: The user must sign the EIP-712 message to complete key registration.

steps.title: Execute Sequential Action Params
steps.description: The action params returned from setup are executed sequentially — the second action is only called after the first fetch completes.
steps.important: Ensure your implementation handles the sequential nature of action params correctly to avoid race conditions.

steps.title: Authenticate API Requests
steps.description: Use the generated Orderly key pair to sign and authenticate API requests with the required headers.
steps.important: The timestamp must be current UTC time in milliseconds for the signature to be valid.

commonIssues.issue: Authentication fails with invalid signature.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the timestamp is current UTC time in milliseconds and that the ed25519 key pair was correctly generated and registered.

commonIssues.issue: Key not persisting across sessions.
commonIssues.solution: The Orderly key is stored in localStorage. Ensure your application does not clear localStorage unexpectedly and that the key registration flow completes successfully.

commonIssues.issue: Sequential action params failing.
commonIssues.solution: The second action is only called after the first fetch completes. Ensure your implementation properly awaits each action before proceeding to the next.

workflows.name: Capturing Builder Revenue and Understanding Fee Mechanics
workflows.description: Understand how builders capture revenue on Orderly through broker fee layers, maker fee rebates, order_tag attribution, and the Builder Staking Programme.
prerequisites: Active broker ID registered with Orderly

steps.title: Route Orders Through Your Broker ID
steps.description: To capture revenue, builders must set up their own Orderly broker and route all orders through their broker ID. Routing trades through another broker's ID will not allow fee capture.
steps.important: Orderly does not currently support per-order builder codes like some other DEXs. API/SDK integration allows backend-only order routing without requiring a frontend.

steps.title: Add Custom Fee Layer
steps.description: Builders can add their own fee layer (e.g., a taker spread markup) on top of Orderly's base fees within their own system.
steps.important: Any amount above Orderly's base fee is retained by the broker.

steps.title: Leverage Maker Fee Rebates via Builder Staking
steps.description: Stake $ORDER tokens to access negative maker fees ranging from -0.5 bps to 0 bps (Silver tier and above). Negative maker fees settle immediately on each execution for traders.
steps.important: Builder maker and taker revenue are batched and settled once per day. Builders can keep the rebate as revenue or pass it to users as trading incentives.

steps.title: Use order_tag for Volume Attribution
steps.description: Set the order_tag field to any string value when placing orders to attribute trades and receive a share of broker fees. This allows third-party integrations (e.g., trading terminals) to track volume.
steps.important: The order_tag overrides the user's default referral code when present and does not need to be pre-created by Orderly.

steps.title: Check Volume Attributed to Broker or Referral Code
steps.description: Use the private REST API to retrieve volume data attributed to your broker or specific referral codes.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot capture fees when routing through another broker's ID.
commonIssues.solution: You must route all orders through your own broker ID. Routing through another broker's ID (e.g., Aegis) will not allow fee capture.

commonIssues.issue: Maker rebates not appearing.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your DEX is at Silver tier or above in the Builder Staking Programme. Negative maker fees settle immediately per execution, but builder revenue is batched daily.

commonIssues.issue: Understanding fee split between broker, referrer, and trader.
commonIssues.solution: The referrer and referee share the broker's net fee. Example: 4 bps taker fee with 3 bps Orderly base = 1 bps broker fee. With 50/50 referral split: broker gets 0.5 bps, referrer gets 0.5 bps, trader gets no discount.

steps.important: Rate limits are configured at the IP level by the security team and can be whitelisted for specific broker use cases (e.g., backend authentication flows).

steps.important: Unsettled PnL may remain non-zero after closure (from residual cost_position) until settlement is executed on-chain. TP/SL closures are executed via reduce-only algo orders.

commonIssues.issue: Position shows non-zero PnL but appears closed.
commonIssues.solution: Check PositionQty == 0 for closed status. Unsettled PnL from residual cost_position remains until on-chain settlement is executed. This does not affect the open/closed status.

commonIssues.issue: TradingView chart not loading historical data.

steps.title: Understand Excalibur Club Eligibility

// Use the builder users volumes endpoint:
GET /v1/builder/users/volumes

steps.title: Understand Trading Rewards Mechanism
steps.description: Trading rewards are distributed from a pool (e.g., 1M ORDER per epoch) proportionally based on a DEX's share of total Orderly volume. Users earn based on staked esORDER and trading volume with a dynamic multiplier.
steps.code:
// Trading rewards documentation:
// https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/tokenomics/trading-rewards/trading-rewards-mechanism
steps.important: Historically, rewards equated to approximately 1.5–2 bps equivalent. The exact multiplier formula depends on staked amount, individual trading volume, and total platform volume.

steps.title: Leverage Builder Staking Programme
steps.description: Stake $ORDER tokens to access lower base fee tiers (Silver, Diamond) and negative maker fees. Staking currently provides APY paid in USDC.

commonIssues.issue: Excalibur Club rebate not appearing.

commonIssues.issue: Trading rewards lower than expected.
commonIssues.solution: The multiplier is dynamic and depends on staked esORDER amount, individual trading volume relative to total platform volume. Check the mechanism documentation for the current formula.

workflows.name: Managing Isolated Margin Positions via API
workflows.description: Set leverage, retrieve liquidation prices, and adjust margin for isolated margin positions using the Orderly REST API.
prerequisites: Orderly API credentials (API key and secret)
Active Orderly account with no open positions or pending orders on target symbol (for margin mode switching)
Understanding of isolated vs cross margin behavior

steps.title: Verify Current Margin Mode
steps.description: Check the current margin mode for a symbol before attempting to change it. You can only switch margin mode when there are no open positions or pending orders.
steps.code:
GET /v1/client/margin_modes
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id

steps.title: Set Leverage for Isolated Margin
steps.description: Use the singular `/v1/client/leverage` endpoint (NOT the plural `/v1/client/leverages`) to set leverage for a specific symbol in Isolated Margin mode.
steps.code:
POST /v1/client/leverage
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id
Body: {
  "symbol": "PERP_BTC_USDC",
  "leverage": 3,
  "margin_mode": "ISOLATED"
}
steps.important: The plural `/v1/client/leverages` endpoint updates ALL symbols atomically and uses Cross margin behavior. Always use the singular endpoint for isolated margin per-symbol configuration.

steps.title: Get Estimated Liquidation Price
steps.description: Retrieve the estimated liquidation price for isolated positions using the isolated positions endpoint.

steps.title: Add Margin to Existing Isolated Position
steps.description: Increase or decrease collateral for an existing isolated position without changing the position size.
steps.code:
POST /api/v1/adjust_isolated_margin
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id
Body: {
  "subaccountId": "12345",
  "symbol": "PERP_BTC_USDC",
  "amount": 100,
  "type": "ADD"
}
steps.important: Set `type` to `"ADD"` for increasing margin or `"REDUCE"` for decreasing margin. This does not change the position size.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot switch margin mode for a symbol.
commonIssues.solution: You can only switch margin mode when you have no open positions or pending orders on that symbol. Close all positions and cancel pending orders first, then verify via GET /v1/client/margin_modes.

commonIssues.issue: Leverage change affects all symbols instead of just one.
commonIssues.solution: You are likely using the plural `/v1/client/leverages` endpoint which updates all symbols atomically with Cross margin behavior. Use the singular `/v1/client/leverage` endpoint for per-symbol isolated margin configuration.

commonIssues.issue: Position quantity smaller than filled order amount.
commonIssues.solution: This typically indicates a partial liquidation occurred. Check the user's position history for liquidation events. Liquidations trigger when the maintenance margin ratio (MMR) is breached. Provide the wallet address to Orderly tech support or check: https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/address/{ADDRESS}?broker_id={BROKER_ID}
