Understanding of Orderly's on-chain and off-chain data sources

steps.title: Set Up Dune Analytics Dashboards
steps.description: Use pre-built Dune Analytics queries filtered by your broker ID to track daily volume and daily active users.
steps.important: The Orderly team can add your DEX to these dashboards for easier tracking.

steps.title: Fetch Volume Data via API
steps.description: Use the broker daily volume endpoint for programmatic access to volume data. Results are paginated.
steps.important: Orderly provides volume data by pairs but not by chain breakdown. Use the historical Kline endpoint for per-pair volume: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-evm/evm-api/restful-api/private/get-kline

steps.title: Understand TVL Calculation Differences
steps.description: Orderly's on-chain TVL is tracked via Vault smart contracts across all supported chains (implemented in the DefiLlama adapter). Official TVL also includes Ceffu (off-exchange settlement), which cannot be tracked on-chain.
steps.code:
// DefiLlama adapter source:
// https://github.com/DefiLlama/DefiLlama-Adapters/blob/main/projects/orderly-network/index.js
steps.important: DefiLlama and Dune TVL figures may differ from Orderly's official reported TVL because the official figure includes Ceffu off-exchange settlement balances.

steps.title: Track User Trading Rewards
steps.description: Fetch $ORDER and $esORDER trading rewards (claimable and already claimed) using a combination of API and smart contract calls.
steps.important: You need data from both the Orderly API (total rewards) and the smart contract (already claimed amounts) to calculate claimable rewards.

commonIssues.issue: DefiLlama TVL doesn't match Orderly's official TVL.
commonIssues.solution: This is expected. DefiLlama only tracks on-chain Vault smart contract balances. Orderly's official TVL also includes Ceffu (off-exchange settlement) balances which cannot be tracked on-chain.

commonIssues.issue: Volume API returns incomplete data.
commonIssues.solution: Results are paginated with a default max of 50 records per page. Use the `&page=` parameter to loop through all pages and aggregate the full dataset.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot get volume breakdown by chain.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly provides volume data by pairs but not by chain. Use Dune Analytics dashboards for chain-level breakdowns.

workflows.name: Troubleshooting SDK Integration Issues
workflows.description: Resolve common SDK integration issues including withdrawal failures, Next.js compatibility, wallet registration updates, Solana adapter bundling errors, PnL settlement failures, watchlist persistence, wallet compatibility, SSL certificate problems, and embedding the DEX in existing applications.
prerequisites: Access to browser developer tools for debugging
Basic understanding of your build system (webpack/vite)

steps.title: Fix Intermittent Withdrawal Failures
steps.description: Intermittent withdrawal failures are likely caused by an outdated SDK version. The root cause is related to cross-chain messaging: after the LayerZero exploit, the system was migrated from Single DVN to DVN 3, and older SDK versions may not handle this correctly.
steps.code:
// Upgrade to SDK v3.0.2 or later
"@orderly.network/react": "^3.0.2"
steps.important: This is a critical fix. Users may experience intermittent withdrawal failures if the SDK is not updated.

steps.title: Apply Mandatory Wallet Registration Update
steps.description: SDK v3.0.4 includes a critical feature update for wallet registration requests. While the current registration process continues to work, it may encounter issues in the future without this update.
steps.code:
// Upgrade to SDK v3.0.4 or later
"@orderly.network/react": "^3.0.4"
steps.important: The recommendation level is high-mandatory for SDK builders. Apply this update as soon as possible.

steps.title: Fix Next.js SWR Export Error
steps.description: If you encounter the 'export default (reexported as useSWR) was not found in swr' error when integrating Orderly with Next.js, add the 'use client' directive.

steps.title: Fix Solana Adapter Bundling for EVM-Only Projects
steps.description: The @orderly.network/hooks package hardcodes the Solana adapter as a dependency, forcing EVM-only integrators to bundle 242+ Solana packages causing OOM builds.
steps.important: This is a known high-impact builder experience issue. Monitor SDK release notes for the fix making Solana adapters optional.

steps.title: Fix 'transactRemote is not exported' Error
steps.description: This error occurs due to version incompatibility with @solana-mobile/wallet-adapter-mobile after upgrading to SDK v2.1.1.

steps.title: Debug PnL Settlement Failures
steps.description: When a user cannot settle PnL, verify the wallet is actually signing the settle_pnl request and that it reaches Orderly's servers.
steps.important: If the request never hits Orderly's servers, the issue is on the client side (e.g., signing failure). Provide the user's wallet address to Orderly tech support for further debugging.

steps.title: Fix Watchlist/Favorites Not Persisting
steps.description: Implement a custom ConfigStore to properly persist watchlists and favorites in local storage.
steps.important: The default ConfigStore does not separate watchlists by network. Implement custom logic using networkId if your app serves both mainnet and testnet from the same URL.

steps.title: Fix Binance Wallet Chain-Switching Errors
steps.description: Integrate the Binance Blocknative connector to resolve chain-switching issues with Binance Wallet connected via WalletConnect.

steps.title: Handle USDC Decimal Precision on BNB Chain
steps.description: USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain, but Orderly only supports 6 decimals for deposits and withdrawals.
steps.important: Precision mismatches will cause deposit/withdrawal failures. Always refer to the API response rather than assuming decimal precision.

steps.title: Fix SSL Certificate Errors After Domain Changes
steps.description: When changing from a root domain to a subdomain (or vice versa), SSL certificates need to be re-provisioned.
steps.important: SSL certificates are provisioned automatically when you configure your custom domain through Orderly One and set correct DNS records. Propagation may take time. Root-to-subdomain changes require a new certificate unless using a wildcard certificate.

steps.title: Embed DEX in Existing Application
steps.description: If you need the DEX integrated as part of your existing app rather than hosted on its own domain, migrate the Orderly One (low-code) source code into your own codebase or use the Orderly SDK directly.
steps.important: Orderly One by default is designed to be hosted on a custom domain as a standalone DEX. Embedding it within another application requires moving the code into your project.

steps.title: Generate Client Library from OpenAPI Spec
steps.description: Use the canonical OpenAPI spec to generate client code in your preferred language using a Swagger code generator.
steps.important: API authentication (EIP-712 signing) is the trickiest part to implement. Refer to the authentication docs and language-specific examples for guidance.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawals intermittently failing for users.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.0.2 or later. The issue is related to the LayerZero DVN migration from Single DVN to DVN 3.

commonIssues.issue: 'useSWR' export error in Next.js.
commonIssues.solution: Add the 'use client' directive to the file using the Orderly SDK configuration.

commonIssues.issue: Wallet registration may fail in the future.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.0.4+ which includes a critical wallet registration request update. This is high-mandatory.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot embed Orderly One DEX in existing app.
commonIssues.solution: Migrate the Orderly One source code into your own codebase, or use the Orderly SDK directly with your broker ID for integration.

commonIssues.issue: Build fails with out-of-memory (OOM) errors.
commonIssues.solution: This is likely caused by the Solana adapter bundling issue. Configure tree-shaking to exclude Solana modules or pin to an earlier SDK version.

commonIssues.issue: Limit orders and positions not showing on TradingView chart.
commonIssues.solution: This functionality requires the paid version of TradingView. Some features may be available in the free version but are not implemented in the Orderly TradingPage component for the free tier.

commonIssues.issue: Mobile tabs (Trading, Portfolio, Markets) not appearing.
commonIssues.solution: Mobile tab navigation requires explicit configuration in your app config. Refer to: https://github.com/OrderlyNetworkDexCreator/dex-creator-template/blob/main/app/utils/config.tsx#L231-L233 and ensure you are using a recent SDK version.

workflows.name: Understanding Orderly Vault and Subaccount Architecture
workflows.description: Understand how Orderly's vault model handles fund custody and trading, and how subaccounts relate to the main account for independent trading states.
prerequisites: Understanding of on-chain vs off-chain settlement

steps.title: Understand the Vault Model
steps.description: Orderly vaults are on-chain asset management tools. Funds are deposited on Orderly, then mirrored to a custodial account (Ceffu) for trading on Binance.
steps.important: Strategy providers run their strategies on Binance using the mirrored funds. This architecture provides deep liquidity while maintaining on-chain custody.

steps.title: Understand Subaccount Architecture
steps.description: Subaccounts are derived from and share the same main wallet address. Each subaccount has its own independent trading state.
steps.important: Subaccounts are treated as independent trading accounts. The main account has control over all its subaccounts, enabling portfolio separation and risk management.

steps.title: Use Subaccounts for Risk Management
steps.description: Leverage subaccounts to separate trading strategies, isolate risk, or manage different portfolios under a single wallet address.
steps.important: Each subaccount maintains its own margin and liquidation state, preventing cross-contamination of risk between strategies.

commonIssues.issue: Confusion about where funds are actually held.
commonIssues.solution: Funds are deposited on-chain in Orderly Vault smart contracts, then mirrored to Ceffu for trading execution on Binance. The on-chain vault maintains custody while Ceffu enables off-exchange settlement.

commonIssues.issue: Subaccount balances not reflecting correctly.
commonIssues.solution: Each subaccount has independent balances. Ensure you are querying the correct subaccount. The main account can view and control all subaccounts.

relatedWorkflows: Setting Up Permissionless Vaults
Managing Isolated Margin Positions via API

workflows.name: Integrating Privy Wallet with Custom UI
workflows.description: Integrate Privy wallet authentication with Orderly SDK using a custom UI (without Orderly's prebuilt React components), ensuring proper wallet recognition and account state management.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK with wallet-connector-privy package installed

steps.title: Wrap Application with Providers
steps.description: Wrap your custom UI with WalletConnectorPrivyProvider and OrderlyAppProvider, configuring Privy, Wagmi, and Solana settings.
steps.code:
<WalletConnectorPrivyProvider
  network={networkId === 'mainnet' ? Network.mainnet : Network.testnet}
  privyConfig={{ appid: privyAppId, config: { loginMethods: ['email'] } }}
  wagmiConfig={{ connectors: getEvmConnectors() }}
  solanaConfig={getSolanaConfig(networkId)}
>
  <OrderlyAppProvider brokerId='...' brokerName='...' networkId={networkId}>
    <YourCustomUI />
  </OrderlyAppProvider>
</WalletConnectorPrivyProvider>

steps.title: Implement Connect Button with useWalletConnector
steps.description: Use the useWalletConnector hook to connect via Privy. You MUST use this hook — do not call Privy's login/OAuth hooks directly.

steps.title: Read Account State
steps.description: After connecting, read wallet and account state from the appropriate hooks.
steps.important: Orderly recognizes the account ONLY when the wallet connects through useWalletConnector().connect(...) with WalletConnectType.PRIVY. Calling Privy's login hooks directly will not register the wallet with Orderly.

commonIssues.issue: Wallet connects in Privy but Orderly does not recognize the account.
commonIssues.solution: You must use useWalletConnector().connect({ walletType: WalletConnectType.PRIVY }) instead of calling Privy's login/OAuth hooks directly. Orderly only recognizes accounts connected through its own hook.

commonIssues.issue: Account state shows as disconnected after Privy login.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure both WalletConnectorPrivyProvider and OrderlyAppProvider wrap your component tree in the correct order, and that you are reading state from useAccount() after the connect() call resolves.

workflows.name: Managing Orders via Hooks SDK and REST API
workflows.description: Create, edit, and manage regular and algorithmic orders using the Orderly Hooks SDK or REST API, including TP/SL configuration with Mark Price offsets and Trailing Stop orders.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v3.1.0+ (for latest TP/SL and isolated margin fixes) or REST API access
Active Orderly account with sufficient margin

steps.title: Edit Orders Using Hooks SDK
steps.description: Use the useOrderStream hook to update existing regular or algorithmic orders.

steps.title: Edit Orders Using REST API
steps.description: Use the PUT endpoints to modify existing orders. Ensure all required fields are included and data types match.
steps.important: Pay attention to data types — order_quantity and order_price should be strings, and reduce_only should be explicitly set (null or boolean). Mismatched data types between creation and update requests are a common source of errors.

steps.title: Configure TP/SL with setValue
steps.description: Set Take Profit and Stop Loss values programmatically using the setValue function with appropriate keys.
steps.important: From SDK v2.12.3, TP/SL Offset and Offset% values are calculated from the Mark Price. SDK v2.12.2 improved chart-dragging TP/SL to use mark price instead of entry price, enabling 'lock-profit' stop-loss scenarios.

steps.title: Use Advanced TP/SL Features
steps.description: Leverage SDK version-specific TP/SL capabilities for enhanced trading strategies.
steps.important: Partial TP/SL supports both market and limit order execution, while Full Position TP/SL supports only market orders.

commonIssues.issue: Order update fails with type mismatch error.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure order_price and order_quantity are strings (not numbers), and reduce_only is explicitly set to null or a boolean. Match the data types used during order creation.

commonIssues.issue: Isolated margin max-out order rejected with 'margin will be insufficient after'.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.0+. This version fixes the issue by reserving a taker fee buffer that matches the backend frozen-margin formula, aligning isolated margin behavior with cross margin.

commonIssues.issue: TP/SL not triggering at expected price.
commonIssues.solution: Verify whether you are using entry price or mark price offsets. From SDK v2.12.3, offsets are calculated from Mark Price. Check your SDK version and adjust expectations accordingly.

workflows.name: Setting Up Testnet and Automated Testing
workflows.description: Configure a testnet environment for automated testing against Orderly, including faucet access, broker ID provisioning, and API testing without real funds.
prerequisites: Orderly account or wallet for testnet

steps.title: Access Testnet Environment
steps.description: Use the Orderly testnet which shares the same API as mainnet but with a different base URL. If using the SDK, testnet is handled automatically based on the selected network.

steps.title: Get Testnet Funds via Faucet
steps.description: Use the faucet endpoint to get testnet USDC credited directly to your Orderly account (not your wallet). The funds can be withdrawn to any supported chain.
steps.important: The faucet credits USDC directly to your Orderly account, not your wallet. Testnet broker IDs are not fully isolated — other users could theoretically use the same broker ID.

steps.title: Configure API for Testnet
steps.description: Point your API calls to the testnet base URL and use testnet-specific API keys and account IDs.

steps.title: Run Automated Tests
steps.description: Execute your test suite against the testnet API. Test deposits, withdrawals, order placement, and position management.
steps.important: Orderly can provision a dedicated broker ID on testnet for testing purposes. Contact the Orderly team if you need an isolated test environment.

commonIssues.issue: Faucet USDC not appearing in account.
commonIssues.solution: The faucet credits USDC directly to your Orderly account, not your on-chain wallet. Check your Orderly account balance, not your wallet balance.

commonIssues.issue: Testnet broker ID conflicts with other users.
commonIssues.solution: Testnet broker IDs are not fully isolated. Contact Orderly to provision a dedicated broker ID for your testing needs.

commonIssues.issue: API keys work on mainnet but not testnet.
commonIssues.solution: API keys and account IDs are unique per environment. Register separate keys for testnet at the broker registration portal.

workflows.name: Connecting to Orderly via CCXT in Python
workflows.description: Connect to a specific Orderly broker instance (e.g., Mode) using the CCXT library in Python for algorithmic trading and data retrieval.
prerequisites: Orderly API key, secret, and account ID
Broker ID for the target instance

steps.title: Install CCXT and Configure Exchange
steps.description: Use the ccxt.woofipro exchange class (not ccxt.woo, which targets the WooX CEX) and configure it with your Orderly credentials.
steps.important: Use ccxt.woofipro, NOT ccxt.woo. The woo class targets the WooX centralized exchange, not Orderly Network.

steps.title: Register API Keys for Your Broker
steps.description: API keys and account IDs are unique per broker. Register your keys at the broker registration portal.
steps.important: Each broker instance requires its own set of API keys. Keys registered for one broker will not work with another.

steps.title: Fetch Historical Kline and Funding Rate Data
steps.description: Retrieve historical OHLCV data and funding rates using the public API endpoints.

workflows.name: Authenticating Orderly API Requests
workflows.description: Generate Ed25519 signatures and authenticate private REST and WebSocket requests to the Orderly API, including signature generation, header configuration, and examples in TypeScript and Python.
prerequisites: Orderly account ID and private key (obtainable from broker registration portal)
Backend environment for making API requests

steps.title: Obtain or Generate an Ed25519 Key Pair
steps.description: Create an ed25519 key pair yourself and register it in Orderly's infrastructure by sending the public key along with an EIP-712 signature. Orderly never sees your private key.
steps.important: If your API key expires, create a new one instead of renewing. Navigate to Portfolio → API on the DEX, or use the broker registration tool.

steps.title: Construct the Signature Message
steps.description: Normalize the message by concatenating: timestamp (ms) + HTTP method (uppercase) + request path including query parameters (without base URL) + JSON-stringified body (if present).
steps.important: The path must include query parameters if they exist (e.g., /v1/order?symbol=PERP_ETH_USDC). Omit BODY_STRING for requests without a body. The timestamp must be current or the request will be rejected. Ensure your server clock is synchronized.

steps.title: Sign Requests in TypeScript
steps.description: Use @noble/curves/ed25519 and @scure/base libraries to sign the message and encode the signature.
steps.important: The orderly-key header should be formatted as ed25519:<base58-encoded-public-key>.

steps.title: Sign Requests in Python
steps.description: Use the cryptography library's Ed25519PrivateKey and base58/base64 utilities.
steps.code:
import json
from base58 import b58decode
from base64 import urlsafe_b64encode
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.ed25519 import Ed25519PrivateKey

def generate_orderly_signature(method, path, body, timestamp, orderly_secret):
    body_string = json.dumps(body) if body else ""
    message = f"{timestamp}{method}{path}{body_string}"
    private_key = Ed25519PrivateKey.from_private_bytes(b58decode(orderly_secret))
    signature = private_key.sign(message.encode("utf-8"))
    return urlsafe_b64encode(signature).decode("utf-8").rstrip("=")
steps.important: Strip trailing '=' characters from the base64url-encoded signature.

steps.title: Set Required Authentication Headers
steps.description: Include all four required headers in every private endpoint request.
steps.important: The orderly-key must be in ed25519 format. The signature must be base64url-encoded.

steps.title: Authenticate WebSocket Connections
steps.description: Private WebSocket connections use the Orderly Key for authentication. The signature message for WebSocket auth is the timestamp only (method, path, and body are blank).
steps.important: Send ping messages regularly to maintain the WebSocket connection.

steps.title: Implement Dead Man's Switch
steps.description: Use the dead man's switch endpoint to automatically cancel all open orders if the client loses connectivity.
steps.important: The dead man's switch must be called repeatedly to keep resetting the timer. If the timer expires, all open orders are cancelled.

steps.title: Test Authentication with Example Code
steps.description: Use the provided example implementations to verify your authentication setup works correctly.

steps.title: Programmatically Validate Orderly Keys (Optional)
steps.description: Use the public endpoint to check the validity of a user's Orderly key without requiring their signature. Useful for backend systems that need to validate keys server-side.

commonIssues.issue: Signature verification fails with 'invalid signature' error.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the message is constructed exactly as specified: timestamp + method + path with query params + body string. Verify that the timestamp is in milliseconds, the method is uppercase, and the body is JSON-stringified without extra whitespace. Verify that the ed25519 key is properly formatted.

commonIssues.issue: Signature verification fails intermittently.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your server clock is synchronized using NTP. Even small clock drifts can cause timestamp validation failures.

commonIssues.issue: API key expired.
commonIssues.solution: Create a new API key instead of renewing the expired one. Navigate to Portfolio → API on the DEX, or use the broker registration tool at https://github-dev.orderly.network/broker-registration/.

commonIssues.issue: WebSocket connection drops unexpectedly.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are sending ping messages regularly. If the connection drops, reconnect and re-authenticate with a fresh timestamp and signature.

commonIssues.issue: Rate limit errors (HTTP 429).
commonIssues.solution: Orderly has two layers: GCP rate limit (600 req/5 min per IP) and endpoint-specific limits (e.g., 10 req/sec for GET /v1/orderly_key). Orderly reads the IP address directly from the connection (not from X-Forwarded-For headers). Brokers can apply for IP whitelisting to bypass the GCP limit by providing specific IP addresses to Orderly support. CIDR blocks are not supported.

commonIssues.issue: Rate limit errors during high-traffic periods.
commonIssues.solution: Apply for IP whitelisting with Orderly support. Implement client-side rate limiting and request queuing to stay within endpoint-specific limits.

commonIssues.issue: Users from restricted regions can still access the DEX.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly's geo-blocking is frontend-only. If you need stricter enforcement, implement additional server-side geo-blocking via Cloudflare or your hosting provider.

commonIssues.issue: UI does not handle maintenance windows.
commonIssues.solution: Poll the system status endpoint regularly and display appropriate user-facing messages. Disable trading buttons and order submission during maintenance.

workflows.name: Generating and Registering an Orderly Key
workflows.description: Generate an ed25519 key-pair and register it as an Orderly Key for API authentication, supporting both TypeScript and Python implementations.
prerequisites: An EVM wallet with an existing Orderly account registration
Node.js with ethers.js and @noble/curves (for TypeScript) OR Python with eth_account and cryptography (for Python)
Connected chain ID and broker ID

steps.title: Generate an ed25519 Key-Pair
steps.description: Generate a new ed25519 private key and encode the public key in the required format: 'ed25519:<base58-encoded-public-key>'.
steps.important: Store the private key securely. You will need it to sign all subsequent API requests.

steps.title: Construct the AddOrderlyKey EIP-712 Message
steps.description: Build the EIP-712 typed-data message with the required fields: brokerId, chainId, orderlyKey, scope, timestamp, and expiration.
steps.important: The scope field determines what actions the key can perform. Use 'read' for data queries, 'trading' for order placement, and 'asset' for deposits/withdrawals. Combine with commas for multiple permissions.

steps.title: Sign the Message Using EIP-712
steps.description: Sign the AddOrderlyKey message using the off-chain EIP-712 domain with verifyingContract set to 0xCcCCccccCCCCcCCCCCCcCcCccCcCCCcCcccccccC.
steps.important: The off-chain domain (verifyingContract: 0xCcCCccccCCCCcCCCCCCcCcCccCcCCCcCcccccccC) is used specifically for Registration and AddOrderlyKey. Other operations like Withdraw and SettlePnl use the on-chain Ledger contract address instead.

steps.title: Register the Key via REST API
steps.description: POST the signed message, signature, and user address to the /v1/orderly_key endpoint.
steps.important: The account must already be registered on the Orderly network before adding a key. If the account is not registered, key registration will fail.

commonIssues.issue: Key registration fails with 'account not found' error.
commonIssues.solution: The wallet must first be registered as an Orderly account. Complete the account registration flow (which also uses EIP-712 signing) before attempting to add an Orderly Key.

commonIssues.issue: API requests return authentication errors after key registration.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are signing API requests with the ed25519 private key (not the EVM wallet). Use the net.i2p.crypto.eddsa library in Java, @noble/curves in TypeScript, or cryptography.hazmat in Python to sign with the Orderly Key.

commonIssues.issue: Signature verification fails during key registration.
commonIssues.solution: Verify that the EIP-712 domain uses the off-chain verifyingContract (0xCcCCccccCCCCcCCCCCCcCcCccCcCCCcCcccccccC), not the on-chain Ledger contract. Also ensure chainId matches the connected network.

workflows.name: Signing Orderly API Requests in Java
workflows.description: Sign Orderly REST API requests using Java with the ed25519 cryptographic library for private endpoint authentication.

steps.title: Add Dependencies
steps.description: Include the ed25519 Java library in your project for cryptographic signing operations.
steps.code:
// Maven dependency
<dependency>
  <groupId>net.i2p.crypto</groupId>
  <artifactId>eddsa</artifactId>
  <version>0.3.0</version>
</dependency>
steps.important: The net.i2p.crypto.eddsa library provides the EdDSAEngine and EdDSAPrivateKey classes needed for signing.

steps.title: Create the EdDSA Private Key
steps.description: Decode your base58-encoded secret key and create an EdDSAPrivateKey instance using the ED_25519 curve specification.
steps.important: The secret key is the raw ed25519 private key bytes encoded in base58, not the EVM wallet private key.

steps.title: Construct and Sign the Message
steps.description: Build the message string from the request parameters, sign it using EdDSAEngine, and encode the signature in URL-safe Base64.
steps.important: Use Base64.getUrlEncoder() (URL-safe encoding), not the standard Base64 encoder. The signature must be URL-safe to be transmitted in HTTP headers.

steps.title: Set Authentication Headers
steps.description: Attach the required authentication headers to your HTTP request.
steps.important: The Content-Type must be 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' for GET and DELETE requests, and 'application/json' for POST and PUT requests. Mismatched Content-Type will cause signature verification to fail.

commonIssues.issue: Signature verification fails on the server side.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the message string is constructed exactly as specified: timestamp + HTTP method + request path + body/query string. Any deviation in formatting will produce an invalid signature.

commonIssues.issue: Base64 encoding produces invalid characters in headers.
commonIssues.solution: Use Base64.getUrlEncoder() instead of Base64.getEncoder(). The URL-safe variant replaces '+' and '/' with '-' and '_', which are safe in HTTP headers.

commonIssues.issue: Timestamp rejection errors.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your system clock is synchronized. The orderly-timestamp must be within an acceptable window of the server time. Use NTP to keep your clock accurate.

workflows.name: Implementing Vault Deposits and Withdrawals
workflows.description: Complete workflow for depositing tokens into and withdrawing funds from the Orderly Vault, covering standard EOA deposits, smart contract/multisig vault deposits (including delegate signer setup and depositTo), fee calculation, EIP-712 signing, PnL settlement, cross-chain withdrawal handling, and on-chain balance verification.
prerequisites: Registered Orderly account with an Orderly Key (scope: 'asset')
EVM wallet with sufficient tokens for deposit and ETH for gas
Vault and Ledger contract addresses from the Smart Contract Addresses page
Smart contract wallet (multisig, vault, etc.) if using delegate signer flow
Delegate signer private key (for smart contract vault operations)
Understanding of Orderly's delegate signer flow

steps.title: Set Up Delegate Signer (Smart Contract Vaults)
steps.description: If operating a smart contract vault (multisig, strategy vault), configure a delegate signer that can sign trading actions and withdrawals on behalf of the vault.
steps.important: Deposits are made through smart contract methods (deposit / depositTo). Withdrawals must be signed by the wallet private key of the delegated signer.

steps.title: Approve the Vault Contract
steps.description: Call the ERC-20 approve function on the token contract to allow the Vault smart contract to spend your deposit amount.
steps.important: The Vault contract address is available on the Smart Contract Addresses page. Ensure you approve the exact deposit amount or use max uint256 for unlimited approval.

steps.title: Calculate the Deposit Fee
steps.description: Call the Vault contract's getDepositFee function to determine the required fee in WEI. Construct a DepositData struct with accountId, brokerHash, tokenHash, and tokenAmount.
steps.important: The deposit fee must be sent as msg.value when calling the deposit function. The fee is denominated in WEI (native gas token).

steps.title: Execute the Deposit
steps.description: Call the Vault contract's deposit function with the DepositData struct and send the calculated deposit fee as the transaction value.
steps.important: All Vault contracts are verified on block explorers, so ABIs can be retrieved directly from the explorer.

steps.title: Deposit from Multisig via Broker Registration Portal
steps.description: For multisig wallets (e.g., Safe, Avocado), use the broker registration portal with WalletConnect to deposit funds.
steps.important: If the balance does not appear or the connection fails, try switching the chain back and forth in the wallet interface to refresh the RPC connection.

steps.title: Deposit on Behalf of Another User
steps.description: Use the depositTo smart contract function to deposit funds into another user's Orderly account.
steps.code:
// Call depositTo on the vault contract:
vault.depositTo(accountId, brokerHash, tokenHash, amount)
steps.important: If you abstract away wallet connection entirely, you will need to proxy all trading API interactions through your own backend since Orderly tracks users via their wallet address and Orderly key.

steps.title: Settle PnL Before Withdrawal
steps.description: Before withdrawing, settle any realized and unrealized PnL into your USDC balance. This is a three-step process: get nonce, sign EIP-712 message, and submit settlement request.
steps.important: PnL settlement can be triggered at any time by the account owner or by other users. If PnL is not settled before withdrawal, the withdrawal may fail due to insufficient withdrawable_balance.

steps.title: Execute Withdrawal
steps.description: Withdraw funds by obtaining a withdrawal nonce, signing an EIP-712 Withdraw message, and submitting via the REST API.
steps.important: The receiver address must equal the account address. The Withdraw message uses the on-chain Ledger contract as verifyingContract, not the off-chain address used for key registration. Also check if the target chain has sufficient liquidity — if not, an additional cross-chain fee is deducted.

steps.title: Handle Insufficient Vault Balance on Withdrawal
steps.description: If a withdrawal fails due to insufficient vault balance on the source chain, use cross-chain withdrawal or switch chains.
steps.important: Before setting allow_cross_chain_withdraw to true, verify via the vault balance API that the chain supports rebalancing. Setting this on unsupported chains will cause the request to fail. The system has auto-rebalancing mechanisms, but they are not instantaneous.

steps.title: Verify On-Chain Account Balance
steps.description: For on-chain account balance/PnL verification, implement a pull-based oracle approach since Orderly does not natively push account values on-chain.
steps.important: Orderly does not push account values on-chain. A pull-based oracle approach is needed for on-chain verification of account balance and PnL.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal fails due to insufficient withdrawable_balance.
commonIssues.solution: Settle your PnL first using the Settle PnL flow before attempting a withdrawal. Unrealized PnL is not included in withdrawable balance until settled.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal fails with insufficient vault balance on source chain.
commonIssues.solution: Use allow_cross_chain_withdraw: true (after verifying chain supports rebalancing) or switch to a chain with sufficient vault balance. The system auto-rebalances but not instantaneously.

commonIssues.issue: Deposit transaction reverts.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you have approved the Vault contract to spend the exact token amount, and that you are sending the correct deposit fee as msg.value. Verify the DepositData struct fields are correctly computed (especially brokerHash and tokenHash).

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal signature rejected.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the on-chain Ledger contract address as the verifyingContract in the EIP-712 domain, not the off-chain address (0xCcCCccccCCCCcCCCCCCcCcCccCcCCCcCcccccccC) used for key registration.

commonIssues.issue: Multisig deposit transaction not appearing.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you selected 'EOA wallet' as the registration type even for multisig wallets. If the connection fails, switch chains back and forth in the wallet interface to refresh the RPC connection.

commonIssues.issue: Cross-chain withdrawal incurs unexpected fees.
commonIssues.solution: Check if the target chain has sufficient liquidity before withdrawing. If liquidity is insufficient, an additional cross-chain fee will be deducted from the withdrawal amount.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot verify account balance on-chain.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly does not push account values on-chain. Implement a pull-based oracle approach to read account data from Orderly's API and verify it on-chain.

workflows.name: Subscribing to Real-Time WebSocket Data Streams
workflows.description: Subscribe to public and private WebSocket streams for orderbook snapshots, trade executions, and private execution reports on Orderly.
prerequisites: For private streams: a registered Orderly Key with appropriate scope

steps.title: Connect to the WebSocket Endpoint
steps.description: Establish a WebSocket connection to the appropriate endpoint (public or private).
steps.important: Public streams (orderbook, trades) do not require authentication. Private streams (execution reports, positions) require a valid Trading Key.

steps.title: Subscribe to Orderbook Data
steps.description: Send a subscribe message for real-time orderbook updates on a specific symbol.
steps.important: The topic format is '{symbol}@orderbook'. The 'id' field is a client-generated string used to match subscription confirmations.

steps.title: Subscribe to Trade Execution Events
steps.description: Subscribe to real-time trade events as they occur on a specific market.
steps.important: Trade events are pushed in real time as executions occur. The topic format is '{symbol}@trade'.

steps.title: Subscribe to Private Execution Reports
steps.description: Subscribe to private execution report updates for your orders. Optionally filter by specific symbols.
steps.important: The 'params' object and 'params.symbol' are optional. If omitted, you receive execution reports for all symbols. The push interval is real-time.

commonIssues.issue: WebSocket connection drops frequently.
commonIssues.solution: Implement automatic reconnection logic with exponential backoff. Re-subscribe to all topics after reconnecting.

commonIssues.issue: Private stream authentication fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your Orderly Key has the 'trading' scope and that you are passing the correct authentication headers (orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id) during the WebSocket handshake.

commonIssues.issue: No data received after subscribing.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the topic format is correct (e.g., 'PERP_BTC_USDC@orderbook', not 'PERP_BTC_USDC_orderbook'). Check the server confirmation response for 'success: true'.

workflows.name: Performing Internal Transfers Between Orderly Accounts
workflows.description: Transfer tokens between Orderly accounts using EIP-712 signed messages and the internal transfer API.
prerequisites: Registered Orderly account with an Orderly Key (scope: 'asset')
Sufficient available balance in the sender's account

steps.title: Obtain a Transfer Nonce
steps.description: Call the transfer nonce endpoint with standard Orderly authentication headers.
steps.code:
GET /v1/transfer_nonce
Headers:
  orderly-timestamp: <UNIX ms>
  orderly-account-id: <sender account ID>
  orderly-key: <ed25519 public key>
  orderly-signature: <signed request>
steps.important: The nonce is required for the EIP-712 message and prevents replay attacks.

steps.title: Sign the InternalTransfer EIP-712 Message
steps.description: Construct and sign an EIP-712 message of type InternalTransfer using the on-chain domain with the Ledger contract address.
steps.important: Use the on-chain Ledger contract address as verifyingContract, not the off-chain address (0xCcCCccccCCCCcCCCCCCcCcCccCcCCCcCcccccccC) used for key registration.

steps.title: Submit the Internal Transfer Request
steps.description: POST the signed message and parameters to the internal transfer endpoint.
steps.code:
POST /v2/internal_transfer
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "signature": "0x...",
  "message": {
    "receiver": "0x...bytes32...",
    "token": "USDC",
    "amount": "100000000",
    "transferNonce": 12345
  },
  "chainId": 42161,
  "chainType": "evm",
  "userAddress": "0xSenderWalletAddress",
  "verifyingContract": "0xLedgerContractAddress"
}
steps.important: The userAddress must match the wallet address associated with the Orderly Account ID making the request. Mismatched addresses will cause the transfer to fail.

commonIssues.issue: Transfer fails with signature verification error.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the on-chain Ledger contract address as the verifyingContract in the EIP-712 domain, and that the userAddress matches the wallet associated with the sender's Orderly account.

commonIssues.issue: Transfer rejected due to insufficient balance.
commonIssues.solution: Internal transfers draw from the available balance. Ensure sufficient funds are available (not locked in isolated margin positions or pending orders).

commonIssues.issue: Invalid receiver account ID.
commonIssues.solution: The receiver must be a valid bytes32 Orderly account ID. Verify the recipient's account ID format before submitting the transfer.

workflows.name: Setting Up the Orderly React SDK with Wallet Connection
workflows.description: Install and configure the Orderly React SDK with wallet connection support for both EVM and Solana chains, including layout scaffolding.

steps.title: Install Core SDK Packages
steps.description: Install the base UI and React application packages along with the styles.
steps.important: The styles import is required for proper rendering of all Orderly UI components.

steps.title: Configure OrderlyAppProvider
steps.description: Wrap your application with the OrderlyAppProvider component, passing required configuration props.
steps.code:
import { OrderlyAppProvider } from "@orderly.network/react-app";

<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  brokerName="Your Broker Name"
  networkId="testnet"  // or "mainnet"
  appIcons="/path/to/icons"
>
  {children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
steps.important: The networkId cannot change during runtime. Use a page refresh or separate domain when switching between testnet and mainnet.

steps.title: Add Wallet Connection Support
steps.description: Install and configure the wallet connector to support both EVM and Solana wallets.
steps.important: The WalletConnectorProvider must wrap the OrderlyAppProvider. For Solana support, pass the solanaInitial prop with the desired network. Alternatively, integrate third-party wallet libraries by implementing the WalletConnectorContextState interface from @orderly.network/hooks.

steps.title: Add Navigation and Layout Scaffolding
steps.description: Install the scaffold library and use the Scaffold component for built-in navigation and layout.
steps.important: The Scaffold component provides built-in top navigation, side navigation, and footer. Configure routerAdapter with onRouteChange (to handle navigation clicks) and currentPath (the active route).

commonIssues.issue: UI components render without styles.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you have imported '@orderly.network/ui/dist/styles.css' in your application entry point.

commonIssues.issue: Solana wallets not appearing in the connector.
commonIssues.solution: Verify that the WalletConnectorProvider is wrapping the OrderlyAppProvider and that the solanaInitial prop is correctly configured with the desired network.

commonIssues.issue: Navigation links do not work in the Scaffold.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the routerAdapter prop is properly configured with both onRouteChange (a function to handle route changes) and currentPath (the current active route string).

workflows.name: Installing and Configuring the Orderly React Hooks SDK
workflows.description: Set up the Orderly React Hooks SDK with custom stores, wallet adapters for EVM and Solana, and the OrderlyConfigProvider.

steps.title: Install Hooks SDK Packages
steps.description: Install the hooks SDK and its types package.
steps.code: npm install @orderly.network/types @orderly.network/hooks
steps.important: Both @orderly.network/types and @orderly.network/hooks are required.

steps.title: Configure OrderlyConfigProvider
steps.description: Wrap your root component with OrderlyConfigProvider, passing your brokerId and networkId.
steps.important: networkId accepts either 'mainnet' or 'testnet'.

steps.title: Use Custom ConfigStore and OrderlyKeyStore (Optional)
steps.description: If you have already implemented the Orderly Key creation process or need to customize it, pass your own store instances instead of using the default brokerId prop.
steps.important: Both stores must implement the ConfigStore and OrderlyKeyStore interfaces from @orderly.network/core. When using custom stores, omit the brokerId prop.

steps.title: Integrate EVM and Solana Wallet Adapters
steps.description: Pass wallet adapter instances to the walletAdapters prop on OrderlyConfigProvider.
steps.important: Use DefaultEVMWalletAdapter from @orderly.network/default-evm-adapter (initialized with an EthersProvider from @orderly.network/web3-provider-ethers) for EVM chains, and DefaultSolanaWalletAdapter from @orderly.network/default-solana-adapter for Solana.

commonIssues.issue: Hooks return undefined or throw errors.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the OrderlyConfigProvider wraps all components that use Orderly hooks. The provider must be an ancestor of any component calling hooks like useAccount.

commonIssues.issue: Custom keyStore not being used.
commonIssues.solution: When passing custom configStore and keyStore, do not also pass the brokerId prop. The custom stores replace the default broker-based configuration.

commonIssues.issue: Wallet adapter not connecting.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you have installed the required adapter packages (@orderly.network/default-evm-adapter, @orderly.network/default-solana-adapter, @orderly.network/web3-provider-ethers) and that the EthersProvider is properly initialized.

workflows.name: Analyzing Top Traders and Whale Activity
workflows.description: Retrieve leaderboards of top trading addresses on Orderly, drill into specific whale addresses for detailed position and order history analysis.
prerequisites: Access to Orderly Public Info API
Understanding of Orderly market symbols (e.g., PERP_BTC_USDC)

steps.title: Fetch Top Addresses Leaderboard
steps.description: Send a request with type `topAddresses` to the Public Info API. Filter by symbol, choose a ranking metric, set a minimum notional threshold, and paginate as needed.
steps.important: The endpoint has a weight of 10. Limit ranges from 1–200. Use cursor-based pagination for additional pages.

steps.title: Drill Into a Specific Whale Address
steps.description: After identifying an address from the topAddresses leaderboard, use the whaleContext or accountState endpoint to get detailed per-address information.
steps.important: Use whaleContext for a comprehensive view of a whale's activity, or accountState for a snapshot of their current positions and balances.

steps.title: Analyze and Visualize Data
steps.description: Aggregate the retrieved data to build dashboards, alerts, or reports on whale activity, top PnL performers, or high-volume traders.
steps.important: Combine topAddresses with platformPositions data for a complete picture of market positioning.

commonIssues.issue: API returns empty results for topAddresses.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the symbol is correct (e.g., PERP_BTC_USDC) and that the min_notional threshold is not set too high. Try lowering the threshold or removing it.

commonIssues.issue: Whale context endpoint returns limited data.
commonIssues.solution: The address may not have significant activity on Orderly. Verify the address was actually returned from the topAddresses leaderboard for the correct symbol.

workflows.name: Retrieving Platform-Wide Position Snapshots
workflows.description: Fetch a snapshot of all open positions across the Orderly platform, with filtering and pagination support for large-scale analysis.
prerequisites: Access to Orderly Public Info API

steps.title: Fetch Platform Positions
steps.description: Send a request with type `platformPositions` to the Public Info API. Filter by symbol, broker_id, and min_notional to narrow results.
steps.important: Limit ranges from 1–5000 (default 500). Results are sorted by position ID descending.

steps.title: Paginate Through All Results
steps.description: Use cursor-based pagination to fetch all positions. The response includes a `next_cursor` field; pass it as the `cursor` parameter in subsequent requests.
steps.important: A null value for next_cursor indicates there are no more results to fetch.

steps.title: Aggregate and Analyze Position Data
steps.description: Process the fetched positions to compute metrics like total open interest, average leverage, or distribution of position sizes.
steps.important: The min_notional filter (default 0) helps exclude dust positions from analysis.

commonIssues.issue: Pagination seems to return duplicate positions.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are passing the exact next_cursor value from the previous response. Do not modify or truncate the cursor string.

commonIssues.issue: Large result sets cause timeouts.
commonIssues.solution: Reduce the limit per page and use min_notional to filter out small positions. Process results incrementally rather than loading everything into memory.

relatedWorkflows: Building a Liquidation Heatmap

workflows.name: Building a Liquidation Heatmap
workflows.description: Create a liquidation heatmap by aggregating estimated liquidation prices from all open positions on Orderly into price buckets.
prerequisites: Access to Orderly Public Info API platformPositions endpoint

steps.title: Fetch All Open Positions
steps.description: Use the platformPositions request type to retrieve all open positions. Filter by symbol and min_notional to focus on relevant positions.
steps.important: The endpoint returns up to 5000 rows per page. Use cursor-based pagination to fetch all positions.

steps.title: Extract Estimated Liquidation Prices
steps.description: From each position row, extract the `est_liq_price` field which represents the estimated liquidation price for that position.
steps.important: Positions with null or zero est_liq_price should be excluded from the heatmap.

steps.title: Aggregate Into Price Buckets
steps.description: Group the liquidation prices into price buckets (e.g., $100 intervals for BTC) and sum the notional value of positions in each bucket.
steps.important: Choose bucket sizes appropriate for the asset's price range. Smaller buckets give more granularity but may be noisy.

steps.title: Visualize the Heatmap
steps.description: Render the aggregated data as a heatmap showing price levels on one axis and cumulative notional at risk on the other.
steps.important: Highlight clusters of liquidation prices as these represent potential cascade liquidation zones.

commonIssues.issue: Heatmap shows no data.
commonIssues.solution: Verify that positions are being fetched correctly and that est_liq_price values are non-null. Some positions may not have a calculable liquidation price.

commonIssues.issue: Heatmap is too noisy or too sparse.
commonIssues.solution: Adjust the bucket size. Increase bucket size for smoother visualization or decrease it for more detail. Also adjust the min_notional filter.

commonIssues.issue: Pagination misses positions during fetch.
commonIssues.solution: Positions are sorted by position ID descending. New positions opened during pagination may be missed. For real-time accuracy, re-fetch periodically.

workflows.name: Triage Failed Transactions and Orders
workflows.description: Systematically diagnose failed deposits, withdrawals, registrations, or orders on Orderly by distinguishing on-chain failures from API failures and following a structured escalation path.
prerequisites: User's wallet address, transaction hashes, and error messages

steps.title: Collect Failure Details
steps.description: Gather the wallet address, builder ID, chain, market symbol, timestamp, and any transaction hash, order ID, or API error message from the user.
steps.important: Distinguish whether the failure is on-chain (transaction submitted to blockchain) or at the Orderly API/order placement level.

steps.title: Classify the Failure Type
steps.description: Determine if the failure is on-chain or API-level. On-chain failures involve transactions that reverted, ran out of gas, or are stuck pending. API failures are indicated by error codes in the response.
steps.important: Always determine which category the failure falls into before proceeding with further troubleshooting.

steps.title: Check Prerequisites and Flow
steps.description: For wallet/account setup issues, verify the user followed the Accounts and Wallet Authentication guides. For trading requests, confirm the correct payload was submitted and review API error codes.
steps.important: For on-chain failures, confirm the user is interacting with a supported deployment from the address list.

steps.title: Inspect On-Chain Transaction (if applicable)
steps.description: If the failure is on-chain, inspect the transaction in the relevant block explorer for revert reasons, gas issues, or confirmation delays.
steps.important: Look for specific revert reasons that indicate insufficient balance, slippage, or contract-level errors.

steps.title: Use Orderly Dashboard for Account Inspection
steps.description: Use the Orderly Dashboard at https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/ to retrieve user account state and history for diagnostic purposes.
steps.important: The dashboard provides visibility into account state, order history, and transaction records that may not be visible to the user.

steps.title: Escalate to Orderly Support (if unresolved)
steps.description: If the issue remains unresolved, escalate to Orderly support with all collected details, the failing request payload, and any explorer or API response evidence.
steps.important: Check the Integration FAQs (https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/integration-faqs) and Troubleshooting section before escalating.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot determine if failure is on-chain or API-level.
commonIssues.solution: Check if a transaction hash was generated. If yes, it's on-chain — inspect the block explorer. If no hash exists and an API error was returned, it's an API-level failure.

commonIssues.issue: User claims transaction succeeded but funds not credited.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the transaction on the block explorer. Check if it was sent to the correct contract address on a supported chain. Use the Orderly Dashboard to check if the deposit was processed.

commonIssues.issue: API returns generic error without clear cause.
commonIssues.solution: Review the full request payload against the API documentation. Check for missing required fields, incorrect formatting, or authentication issues.

workflows.name: Diagnosing Stuck or Delayed Withdrawals
workflows.description: Systematically diagnose withdrawal delays on Orderly by checking the Dune dashboard, LayerZero explorer, and escalating to support when needed.
prerequisites: User's wallet address and withdrawal details
Access to Orderly Support Dune dashboard

steps.title: Check Orderly Support Dune Dashboard
steps.description: Visit the Orderly Support Dune dashboard to verify whether the withdrawal went through to any chain. Refresh the dashboard before checking.
steps.code:
// Dune Dashboard:
https://dune.com/orderly_network/orderly-support-dashboard
steps.important: Users sometimes request withdrawals to the wrong chain. Always refresh the dashboard before checking, as data may be cached.

steps.title: Check LayerZero Explorer for Cross-Chain Messages
steps.description: If the withdrawal is not visible on Dune, go to the LayerZero explorer, select 'Source: Orderly', and look for cross-chain messages.
steps.important: If a message shows as in-flight and was created more than 10 minutes ago, the withdrawal is being delayed due to LayerZero cross-chain messaging.

steps.title: Assess LayerZero Message Status
steps.description: Determine if the cross-chain message is in-flight, completed, or failed. In-flight messages older than 10 minutes indicate a LayerZero delay.
steps.important: LayerZero cross-chain messaging can experience delays during network congestion. Most messages complete within a few minutes.

steps.title: Escalate to Orderly Support
steps.description: If neither the Dune dashboard nor LayerZero explorer resolves the issue, contact Orderly support with the user's details.
steps.important: Provide as much detail as possible to expedite the support process.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal not showing on Dune dashboard.
commonIssues.solution: The withdrawal may not have been processed yet, or the user may have requested it to a different chain than expected. Check LayerZero explorer next.

commonIssues.issue: LayerZero message stuck in-flight for over 10 minutes.
commonIssues.solution: This indicates a LayerZero cross-chain messaging delay. Monitor the message status. If it remains stuck for an extended period, escalate to Orderly support.

commonIssues.issue: User withdrew to the wrong chain.
commonIssues.solution: Check the Dune dashboard for the actual destination chain. The funds may have been delivered to a different chain than the user expected.

workflows.name: Developing and Publishing Orderly Plugins with Devkit CLI
workflows.description: Install the Orderly devkit CLI, scaffold a new plugin from the template, develop and test it locally, and publish it to the Orderly Builders Marketplace.

steps.title: Install the Devkit CLI
steps.description: Install the Orderly devkit CLI globally using pnpm. The executable name is `orderly-devkit`.
steps.code:
pnpm add -g @orderly.network/devkit

# Verify installation:
orderly-devkit --help

# Or run without global install:
pnpm dlx @orderly.network/devkit --help
steps.important: Requires Node.js v20.19.0 or newer. The executable is `orderly-devkit`, not `orderly`.

steps.title: Install Agent Skills and MCP Server (Optional)
steps.description: Install AI agent skills and the SDK Docs MCP server for AI-assisted plugin development.
steps.code:
# Install plugin agent skills:
orderly-devkit skills install

# List available skills:
orderly-devkit skills install --list

# Target a specific AI client:
orderly-devkit skills install --agent cursor

# Install SDK Docs MCP:
orderly-devkit mcp install

# Or with specific client:
orderly-devkit mcp install --client cursor --scope project
steps.important: Agent skills include: orderly-plugin-create, orderly-plugin-write, orderly-plugin-add, and orderly-plugin-submit. These are optional but recommended for AI-assisted development.

steps.title: Scaffold a New Plugin
steps.description: Create a new plugin from the official template using the devkit CLI. Use interactive mode or provide all required flags for non-interactive creation.
steps.code:
# Interactive mode:
orderly-devkit create plugin

# Non-interactive mode:
orderly-devkit create plugin --no-interactive \
  --name MyPlugin \
  --id my-plugin \
  --interceptor Trading.OrderEntry.SubmitSection \
  --target ./MyPlugin \
  --skip-install
steps.important: The --name is normalized to PascalCase. The --id is a kebab-style string used for registerPlugin and the manifest. The --interceptor must be a valid interceptor target. The --target must be an empty or non-existent directory.

steps.title: Build and Run Locally
steps.description: Navigate into the generated plugin directory, install dependencies, and start the development server.
steps.code:
cd ./MyPlugin
pnpm install
pnpm run dev
steps.important: To wire the plugin into a host app, use the OrderlyAppProvider plugins configuration: plugins={[registerMyPlugin()]}

steps.title: Authenticate with the Marketplace
steps.description: Log in to the Orderly Builders Marketplace via browser OAuth before submitting plugins.
steps.code:
orderly-devkit login

# Verify session:
orderly-devkit whoami

# Re-authenticate if needed:
orderly-devkit login --force

# Clear session:
orderly-devkit logout
steps.important: The OAuth redirect callback listens on a fixed port (default 9876). If the port is in use, free it and retry — there is no --port flag.

steps.title: Validate with Dry Run
steps.description: Run a dry run to validate the manifest, package.json, repoUrl, pluginId, tags, and usagePrompt before submitting.
steps.code: orderly-devkit submit --path . --dry-run
steps.important: Fix any validation errors reported by the dry run before proceeding with a real submission.

steps.title: Submit to the Marketplace
steps.description: Submit the plugin to the Orderly Builders Marketplace. A successful submission returns HTTP 201 and the plugin enters under_review status.
steps.code:
orderly-devkit submit --path . \
  --tags UI,Trading \
  --storybook-url https://example.com/storybook
steps.important: Invalid tags are dropped with a warning. The plugin typically enters under_review status after submission and undergoes a security review before going live.

steps.title: Manage Existing Listings
steps.description: Use the devkit CLI to list, view, and update existing plugin listings on the Marketplace.
steps.code:
# List your plugins:
orderly-devkit list
orderly-devkit list --json

# View a specific plugin:
orderly-devkit view <plugin-id>

# Update an existing listing:
orderly-devkit update --path ./my-plugin
orderly-devkit update --path ./my-plugin --dry-run
steps.important: The update command requires pluginId to be present in .orderly-manifest.json. Treat Marketplace responses as the source of truth for listing metadata.

commonIssues.issue: Login fails with port-in-use error.
commonIssues.solution: The OAuth callback uses a fixed port (default 9876). Free the port by stopping any process using it, then retry. There is no --port flag to change it.

commonIssues.issue: 401 error when submitting or updating.
commonIssues.solution: Run orderly-devkit login to authenticate or re-authenticate. Verify your session with orderly-devkit whoami.

commonIssues.issue: Submit fails with validation errors.
commonIssues.solution: Run with --dry-run first to identify issues. Ensure package.json has a valid name field, the git origin remote is set (for repoUrl), and the usagePrompt meets length requirements.

commonIssues.issue: Plugin interceptor not found during development.
commonIssues.solution: Use the Developer/Inspector tooling in dev mode to enumerate all interceptor paths registered by your SDK version. Refer to @orderly.network/plugin-core on npm for architecture details.

relatedWorkflows: Integrating with SDK v3 Plugin System
Building a Trading Interface with Pre-built Components

workflows.name: Deploying and Expanding Permissionless Vaults
workflows.description: Create a Permissionless Vault on Orderly, manage cross-chain deployment, and handle recovery scenarios for failed LayerZero messages.
prerequisites: EVM wallet with sufficient gas and 0.1 ETH Vault Operation Reserve

steps.title: Configure Vault Parameters
steps.description: Select vault parameters through the frontend: vault name, description, broker, strategy provider (SP) address, SP name, performance fee rate, deployment chain, and first period start time.
steps.important: The performance fee rate is locked in at vault creation and cannot be changed. Choose carefully.

steps.title: Deploy the Vault
steps.description: Sign a single createPermissionlessVault() transaction on your chosen chain. The factory contract deploys the vault using CREATE3 (deterministic address), registers it with the cross-chain manager, and sends a configuration message to the Orderly Chain via LayerZero V2.
steps.important: The deterministic address is derived from the vault parameters. Different parameters produce a different address.

steps.title: Wait for Ledger Registration
steps.description: The Orderly Chain ledger receives the cross-chain message and automatically configures the vault (broker assignment, fee rates, SP authorization), typically within 1–5 minutes.
steps.important: Registration is automatic and typically completes within 1–5 minutes. If it takes longer, check for LayerZero message delivery issues.

steps.title: Verify Provisioning and Go Live
steps.description: The indexer captures on-chain events and syncs vault data to the CeFi backend, which auto-provisions all necessary accounts and configurations. The vault then appears in the vault listing and is ready for LP deposits.
steps.important: All provisioning is automatic. No manual backend configuration is required.

steps.title: Add Additional Chain Support
steps.description: To expand to additional chains, call createPermissionlessVault() on each new chain's factory with the same parameters. The same deterministic salt produces the same vault address.
steps.important: Adding a new chain requires paying the same fees (gas, cross-chain fee, and 0.1 ETH Vault Operation Reserve). Expand one chain at a time.

steps.title: Handle Cross-Chain Recovery (if needed)
steps.description: If the LayerZero message fails during vault creation, use recovery options to complete registration.
steps.important: The vault remains usable on its deployment chain (deposits and withdrawals work) even if cross-chain registration is pending. Only cross-chain settlement is blocked until registration completes.

commonIssues.issue: Vault deployed but not appearing in listing.
commonIssues.solution: Wait 1–5 minutes for cross-chain registration. If still not visible after 30 minutes, check LayerZero message status or call resendConfiguration() on the factory.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot add a new chain to existing vault.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the exact same parameters as the original creation. Different parameters produce a different deterministic address and will create a separate vault.

commonIssues.issue: LayerZero message fails during creation.
commonIssues.solution: LayerZero V2 has built-in retry. If the message remains undelivered, call resendConfiguration() on the factory contract. The operation is idempotent and safe to retry.

workflows.name: Deposit Funds into an Orderly Account
workflows.description: Approve a supported token and call the Orderly Vault deposit contract so funds are credited to an Orderly account under your broker ID.
prerequisites: Registered Orderly account and account ID
Valid broker ID (brokerHash is keccak256 of the broker ID string)
A supported token/chain pair and its Vault + token contract addresses
Wallet with gas for the target chain

steps.title: Confirm the token and chain are supported
steps.description: Use the supported collateral info endpoint to verify the token/chain combination and check deposit availability. For custodial or CEX senders that cannot call contracts, use the Deposit by Transfer flow instead of the Vault deposit.

steps.title: Approve ERC20 spending by the Vault
steps.description: For ERC20 tokens, approve the Vault contract to spend the deposit amount. Native tokens (for example OKB on X Layer) skip approval and are deposited through the payable deposit function.

steps.title: Build the DepositData struct
steps.description: accountId is the Orderly account ID in bytes32; brokerHash is keccak256(utf8(brokerId)); tokenHash is keccak256(utf8(token)); tokenAmount uses the token's on-chain decimals (USDC uses 6).
steps.important: A mismatched brokerHash or tokenHash credits the wrong account or token. Derive both from the exact strings.

steps.title: Quote the deposit fee and call deposit
steps.description: Read getDepositFee(receiver, depositInput), then call deposit(depositInput, { value: fee }) for ERC20, or value = principal + fee for native tokens. Only the principal is credited as collateral.

steps.title: Wait for cross-chain credit and verify
steps.description: Deposits can take time to reflect while the cross-chain transfer finalizes. Confirm the credited balance with GET /v1/client/info or the asset history endpoint before placing orders.

commonIssues: Deposit not credited yet: cross-chain finalization can take time; check asset history before retrying
Wrong decimals: pass on-chain units (6 for USDC), not ledger units
Missing approve: ERC20 deposits revert without an allowance for the Vault
Native token sent directly to the Vault address instead of through the payable deposit call
relatedWorkflows: Withdraw Funds from Orderly
Understanding Orderly Withdrawal Security and Mechanisms
Implementing Gasless Deposits and Internal Transfers

workflows.name: Withdraw Funds from Orderly
workflows.description: Request a withdrawal by signing an EIP-712 Withdraw message with the on-chain domain and submitting it to the withdrawal API.
prerequisites: Orderly account with a positive withdrawable balance
Realized PnL settled if the withdrawal includes trading profits
API credentials (orderly key) for the REST call

steps.title: Settle PnL if needed
steps.description: Realized profit from open or recently closed positions must be settled through the Settle PnL flow before it enters withdrawable_balance. Withdrawing before settlement can exceed the available balance and fail.

steps.title: Choose the destination chain and check fees
steps.description: Read current withdrawal fees and minimums from the supported collateral info endpoint. If the destination chain lacks liquidity, an additional cross-chain fee can be deducted.

steps.title: Get a withdrawal nonce
steps.description: Call the withdrawal nonce endpoint and use the returned value in the signed message.

steps.title: Sign the EIP-712 Withdraw message
steps.description: Use the on-chain domain (name Orderly, version 1, destination chainId, Ledger verifyingContract) - not the off-chain API-auth domain. Fields: brokerId, chainId, receiver, token, amount, withdrawNonce, timestamp.
steps.important: amount is a uint256 in the signed message but must be serialized as a string in the REST payload.

steps.title: Submit the withdrawal request
steps.description: POST /v1/withdraw_request with { message, signature, userAddress } and the standard Ed25519 API auth headers. Track the withdrawal status until the funds arrive.

commonIssues: Unsettled PnL makes the requested amount exceed the withdrawable balance
Using the off-chain auth domain instead of the on-chain Ledger domain
Sending amount as a JSON number instead of a string in the REST payload
Wrong token decimals for the destination chain
relatedWorkflows: Deposit Funds into an Orderly Account
Understanding Orderly Withdrawal Security and Mechanisms
Diagnosing Stuck or Delayed Withdrawals

workflows.name: Place and Manage a Limit Order
workflows.description: Create, track, edit, and cancel a limit order through the signed Orderly REST API.
prerequisites: Registered account with a valid orderly key
Sufficient collateral for margin and fees

steps.title: Read the symbol rules
steps.description: Fetch quote_min/max, quote_tick, base_min/max, base_tick, and min_notional. Prices and quantities must land exactly on ticks; Orderly does not round for you.

steps.title: Sign the request
steps.description: Sign timestamp + method + path + body with the Ed25519 orderly key and send orderly-account-id, orderly-key, orderly-signature, and orderly-timestamp headers.

steps.title: Create the order
steps.description: POST /v1/order with symbol, side, order_type=LIMIT, order_price, order_quantity, and margin_mode when the symbol is isolated-margin only.
steps.important: Use IOC with a protection price for market-style entries, and reduce_only=true to close a position without flipping sides.

steps.title: Track the order
steps.description: Subscribe to the executionreport WebSocket topic for fills and status changes, or poll GET /v1/orders with status filters.

steps.title: Edit or cancel
steps.description: PUT /v1/order changes price or quantity before the fill; DELETE /v1/order cancels a single order; DELETE /v1/orders cancels all pending orders.

commonIssues: Price or quantity off the tick size
Missing leverage setting for the symbol
Signature mismatch because the body was reserialized after signing
relatedWorkflows: Creating Bracket Orders with Take Profit and Stop Loss via API
Managing Orders via Hooks SDK and REST API

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, and set up default trading fees.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions

steps.title: Register Broker ID with Orderly Team
steps.description: Provide your unique Broker ID (a string identifier), Broker Name, Default Taker Fee, Default Maker Fee, and initial Broker tier/level (e.g., 'public') to the Orderly team for backend configuration.
steps.important: Broker tiers can increase based on trading volume, which reduces Orderly's base taker fee. Default fees are typically configured at setup (e.g., 6 bps taker, 3 bps maker).

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature. Registration must be done separately for testnet and mainnet.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. For example, if a broker sets a 0.05% taker fee, they earn 0.05% - 0.03% = 0.02% per trade. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates. The Orderly team can share an internal script for periodic fee maintenance if needed.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account. Check the balance by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet or using the private Get Current Holding endpoint.

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity. After the change, the attacker can only potentially modify the DEX itself and the broker ID. Orderly support will also update the Orderly One login wallet. Monitor the DEX closely during the transition.

commonIssues.issue: Custom fees below standard tier not applying.
commonIssues.solution: Custom trading fees below the standard tier require the builder to be in the Diamond tier of the Builder Staking Programme. Additionally, the DEX must be 'graduated' (not using a shared broker ID). If not graduated, fees cannot be modified. Contact the Orderly team to request trial periods for custom fee structures.

relatedWorkflows: Generating Orderly API Credentials

Implementing Custom Fee Tiers for Users

workflows.name: Generating Orderly API Credentials
workflows.description: Generate Orderly API Key and Secret (ORDERLY_SECRET) for programmatic access to Orderly's trading and account APIs.
prerequisites: Access to broker registration tool or Orderly SDK

steps.title: Generate Key and Secret Pair
steps.description: The Orderly Key and Secret are generated permissionlessly by signing an EIP-712 message with an EVM wallet (or using the Solana equivalent). The private key generated during this process serves as the ORDERLY_SECRET.
steps.important: The secret key is shown only once when creating an Orderly key. Store it securely.

steps.title: Register Key with Orderly
steps.description: After generating the key pair, register it with Orderly to associate it with your account.

steps.title: Use Credentials for API Authentication
steps.description: Use the generated credentials to authenticate API requests by including the required headers.

steps.title: Store Keys for Automated Trading (Bots)
steps.description: For trading bots that trade on behalf of users, the application must store the user's Orderly Key securely since automated products cannot rely on users generating keys in their browser at trade execution time.
steps.important: It is recommended to have at least a UI where users can register and store their Orderly Key in the application's infrastructure so that bots can trade on their behalf, as well as handle deposits and withdrawals.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot find orderly-account-id or orderly-key.
commonIssues.solution: Obtain these from your DEX under Portfolio -> API Keys, or from the broker registration page at https://github-dev.orderly.network/broker-registration/.

commonIssues.issue: Signature verification fails on API requests.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the orderly-signature is generated by signing the request body with the correct secret key. The secret is shown only once during key creation — if lost, generate a new key pair.

commonIssues.issue: Trading bot cannot execute trades.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the bot has access to the user's stored Orderly Key. The infrastructure must control and store these keys securely for automated trading.

relatedWorkflows: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
