workflows.name: Tracking User Holdings and Volume via Builder APIs
workflows.description: Use Orderly's Builder APIs to track user deposits, collateral holdings, and trading volume on your DEX.
prerequisites: Active Orderly-powered DEX with a broker ID
Understanding of keccak256 hashing for token identification

steps.title: Fetch User List via Builder's Leaderboard API
steps.description: Get a list of users on your DEX using the Builder's Leaderboard API.

steps.title: Fetch User Deposits via Events API
steps.description: Retrieve deposit events for users using the events API. Use the 'token_hash' parameter (keccak256 hash of the token) to filter by specific tokens.

steps.title: Fetch Collateral Info
steps.description: Use the supported collateral info endpoint to get information about available collateral assets.
steps.important: Orderly uses cross margin, meaning the user's entire holdings are taken into account. There is no exact public way to get specific token holdings or track which collateral is used for specific positions.

steps.title: Get Exact Holdings via Read-Only Key
steps.description: For exact holdings, users can create a read-only Orderly key and share it with the builder to query via the get-current-holding endpoint.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot track which collateral is used for specific positions.
commonIssues.solution: This is by design due to cross margin. The user's entire holdings are considered as collateral. For exact per-token holdings, users must share a read-only Orderly key.

commonIssues.issue: WebSocket balance does not match DEX display.
commonIssues.solution: The WebSocket balance endpoint only triggers on collateral changes and does not include unrealized PnL. The DEX total value includes USDC holdings, non-USDC holdings at index price, and unsettled PnL.

commonIssues.issue: token_hash parameter not matching.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the correct keccak256 hash of the token string. Refer to the reference implementation at the orderly-dashboard repository.

relatedWorkflows: Generating Orderly API Credentials
Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration

workflows.name: Customizing Orderly SDK Theme and Branding
workflows.description: Customize the theme, colors, and design of your Orderly-based DEX using CSS variables, the Theme Builder, and the Orderly One editor.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK integrated or Orderly One DEX created
Brand colors and design assets prepared

steps.title: Use the Orderly Theme Builder
steps.description: Open the Orderly Theme Builder (Storybook) to visually select colors, fonts, and other style options, then copy the generated CSS code.

steps.title: Override CSS Variables in Your Project
steps.description: Apply custom theme by overriding CSS variables. In SDK v1, variables use the '--orderly' prefix; in SDK v2.8+, the prefix changed to '--oui'.
steps.important: To create a light theme, mainly tweak the base/foreground variables. You may need to clear localStorage for theme changes to take effect.

steps.title: Change Section Colors in Orderly One
steps.description: For Orderly One DEXs, click 'Edit Desktop' and then click directly on the different sections of the page to change their colors using the color picker.
steps.important: You do not need to go into the 'Themes' menu to change colors; the color picker is available directly from the section editing screen.

steps.title: Hide 'Powered by Orderly' Footer (Orderly One)
steps.description: Add custom CSS to hide the 'Powered by Orderly' footer text in Orderly One.

steps.title: Configure Logo Display
steps.description: To make your logo blend seamlessly into the top navigation bar, remove the logo's background (make it transparent) or set the logo background to the same color as your DEX background.
steps.important: Use a light-colored logo for best results against a dark navigation bar. Use image editing tools to remove the background before uploading.

steps.title: Change Default Trading Pair
steps.description: Modify the default trading symbol displayed on your DEX by updating the configuration in your codebase.

commonIssues.issue: Theme changes not taking effect.
commonIssues.solution: Clear localStorage for theme changes to take effect. For Orderly One, ensure you click 'Update DEX configuration' after applying CSS changes.

commonIssues.issue: Brand gradient and button colors not editable in Orderly One.
commonIssues.solution: There is a known bug where the brand gradient and button colors do not sync with the primary color setting. As a workaround, set these colors by editing the CSS directly.

commonIssues.issue: CSS variable prefix mismatch after SDK upgrade.
commonIssues.solution: In SDK v1, variables use the '--orderly' prefix; in SDK v2.8+, the prefix changed to '--oui'. Update all CSS variable references when upgrading.

commonIssues.issue: Leverage indicator color not changing.
commonIssues.solution: The leverage indicator uses the 'Primary' color setting. Ensure you are modifying the correct Primary color field. It uses just the 'Primary' color, not the gradient.

relatedWorkflows: Customizing Orderly One DEX Theme and Design

workflows.name: Configuring DNS for Custom Domain with Orderly One
workflows.description: Configure DNS settings to host your Orderly One DEX on a custom domain, including subdomain setup when the main domain is already in use.
prerequisites: Orderly One DEX created and configured
Access to your DNS provider (e.g., GoDaddy, Cloudflare)

steps.title: Choose Subdomain if Main Domain is Occupied
steps.description: If your main domain (e.g., www.yourdomain.com) is already assigned to another service via a CNAME record, you cannot assign a second CNAME with the same name. Use a subdomain for your DEX (e.g., app.yourdomain.com).
steps.important: You do not need to purchase a new domain. A subdomain works perfectly for hosting your DEX alongside other services.

steps.title: Add CNAME Record in DNS Provider
steps.description: In your DNS provider (e.g., GoDaddy), add a new CNAME record pointing your subdomain to Orderly's hosting.
steps.important: Ensure no conflicting records exist for the same subdomain name.

steps.title: Set Domain in Orderly One
steps.description: In the Orderly One dashboard, set the domain to your subdomain (e.g., app.yourdomain.com) and redeploy the DEX.
steps.important: After updating the DNS and Orderly One settings, allow time for DNS propagation (typically 15 minutes to a few hours).

commonIssues.issue: Cannot assign CNAME to main domain.
commonIssues.solution: If the main domain already has a CNAME record for another service, use a subdomain instead. You cannot have two CNAME records with the same name.

commonIssues.issue: DEX not loading on custom domain after DNS setup.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the CNAME record points to orderlynetworkcreator.github.io, ensure the domain is correctly set in Orderly One, and allow time for DNS propagation.

relatedWorkflows: Customizing Orderly One DEX Theme and Design
Migrating to Orderly One from Custom SDK

workflows.name: Adding Assets Page to Orderly SDK Template
workflows.description: Add the missing Assets page (/portfolio/assets) to your Orderly SDK template by importing and rendering the AssetsModule.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK integrated with a custom or template-based DEX

steps.title: Import AssetsModule
steps.description: Import the AssetsModule from the @orderly.network/portfolio package.
steps.code: import { AssetsModule } from '@orderly.network/portfolio';

steps.title: Render the Assets Page Component
steps.description: Create a page component that renders the AssetsPage from AssetsModule.

steps.title: Configure Meta Function for Remix (If Applicable)
steps.description: If you are using the Remix template, configure the meta function for the page title to ensure proper SEO and tab display.
steps.important: If the page is still missing after adding the component, share your source code with the Orderly team for assistance.

commonIssues.issue: Assets page still not visible after adding the component.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the route is properly registered in your routing configuration. If using Remix, verify the file is in the correct routes directory. Share your source code with the Orderly team if issues persist.

commonIssues.issue: Page title not displaying correctly in Remix.
commonIssues.solution: Configure the meta function for the Assets page route to set the proper page title.

workflows.name: Opening Positions with Take Profit and Stop Loss via API
workflows.description: Open trading positions with Take Profit (TP) and Stop Loss (SL) orders using the Orderly Create Algo Order API endpoint.

steps.title: Review Algo Order Documentation
steps.description: Review the algorithmic order documentation and examples to understand TP/SL order configurations.
steps.code:
// Algo order samples and documentation:
// https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/algo-order-samples

steps.title: Construct the Algo Order Request
steps.description: Use the Create Algo Order endpoint to submit a position with attached TP and SL parameters.
steps.important: Algorithmic orders including TP/SL configurations are handled through a dedicated endpoint, separate from standard market/limit orders.

steps.title: Verify Order Execution

steps.important: Monitor the order status through the API or WebSocket to confirm TP and SL levels are active.

commonIssues.issue: TP/SL orders not triggering at expected prices.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the TP and SL price parameters are correctly formatted and within valid ranges. Check the algo order documentation for exact parameter requirements.

commonIssues.issue: Algo order request returns authentication error.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure all required headers (orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id) are correctly set and the signature is valid for the request body.

workflows.name: Fixing Python SDK _dispatch_request Function
workflows.description: Fix the _dispatch_request function in the official Orderly Python SDK to properly handle headers and request bodies for POST/PUT and GET/DELETE requests.

steps.title: Locate the _dispatch_request Function
steps.description: Open the orderly_evm_connector/api.py file and find the _dispatch_request function.
steps.code:
// File: orderly_evm_connector/api.py
// Function: _dispatch_request

steps.title: Replace the Function Implementation
steps.description: Replace the existing _dispatch_request function with the corrected version that properly handles Content-Type headers for different HTTP methods.
steps.important: The fix ensures POST/PUT requests send JSON bodies with the correct Content-Type header, while GET/DELETE requests use form-urlencoded.

steps.title: Test API Calls
steps.description: After applying the fix, test both GET and POST API calls to verify they work correctly with the proper headers.
steps.important: Verify that POST requests now send JSON bodies and GET requests use form-urlencoded format.

commonIssues.issue: POST requests failing with 400 or 415 errors.
commonIssues.solution: This is the exact issue the fix addresses. The original function does not set the correct Content-Type header for POST/PUT requests. Apply the replacement function.

commonIssues.issue: GET requests failing after applying the fix.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the else branch correctly sets 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=utf-8' for GET and DELETE requests.

workflows.name: Understanding the Builder Tier System and Booster Distributor Program
workflows.description: Understand how the Orderly Builder Tier System categorizes builders and how the Booster Distributor Program provides direct access to the Platinum tier.
prerequisites: Understanding of staking and volume requirements

steps.title: Review Builder Tier Categories
steps.description: The Tier System categorizes builders into Public, Silver, and Gold tiers based on 30-day average trading volume or ORDER tokens staked. A builder's tier defaults to Public based on their current 30-day average trading volume.
steps.important: Benefits include marketing support, listing campaigns, and fee reductions. Builders can upgrade to higher tiers by increasing trading volume or staking ORDER tokens.

steps.title: Understand the Booster Distributor Program
steps.description: The Booster Distributor Program provides direct access to the Platinum tier. Distributors can grant other builders (including their own DEX) Platinum tier status, allowing them to create a new DEX with a new broker ID and skip staking/volume requirements.
steps.important: DEX owners are generally not turned into distributors to prevent gaming the system. Boosted Distributors are gated and only provided to verified users.

steps.title: Maintain Distributor Status
steps.description: If granted distributor status, ensure you generate enough volume and revenue within 2 months to maintain the tier.
steps.important: If distributors don't generate enough volume/revenue after 2 months, they lose the tier.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot access custom fee configurations.
commonIssues.solution: Custom trading fees below the standard tier require Diamond tier status in the Builder Staking Programme. Work on increasing volume or staking ORDER tokens to upgrade your tier.

commonIssues.issue: Distributor status revoked.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure sufficient volume and revenue are generated within the 2-month window. Contact the Orderly team if you believe the revocation was in error.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, and set up default trading fees.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions

steps.title: Provide Broker Details to Orderly Team
steps.description: Submit your desired Broker ID (unique string identifier), Broker Name, Default Taker Fee Rate, and Default Maker Fee Rate to the Orderly team. Specify whether you want to use the public tier (relying on volume to reach higher tiers) or stake ORDER tokens via the Builder Staking Programme.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base taker fee (e.g., 2.5 bps), and anything above that is retained by the broker. Higher builder tiers (Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond) unlock reduced base fees.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The admin wallet also serves as the fee wallet. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature. Admin wallet setup may require a multisig approval process on Orderly's side before fees can be collected.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees via API
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication with your admin wallet's Orderly key.
steps.important: Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates using different orderly_endpoint values. Fee changes may require some time to propagate to the UI.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection
steps.description: Platform fees are sent directly to the registered admin wallet's Orderly account (not directly to the on-chain wallet balance). Log into your DEX frontend using the admin wallet address to view accrued fees.
steps.important: You can use the broker ID immediately for development, but fee collection begins only after the admin wallet is fully configured. Fees should be available across most supported chains.

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: Fees not appearing in admin wallet balance.
commonIssues.solution: Fees are credited to the Orderly account associated with the admin wallet, not the on-chain wallet balance directly. Log into the DEX frontend with the admin wallet to check the Orderly account balance.

Access to Admin Tool or Orderly One dashboard

steps.title: Upgrade SDK
steps.description: Ensure your DEX is running SDK version 2.9.0 or later. For Orderly One DEXs, ensure you are on the latest version available on the platform.
steps.important: As of SDK v2.12.4, users can bind a referral code to their existing account at any time post-registration, rather than being required to provide a code during registration.

steps.title: Activate the Referral Program
steps.description: Enable or upgrade the referral program via the Admin Tool or through the Orderly One dashboard.
steps.code:
// Admin Portal:
https://admin.orderly.network/login

steps.title: Configure Referral Code Parameters
steps.description: When creating a referral code, configure the rebate rates. All values are expressed as absolute decimals (e.g., 0.5 means 50% of fees).
steps.important: The owner of the referral code can adjust the split between referrer and referee at any time. Referral rebates are settled in USDC regardless of the collateral asset used, and are sent to users once per day.

steps.title: Use order_tag for Per-Order Referral Tracking
steps.description: Attach a referral code at the order level using the `order_tag` field in the create order API. This overrides any account-level referral binding.
steps.code:
POST /v1/order
Body: {
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "order_type": "MARKET",

steps.title: Review Broker and Affiliate Guides
steps.description: Refer to the dedicated Quick Guide for Brokers and Quick Guide for Affiliates in the Orderly documentation for detailed setup instructions and best practices.
steps.important: The Multilevel Referral Program supports multi-tier referral structures, allowing brokers to incentivize communities at scale.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot register referral code for a KOL/affiliate.
commonIssues.solution: The KOL/affiliate must first connect their wallet and sign in to create an Orderly account. Attempting to register a ref code before the user has signed in will result in an 'address is not registered' error.

commonIssues.issue: Rebates not appearing for users.
commonIssues.solution: Rebates are settled once per day in USDC. Ensure the referral code is correctly bound to the user's account and that the rebate rates are properly configured.

commonIssues.issue: Users unable to bind referral code after registration.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your SDK is updated to v2.12.4 or later, which enables binding referral codes to existing accounts at any time post-registration.

steps.title: Sync Frontend Configuration
steps.description: When new permissionless markets are announced, update your frontend configuration to support the new symbols. Monitor Orderly announcements for new listings.
steps.important: Permissionless listings allow builders to list any asset not currently on Orderly. As the market owner, the builder earns 100% of liquidation fees plus 50% of Orderly's base fee on that market.

steps.title: Handle Chart Data for New Markets
steps.description: SDK v3.1.3 optimizes K-line history loading so the chart stops requesting unavailable historical data before a market's listing time, reducing unnecessary requests and improving page stability.
steps.important: Permissionlessly listed markets are Isolated-only to limit risk exposure.

steps.title: Notify Users of New Markets
steps.description: Inform your users about newly available permissionless markets and any specific trading rules (e.g., isolated margin only).

commonIssues.issue: Permissionless symbols show empty values in funding rate modal on mobile.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.0.3 or later, which fixes the display of Interval, Funding Cap/Floor, and Estimated Funding Fee values.

commonIssues.issue: Chart requests fail or cause instability for newly listed markets.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.3+ which optimizes K-line history loading to stop requesting unavailable historical data before a market's listing time, improving page stability.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot use Cross Margin on permissionless markets.
commonIssues.solution: This is by design. Permissionlessly listed markets only support Isolated Margin to limit risk exposure.

workflows.name: Customizing Orderly One DEX Theme and Design
workflows.description: Customize the theme, colors, and design elements of your Orderly One DEX using the built-in editor, CSS overrides, and mobile-specific configurations.

steps.title: Customize CSS Variables
steps.description: Paste CSS variables into the Theme Customization section. Use '--oui-' prefixed custom properties for colors, gradients, spacing, border radius, and font family.

steps.title: Change Specific UI Element Colors
steps.description: The leverage indicator and similar UI elements use the 'Primary' color setting. Update the Primary color in your Orderly One configuration to change them.
steps.important: The Primary color also affects the links at the top of the page, which use a gradient between 'Primary' and 'Primary Light'. The leverage indicator specifically uses just the 'Primary' color. If you removed sync from primary colors but the element still appears in the old color, ensure you are modifying the correct Primary color field.

steps.title: Configure Mobile Logo Display
steps.description: On mobile, the DEX defaults to showing the secondary logo. If the uploaded secondary logo does not include text (e.g., only shows an icon), you can change this behavior.
steps.important: To fix mobile logo display, either update the code to select the main logo for mobile display, or upload a different secondary logo that includes the desired text. This customization requires modifying the frontend code of your DEX.

steps.title: Fork Repository for Deeper Customization
steps.description: For deeper customization beyond the no-code template, fork the generated GitHub repository and modify the code directly.
steps.important: When using your own repository, you will not receive automatic SDK updates but will be notified of available updates.

steps.title: Enable QR Code Feature
steps.description: The QR code allows users to scan from their laptop to switch to mobile trading and create a Progressive Web App (PWA) on their phone.
steps.important: The QR code feature only works after a customized URL has been set for the DEX. It will not work with generic URLs.

commonIssues.issue: Brand gradient and button colors not editable in OrderlyOne.
commonIssues.solution: There is a known bug where the brand gradient and button colors do not sync with the primary color setting. As a workaround, set these colors by editing the CSS directly.

commonIssues.issue: Theme changes not taking effect.
commonIssues.solution: You may need to clear localStorage for theme changes to take effect. Also ensure you click 'Update DEX configuration' after applying CSS changes.

commonIssues.issue: Leverage indicator color not changing.
commonIssues.solution: The leverage indicator uses the 'Primary' color setting. Ensure you are modifying the correct Primary color field. It uses just the 'Primary' color, not the gradient.

commonIssues.issue: Mobile logo shows icon only without text.
commonIssues.solution: Upload a secondary logo that includes the desired text, or modify the frontend code to use the main logo for mobile display.

commonIssues.issue: QR code not appearing on the trading page.
commonIssues.solution: Set a customized URL for your DEX. The QR code feature does not work with generic/default URLs.

steps.title: Enable TradingView Chart Labels
steps.description: In SDK v2.12.0 and later, position lines on the TradingView chart (positions, TP/SL, liquidation lines) display cross/isolated margin mode labels along with leverage.
steps.important: SDK v2.12.0+ also adds a Liquidation Price Line toggle for better chart visualization.

steps.title: Handle Position Closing from Chart

steps.title: Handle Max Order Amount for Isolated Margin
steps.description: In SDK v3.1.0, maxing out an isolated margin market order with the slider at 100% no longer triggers a 'margin will be insufficient after' rejection.
steps.important: The SDK now reserves a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula, preventing false rejections.

commonIssues.issue: 'Margin will be insufficient after' error when using 100% slider on isolated margin market orders.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.0 or later, which reserves a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula.

commonIssues.issue: Reduce-only validation error when closing isolated margin positions from TradingView.

commonIssues.issue: Isolated margin mode not available in the UI.

steps.title: Implement Geo IP Detection
steps.description: Use a geo IP API to determine the user's location and map it to the appropriate language code.

steps.title: Apply Language Setting
steps.description: Set the detected language as the default for the DEX interface before rendering the trading components.
steps.important: The language toggle button can also be re-enabled in the UI for manual switching by users who prefer a different language.

commonIssues.issue: Brief flash of default language before geo-detected language loads.
commonIssues.solution: Use server-side rendering with Node.js to detect location and set the language before sending static assets to the client.

commonIssues.issue: Geo IP API returns incorrect location.
commonIssues.solution: Use a reliable geo IP service and provide a manual language toggle as a fallback for users.

workflows.name: Launching Trading Competitions and Campaigns
workflows.description: Set up and manage trading competitions, points programs, and campaigns on your Orderly-powered DEX using the Campaigns API, Perps Competition system, and Fuul integration.

steps.title: Set Up Campaign with Orderly Team
steps.description: Provide campaign details to the Orderly team: campaign name, start/end dates, and trading task details (e.g., volume-based leaderboard). You will receive a campaign_id.
steps.important: For custom response formats (e.g., Gate Wallet, Layer3), provide requirements well in advance to allow the Orderly team to configure the appropriate API.

steps.title: Query Campaign Data via API
steps.description: Use the Campaigns API to fetch user progress, rankings, and campaign-specific data.
steps.important: Campaign PnL is calculated as: PnL = Account Value (end) - Account Value (start) - total deposit value + total withdrawal value. This is a global account-level PnL and cannot be attributed to individual symbols.

steps.title: Integrate with Quest Platforms (Galxe, Layer3)
steps.description: For Galxe integrations, use a JavaScript expression to evaluate task completion from the standard API response.
steps.important: Standard campaign API response wraps data in a `data` object (e.g., {"success": true, "data": {"volume": 1000}}). Custom formats (e.g., {"status": "success"}) require dedicated development by the Orderly team.

steps.title: Configure Perps Competition (Season) Parameters
steps.description: For Perps Competitions, configure season-based parameters via the backend before the competition starts.
steps.important: Trading periods and claim periods can be adjusted as needed. All parameters are configured via the backend and can be updated before the competition starts.

steps.title: Launch via Fuul (Orderly One)
steps.description: For Orderly One DEXs, launch permissionless trading competitions and points programs directly through the Fuul integration with no coding required.
steps.important: Campaign data is archived after the campaign ends. Starting from Campaign 75, the archiving window is 6 months. Export any needed data before the deadline.

commonIssues.issue: Errors when saving or publishing a points campaign on Orderly One.
commonIssues.solution: Clear your browser's local storage to force the creation of a new Orderly key, then retry. You must connect using the EOA wallet that was originally used to create the DEX.

commonIssues.issue: Campaign data no longer accessible.
commonIssues.solution: Campaign data is archived after the campaign ends (6 months for campaigns after ID 75, 1 month for campaigns before ID 75). Export data before the archiving deadline.

commonIssues.issue: PnL calculation seems incorrect for individual symbols.
commonIssues.solution: Campaign PnL is account-level, not per-symbol. The system tracks account-level value changes rather than position-level PnL per trading pair. The /v1/public/campaign/ranking endpoint includes unrealized PnL (UPnL), while /v1/broker/leaderboard/daily reflects only realized PnL.

workflows.description: Add support for new chains like Story, Solana, or Sei to your Orderly-powered DEX using the chainFilter prop in OrderlyAppProvider.

Broker ID registered on the target chain (if applicable)

steps.description: Import the necessary chain types from @orderly.network/types for built-in chains.
steps.code: import { Arbitrum, Optimism } from "@orderly.network/types";

steps.title: Configure chainFilter Prop
steps.description: Use the chainFilter prop on OrderlyAppProvider to specify which chains to enable, including custom chains by their ID.
steps.code:
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  brokerName="Your Broker"
  networkId="mainnet"
  chainFilter={{
    mainnet: [
      Arbitrum,
      Optimism,
      { id: 90009090 }, // Solana
      { id: 1514 },     // Story
    ],
  }}
>
  {children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
steps.important: Chain IDs can be found at chainlist.org. For Solana, use ID 90009090. For Story, use ID 1514.

steps.title: Add Testnet Chains (Optional)
steps.description: To add testnet chains like Monad Testnet, use the testnet key in chainFilter with full chain configuration.
steps.important: Your broker_id must be registered on testnet as well. If testnets are not visible, ensure `showTestnet` is not set to `false` in overrides.

steps.title: Handle Network Switching
steps.description: The `networkId` cannot change during runtime. Use a page refresh or separate domain when switching between testnet and mainnet.
steps.important: For Solana support, ensure you are using SDK v2.0.0+ (Hooks SDK) and have applied the Solana Multi-DVN security upgrade (v2.12.3+).

commonIssues.issue: Chain does not appear in the chain selector.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the chain ID is correct and that the chainFilter prop is properly structured. For testnets, ensure `showTestnet` is not set to false.

commonIssues.issue: Solana deposits/withdrawals fail.

steps.description: Ensure your DEX is running SDK version 2.9.0 or later. For Orderly One DEXs, ensure you are on the latest version available on the platform.

steps.title: Configure Referral Code Parameters
steps.description: When creating a referral code, configure the rebate rates. All values are expressed as absolute decimals (e.g., 0.5 means 50% of fees).
steps.important: Referral rebates are settled in USDC regardless of the collateral asset used, and are sent to users once per day.

steps.title: Use order_tag for Per-Order Referral Tracking
steps.description: Attach a referral code at the order level using the `order_tag` field in the create order API. This overrides any account-level referral binding.
steps.code:
POST /v1/order
Body: {
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "order_type": "MARKET",
  "order_quantity": "0.01",
  "side": "BUY",
  "order_tag": "BBBB" // Overrides account-level referral code 'AAAA'
}
steps.important: If a user is bound to ref code 'AAAA' at the account level but the trade is submitted with order_tag 'BBBB', the trade will be counted towards 'BBBB'.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot register referral code for a KOL/affiliate.

steps.title: Stake $ORDER Tokens

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, set up default trading fees, and withdraw broker revenue.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved manual setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions
Defined fee structure (Orderly base taker fee is 0.03%, no maker fee)

steps.title: Request Broker ID from Orderly Team
steps.description: Provide your preferred Broker ID string, Broker Name, Default Taker Fee, Default Maker Fee, and Tier to the Orderly team. Alternatively, use Orderly One (no-code solution) which sets up a broker ID automatically for 1,000 USDC (or $750 in ORDER).
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. For example, if you set taker fee at 0.06%, you earn 0.03%. Brokers can reduce their base fee by staking ORDER tokens through the Builder Staking Program (Diamond tier reduces base to 1 bps).

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature. For testing, use an EOA your dev team can easily access.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly (takes ~1 day for multisig), log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Fees can be changed later once the admin wallet is set up. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates. Builder rebates are configurable: if maker/taker is set to 0bps/5bps with a 3bps base taker fee, the builder rebate would be 0/2bps.

steps.title: Withdraw Broker Revenue
steps.description: Log in to your DEX trading interface using the admin wallet. Accumulated broker fees appear as trading balance. Withdraw from there to your desired wallet.
steps.important: Withdrawals incur a fee (typically $1 on most chains, $10 on Ethereum). LayerZero bridging fees may also apply for cross-chain withdrawals.

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: Broker fees not appearing in account balance.
commonIssues.solution: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account. Check the balance by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet or using the private Get Current Holding endpoint (GET /v1/holding).

steps.title: Define Fee Tier Structure

steps.title: Set Up the Broker Fee Admin Script
steps.description: Use Orderly's provided script for setting broker fees based on trading volume. Clone the repository and configure it for your tier structure.

steps.title: Run Script on Schedule
steps.description: Set up a cron job or scheduled task to run the script daily (or at your preferred interval) to check each user's trading volume and update their fee rate through the Orderly API.
steps.important: The script queries user volumes and calls the Orderly API to update individual fee rates for users who qualify for different tiers.

steps.title: Alternative: Fixed Fee for All Users
steps.description: If you prefer a simple approach without volume tiers, set the default fee to your desired rate and all users will trade at that rate.

commonIssues.issue: Fee tier updates not taking effect for users.

workflows.name: Integrating Staking Functionality for ORDER Tokens via API
workflows.description: Integrate on-chain staking of ORDER tokens via the proxy contract, including LayerZero fee handling for cross-chain staking operations.

steps.title: Approve ORDER Token for Proxy Contract
steps.description: Before staking, the user must approve the proxy contract to spend their ORDER tokens.
steps.important: The approval must be completed before calling the stakeOrder function.

steps.title: Fetch LayerZero Fee
steps.description: Call the quoteStakeOrder view function on the proxy contract to get the required LayerZero bridging fee.
steps.important: The Orderly app multiplies the quoted fee by 1.1, though the exact reason is undocumented. This buffer helps prevent transaction failures due to fee fluctuations.

steps.title: Call stakeOrder Function
steps.description: Execute the staking transaction by calling stakeOrder with the ORDER amount and attaching the LayerZero fee as msg.value.
steps.important: Attach the adjusted LZ fee as the `value` parameter. Insufficient value will cause the transaction to revert.

steps.title: Handle Unstaking
steps.description: To unstake, users can press the down arrow in the staking interface to reveal the unstake button, or call the unstake function on the proxy contract.
steps.important: See tokenomics addresses for all relevant contract addresses: https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/tokenomics/addresses

commonIssues.issue: Staking transaction reverts with insufficient value.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are attaching the LayerZero fee (multiplied by 1.1) as msg.value. Call quoteStakeOrder first to get the current fee estimate.

commonIssues.issue: Approval transaction succeeds but staking fails.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the approved amount is sufficient and that the user has enough native token (ETH) to cover the LayerZero fee.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot find unstake option in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Press the down arrow in the staking interface to reveal the unstake button.

workflows.name: Creating Backend-Authenticated Trading with Orderly Keys
workflows.description: Set up backend-authenticated trading flows (e.g., for insurance fee deduction) by creating Orderly keys in the browser, storing them on your backend, and routing trades through your server.
prerequisites: Backend server capable of secure key storage

steps.title: Create Orderly Key in Browser
steps.description: Generate an Orderly key locally in the user's browser with trade and asset scope (read scope is also useful). This key pair is used for API authentication without requiring wallet signatures for every request.
steps.important: The ORDERLY_SECRET is not provided by Orderly — you must generate it yourself. It is used for generating request signatures as part of API authentication.

steps.title: Send Key to Backend for Storage
steps.description: Transmit the generated Orderly key to your backend server for secure storage. The backend will use this key to sign API requests on behalf of the user.
steps.important: Store the key securely on your backend. Never expose the secret in client-side code or logs.

steps.title: Route Trades Through Backend
steps.description: When a user initiates a trade, route the request through your backend. Your backend uses the stored Orderly key to create trades via the Orderly API.

steps.title: Deduct Fees via Internal Transfer
steps.description: After trade execution, deduct insurance or service fees by creating an internal transfer from the user's Orderly account to your broker's Orderly account.
steps.important: After internal transfer to your Orderly account, you can withdraw the accumulated fees. Withdrawing to another address may require whitelisting your smart contract address.

commonIssues.issue: API requests fail with authentication errors.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the orderly-key is correctly registered and that signatures are properly generated using the orderly-secret. Check timestamp synchronization — timestamps must be within the allowed window.

commonIssues.issue: Internal transfer fails.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the user has sufficient balance and that the transfer amount does not exceed available funds after accounting for open position margins.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal to external address fails.
commonIssues.solution: Withdrawing to another address may require whitelisting your smart contract address with the Orderly team.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, set up default trading fees, and manage fee-accruing wallet updates.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature.

steps.title: Register a Solana Admin Wallet (If Applicable)
steps.description: The broker registration page only supports EVM wallets. To register a Solana wallet as your admin wallet, run your DEX UI locally, set it to mainnet, configure your correct broker ID, and connect your Solana wallet to sign the registration message.
steps.important: After signing locally, share the Solana wallet address with the Orderly team to complete the admin setup manually.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection and Withdraw Fees
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account (held on Orderly L2, not on the settlement chain). Check the balance using the Get Current Holding endpoint or by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet.
steps.important: Fees are held on Orderly L2. To withdraw, use the withdrawal flow with EIP-712 signing or log in to your DEX UI with the admin wallet to initiate withdrawals to any supported chain.

steps.title: Update Fee-Accruing Admin Wallet (If Needed)
steps.description: To change the fee-accruing admin wallet after initial setup, register an Orderly account with the new wallet address and contact the Orderly team.
steps.important: The update cannot be done through the DEX UI. Both testnet and mainnet admin wallets should be registered for completeness.

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: 'Quorum not met' error during graduation fee verification.
commonIssues.solution: If the error persists and the manual verification field is not clickable, provide your wallet address and desired broker ID to Orderly support for manual processing.

workflows.name: Generating and Managing Orderly API Credentials
workflows.description: Generate Orderly API keys and secrets for authentication, manage key expiration, create read-only monitoring keys, and derive public keys from private keys.

steps.title: Generate Orderly Key via Wallet Authentication
steps.description: The Orderly key (public) and secret (private) are generated through wallet authentication. After generation, keys are stored in browser local storage.
steps.important: You only need a registered account to generate a key. The key and secret are stored in local storage after generation.

steps.title: Set Custom Key Expiration
steps.description: By default, Orderly keys expire after 30 days. Set a custom expiration period during key creation to avoid frequent key rotation.
steps.important: If no expiry date is explicitly set, the key expires after 30 days by default.

steps.title: Create Read-Only Monitoring Key
steps.description: Create a separate, independent Orderly API key with read-only scope for monitoring services to avoid affecting trading API rate limits.
steps.important: Rate limiting is enforced per account, but monitoring rate limits do not affect trading API keys since trading endpoints have additional, separate rate limit configurations.

steps.title: Retrieve API Key from Browser Local Storage
steps.description: The Orderly API key and secret are stored in browser local storage after connecting the wallet. Look for a key like 'orderly_mainnet_[number]' containing accountId and orderlyKey.
steps.important: The public key (API key) must be derived from the private key stored in local storage.

steps.title: Derive Public Key from Private Key Manually
steps.description: The Orderly public key can be derived from the 64-byte private key by taking the last 32 bytes and Base58 encoding them.
steps.important: The private key is 64 bytes. Only the last 32 bytes are used for the public key derivation.

steps.title: Generate Keys with Solana Admin Wallet
steps.description: Use the DefaultSolanaWalletAdapter from the Orderly SDK for Solana admin key generation and signing.
steps.important: Orderly does not yet have dedicated Solana examples for admin key generation, but the DefaultSolanaWalletAdapter includes signing functionality.

commonIssues.issue: API key expires unexpectedly.
commonIssues.solution: Set a custom expiration period during key creation. Default expiration is 30 days. Expired keys must be replaced by generating new ones.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot find API key in local storage.
commonIssues.solution: Look for a key like 'orderly_mainnet_[number]'. Ensure the wallet was properly connected and the account was registered before key generation.

commonIssues.issue: Monitoring service hits rate limits that affect trading.
commonIssues.solution: Create a separate read-only API key for monitoring. Trading and monitoring rate limits are configured independently.

relatedWorkflows: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration

workflows.name: Handling Account Abstraction Wallets with Delegate Signer
workflows.description: Implement the Delegate Signer feature to support Account Abstraction (smart contract) wallets and fix EIP-712 signature verification errors when using delegate withdrawals.
prerequisites: AA wallet or delegate signer wallet setup

steps.title: Understand the AA Wallet Limitation
steps.description: Orderly Network requires EIP-712 signatures, which smart contract wallets (AA wallets) cannot natively sign. Implement the Delegate Signer feature to allow a designated EOA to sign on behalf of the AA wallet.
steps.code:
// Delegate Signer documentation:
// https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-evm/user-flows/delegate-signer
steps.important: Alternatively, AA wallets can manage user liquidity between chains while an EOA handles Orderly-specific signing.

steps.title: Configure EIP-712 Typed Data for Delegate Withdrawals
steps.description: When constructing the EIP-712 typed data for delegate withdrawals, ensure the delegateContract field type is set to 'address'.
steps.important: Using the wrong type for delegateContract is a common cause of signature verification failures.

steps.title: Sign with the Correct Key
steps.description: The EIP-712 signature must be produced by the delegated signer's wallet private key, not the Orderly secret key.
steps.important: The Orderly secret key is only used for the 'orderly-signature' header authentication, not for EIP-712 delegate signing.

commonIssues.issue: EIP-712 signature verification error on delegate withdrawal.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the delegateContract field type is 'address' (not 'string') and that the signature is produced by the delegated signer's wallet private key, not the Orderly secret key.

commonIssues.issue: AA wallet cannot sign Orderly transactions.
commonIssues.solution: Implement the Delegate Signer feature to designate an EOA to sign on behalf of the AA wallet. Reference: https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/delegate-signer

workflows.name: Customizing SDK Trading Interface Theme and Charts
workflows.description: Customize the Orderly SDK trading interface including light/dark themes, CSS variables, TradingView chart colors, PnL card sharing, and component-level styling.

steps.title: Override CSS Variables for Theming
steps.description: The Orderly SDK uses CSS variables prefixed with '--oui-' for theming. Override these variables in your CSS to create custom themes.
steps.important: Be cautious with overrides like '.oui-text-transparent { color: inherit !important; }' as they can cause text visibility issues in certain themes.

steps.title: Customize TradingView Chart Colors
steps.description: Use the tradingViewConfig object with overrides and studies_overrides to customize chart candle colors, volume colors, and background.
steps.important: Some studies_overrides (like volume colors) may only work in paid TradingView versions. SDK v1.3.2+ includes fixes for TradingView override configuration support.

steps.title: Configure PnL Card Sharing
steps.description: Configure PnL card sharing via the shareOptions prop on OrderlyAppProvider with custom colors, background images, and layout.
steps.code:
<OrderlyAppProvider
  shareOptions={{
    pnl: {
      profitColor: 'green',
      lossColor: 'red',
      backgroundImages: [
        '/images/poster_bg_1.png',
        '/images/poster_bg_2.png',
      ],
      layout: {
        message: {
          width: 100,
          height: 25,
          fontSize: 16,
          position: { left: 300, top: 150 }
        }
      }
    }
  }}
>
  {children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>

// For per-position poster data, use the usePoster hook
// with position data from usePositionStream
steps.important: Use profitColor and lossColor (not fontColor or color) to set PnL text colors. Referral codes are displayed on PnL cards by default if a referral code belongs to the account.

steps.title: Add Custom Component IDs for CSS Targeting
steps.description: SDK v1.3.2+ adds component IDs to the orderbook and trades modules, enabling brokers to customize these modules via CSS.
steps.important: Upgrade to SDK v1.3.2 or later to access component IDs for the orderbook and trades modules.

commonIssues.issue: Chart color changes only appear on desktop but not mobile.
commonIssues.solution: Clear localStorage as the SDK may cache chart settings. A known SDK bug affecting mobile chart color configuration was addressed in subsequent SDK updates.

commonIssues.issue: TradingView overrides not applying.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using SDK v1.3.2+ which includes fixes for TradingView override configuration. Clear browser cache when testing, as local cache can override default settings.

commonIssues.issue: Text visibility issues after theme customization.
commonIssues.solution: Avoid overly broad CSS overrides like '.oui-text-transparent { color: inherit !important; }'. Test your theme in both light and dark modes.

commonIssues.issue: colorConfig property doesn't change candlestick colors.
commonIssues.solution: The colorConfig property (downColor, upColor, etc.) applies to on-chart trading elements only. Use TradingView chart overrides for actual K-line/candlestick colors.

workflows.name: Monitoring Account Health and Trading Data via API
workflows.description: Retrieve real-time account health information, trading volumes, referral history, funding fees, and broker statistics using Orderly's WebSocket and REST APIs.

steps.title: Subscribe to Real-Time Account Health via WebSocket
steps.description: Subscribe to three WebSocket topics for comprehensive real-time account health data.
steps.important: Documentation: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/evm-api/websocket-api/private/account, /balance, /position-push

steps.title: Retrieve User Trading Volume Statistics
steps.description: Use the private API endpoint to get user-level trading volume data including 7-day, 30-day, life-to-date, and year-to-date volumes.
steps.important: 'ltd' means 'life to date', not 'last trading day'.

steps.title: Retrieve Broker Volume and Statistics
steps.description: Use public and private endpoints to get broker-level trading volume, TVL, and user data.
steps.important: Orderly does not provide a direct API for number of trades (one order can result in multiple trades). Use the Dune dashboard filtered by broker_id for transaction counts.

steps.title: Retrieve Referral and Funding Fee History
steps.description: Use dedicated private endpoints to get referral history with earnings data and funding fee history.
steps.important: Funding fee data may also be visible on the Portfolio page in the Orderly SDK UI.

steps.title: Track Partner Volume with Order Tags
steps.description: Track orders from specific partners by using the order_tag parameter when placing orders, then query volume filtered by tag.
steps.important: Assign a unique referral code as the order_tag value for all orders from a specific partner.

steps.title: Fetch Vault APY Programmatically
steps.description: Retrieve APY values for Orderly vaults via the public API endpoint.
steps.important: This is a public endpoint and does not require authentication.

commonIssues.issue: WebSocket connection drops frequently.
commonIssues.solution: Implement reconnection logic with exponential backoff. Ensure your WebSocket client handles reconnection gracefully.

commonIssues.issue: Volume data seems inconsistent.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the correct endpoint for your use case. Broker-level volume (/v1/client/volume) requires authentication and aggregates across all users. Public broker volume (/v1/public/broker-volume) is accessible without auth.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot get per-broker Open Interest data.
commonIssues.solution: Open Interest is only available system-wide (not per-broker) via the public API. Use /v1/public/get-open-interests-for-all-symbols.

workflows.name: Troubleshooting Withdrawal and Order Placement Errors
workflows.description: Resolve common API errors when withdrawing funds and placing orders, including amount errors, price filter violations, and PnL settlement requirements.
prerequisites: Understanding of Orderly trading and withdrawal flows

steps.title: Fix 'Amount Error' (Code 5) on Withdrawals
steps.description: The 'Amount error' occurs when the withdrawal amount is less than the withdrawal fee. Ensure the amount exceeds the fee and is specified with correct decimal precision.
steps.important: The withdrawal fee is dynamic and varies by chain. Always check the /v1/public/token endpoint for current fees.

steps.title: Settle Unsettled PnL Before Withdrawing
steps.description: All PnL must be settled before withdrawing. Unsettled PnL inflates total_collateral_value but is not reflected in the withdrawable holding balance.
steps.important: Use the PnL settlement endpoint if withdrawal fails due to unsettled PnL.

steps.title: Fix 'Price Filter Requirement' Error (Code -1104)
steps.description: This error occurs when order price or quantity does not conform to the symbol's tick size or lot size filters.
steps.important: Check the symbol's trading rules from the available symbols endpoint for exact precision requirements.

steps.title: Understand Withdrawal Processing Times
steps.description: Withdrawal processing time depends on the destination chain, typically ranging from a few minutes to around 30 minutes.
steps.important: A withdrawal fee is charged (deducted from the withdrawal amount) to cover cross-chain messaging costs. The fee varies by chain.

steps.title: Retrieve Available Trading Symbols
steps.description: Use the public REST API to get all supported trading pairs and their precision requirements.
steps.important: Use this endpoint to verify precision requirements before placing orders to avoid filter errors.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal fails with 'Amount error' (code 5).
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the withdrawal amount exceeds the dynamic withdrawal fee and is specified with 6 decimal places. Settle all PnL before withdrawing.

commonIssues.issue: Order rejected with 'price filter requirement' error (code -1104).
commonIssues.solution: Verify that order_price follows quote_tick increments and order_quantity respects base_tick decimal precision. Use order_quantity (not order_amount) for futures/perpetual orders.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal takes longer than expected.
commonIssues.solution: Processing time varies by chain (few minutes to ~30 minutes). During high network congestion, withdrawals may take longer. Check the destination chain's status.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal to specific chain fails with error code 28.
commonIssues.solution: That chain may not be enabled for your broker. Some chains have exclusivity arrangements. Contact Orderly support to enable additional chains.

workflows.name: Configuring SEO and Brand Metadata for Orderly One DEX
workflows.description: Customize SEO metadata, Open Graph tags, and social media link previews for your Orderly One-based perpetual DEX so that your brand appears instead of 'Orderly Network'.
prerequisites: Hosting on a platform like Vercel (recommended)

steps.title: Move Configuration to Build-Time Environment Variables
steps.description: The default Orderly One setup loads config dynamically from /public/config.js at runtime, causing social media crawlers to capture the default 'Orderly Network' name. Move configuration to .env build-time variables.
steps.code:
# .env file
VITE_APP_NAME=YourBrand
VITE_APP_DESCRIPTION="Your description"
VITE_SEO_SITE_NAME="YourBrand Perps"
VITE_SEO_SITE_DESCRIPTION="Your description"
VITE_SEO_SITE_URL=https://yourdomain.com
VITE_SEO_SITE_LANGUAGE=en
VITE_SEO_SITE_LOCALE=en_US
VITE_SEO_THEME_COLOR=#000000
VITE_SEO_KEYWORDS="dex, perps, crypto"
steps.important: Social media crawlers do not execute JavaScript, so runtime-loaded config will not be captured. Build-time variables ensure crawlers see your brand.

steps.title: Configure Additional Build-Time Variables
steps.description: Set other useful build-time variables for broker configuration and UI customization.
steps.code:
# Additional .env variables
VITE_ORDERLY_BROKER_ID=your_broker_id
VITE_ORDERLY_BROKER_NAME="Your Brand"
VITE_DEFAULT_CHAIN=1
VITE_ORDERLY_MAINNET_CHAINS=1,42161,10
VITE_PRIVY_APP_ID=your_privy_id
VITE_ENABLED_MENUS=trade,vaults
VITE_TRADING_VIEW_COLOR_CONFIG={...}
steps.important: These variables are embedded at build time and will be available to crawlers and in the initial HTML response.

steps.title: Deploy and Verify
steps.description: Deploy your DEX with the new environment variables and verify that social media link previews show your brand.
steps.important: A native Open Graph feature that works without moving config to .env is on the Orderly team's backlog but has no confirmed release timeline.

commonIssues.issue: Social media previews still show 'Orderly Network'.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure configuration is set as build-time environment variables (.env), not runtime config (/public/config.js). Crawlers do not execute JavaScript.

commonIssues.issue: Environment variables not being picked up after deployment.
commonIssues.solution: Rebuild the application after changing .env variables. Vite embeds VITE_* variables at build time, so a new build is required for changes to take effect.

workflows.description: Understand the Builder Staking Program tiers, their requirements, and how they affect base taker fees for your Orderly-powered DEX.

steps.title: Review Tier Requirements
steps.description: The Builder Staking Program categorizes builders into tiers based on 30-day trading volume or ORDER tokens staked.
steps.important: Builders can qualify through EITHER trading volume OR ORDER token staking — whichever threshold is met first.

steps.title: Upgrade Tier via Volume or Staking
steps.description: Increase your 30-day trading volume or stake more ORDER tokens to upgrade to a higher tier and reduce base taker fees.
steps.important: Higher tiers provide reduced base taker fees, meaning the broker retains a larger share of the trading fees collected.

steps.title: Leverage Tier Benefits
steps.description: Silver and Gold tier builders receive additional benefits including marketing support and listing campaigns beyond fee reductions.
steps.important: Contact the Orderly team to learn about specific marketing and listing campaign benefits available at your tier level.

commonIssues.issue: Unsure which tier my DEX qualifies for.
commonIssues.solution: Check your 30-day trading volume and ORDER staking amount against the tier thresholds. Contact the Orderly team for tier verification.

commonIssues.issue: Want to reduce fees but don't have enough volume.
commonIssues.solution: Consider staking ORDER tokens as an alternative path to tier upgrades. 2M ORDER for Platinum or 7M ORDER for Diamond.

workflows.name: Managing Order Execution and Position Lifecycle
workflows.description: Create, manage, and close positions using the Orderly SDK hooks and REST API, including market/limit orders, TP/SL orders, and position margin calculations.
prerequisites: User wallet connected and Orderly account registered
Basic understanding of perpetual futures trading

steps.title: Create Orders Using useOrderEntry Hook
steps.description: Use the useOrderEntry hook to manage order state reactively. Bind input changes to setValue() and submit via onSubmit().
steps.important: Do not maintain separate order state with useState — use the hook's setValue exclusively. The formattedOrder object represents the current order state and is what gets validated and submitted.

steps.title: Close a Long Position
steps.description: To close a long position, send a SELL order with reduce_only: true. For a market close, omit order_price and set order_type to MARKET.
steps.important: Position quantity is positive for long and negative for short positions. Always use reduce_only: true when closing to avoid accidentally opening a new position.

steps.title: Create TP/SL Orders
steps.description: TP/SL orders are stop orders with reduce_only enabled. Submit two separate orders for TP and SL. Use the useTPSLOrder hook for TP/SL-specific operations.
steps.important: When creating TP/SL for an entire position, quantity may show as 0, which represents the full position. Offset percentage inputs use decimal format (0.1 = 10%).

steps.title: Calculate Position Margin and Liquidation Price
steps.description: Position margin is calculated as: margin = Math.abs(positionSize) * markPrice * mmr. Use useOrderEntry for real-time estimated liquidation price before entering a position.
steps.important: Use the absolute value of position size since it can be positive (long) or negative (short). MMR details: https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/perpetual-futures/formulas-definitions#maintenance-margin-ratio

steps.title: Subscribe to Order Execution Events
steps.description: Subscribe to the executionreport WebSocket topic to track fills, cancellations, and rejections in real time.
steps.important: The useOrderStream and usePositionStream hooks also auto-update when orders are filled or positions change, though there may be a slight delay in WebSocket push updates.

commonIssues.issue: useOrderEntry validation fails unexpectedly.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using setValue() exclusively to update order state rather than maintaining separate useState variables. The helper.validate() function validates the in-memory formattedOrder state.

commonIssues.issue: TP/SL orders not cancelling properly.
commonIssues.solution: Use cancelAlgoOrder() instead of cancelOrder() for TP/SL and algorithmic orders. The standard cancelOrder function does not work for algo orders.

commonIssues.issue: Filled orders show unexpected entry price.
commonIssues.solution: For filled orders, use the average_executed_price field (not the price field). The price field is only populated for limit orders and represents the limit price set by the user.

workflows.name: Managing Account Collateral, Leverage, and PnL Settlement
workflows.description: Monitor account health metrics including collateral, leverage, margin ratio, and PnL, and programmatically settle PnL before withdrawals.
prerequisites: User wallet connected and Orderly account registered

steps.title: Get Account Collateral and Value
steps.description: Use the useCollateral hook to retrieve total collateral, free collateral, total account value, available balance, and unsettled PnL.
steps.important: Definitions available at: https://orderly.network/docs/trade-on-orderly/perpetual-futures/formulas-definitions

steps.title: Get and Adjust Account Leverage
steps.description: Use useMarginRatio() for current leverage and margin ratio, and useLeverage() to get and update maximum account leverage.
steps.important: Leverage is account-wide, not per-trade. Changing leverage affects all positions.

steps.title: Calculate Unrealized PnL
steps.description: Use the formula pnl = qty * (markPrice - openPrice) or the SDK helper function to calculate unrealized PnL for a position.
steps.important: For unrealized ROI percentage, use totalUnrealizedROI from the account data and multiply by 100.

steps.title: Settle PnL Programmatically
steps.description: Call account.settle() to settle unrealized PnL into withdrawable balance. This must be done explicitly — it is not automatic.
steps.important: Settling only changes withdrawable balance if PnL is positive. Only call settle when unsettledPnL !== 0. Settling applies to the entire account's PnL, not individual positions.

steps.title: Settle PnL via REST API
steps.description: To settle PnL via the REST API, first obtain the settle PnL nonce, then call the Request PnL Settlement endpoint.
steps.important: Users cannot withdraw the full amount of their profits unless PnL is settled first.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal fails with insufficient balance despite visible profits.
commonIssues.solution: Call account.settle() before attempting withdrawal. Unrealized PnL must be explicitly settled to become withdrawable.

commonIssues.issue: Leverage update does not take effect.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the update function from useLeverage() hook and waiting for the mutation to complete. Leverage is account-wide and affects all positions.

commonIssues.issue: Unsettled PnL shows as 0 but account value seems incorrect.
commonIssues.solution: Check useCollateral() for all balance components. If unsettledPnL is 0, all PnL has already been settled. Verify totalValue and availableBalance separately.

workflows.name: Integrating Custom Wallet Providers with Orderly SDK v2
workflows.description: Connect custom wallet providers such as Privy, Reown/AppKit, or Wagmi to the Orderly SDK v2 using the WalletConnectorContext and wallet adapter pattern.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.2.0+ installed (v2.11.2+ recommended for Privy Solana fixes)
Wallet provider SDK installed (e.g., Privy, Wagmi, Reown)
React application with OrderlyAppProvider or OrderlyConfigProvider

steps.title: Set Up Orderly Provider with Wallet Adapter
steps.description: For SDK v2, use OrderlyConfigProvider (hooks-only) or OrderlyAppProvider (with UI components). Pass the wallet adapter via the walletAdapters prop.
steps.important: The main change from v1 to v2 is the walletAdapters prop on the config provider. Migration guide: https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/migrate

steps.title: Integrate Privy as Wallet Provider
steps.description: For Privy integration (SDK v2.2+), implement a custom PrivyProvider by replacing the default EthersProvider in the OrderlyProvider wrapper.
steps.important: SDK v2.8.13 fixed network switching issues with Privy login. SDK v2.11.2 fixed a bug causing duplicate Solana addresses via Privy.

steps.title: Implement Custom Wallet Connector Context
steps.description: For fully custom wallet integrations, provide a WalletConnectorContext.Provider that wraps the Orderly provider.
steps.important: The wallet connector context allows you to bridge any wallet SDK (Reown/AppKit, Wagmi, etc.) to Orderly's internal wallet interface.

steps.title: Configure Network and Chain Switching
steps.description: Set the networkId to 'mainnet' or 'testnet' on the provider. Use account.switchChainId() to switch the active chain for data hooks at runtime.
steps.important: Trading data like orders and positions are not chain-specific — they are aggregated across all chains. The networkId cannot change during runtime; use a page refresh when switching between testnet and mainnet.

commonIssues.issue: ethers v6 TypeScript build error with Next.js: 'Type Buffer<ArrayBufferLike> is not assignable to type Buffer<ArrayBuffer>'.
commonIssues.solution: Update @types/node and add webpack fallback configuration to next.config.ts: config.resolve.fallback = { ...config.resolve.fallback, fs: false, net: false, tls: false }. Additionally, ethers v6 ships raw TypeScript source files that may break webpack — a postinstall script to delete them may be needed.

commonIssues.issue: Privy login causes network switching failures.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v2.8.13 or later, which fixed network switching issues with Privy login.

commonIssues.issue: Duplicate Solana addresses appearing with Privy.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v2.11.2 or later, which fixed a bug causing duplicate Solana addresses via Privy.

workflows.name: Authenticating and Subscribing to Orderly WebSocket and REST APIs
workflows.description: Generate valid Ed25519 signatures for REST API authentication, connect to private WebSocket streams, and subscribe to real-time data topics including execution reports, wallet events, and market data.
prerequisites: Orderly API key and secret (Ed25519 keypair)
Understanding of WebSocket and REST API authentication patterns

steps.title: Generate REST API Signature in Python
steps.description: Construct the signing message as {timestamp}{method}{path}{query}{json_body} and sign using Ed25519 with your private key.
steps.code:
# Construct message string:
# {timestamp}{method}{path}{query}{json_body}
# - timestamp: milliseconds since epoch
# - method: uppercase HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.)
# - path: endpoint path (e.g., /v1/order)
# - query: includes '?' prefix if present
# - json_body: compact JSON string (no spaces, sorted keys)

# Sign with Ed25519 and base64url-encode the result

# Required headers:
# orderly-timestamp: <timestamp_ms>
# orderly-account-id: <account_id>
# orderly-key: ed25519:<api_key>
# orderly-signature: <base64url_signature>
steps.important: When sending POST/PUT requests, ensure the exact same JSON string used for signing is sent as the request body. Any difference will cause signature verification to fail.

steps.title: Authenticate with Private WebSocket
steps.description: Connect to the private WebSocket endpoint and authenticate using an Ed25519 signature of the current timestamp.
steps.important: Generate a fresh Ed25519 signature of the current timestamp (milliseconds) for each WebSocket authentication attempt.

steps.title: Subscribe to Execution Report Topic
steps.description: After authentication, subscribe to the executionreport topic to receive real-time order fills, cancellations, and rejections.
steps.important: Broker admins can also receive execution reports for specific accounts via wss://ws-broker.orderly.org/ws/stream/{account_id}.

steps.title: Subscribe to Wallet Events
steps.description: Subscribe to the wallet topic to receive real-time deposit and withdrawal event notifications.
steps.important: Wallet events include both deposits and withdrawals. Use this to update UI in real time when funds move.

steps.title: Retrieve Trade Data Beyond REST API Limits
steps.description: The /v1/public/market_trades REST endpoint has a limit of 500 transactions per request. Use WebSocket for real-time trades or kline endpoints for aggregated volume.
steps.code:
# REST endpoint (500 tx limit):
GET https://api-evm.orderly.org/v1/public/market_trades

# For aggregated volume over time buckets (24h, 7d):
# Use kline endpoints
# Note: kline data does not include buy/sell direction

# For real-time trades beyond 500 limit:
# Subscribe to market trades WebSocket topic
steps.important: For aggregated volume calculations over time buckets, kline endpoints are recommended, though they do not include buy/sell (long/short) direction information.

commonIssues.issue: REST API returns 401 Unauthorized despite correct API key.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the JSON body used for signing is exactly the same as the request body (compact, no spaces, sorted keys). Verify timestamp is within acceptable range and headers are correctly formatted.

commonIssues.issue: WebSocket connection drops frequently.
commonIssues.solution: Set ping_interval=10 and ping_timeout=5 to maintain the connection. Implement reconnection logic with exponential backoff.

commonIssues.issue: Market trades endpoint returns fewer results than expected.
commonIssues.solution: The /v1/public/market_trades endpoint has a hard limit of 500 transactions per request. Subscribe to the WebSocket market trades topic for real-time data beyond this limit.

Managing Order Execution and Position Lifecycle

workflows.name: Retrieving User Trading Statistics, History, and Rewards Data
workflows.description: Query user trading volumes, deposit/withdrawal history, portfolio performance, points/rewards data, and broker-level analytics using Orderly REST API endpoints and SDK hooks.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.0.0+ or direct REST API access
Authenticated user session or API credentials

steps.title: Get User Trading Volume and Statistics
steps.description: Use REST API endpoints to retrieve daily volume, user volume statistics, and overall user statistics.
steps.important: For account UID, use the useAccountInstance hook and access account#keyStore.

steps.title: Retrieve Deposit and Withdrawal History
steps.description: Use the usePrivateQuery hook with the asset history endpoint to get deposit and withdrawal records.
steps.important: Withdrawal transaction hashes may take time to appear in the response due to block confirmation requirements (e.g., ~500 blocks on Polygon).

steps.title: Get User Points and Trading Rewards
steps.description: Use the public points endpoint for historical Merits data, or the current epoch estimate endpoint for active Trading Rewards.
steps.important: The Merits campaign has ended and been replaced by Trading Rewards. Use the current epoch estimate endpoint for active reward data.

steps.title: Construct Portfolio Performance Chart
steps.description: Use the get-user-daily-statistics endpoint to retrieve historical PnL data including both realized and unrealized PnL for charting.
steps.important: This endpoint provides daily snapshots suitable for constructing time-series performance charts.

steps.title: Get Broker-Level Analytics
steps.description: Retrieve broker volume, user lists, and fund flow data using broker-specific endpoints and Dune dashboards.
steps.important: The get-brokers-users-volumes endpoint provides a breakdown of all traders' volumes associated with your broker ID.

steps.title: Display Deposit Status in UI
steps.description: Use the useDepositStatusScript hook to show pending deposit counts, estimated completion times, and trading availability.
steps.important: There may be a delay before pending deposits appear in the API response due to cross-chain confirmation times (e.g., ~500 blocks on Polygon).

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal transaction hash not appearing in history.
commonIssues.solution: Wait for sufficient block confirmations (e.g., ~500 blocks on Polygon). The hash will appear once the transaction is confirmed on-chain.

commonIssues.issue: Deposit status not updating in real time.
commonIssues.solution: The DepositStatusWidget may not update in real-time without a page refresh. Use useDepositStatusScript hook for more reactive updates, or subscribe to the wallet WebSocket topic.

commonIssues.issue: Points endpoint returns empty data.
commonIssues.solution: The Merits campaign has ended. Use the current epoch estimate endpoint for active Trading Rewards data instead.
