workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, set up default trading fees, and manage staking tiers for fee reductions.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions
ORDER tokens (optional, for staking tier upgrades)

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig wallets (e.g., Safe) are supported via the delegate signer feature. Many brokers use a multisig on mainnet for security.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0% maker / 0.025% (2.5 bps) taker fee for crypto markets and 0% maker / 0.045% (4.5 bps) taker for RWA markets. Anything above the base fee is 100% retained by the broker. The median broker taker fee is around 0.06%. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates.

steps.title: Upgrade Builder Tier via Staking (Optional)
steps.description: Stake ORDER tokens to achieve higher builder tiers and reduce the base taker fee. The staking wallet can be different from the admin wallet.
steps.important: If the staking address differs from the admin wallet, contact Orderly support to manually link them. Tier status and fee configuration can be verified by the Orderly team on their backend.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account balance (not sent directly to the wallet address). You must create an Orderly key for the wallet to view and access the accumulated fees.
steps.code:
GET /v1/holding
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Register a new preferred admin wallet (including multisig support) via the broker registration tool at https://github-dev.orderly.network/broker-registration/, then provide the new address to the Orderly team to complete the update.

commonIssues.issue: Staking tier not reflecting in fee calculations.
commonIssues.solution: If the staking wallet differs from the admin wallet, contact Orderly support to manually link them. The team can verify tier status on their backend.

workflows.name: Registering a New Broker on Orderly
workflows.description: End-to-end process for registering a new broker on Orderly, including providing broker details, setting up the admin wallet, and linking to Orderly One if applicable.
prerequisites: Defined broker ID, broker name, and fee structure
Contact with Orderly team for confirmation

steps.title: Provide Broker Details to Orderly
steps.description: Submit the following details to the Orderly team for confirmation and profile configuration.
steps.important: The entire registration process typically takes 2–3 days.

steps.title: Wait for Orderly to Configure Broker Profile
steps.description: After confirmation, Orderly configures the broker profile on their backend. You will be notified when setup is complete.
steps.important: Admin access will be available at https://admin.orderly.network/login once configured.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register your admin wallet using the broker registration app with your broker ID on both mainnet and testnet.
steps.important: You can use different wallets for mainnet and testnet. A multisig like Safe is common for mainnet. After registration, share the address with the Orderly team to complete setup.

steps.title: Register Orderly Account Linked to Broker
steps.description: Create an Orderly account linked to your broker ID by connecting your admin wallet and signing the EIP-712 key registration message.
steps.important: The admin wallet is responsible for collecting fees and has exclusive access to APIs such as referral codes and fee rebates.

steps.title: Link Broker ID to Orderly One (If Applicable)
steps.description: If your DEX was created using the Orderly One no-code solution, provide the broker ID and DEX URL to Orderly support for manual linkage.
steps.important: This step is only needed if using Orderly One. Custom SDK integrations are automatically linked via the brokerId prop.

commonIssues.issue: Broker ID already exists.
commonIssues.solution: Broker IDs must be unique. Choose a different identifier or contact Orderly support if you believe there's a conflict.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet not recognized after registration.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you shared the registered wallet address with the Orderly team and they have enabled it on the backend. Registration on the portal alone is not sufficient.

commonIssues.issue: Orderly One DEX not reflecting broker fees.
commonIssues.solution: The Orderly team must manually link the broker ID to the Orderly One DEX. Contact support with your broker ID and DEX URL.

workflows.description: Set up a testnet broker ID and environment for testing your Orderly integration before deploying to mainnet.
prerequisites: Mainnet broker ID (or request both simultaneously)
EVM wallet for testnet admin functions

steps.title: Request Testnet Broker ID
steps.description: Contact the Orderly team to request a testnet broker ID. Provide your broker ID, broker name, and desired fee rates.
steps.important: Testnet and mainnet are separate environments with identical design but different trading/engine data. No separate database setup is needed—just link to the Orderly backend.

steps.title: Register Testnet Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register an admin wallet for the testnet environment using the broker registration tool.
steps.important: You can use a different wallet for testnet than mainnet.

steps.title: Access Testnet Admin Portal
steps.description: Log in to the testnet admin portal to manage your testnet broker configuration.
steps.code:
// Testnet admin portal:
https://testnet-admin.orderly.network/

steps.title: Obtain Testnet Tokens
steps.description: Use the Orderly faucet or request testnet USDC/ETH tokens from the Orderly team for testing deposits and trading.
steps.important: Testnet tokens are available on networks like Arbitrum Sepolia. Contact the Orderly team if the faucet doesn't have sufficient funds.

commonIssues.issue: Testnet broker ID not found in dropdown.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the Orderly team has configured your testnet broker profile before attempting registration.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot get testnet tokens from faucet.
commonIssues.solution: Contact the Orderly team directly to request testnet USDC/ETH tokens on your preferred testnet (e.g., Arbitrum Sepolia).

workflows.name: Choosing an SDK Integration Path
workflows.description: Evaluate and select the appropriate Orderly SDK integration option based on your customization needs, development resources, and time-to-market requirements.
prerequisites: Defined DEX requirements and customization needs
Development team with React or general JavaScript experience
Broker ID (or plan to obtain one)

steps.title: Evaluate Integration Options
steps.description: Review the five available integration paths and their trade-offs between speed and customizability.
steps.important: The integration process is the same for all supported chains. You can start with one chain and add others (e.g., Solana) later in a couple of hours.

steps.title: Select Based on Customization Needs
steps.description: Choose the option that best fits your requirements.
steps.important: Components SDK: Least customizable but fastest to market. Hooks SDK: Full frontend control with React. Core SDK: Use any UI framework (Vue, Svelte, etc.). No SDK: Maximum control but most development effort.

steps.title: Clone Example Repository
steps.description: Start from an example repository to accelerate development.

steps.title: Configure Broker ID and Network
steps.description: Set your broker ID and network in the OrderlyAppProvider component.
steps.code:
import { OrderlyAppProvider } from "@orderly.network/react";

<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  brokerName="Your Broker"
  networkId="mainnet"
>
  {children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>

commonIssues.issue: Unsure which SDK to choose.
commonIssues.solution: Start with the Components SDK for fastest time-to-market. If you need custom UI elements (e.g., a delta-neutral strategy button), use the Hooks SDK with the example-dex repo as a starting point.

commonIssues.issue: Core SDK documentation is incomplete.
commonIssues.solution: The Core SDK is a minimal wrapper for the API and EIP-712 signing. Refer to the REST API docs for endpoint details and use the Core SDK source code as reference.

commonIssues.issue: Need to extend Components SDK beyond theming.
commonIssues.solution: The main trading page source is available at https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/js-sdk/blob/main/packages/trading/src/pages/trading/trading.page.tsx. Import standalone components individually, or switch to the Hooks SDK for full customization.

workflows.name: Listing Permissionless Perpetual Markets
workflows.description: List new perpetual trading markets on your Orderly-powered DEX without waiting for Orderly to add them, including pre-TGE tokens, crypto, RWA, FX, and commodities.
prerequisites: Active broker account with admin access
Orderly SDK v3.1.1+ for pre-TGE market support

steps.title: Review Permissionless Listing Documentation
steps.description: Understand the permissionless listing framework and requirements.
steps.code:
// Documentation:
https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/permissionless-listing
steps.important: All broker tiers can list up to 5 assets as a promotional allowance. Brokers earn 100% of liquidation fees and 50% of transaction fees from listed assets.

steps.title: Configure Oracle for Pre-TGE or Custom Assets
steps.description: For pre-TGE or custom assets, provide the token name, initial price, and price tick to the Orderly team so they can configure the oracle. There is no self-serve oracle selection for pre-TGE assets.
steps.important: For standard crypto assets with existing oracle support, you can skip this step and proceed directly to listing.

steps.title: Initiate Listing via Admin Portal
steps.description: Use the admin portal to initiate the permissionless listing.
steps.code:
// Admin portal permissionless listing:
https://admin.orderly.network/permissionless-listing
steps.important: Test on testnet first with arbitrary values before launching on mainnet.

steps.title: Sync Frontend Configuration
steps.description: Ensure your SDK supports permissionlessly listed symbols. SDK v2.12.0+ provides full UI rendering and trading support. SDK v3.0.3+ fixes display issues.
steps.important: Permissionlessly listed markets are Isolated-only to limit risk exposure.

steps.title: Set Up Custom Oracle (Optional)
steps.description: For full control over price feeds, use Custom Oracles to push asset prices directly to Orderly, combining your own sources with existing CEX/oracle feeds.
steps.code:
// Custom Oracle documentation:
https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/custom-oracle#custom-oracle
steps.important: Custom Oracles support any asset type: FX pairs, US stocks, commodities, interest rates, and crypto.

commonIssues.issue: Permissionless symbols show empty values in UI.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.0.3 or later, which fixes the display of Interval, Funding Cap/Floor, and Estimated Funding Fee values.

commonIssues.issue: Pre-TGE market not appearing after listing.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the Orderly team has configured the oracle for your pre-TGE asset. SDK v3.1.1+ is required for pre-TGE market support.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot use Cross Margin on permissionless markets.
commonIssues.solution: This is by design. Permissionlessly listed markets only support Isolated Margin to limit risk exposure.

workflows.name: Building Copy Trading Features
workflows.description: Implement copy trading functionality on your Orderly-powered DEX using admin query APIs, WebSocket streams, and the Order enum feature for per-order fee customization.
prerequisites: Active broker account with admin wallet

steps.title: Access Admin Query APIs
steps.description: Use the admin query REST APIs to access transaction information for your own users. User trading data is not publicly exposed—only the DEX admin can access trades for users within their own DEX.
steps.important: All admin API requests must be signed with your admin wallet's Orderly API credentials.

steps.title: Subscribe to Real-Time WebSocket Updates
steps.description: For real-time updates without rate limiting, subscribe to WebSocket topics using your admin account ID.
steps.important: Replace {account_id} with your admin account ID. This provides real-time trade and position updates for all users on your DEX.

steps.title: Implement Order Enum for Copy Trading Fees
steps.description: Use the Order enum feature to set custom/additional trading fees on a per-order basis. This is useful for charging extra fees to users subscribing to leader signals.
steps.code:
// Integration guide:
https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/user-flows/order-enum-integration-guide
steps.important: The Order enum feature allows brokers to set custom fees per order, enabling monetization of copy trading signals.

steps.title: Build Leader/Follower UI
steps.description: Create a user interface that displays leader traders' performance metrics and allows followers to automatically copy their trades.
steps.important: Use the admin APIs to calculate leader PnL, win rates, and other performance metrics. Note that account_id values are EVM-formatted even for Solana users because settlement happens on the EVM-based L2.

commonIssues.issue: Admin WebSocket connection fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the correct admin account ID in the WebSocket URL. The account ID must be associated with your broker's admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot identify which chain a user deposited from.
commonIssues.solution: Trading on Orderly is chain-agnostic (settlement on L2), so there is no chain field on trades. Use the public API endpoints that power the Orderly dashboard (inspect network tab at https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/) to get deposit chain information.

commonIssues.issue: Per-order fees not applying correctly.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your integration follows the order enum integration guide exactly. Contact Orderly support if fees are not being applied as expected.

steps.description: Configure your broker ID in the Orderly MCP server to enable AI agents to trade through the Orderly infrastructure.
steps.important: This enables AI-powered trading interfaces to execute trades directly on your DEX through standardized MCP protocols.

steps.title: Configure AI Agent Access
steps.description: Set up authentication and access controls for AI agents connecting to your MCP server.
steps.important: Ensure proper risk management and position limits are configured for AI-driven trading.

steps.title: Test AI Agent Trading

steps.important: Test thoroughly on testnet before enabling on mainnet.

workflows.name: Configuring TradingView Advanced Charts
workflows.description: Set up TradingView-compatible charting in your Orderly-powered DEX, including obtaining a TradingView license and configuring the Orderly trading-view library.

steps.title: Obtain TradingView License
steps.description: Apply for and obtain your own TradingView Advanced Charting library license. The Orderly library wraps TradingView, so without your own license, the chart component will not function.
steps.code:
// Apply for TradingView license:
https://www.tradingview.com/advanced-charts/
steps.important: This is a mandatory prerequisite. The Orderly @orderly.network/trading-view library will not work without a valid TradingView license.

steps.title: Configure TradingView Library
steps.description: Integrate the Orderly trading-view library with your TradingView license in your DEX application.
steps.important: Follow the TradingView documentation for proper library initialization and configuration.

steps.title: Fetch TradingView-Compatible Chart Data
steps.description: Use the Orderly REST API endpoint for TradingView history bars to provide chart data.
steps.code:
// TradingView history bars endpoint:
// https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-evm/evm-api/restful-api/public/get-tradingview-history-bars
steps.important: Orderly charts are not directly integrated into TradingView—you use the REST API endpoint to feed data into your TradingView chart component.

commonIssues.issue: Chart component does not render.
commonIssues.solution: Verify that you have a valid TradingView Advanced Charting library license. The Orderly wrapper requires this license to function.

commonIssues.issue: Chart data not loading for new permissionless markets.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.3+ which optimizes K-line history loading to stop requesting unavailable historical data before a market's listing time.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, set up default trading fees, and manage custom user fee tiers.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions

steps.title: Register Broker ID with Orderly Team
steps.description: Provide the following details to the Orderly team to create your broker ID: Broker ID (must be lowercase), Broker Name, Default Taker Fee, Default Maker Fee, Tier (e.g., 'public' if not staking tokens), and an admin wallet address.
steps.important: The base fee for the public tier is 3bps taker / 0bps maker. Custom fees added on top go 100% to the broker, paid daily in USDC. Brokers can choose the Public Tier and scale through trading volume, or stake ORDER to access higher broker tiers.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. Connect the wallet and complete the standard Orderly account registration flow on your DEX UI. The Orderly team must first set up the broker ID on mainnet.
steps.important: The same wallet can be used for both testnet and mainnet, though using different wallets is possible. Frequent changes to the admin wallet are not recommended. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal and Generate API Credentials
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal and generate API credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates. Negative maker fees (maker rebates) are now supported natively and can be configured via the admin dashboard.

steps.title: Implement Custom User Fee Tiers
steps.description: Use the custom fee rate API to programmatically set per-user fee rates. For periodic tier updates, run a backend script that calls the update endpoint (e.g., daily).
steps.important: Custom fee structures can also be configured via the admin portal UI at https://admin.orderly.network/.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account. Check the balance by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet or using the private Get Current Holding endpoint.
steps.code:
GET /v1/holding
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: API credentials lost after clearing cache.
commonIssues.solution: You can regenerate new keys for the same account without needing to create a new account. Log in to the admin portal and click 'Create Orderly Key' again.

workflows.name: Launching Trading Competitions and Campaigns
workflows.description: Set up and manage trading competitions, points programs, and campaigns on your Orderly-powered DEX using the Campaigns API, Points Program API, and SDK hooks.

steps.title: Set Up Campaign with Orderly Team
steps.description: Provide campaign details to the Orderly team: Name, Broker, Broker ID, Start/End Time (UTC), Register (true/false), optional Register Start/End Time, Symbol filter, Referral code, and Calculation Scope (user address, pnl, trading volume, ROI, trading fee, campaign register time, account register time).
steps.important: Each campaign gets a unique campaign_id. Campaign data remains available via the /ranking API for at least 90 days after the campaign ends. Test campaigns can be created before official launch. For sub-campaigns or sprints, create separate non-registration campaigns (register=false) so all users are automatically included.

steps.title: Enable User Campaign Sign-Up via SDK
steps.description: Use the useCampaignsScript hook from @orderly.network/trading-leaderboard to allow users to join campaigns programmatically.

steps.title: Query Campaign Data via API
steps.description: Use the Campaigns API to fetch user progress, rankings, and campaign-specific data.
steps.important: Campaign PnL is calculated as: PnL = Account Value (end) - Account Value (start) - total deposit value + total withdrawal value. This is a global account-level PnL.

steps.title: Use Points Program API for Mini-Campaigns
steps.description: The Points Program awards users points based on daily trading volume, PnL, and referral activity. Use the stages API to retrieve point program information.
steps.code:
GET /v1/public/points/stages
// Documentation: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/restful-api/public/get-information-about-stages
steps.important: You can set weights for each parameter (volume, PnL, referrals). The leaderboard ranks users by total points earned.

steps.title: Filter Competition Eligibility by Net Deposit
steps.description: Use the asset history endpoint to calculate net deposits for competition eligibility filtering.

steps.title: Integrate with Quest Platforms (Galxe, Layer3)
steps.description: For Galxe integrations, use a JavaScript expression to evaluate task completion from the standard API response.
steps.important: Standard campaign API response wraps data in a `data` object (e.g., {"success": true, "data": {"volume": 1000}}).

steps.title: Launch via Fuul (Orderly One)
steps.description: For Orderly One DEXs, launch permissionless trading competitions and points programs directly through the Fuul integration with no coding required.
steps.important: Campaign data is archived after the campaign ends. Starting from Campaign 75, the archiving window is 6 months. Export any needed data before the deadline.

commonIssues.issue: Errors when saving or publishing a points campaign on Orderly One.
commonIssues.solution: Clear your browser's local storage to force the creation of a new Orderly key, then retry. You must connect using the EOA wallet that was originally used to create the DEX.

commonIssues.issue: Campaign data no longer accessible.
commonIssues.solution: Campaign data is archived after the campaign ends (6 months for campaigns after ID 75, 90 days for ranking API). Export data before the archiving deadline.

commonIssues.issue: PnL calculation seems incorrect for individual symbols.
commonIssues.solution: Campaign PnL is account-level, not per-symbol. The system tracks account-level value changes rather than position-level PnL per trading pair.

commonIssues.issue: User cannot join campaign programmatically.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the user is authenticated and proper header authentication is applied. The campaign must have register=true for sign-up to be required.

workflows.name: Handling Permissionless Token Listings
workflows.description: Manage permissionless token listings on your Orderly-powered DEX, including creating listings, syncing frontend configurations, using custom oracles, and supporting new markets automatically.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.12.0 or later (v3.0.3+ recommended for mobile fixes)
$50K deposit for Insurance Fund (for new permissionless listings)

steps.title: Create Permissionless Listing
steps.description: Access the Orderly admin panel and navigate to the permissionless listing section. Select your oracle and market maker to list any asset not currently on Orderly.
steps.important: A $50K deposit is required to set up the Insurance Fund (not for liquidity — liquidity is provided by market makers). The deposit generates yield while the market is listed and is returned upon delisting. As the market owner, you earn 100% of liquidation fees and 50% of Orderly's base fee on that market.

steps.title: Configure Custom Oracle (Optional)
steps.description: Push asset prices directly to Orderly for permissionless perpetual markets on any asset type (FX pairs, US stocks, commodities, interest rates, crypto) using Custom Oracles.
steps.code:
// Custom Oracle Documentation:
https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/custom-oracle#custom-oracle
steps.important: Custom Oracles allow builders to push asset prices directly to Orderly without waiting for Orderly to add data sources. Combine your own price sources with existing CEX/oracle feeds for robustness.

steps.title: Upgrade SDK for Permissionless Support
steps.description: Ensure your SDK is at least v2.12.0 for full UI rendering and trading support of permissionlessly listed symbols. SDK v3.0.3+ fixes display issues on mobile.

steps.title: Sync Frontend Configuration
steps.description: When new permissionless markets are announced, update your frontend configuration to support the new symbols. Monitor Orderly announcements for new listings.
steps.important: Permissionlessly listed markets are Isolated-only to limit risk exposure.

steps.title: Determine RWA Market Open/Close Status
steps.description: For RWA (Real World Asset) markets, use the RWA info API to determine market trading hours programmatically.
steps.code:
// Use the base symbol (e.g., PERP_CRCL_USDC) rather than variant symbols:
GET /v1/public/rwa/info?symbol=PERP_CRCL_USDC
steps.important: RWA markets can still be traded even when the underlying traditional market is closed. Ensure your frontend SDK is updated to the latest version for correct market status display.

steps.title: Handle Chart Data for New Markets
steps.description: SDK v3.1.3 optimizes K-line history loading so the chart stops requesting unavailable historical data before a market's listing time, reducing unnecessary requests and improving page stability.

commonIssues.issue: Permissionless symbols show empty values in funding rate modal on mobile.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.0.3 or later, which fixes the display of Interval, Funding Cap/Floor, and Estimated Funding Fee values.

commonIssues.issue: Chart requests fail for newly listed markets.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.3+ which optimizes K-line history loading to stop requesting unavailable historical data before a market's listing time.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot use Cross Margin on permissionless markets.
commonIssues.solution: This is by design. Permissionlessly listed markets only support Isolated Margin to limit risk exposure.

commonIssues.issue: Price feed inconsistencies for custom oracle markets.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your price sources are reliable and have sufficient redundancy. Combine multiple sources for accuracy.

workflows.name: Troubleshooting Mobile Wallet and SDK Issues
workflows.description: Resolve common mobile-specific issues including WalletConnect redirect loops, MetaMask infinite popups, Telegram Mini App OAuth errors, and input mode overrides in the Orderly SDK.
prerequisites: Understanding of mobile browser and wallet behavior

steps.title: Fix WalletConnect/MetaMask Infinite Redirect Loops on iOS Safari
steps.description: On iOS Safari, WalletConnect WebSocket connections are terminated when the app enters the background. Upon returning, the SDK may fail to re-bind to the existing session topic, causing repeated deep link attempts that Safari blocks as popups.
steps.important: Mitigation steps: (1) Use the wallet's built-in in-app browser (MetaMask browser, etc.) which bypasses these compatibility issues entirely. (2) Ensure you are using the latest MetaMask Mobile version. (3) Close the DApp and generate a new WalletConnect session. (4) Open the DApp in Chrome or Safari instead of in-app browsers (Telegram, KakaoTalk, etc.). The Orderly team is working on SDK-level fixes for automatic reconnection and topic re-subscription.

steps.title: Fix Mobile Deposit Flow Infinite MetaMask Redirect Popup
steps.description: The infinite redirect popup on iOS Safari during deposit is caused by wallet-read polling (balance/allowance checks every 3000ms) triggering deep links before the WalletConnect session is fully settled.
steps.important: To fix: (1) Disable wallet reads on page mount by forcing walletReadsEnabled/depositReadsEnabled to false initially. (2) Start wallet reads only after explicit user intent (e.g., clicking deposit). (3) Reduce polling frequency on mobile. (4) Avoid wallet-provider reads until the wallet session is fully stable. (5) Implement a 'readiness gate' to block balance/allowance reads until wallet/account/chain states stabilize.

steps.title: Resolve Google OAuth '403: disallowed_useragent' in Telegram Mini Apps
steps.description: Google's policy blocks OAuth requests from embedded WebViews. The Orderly SDK (v2.12.3 and later) detects window.Telegram?.WebApp and routes OAuth requests through the external browser via Telegram.WebApp.openLink() to ensure a secure sign-in experience.
steps.code:
// Upgrade to SDK v2.12.3+ to get this fix:
"@orderly.network/react": "^2.12.3"
steps.important: This fix is automatic once you upgrade to SDK v2.12.3 or later.

steps.title: Handle inputmode='decimal' Override Issue
steps.description: When upstream Orderly SDK updates overwrite custom inputmode='decimal' modifications in input components, the numeric keypad on mobile reverts to a standard text keyboard. Affected files include price inputs, quantity inputs, trigger price inputs, and TPSL dialog components.
steps.important: Report this to the Orderly team for inclusion in the base SDK. The team has acknowledged this and is considering adding different input modes in upcoming releases. Use the useInputMode hook consistently for implementation.

commonIssues.issue: WalletConnect session lost when iOS app enters background.
commonIssues.solution: Use the wallet's built-in in-app browser or open the DApp in Chrome/Safari directly. The Orderly team is working on SDK-level fixes for automatic reconnection.

commonIssues.issue: Infinite MetaMask popup during deposit on mobile.
commonIssues.solution: Implement a 'readiness gate' to block balance/allowance reads until wallet/account/chain states stabilize. Disable wallet reads on page mount and start them only after explicit user intent.

commonIssues.issue: Google OAuth fails in Telegram Mini App WebView.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to Orderly SDK v2.12.3 or later, which automatically routes OAuth requests through the external browser for Telegram Mini Apps.

commonIssues.issue: Numeric keypad reverts to text keyboard after SDK update.
commonIssues.solution: Use the useInputMode hook consistently and report the issue to the Orderly team for inclusion in the base SDK.

workflows.name: Querying Trade, Asset, and Account Data via API and Hooks
workflows.description: Retrieve trade execution history, asset deposits/withdrawals, account balances, and admin-level trade data using the Orderly REST API and Hooks SDK.
prerequisites: Orderly API access or Hooks SDK integrated

steps.title: Get Trade Execution History (Individual Fills)
steps.description: Use the private trades endpoint to retrieve individual trade fills (not orders).

steps.title: Access Archived Trade Data for High-Volume Users
steps.description: For high-volume traders, older trade data may be archived and unavailable through the admin trades endpoint. Use the Orderly Dashboard indexing service for complete historical data.
steps.code:
// Dashboard: https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/
// Query API: https://orderly-dashboard-query-service.orderly.network/swagger-ui/#/
steps.important: The admin trades endpoint also excludes funding fees from realized PnL; use GET /v1/admin/funding-fee-history separately.

steps.title: Fetch Deposit and Withdrawal History
steps.description: Use the asset history endpoint or Hooks SDK to retrieve deposit and withdrawal data.

steps.title: Get Account Balance, Equity, and Margin Information
steps.description: Use the following hooks to retrieve comprehensive account financial data.

steps.title: Retrieve User IP Address for Compliance
steps.description: Orderly provides a public endpoint for frontend use to retrieve the user's IP address for compliance or anti-wash-trading purposes.
steps.code:
GET /v1/public/ip-info
// Documentation: https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/restful-api/public/get-ip-info#get-ip-info
steps.important: Orderly does not store user IP addresses by default. Call this endpoint from your frontend and store the IP in your own systems.

steps.title: Handle Authentication Headers in Hooks SDK
steps.description: When using the Hooks SDK, use usePrivateQuery for authenticated (private) API endpoints — it automatically handles authentication headers. For public endpoints, use useQuery.
steps.important: usePrivateQuery automatically handles orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id, orderly-key, and orderly-signature headers.

commonIssues.issue: Trade data missing for high-volume users in admin endpoint.
commonIssues.solution: Older trade data may be archived. Use the Orderly Dashboard indexing service (https://orderly-dashboard-query-service.orderly.network/swagger-ui/#/) for complete historical data.

commonIssues.issue: Funding fees not included in realized PnL from trades endpoint.
commonIssues.solution: The admin trades endpoint excludes funding fees from realized PnL. Use GET /v1/admin/funding-fee-history separately to retrieve funding fee data.

commonIssues.issue: IP detection returns incorrect geo-blocking results.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly uses an IP detection database that is periodically updated. Report specific cases to the Orderly support team with the user's IP and region for investigation.

commonIssues.issue: Authentication headers not applied in custom API calls.
commonIssues.solution: Use usePrivateQuery instead of useQuery for private endpoints. usePrivateQuery automatically handles all required authentication headers.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, set up default trading fees, and implement volume-based custom fee tiers for users.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions
Contact with Orderly team for initial broker ID creation

steps.title: Request Broker ID from Orderly Team
steps.description: Provide the Orderly team with your Broker ID (string), Broker Name, Environment (Staging & Production), Default Taker Fee, Default Maker Fee, Broker Tier (e.g., 'public'), and optionally a Staking Wallet address for ORDER token staking.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. The staking wallet can be left blank initially and configured later for a broker tier upgrade.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The admin wallet is responsible for collecting fees and has exclusive access to APIs such as referral codes and fee rebates. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature. Many brokers use a multisig on mainnet.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates.

steps.title: Implement Volume-Based Custom Fee Tiers (Optional)
steps.description: To implement volume-based fee tiers for users, fetch each user's trading volume and set their fees individually via the custom fee API. A Python script with Docker container is available for automation.
steps.important: Orderly supports a custom fee feature that allows you to manually set fees for specific accounts. Default broker fees can also be checked and modified in the admin console.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account. Check the balance by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet or using the private Get Current Holding endpoint.
steps.code:
GET /v1/holding
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: Testing API before broker ID is set up.
commonIssues.solution: Use brokerId='demo' for testing on testnet. All WebSocket and REST endpoints work identically to production, but the admin wallet will be a dummy address so you will lose broker fee earnings. Set up your actual broker ID before going live.

workflows.name: Enabling Deposit Zap-in (Auto-Swap Deposits)
workflows.description: Enable the Deposit Zap-in feature that allows users to deposit any token into their Orderly perpetual account, with the token automatically swapped to a supported collateral asset during the deposit process.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.10.1 or later installed

steps.title: Verify SDK Version
steps.description: Ensure your application is using Orderly SDK v2.10.1 or later, which introduced the Deposit Zap-in feature.
steps.code:
// Check your package.json
"@orderly.network/react": "^2.10.1"

steps.title: Enable Swap Deposit Prop
steps.description: Add the `enableSwapDeposit` prop to your `<OrderlyAppProvider>` component to activate the feature.
steps.code:
import { OrderlyAppProvider } from "@orderly.network/react";

<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  brokerName="Your Broker"
  networkId="mainnet"
  enableSwapDeposit
>
  {children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>

steps.title: Configure Dynamic Chain Support (Optional)
steps.description: Zap-In Deposit supports dynamic chain configuration via API, allowing users to deposit from chains that may not be statically configured in your app.
steps.important: The deposited token is automatically swapped to a supported collateral asset (e.g., USDC) during the deposit process.

commonIssues.issue: Deposit Zap-in option does not appear in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the `enableSwapDeposit` prop is correctly set on the OrderlyAppProvider and that you are using SDK v2.10.1 or later.

commonIssues.issue: Swap fails for certain tokens.
commonIssues.solution: Not all tokens may have sufficient liquidity for the auto-swap. Ensure the token has a valid trading pair on the supported DEX aggregators used by the Zap-in feature.

workflows.name: Configuring the Multilevel Referral Program
workflows.description: Enable and configure the Orderly DEX Multilevel Referral Program to scale growth and incentivize communities through multi-tier referral rewards, including post-registration code binding.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.9.0 or later (v2.12.4+ recommended for post-registration binding)
Access to Admin Tool or Orderly One dashboard

steps.title: Upgrade SDK
steps.description: Ensure your DEX is running SDK version 2.9.0 or later. For Orderly One DEXs, ensure you are on the latest version available on the platform. SDK v2.12.4+ is recommended as it allows users to bind referral codes post-registration.
steps.important: As of SDK v2.12.4, users no longer need to provide a referral code during registration. They can bind a referral code to their existing account at any time post-creation.

steps.title: Activate the Referral Program
steps.description: Enable or upgrade the referral program via the Admin Tool or through the Orderly One dashboard. Referral codes must be configured manually in the admin portal — they are not generated automatically.
steps.code:
// Admin Portal:
https://admin.orderly.network/login

steps.title: Configure Referral Code Parameters
steps.description: When creating a referral code, configure the rebate rates. All values are expressed as absolute decimals (e.g., 0.5 means 50% of fees).
steps.important: Referral rebates are settled in USDC regardless of the collateral asset used, and are sent to users once per day.

steps.title: Handle Referral Code Access for Non-EVM Wallets
steps.description: If your wallet doesn't support the required network (e.g., Arbitrum), you have two options: access the admin portal using API Key credentials from your DEX (Portfolio -> API Key), or import your seed phrase into an EVM wallet that supports the network (e.g., Rabby, MetaMask, Brave).
steps.important: A referral code is automatically generated for a user when their trading volume reaches 10K. Alternatively, a broker admin can manually assign a referral code to a specific user via the admin portal.

steps.title: Use order_tag for Per-Order Referral Tracking
steps.description: Attach a referral code at the order level using the `order_tag` field in the create order API. This overrides any account-level referral binding.
steps.code:
POST /v1/order
Body: {
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "order_type": "MARKET",
  "order_quantity": "0.01",
  "side": "BUY",
  "order_tag": "BBBB" // Overrides account-level referral code
}

commonIssues.issue: Cannot register referral code for a KOL/affiliate.
commonIssues.solution: The KOL/affiliate must first connect their wallet and sign in to create an Orderly account. Attempting to register a ref code before the user has signed in will result in an 'address is not registered' error.

commonIssues.issue: Rebates not appearing for users.
commonIssues.solution: Rebates are settled once per day in USDC. Ensure the referral code is correctly bound to the user's account and that the rebate rates are properly configured.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot access admin portal to set up referrals.

workflows.name: Managing System Maintenance and Token Delistings
workflows.description: Handle scheduled system maintenance windows and token delisting processes on your Orderly-powered DEX, including the community Vote to Retain mechanism.

steps.title: Monitor Maintenance Announcements
steps.description: During scheduled system maintenance (typically ~30 minutes), users are unable to place or cancel orders. Algorithmic orders will not trigger, and withdrawals are suspended.
steps.important: Maintenance is used to deploy product updates such as order enum updates, tick size adjustments, custom trading fees per order, and permissionless vault features. Builders should inform users and plan accordingly.

steps.title: Monitor Delisting Announcements
steps.description: Orderly periodically reviews listed tokens and opens a community 'Vote to Retain' process. Delistings can also occur due to project rebranding, token swaps, or market disruptions.
steps.important: Examples: $TON delisted for rebranding, $IP delisted for token swap, $H delisted due to market disruption.

steps.title: Participate in Vote to Retain
steps.description: To retain a token under review, more than 3% of staked $ORDER must vote AGAINST delisting. The voting period typically lasts 5 days.
steps.important: Brokers are encouraged to inform and encourage their communities to participate using their staked $ORDER.

steps.title: Handle Delisted Token Settlement
steps.description: When a token is delisted, the index price is fixed at the average price of the last hour before the delisting time. Open positions are settled at this fixed price.
steps.important: Brokers should inform users in advance so they can prepare and close or manage open positions.

steps.title: Sync Frontend Configuration
steps.description: Remove or update the delisted token from your DEX's frontend configuration and notify users accordingly.
steps.important: Builders are advised to sync their frontend configurations promptly after delisting announcements.

commonIssues.issue: Users confused about position settlement after delisting.
commonIssues.solution: Communicate clearly that the index price is fixed at the average price of the last hour before delisting. All open positions are settled at this price.

commonIssues.issue: Token still showing in UI after delisting.
commonIssues.solution: Update your frontend configuration to remove the delisted token. For SDK builders, ensure your symbol list is synced with Orderly's current listings.

commonIssues.issue: Orders fail during maintenance window.
commonIssues.solution: This is expected behavior. Inform users in advance that order placement, cancellation, and withdrawals are suspended during maintenance (~30 minutes).

workflows.name: Troubleshooting SDK Integration Issues
workflows.description: Resolve common SDK integration issues including withdrawal failures, Next.js compatibility, wallet registration updates, and embedding the DEX in existing applications.

steps.title: Fix Intermittent Withdrawal Failures
steps.description: Intermittent withdrawal failures are likely caused by an outdated SDK version. The root cause is related to cross-chain messaging: after the LayerZero exploit, the system was migrated from Single DVN to DVN 3, and older SDK versions may not handle this correctly.
steps.code:
// Upgrade to SDK v3.0.2 or later
"@orderly.network/react": "^3.0.2"
steps.important: This is a critical fix. Users may experience intermittent withdrawal failures if the SDK is not updated.

steps.title: Apply Mandatory Wallet Registration Update
steps.description: SDK v3.0.4 includes a critical feature update for wallet registration requests. While the current registration process continues to work, it may encounter issues in the future without this update.
steps.code:
// Upgrade to SDK v3.0.4 or later
"@orderly.network/react": "^3.0.4"
steps.important: The recommendation level is high-mandatory for SDK builders. Apply this update as soon as possible.

steps.title: Fix Next.js SWR Export Error
steps.description: If you encounter the 'export default (reexported as useSWR) was not found in swr' error when integrating Orderly with Next.js, add the 'use client' directive.

steps.title: Embed DEX in Existing Application
steps.description: If you need the DEX integrated as part of your existing app rather than hosted on its own domain, migrate the Orderly One (low-code) source code into your own codebase or use the Orderly SDK directly.
steps.important: Orderly One by default is designed to be hosted on a custom domain as a standalone DEX. Embedding it within another application requires moving the code into your project.

steps.title: Generate Client Library from OpenAPI Spec
steps.description: Use the canonical OpenAPI spec to generate client code in your preferred language using a Swagger code generator.
steps.important: API authentication (EIP-712 signing) is the trickiest part to implement. Refer to the authentication docs and language-specific examples for guidance.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawals intermittently failing for users.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.0.2 or later. The issue is related to the LayerZero DVN migration from Single DVN to DVN 3.

commonIssues.issue: 'useSWR' export error in Next.js.
commonIssues.solution: Add the 'use client' directive to the file using the Orderly SDK configuration.

commonIssues.issue: Wallet registration may fail in the future.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.0.4+ which includes a critical wallet registration request update. This is high-mandatory.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot embed Orderly One DEX in existing app.
commonIssues.solution: Migrate the Orderly One source code into your own codebase, or use the Orderly SDK directly with your broker ID for integration.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, set up default trading fees, and withdraw accumulated broker fees.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly team or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions
Details ready: Broker ID (lowercase), Broker Name, Environment (Staging & Production), Default Taker/Maker Fees, RWA fees (if applicable), and Tier

steps.title: Request Broker ID from Orderly Team
steps.description: Provide the Orderly team with your broker details. The broker_id must be lowercase (e.g., 'jojo'), while the broker name can use capital letters and will be displayed on Dune Analytics. During development, you can use 'demo' or an existing broker ID like 'woofi_pro'.
steps.important: Setup takes a couple of days. You can use brokerID 'demo' in the meantime for development. The Orderly team will create and assign a custom broker ID for mainnet deployment when you're close to launch.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments. Testnet and mainnet can use different addresses.
steps.important: The admin wallet is responsible for collecting fees and has exclusive access to APIs like referral codes and fee rebates. The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend (takes 2-3 days). Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Generate Broker Admin API Credentials
steps.description: Generate API credentials by logging into the admin console with your admin wallet. You can also generate them via Dex → Portfolio → API Keys, or through the broker registration tool.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 3 bps (0.03%) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. Makers can receive negative fees (rebates) under the new fee structure. RWA fees have been aligned with crypto fees (e.g., 1-3 bps taker for Diamond tier). Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection and Withdraw Broker Fees
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin account's Orderly L2 balance (not directly to the EOA wallet). To withdraw, log into the broker registration portal with the admin wallet, create an Orderly key if needed, navigate to the Assets tab, and initiate a withdrawal.
steps.important: Withdrawal fees vary by chain (e.g., ~$1-2 for most chains, higher for Ethereum). Withdrawals typically take 30 seconds to a few minutes depending on chain congestion.

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet (takes 2-3 days after registration).

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. To change the admin address, register a new account using your broker_id via the broker registration portal with the new address, then request the Orderly team to update it.

commonIssues.issue: Broker fees not appearing in EOA wallet.
commonIssues.solution: Broker fees are credited to the admin account's Orderly L2 balance, not directly to the EOA wallet. You must log into the broker registration portal and initiate a withdrawal from the Assets tab.

workflows.name: Authenticating API Requests to Orderly Private Endpoints
workflows.description: Set up proper authentication for Orderly's private broker endpoints using ed25519 key signing, including signature generation and header configuration.
prerequisites: Orderly account ID and private key (obtainable from broker registration portal)
Backend environment for making API requests

steps.title: Obtain Orderly Account ID and Private Key
steps.description: Get your Orderly account ID and private key from the broker registration portal. These are required for signing API requests.

steps.title: Construct the Signature Payload
steps.description: The signature is computed by signing the concatenation of timestamp + HTTP method + endpoint path + request body using the Orderly private key (ed25519 format).
steps.important: The timestamp must be current or the request will be rejected. Ensure your server clock is synchronized.

steps.title: Set Required Authentication Headers
steps.description: Include all four required headers in every private endpoint request.
steps.important: The orderly-key must be in ed25519 format. The signature must be base64-encoded.

steps.title: Test Authentication with Example Code
steps.description: Use the provided example implementations to verify your authentication setup works correctly.

steps.title: Programmatically Validate Orderly Keys (Optional)
steps.description: Use the public endpoint to check the validity of a user's Orderly key without requiring their signature. Useful for backend systems that need to validate keys server-side.

commonIssues.issue: Request rejected with authentication error.
commonIssues.solution: Verify that the timestamp is current (within acceptable window), the signature payload is correctly concatenated (timestamp + method + path + body), and the ed25519 key is properly formatted.

commonIssues.issue: Signature verification fails intermittently.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your server clock is synchronized using NTP. Even small clock drifts can cause timestamp validation failures.

commonIssues.issue: Rate limiting on API endpoints.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly reads the IP address directly from the connection (not from X-Forwarded-For headers). For example, GET /v1/orderly_key allows a maximum of 10 requests per second per IP address.

workflows.name: Tracking Real-Time Trading Events and Building Leaderboards
workflows.description: Set up systems to track on-chain trading events, build user leaderboards, and monitor broker volume using Orderly's APIs and open-source indexer.

steps.title: Choose Your Tracking Method
steps.description: Select from three options for tracking trading events: (1) Pull Trading Events API v2, (2) Builders Leaderboard API, or (3) the open-source Orderly Dashboard indexer.
steps.important: Orders are off-chain, but matched trades are on-chain on Orderly L2. There is currently no WebSocket subscription for new trades; you can only filter by account ID/address via the pull API.

steps.title: Use the Pull Trading Events API v2
steps.description: Query on-chain trade events filtered by account ID or address. This is the most flexible option for custom tracking.

steps.title: Use the Builders Leaderboard API
steps.description: Access pre-built leaderboard data that updates every 5 minutes with a 15-20 minute delay.

steps.title: Run the Orderly Dashboard Indexer
steps.description: Clone and run the open-source indexer to continuously listen for on-chain trade events and store them in your own database.
steps.important: The indexer requires a PostgreSQL database configured via the DATABASE_URL in the .env file.

steps.title: Configure Indexer Start Point
steps.description: Control where indexing starts using contract_deploy_height and contract_deploy_timestamp parameters. To skip historical data and only index recent trades, set contract_deploy_height to a recent block number.
steps.important: Once historical sync completes, the indexer will continuously listen for new blocks.

steps.title: Retrieve Broker Trading Volume
steps.description: Monitor your broker's trading volume via the API or Dune dashboard.
steps.important: Volume is not currently available in the admin console. Use the API or Dune dashboard instead.

commonIssues.issue: Leaderboard data seems outdated.
commonIssues.solution: The Builders Leaderboard API updates every 5 minutes with a 15-20 minute delay. For real-time needs, use the Pull Trading Events API or run your own indexer.

commonIssues.issue: Indexer not picking up new trades.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the PostgreSQL database is properly configured and accessible. Check that the indexer process is running and that contract_deploy_height is set correctly.

commonIssues.issue: Need custom scoring/leaderboard based on referrals.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly provides volume data APIs but brokers need to build their own logic on top for custom scoring/leaderboard systems based on referrals.

workflows.name: Handling Embedded WebView Wallet Integration
workflows.description: Integrate Orderly SDK with embedded WebView wallets (e.g., mobile app wallets), including proper chain ID detection and deposit transaction decoding.
prerequisites: Understanding of postMessage communication between WebView and native layer

steps.title: Track Chain ID in React State
steps.description: You cannot reliably detect the chain from the token contract address alone, as the same address may exist on multiple chains. The chainId is not included in the standardized eth_sendTransaction message. Track the chain ID in your React state instead.
steps.important: Do not attempt to derive chain ID from contract addresses — the same address may exist on multiple chains.

steps.title: Include Chain ID in postMessage Payload
steps.description: Pass the current chain ID along when posting messages from the WebView so the native wallet layer can route to the correct RPC.
steps.important: The native wallet layer needs the chain ID to route the transaction to the correct RPC endpoint.

steps.title: Decode Deposit Transaction Data Fields
steps.description: When processing deposit transactions sent to the Orderly vault contract, decode the data field to extract deposit parameters.
steps.important: The Token Hash is the Keccak-256 hash of the token symbol string (e.g., 'USDT'), not the token contract address.

commonIssues.issue: Transactions sent to wrong chain in WebView.
commonIssues.solution: Always include the chainId in your postMessage payload. Do not rely on contract addresses to determine the chain. Use useAppContext() to get the current chain ID.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot identify token from deposit data field.
commonIssues.solution: Compute the Keccak-256 hash of known token symbol strings and match against Argument 3 in the data field. Remember it's the hash of the symbol string, not the address.

commonIssues.issue: Chain ID changes not detected.
commonIssues.solution: Listen for wallet_switchEthereumChain events and update your React state accordingly. Ensure the currentChainId from useAppContext() is always current.

workflows.name: Understanding Liquidation Mechanics and Margin Modes
workflows.description: Understand how liquidation works on Orderly, configure isolated vs cross margin modes, and manage symbol-level leverage settings.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.11.0+ for isolated margin support

steps.title: Understand Liquidation Triggers
steps.description: Liquidation is triggered when the Mark Price movement causes the user's Total Collateral Value to drop below the Maintenance Margin Requirement — not the bankruptcy price where margin reaches zero.
steps.important: Liquidation tiers categorize positions as either High Risk or Low Risk depending on the trading pair. A liquidator takes over a position based on the risk tier category.

steps.title: Calculate Maximum Leverage
steps.description: Maximum leverage is calculated as 1 / base_imr, where base_imr is returned by the public info endpoint. Note that an IMR factor kicks in for larger notionals, reducing effective leverage.
steps.important: An IMR factor kicks in for larger notionals, reducing effective leverage below the theoretical maximum.

steps.title: Configure Isolated Margin Mode
steps.description: Isolated margin mode (SDK v2.11.0+) allows configuring leverage and margin per position rather than account-wide. This limits losses to only the margin assigned to that position.
steps.important: SDK v3.1.0 fixed an issue where maxing out an isolated margin market order at 100% slider was rejected — the SDK now reserves a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula.

steps.title: Configure Symbol-Level Leverage
steps.description: Starting from SDK v2.7.3, leverage can be configured per symbol instead of account-wide, providing greater flexibility and control over individual positions.
steps.important: Note: In the create-order API, there is no leverage field. Users set the margin they want to use for a trade, and the system displays an estimated leverage. The leverage API/hooks refer to the maximum allowed account leverage.

commonIssues.issue: Position liquidated before expected bankruptcy price.
commonIssues.solution: This is by design. Liquidation occurs when collateral drops below the Maintenance Margin Requirement (e.g., 0.6% for BTC), which is always above zero. The bankruptcy price (where margin = 0) is never reached.

commonIssues.issue: Isolated margin market order rejected at 100% slider.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.0+ which reserves a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula, preventing 'margin will be insufficient after' errors.

commonIssues.issue: Closing isolated margin position from TradingView fails.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.3+ which sends the correct margin mode to prevent reduce-only validation errors when closing positions from TradingView position lines.

steps.title: Choose Your Customization Approach
steps.description: Choose between customizing existing SDK components (limited customization, shows 'powered by Orderly') or building your own components using the Orderly hooks SDK (full customization).
steps.important: The DEX can be hosted on your own domain or subdomain (e.g., perps.yourdomain.com).

steps.title: Change the Broker ID in the SDK
steps.description: Update the brokerId and brokerName fields in the app configuration object. After changing, reset your frontend state and re-register the wallet to create a new account under the new broker.

steps.title: Hide the Risk Notice Bar for Permissionless Symbols

steps.title: Enable Testnet Support

steps.title: Retrieve User Keys from the SDK
steps.description: When using the Orderly Hooks SDK, access user keys (account ID, Orderly key, secret key) via the useAccountInstance hook.

commonIssues.issue: Changes to broker ID don't take effect.
commonIssues.solution: Clear localStorage and re-register the wallet after changing the broker ID. Accounts and fees are broker-specific, so a fresh registration is required.

commonIssues.issue: Testnet chains not showing in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure chainFilter does not explicitly exclude testnets and that showTestnet is not set to false in overrides. Testnet is enabled by default.

commonIssues.issue: Need deeper customization than the Components SDK allows.
commonIssues.solution: Use the Orderly Hooks SDK (https://orderly.network/docs/sdks/hooks/overview) to build your own components with full customization, or explore the SDK v3 Plugin System for extension points.

steps.important: The referee gets a discount on trading fees, and the affiliate receives a daily rebate. Referral rebates are settled in USDC regardless of the collateral asset used.

steps.title: Configure Referral Code Parameters
steps.description: When creating a referral code, configure the rebate rates. All values are expressed as absolute decimals (e.g., 0.5 means 50% of fees).

commonIssues.issue: Need custom scoring/leaderboard based on referrals.

workflows.name: Verifying Trade Transparency and Understanding Orderly Architecture
workflows.description: Verify on-chain trade transparency for depositors and understand how Orderly's shared orderbook and multi-broker architecture works.

steps.title: Verify Trades on Orderly Explorer
steps.description: Orderly uses a Layer 2 system that serves as a ledger for all trades. Trade events and many other event categories are published on-chain and can be verified via the Orderly Explorer.
steps.important: All API interactions for orders are off-chain; settlement is sent to Orderly's L2 for verification. Deposits and withdrawals are on-chain.

steps.title: Understand Shared Orderbook Architecture
steps.description: Every broker runs on the same chains. An address has a different account per broker within the Orderly infrastructure, but all brokers share the same liquidity/orderbook.
steps.important: In the UI, individual brokers may choose which chains to display or support, but the underlying liquidity is shared across all brokers.

steps.title: Understand Order and Position Creation
steps.description: You do not need to separately create a position before sending an order. Placing an order via the API creates a position automatically.

commonIssues.issue: Users question whether trades are truly on-chain.
commonIssues.solution: Direct users to the Orderly Explorer (https://explorer.orderly.network/) where they can verify trade events by transaction hash or address. Trades are settled on Orderly L2.

commonIssues.issue: Confusion about why different brokers show different chains.
commonIssues.solution: All brokers share the same liquidity/orderbook and run on the same chains. Individual brokers may choose which chains to display or support in their UI, but the underlying infrastructure is shared.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, set up default trading fees, and understand the Builder Tier System for fee optimization.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions
Broker details: Broker ID, Broker Name, Environment (Production/Staging), Default Fees, Tier, Staking Wallet

steps.title: Submit Broker Registration Details
steps.description: Provide the following information to the Orderly team: Broker ID (e.g., your project name), Broker Name, Environment (Production and Staging), Default Taker Fee and Maker Fee, Tier (e.g., public), and Staking Wallet. Orderly typically processes this within 1–3 working days.
steps.important: Default base fees are 0.03% (3 bps) taker and 0% maker. Brokers can set higher fees and keep 100% of the markup as revenue. For example, setting taker at 0.06% earns the broker 0.03% per trade.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID at the broker registration portal. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication. Fees can be changed later via the admin wallet.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates. Gold Tier brokers benefit from a discounted base taker fee.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection and Withdraw Revenue
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the broker's Orderly account in USDC. Check the balance by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet or using the private Get Current Holding endpoint. Fees can be withdrawn in USDC on supported chains.
steps.code:
GET /v1/holding
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id

steps.title: Optimize Fees via Builder Tier System (Optional)
steps.description: The Builder Tier System categorizes brokers into Public, Silver, Gold, Platinum, and Diamond tiers based on 30-day average trading volume or ORDER tokens staked. Higher tiers unlock reduced base taker fees and additional benefits.
steps.important: Platinum tier (2 bps base taker fee) requires ≥$1B 30-day volume OR 2M ORDER staked. Diamond tier (1 bp base taker fee) requires ≥$10B 30-day volume OR 7M ORDER staked. Custom fees below standard tiers require Diamond tier status and a graduated DEX (not using a shared broker ID).

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: Need to change DEX name or broker ID.
commonIssues.solution: The broker ID and broker name are configured on the Orderly backend and cannot be renamed directly. Set up a new broker ID and update the broker ID in your DEX's .env file. Note that existing users will lose access to their transaction history and funds under the old broker ID (funds are not lost but are no longer accessible under the new broker ID). You can display any name you want on your UI regardless of the broker ID.

workflows.name: Generating Orderly API Credentials
workflows.description: Generate an Orderly secret (API key) for authentication in the Python SDK or REST API, including ed25519 key pair generation, key registration, and IP restriction configuration.
prerequisites: Backend server with static IP (for IP restrictions)

steps.title: Generate ed25519 Key Pair
steps.description: Generate a random ed25519 key pair. Store the private key offline — it should always be kept off-chain for message signing. The public key becomes your 'Orderly key'.
steps.important: A user can have multiple Orderly secrets associated with their account. The private key must never be exposed on-chain or in client-side code.

steps.title: Register Public Key with Orderly
steps.description: Register the public key (your 'Orderly key') with Orderly via the key registration endpoint.

steps.title: Set IP Restrictions for Backend Access (Optional)
steps.description: After creating an Orderly key, restrict API usage to specific static IP(s) for backend server access while allowing users to connect normally from any device.
steps.important: This restricts API usage to the specified static IP(s) while allowing users to connect normally from any device.

steps.title: Automate Key Creation for Copy Trading (Optional)
steps.description: Brokers can automate Orderly account registration and API key creation for copy trading integration by interacting with Orderly's APIs to handle user registration, Orderly key creation via signature, and sending generated keys to the broker's backend.
steps.important: The reference implementation handles: 1) User registration (if not yet done), 2) Orderly key creation via signature, and 3) Sending the generated keys to the broker's backend.

commonIssues.issue: Authentication errors when calling private endpoints.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, and orderly-account-id headers are all correctly set. The signature must be generated using the private key corresponding to the registered public key.

commonIssues.issue: IP restriction blocks legitimate requests.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the IP address in the restriction list matches your server's outbound IP. Use a static IP for your backend server to avoid issues with dynamic IP changes.

workflows.name: Handling USDC Decimal Precision on BNB Chain
workflows.description: Correctly handle USDC decimal precision differences between on-chain (18 decimals) and Orderly (6 decimals) when building deposit and withdrawal flows on BNB Chain.
prerequisites: BNB Chain support in your DEX

steps.title: Query Token Decimals from Public API
steps.description: Before processing any on-chain transaction, always refer to the `decimals` field in the `chain_details` from the Public Token API to determine the correct decimal precision for the token on the specific chain.
steps.important: USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain, but Orderly only supports 6 decimals for deposits and withdrawals. Always use the API-provided decimals value.

steps.title: Apply Correct Decimal Conversion
steps.description: When constructing deposit or withdrawal transactions, convert amounts using the decimals value from the API rather than assuming a fixed decimal count.
steps.important: Precision mismatches can result in deposits that are 10^12 times too large or too small, leading to significant fund loss or failed transactions.

commonIssues.issue: Deposit amount is incorrect after processing.
commonIssues.solution: Verify you are using the `decimals` field from the Orderly Public Token API's `chain_details` rather than the on-chain token contract's decimals. On BNB Chain, USDC has 18 on-chain decimals but Orderly uses 6.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal transaction reverts.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the withdrawal amount is calculated with the correct decimal precision (6 for USDC on Orderly) and that the on-chain transaction uses the proper conversion.
