workflows.name: Understanding Liquidation Mechanics and Stop-Loss Interactions
workflows.description: Understand how Orderly's liquidation engine calculates liquidated amounts, the margin thresholds that trigger liquidation, and how liquidation interacts with stop-loss orders.

steps.title: Understand Liquidation Trigger Conditions
steps.description: Liquidation is triggered when a position's Margin Ratio (MR = collateral / notional) falls below the Maintenance Margin Ratio (MMR). For BTC/ETH, the current MMR threshold is 0.6%.
steps.important: This condition is evaluated independently of any stop-loss orders. If the liquidation trigger price is reached before the stop-loss trigger price, the position will be liquidated and the stop-loss order will not execute.

steps.title: Understand Liquidation Amount Calculation
steps.description: The system liquidates enough of the position so that after liquidation, the Margin Ratio returns to IMR + 5%. For example, if IMR = 2%, the post-liquidation target is ~7%. For BTC/ETH, the system now defaults to full liquidation when MR falls below the 0.6% MMR threshold.
steps.important: Stop-loss orders are trigger orders, not guaranteed executions. Setting a stop-loss very close to the estimated liquidation price carries the risk that liquidation triggers first.

steps.title: Review Liquidation Details
steps.description: Liquidation details including position size before/after, mark price at liquidation, and margin ratio can be reviewed in the Liquidation tab or by requesting a full record from Orderly support with the account address.
steps.important: The estimated liquidation price displayed on the frontend is an estimate that depends on multiple factors across all positions and can fluctuate.

commonIssues.issue: Position liquidated before stop-loss triggered.
commonIssues.solution: This is by design — liquidation and stop-loss are evaluated independently. Set stop-loss orders with sufficient distance from the estimated liquidation price to ensure they trigger first.

commonIssues.issue: Full position liquidated instead of partial.
commonIssues.solution: For BTC/ETH, the system defaults to full liquidation when MR falls below the 0.6% MMR threshold. This is expected behavior for these high-liquidity pairs.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot find liquidation details.
commonIssues.solution: Check the Liquidation tab in the DEX UI, or request a full liquidation record from Orderly support by providing the account address.

workflows.name: Troubleshooting LayerZero Cross-Chain Message Failures
workflows.description: Diagnose and resolve common LayerZero cross-chain message failures including NotEnoughNative errors, InvalidInboundNonce on Solana, Unauthorized errors, and manual message retry procedures.
prerequisites: cast CLI tool installed (for manual retries)
RPC URLs for source and destination chains

steps.title: Check Message Status Programmatically
steps.description: If the LayerZero Scan UI is delayed, use the LayerZero Scan API to check message delivery status programmatically for real-time updates.
steps.important: The web UI can experience indexing delays on testnets or during high-load periods. The API is more reliable for programmatic status checks.

steps.title: Resolve NotEnoughNative Errors
steps.description: The NotEnoughNative error occurs when the relay or executor contract on the destination chain lacks sufficient native gas tokens to execute the message. Top up the relay contract with native tokens on the destination chain.
steps.important: After refueling the relay contract with native tokens (e.g., ETH, SEI), retry the message manually or request the LayerZero team to re-execute pending messages.

steps.title: Manually Retry Failed Messages on EVM
steps.description: If the LayerZero Scan 'Execute' button is unavailable or fails (common on testnets), manually retry by calling lzReceive directly on the destination Endpoint V2 contract.
steps.code:
cast send \
  --rpc-url <DEST_RPC> \
  --private-key $pk \
  <ENDPOINT_V2_ADDRESS> \
  "lzReceive((uint32,bytes32,uint64),address,bytes32,bytes,bytes)" \
  "(<SRC_EID>,<SENDER_BYTES32>,<NONCE>)" \
  <OAPP_ADDRESS> \
  <MESSAGE_HASH> \
  <PAYLOAD_BYTES> \
  0x \
  --value 0
steps.important: Ensure the gas limit is sufficient for execution. If you receive LZ_PayloadHashNotFound, the message has already been cleared/executed.

steps.title: Resolve InvalidInboundNonce on Solana
steps.description: InvalidInboundNonce (Error 6007) occurs when messages are delivered out of order on an ordered execution pathway. If a previous message fails and is not retried successfully before subsequent messages are processed, the nonce sequence breaks.
steps.important: Implement a retry system that processes failed messages in nonce order, and ensure the nextNonce function is correctly implemented in your OApp to support ordered delivery.

steps.title: Resolve Unauthorized Errors on Solana Endpoint
steps.description: The Unauthorized error (Error Code 6010) occurs when the signer does not match the OApp delegate registered in the oapp_registry. Ensure the transaction is signed by the correct delegate address.
steps.important: If you transferred the delegate role, verify the on-chain oapp_registry state reflects the new delegate and that the signer in your instruction matches it exactly (e.g., your multisig PDA).

steps.title: Find Testnet Contract Addresses
steps.description: Testnet contract addresses and DVN configurations can be found in the LayerZero SDK config files or by requesting them from the LayerZero team.
steps.important: Sei devnet faucets may be limited. Request tokens directly from the Sei team or use third-party services like gas.zip. For large-scale testing, coordinate with LayerZero or Sei teams for 1,000+ SEI.

commonIssues.issue: LayerZero Scan 'Execute' button unavailable on testnet.
commonIssues.solution: Use the cast CLI to manually call lzReceive on the destination Endpoint V2 contract. Ensure you have the correct message parameters (source EID, sender, nonce, payload).

commonIssues.issue: LZ_PayloadHashNotFound when retrying.
commonIssues.solution: This means the message has already been cleared/executed. No further action is needed.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot obtain testnet native tokens for relay funding.
commonIssues.solution: Sei devnet faucets may be limited. Request tokens directly from the Sei team, use gas.zip, or coordinate with LayerZero/Sei teams for bulk devnet tokens.

commonIssues.issue: Messages stuck due to nonce ordering on Solana.
commonIssues.solution: Process failed messages in strict nonce order. Implement a retry queue that respects nonce sequencing before attempting to deliver subsequent messages.

workflows.name: Configuring Custom Domain for Orderly DEX
workflows.description: Set up and configure a custom domain for your Orderly-powered DEX, including handling non-standard domain extensions and DNS configuration.
prerequisites: Active DEX deployment (Orderly One or custom)

steps.title: Configure Domain in DEX Profile
steps.description: Custom domains are configured in your DEX profile. Enter your desired domain name in the custom domain settings.
steps.important: The domain must be properly registered and configured in the broker profile.

steps.title: Handle Non-Standard Domain Extensions
steps.description: If you encounter issues with certain domain extensions (e.g., non-.com domains like .trading), use a subdomain format instead of the apex domain.
steps.code:
// Instead of: yourdomain.trading
// Use: dex.yourdomain.trading
steps.important: Non-standard TLDs may have DNS propagation or SSL certificate issues when used as apex domains. Subdomains are more reliable.

steps.title: Update DNS CNAME Record
steps.description: For Orderly One DEXs, update your DNS CNAME record to point to the Orderly hosting endpoint.
steps.important: DNS changes may take up to 48 hours to propagate. Ensure no conflicting A or CNAME records exist.

commonIssues.issue: SSL certificate not provisioning for custom domain.
commonIssues.solution: Try using a subdomain format (e.g., dex.yourdomain.trading) instead of the apex domain, especially for non-standard TLDs.

commonIssues.issue: Domain not resolving after DNS update.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the CNAME record points to orderlynetworkdexcreator.github.io and that no conflicting records exist. DNS propagation can take up to 48 hours.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, set up default trading fees, and withdraw collected fees.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions

steps.title: Request a Custom Broker ID
steps.description: Provide the Orderly team with your desired Broker ID (e.g., 'one_bow'), Broker Name, Default Taker Fee, and Default Maker Fee. Orderly charges a base 0.025% taker fee and no maker fee; any amount above that is retained by the broker.
steps.important: For testnet purposes, any existing broker ID (e.g., 'woofi_pro') can be used temporarily while waiting for your custom ID.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig wallets are supported on mainnet via the delegate signer feature. Different wallets can be used for mainnet and testnet.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials. The Orderly Account ID (a unique ID hashed from the wallet + broker ID combination) can be found using the Orderly account registration tool.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication. Fee settings may require round numbers (e.g., whole basis points).
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.025% (2.5 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. Fees can be changed later by the broker once the admin wallet is set up. RWA markets have higher base fees than crypto markets.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection and Withdraw
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account. Check the balance by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet or using the private Get Current Holding endpoint. Withdraw fees using the Orderly broker fee withdrawal app or directly through your own UI (only with an EOA wallet).
steps.code:
GET /v1/holding
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id

// Fee claim interface:
https://github-dev.orderly.network/broker-registration/
steps.important: If using an EVM admin wallet on an Abstract-only DEX, temporarily enable MetaMask/EVM wallet connection to access the fee claim interface.

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause. Fee settings may require round numbers (whole basis points).

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet. Provide the wallet address to the Orderly team for manual configuration if needed.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot access fee claim interface on Abstract-only DEX.
commonIssues.solution: Temporarily enable MetaMask/EVM wallet connection in your DEX settings to access the fee claim interface with your EVM admin wallet.

workflows.name: Enabling Deposit Zap-in (Auto-Swap Deposits)
workflows.description: Enable the Deposit Zap-in feature that allows users to deposit any token into their Orderly perpetual account, with the token automatically swapped to a supported collateral asset during the deposit process.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.10.1 or later installed

steps.title: Verify SDK Version
steps.description: Ensure your application is using Orderly SDK v2.10.1 or later, which introduced the Deposit Zap-in feature.
steps.code:
// Check your package.json
"@orderly.network/react": "^2.10.1"

steps.title: Enable Swap Deposit Prop
steps.description: Add the `enableSwapDeposit` prop to your `<OrderlyAppProvider>` component to activate the feature.
steps.code:

<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  brokerName="Your Broker"
  networkId="mainnet"
  enableSwapDeposit

steps.title: Configure Dynamic Chain Support (Optional)
steps.description: Zap-In Deposit supports dynamic chain configuration via API, allowing users to deposit from chains that may not be statically configured in your app.
steps.important: The deposited token is automatically swapped to a supported collateral asset (e.g., USDC) during the deposit process.

commonIssues.issue: Deposit Zap-in option does not appear in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the `enableSwapDeposit` prop is correctly set on the OrderlyAppProvider and that you are using SDK v2.10.1 or later.

commonIssues.issue: Swap fails for certain tokens.
commonIssues.solution: Not all tokens may have sufficient liquidity for the auto-swap. Ensure the token has a valid trading pair on the supported DEX aggregators used by the Zap-in feature.

workflows.name: Configuring the Multilevel Referral Program
workflows.description: Enable and configure the Orderly DEX Multilevel Referral Program to scale growth and incentivize communities through multi-tier referral rewards, including API-based referral code management.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.9.0 or later (v2.12.4+ recommended for post-registration binding)
Access to Admin Tool or Orderly One dashboard

steps.title: Upgrade SDK
steps.description: Ensure your DEX is running SDK version 2.9.0 or later. For Orderly One DEXs, ensure you are on the latest version available on the platform.
steps.important: As of SDK v2.12.4, users can bind a referral code to their existing account at any time post-registration, rather than being required to provide a code during registration.

steps.title: Activate the Referral Program
steps.description: Enable or upgrade the referral program via the Admin Tool or through the Orderly One dashboard. Single-level referral is no longer available for builders who have never enabled the referral program before.

steps.title: Create Referral Codes via API
steps.description: Create referral codes programmatically using the `/v1/referral/create` endpoint or via the admin portal. Configure rebate rates as absolute decimals (e.g., 0.5 means 50% of fees).
steps.important: Referral codes are platform-unique but can only be used within the broker that created them. Referral rebates are settled in USDC regardless of the collateral asset used, and are sent to users once per day.

steps.title: Enable Auto-Generation of Referral Codes
steps.description: Automatically generate referral codes for users reaching a trading volume threshold using the auto-referral endpoint.

steps.title: Use order_tag for Per-Order Referral Tracking
steps.description: Attach a referral code at the order level using the `order_tag` field in the create order API. This has higher priority than a user's bound referral code for fee commission allocation.
steps.code:
POST /v1/order
Body: {
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "order_type": "MARKET",
  "order_quantity": "0.01",
  "side": "BUY",
  "order_tag": "BBBB" // Overrides account-level referral code
}

steps.title: Bind Referral Codes via SDK Links
steps.description: Users can bind a referral code via the API or automatically through SDK-handled referral links.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot register referral code for a KOL/affiliate.
commonIssues.solution: The KOL/affiliate must first connect their wallet and sign in to create an Orderly account. Attempting to register a ref code before the user has signed in will result in an 'address is not registered' error.

commonIssues.issue: Rebates not appearing for users.
commonIssues.solution: Rebates are settled once per day in USDC. Ensure the referral code is correctly bound to the user's account and that the rebate rates are properly configured.

commonIssues.issue: Referral code not applying to trades.
commonIssues.solution: Check if the `order_tag` parameter is being used on orders, as it has higher priority than account-level referral bindings. Ensure the referral code was created under the correct broker.

steps.title: Upgrade SDK for Permissionless Support

steps.important: Permissionless listings allow builders to list any asset not currently on Orderly. As the market owner, the builder earns 100% of liquidation fees plus 50% of Orderly's base fee on that market.

steps.title: Sync Frontend Configuration
steps.description: When new permissionless markets are announced, update your frontend configuration to support the new symbols. Monitor Orderly announcements for new listings.
steps.important: Brokers should sync their frontend configuration when new permissionless markets are announced and notify users accordingly.

steps.title: Handle Chart Data for New Markets
steps.description: SDK v3.1.3 optimizes K-line history loading so the chart stops requesting unavailable historical data before a market's listing time, reducing unnecessary requests and improving page stability.
steps.important: Permissionlessly listed markets are Isolated-only to limit risk exposure.

steps.title: Notify Users of New Markets

commonIssues.issue: Chart requests fail for newly listed markets.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.3+ which optimizes K-line history loading to stop requesting unavailable historical data before a market's listing time.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot use Cross Margin on permissionless markets.
commonIssues.solution: This is by design. Permissionlessly listed markets only support Isolated Margin to limit risk exposure.

Understanding of AI agent integration patterns

steps.description: Launch your own MCP (Model Context Protocol) server and add your brokerID to the Orderly MCP configuration. This enables AI agents to discover and interact with your DEX.
steps.important: The MCP server acts as a bridge between AI agents and your Orderly-powered DEX, providing the agent with the context it needs to trade.

steps.title: Provide the MCP URL to AI Agents

workflows.name: Building Trading Bots with CCXT
workflows.description: Build automated trading bots for an Orderly-powered DEX using the CCXT library via the woofipro exchange class.
prerequisites: Orderly API key, secret, and account ID
Broker ID for your Orderly-powered DEX

steps.title: Install CCXT
steps.description: Install the CCXT library in your Python environment.
steps.code: pip install ccxt

steps.title: Retrieve Your Broker ID
steps.description: If you don't know your broker ID, use the get builder list API endpoint with the broker_id parameter left blank to retrieve all registered brokers.

steps.title: Initialize the Exchange Connection
steps.description: Connect to your Orderly-powered DEX using the `woofipro` exchange class with your API credentials.
steps.code:
import ccxt

exchange = ccxt.woofipro({
    'apiKey': 'ed25519:YOUR_API_KEY',
    'secret': 'ed25519:YOUR_SECRET',
    'accountId': 'YOUR_ACCOUNT_ID'
})

# Load available markets
exchange.load_markets()

# Fetch account balance
balance = exchange.fetch_balance()
print(balance)
steps.important: All Orderly brokers share the same underlying API; only the `brokerId` differs. There is no separate v3 API — use the standard Orderly REST endpoints.

steps.title: Execute Trades
steps.description: Use standard CCXT methods to place orders, fetch positions, and manage your trading bot logic.
steps.code:
# Place a market buy order
order = exchange.create_market_buy_order('PERP_ETH_USDC', 0.01)

# Place a limit sell order
order = exchange.create_limit_sell_order('PERP_ETH_USDC', 0.01, 4000)

# Fetch open positions
positions = exchange.fetch_positions()
print(positions)

steps.title: Implement Risk Management
steps.description: Add stop-loss, take-profit, and position sizing logic to your bot. Be aware of Orderly's stop-loss trigger timing behavior.
steps.important: Stop-Loss orders are triggered by the mark price, which updates approximately every 1 second. In high-volatility conditions, the mark price may move past the SL trigger price between updates.

commonIssues.issue: Authentication errors when connecting.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your API key and secret are prefixed with 'ed25519:' and that your accountId is correct. API keys can be generated from the admin wallet at https://www.cryptotraders.exchange/portfolio/api-key.

commonIssues.issue: Markets not loading.
commonIssues.solution: Verify your broker ID is correct and that the DEX is operational. All Orderly brokers share the same underlying API endpoints.

commonIssues.issue: Stop-loss executing at worse price than expected.
commonIssues.solution: This can happen in high-volatility conditions when the mark price moves past the SL trigger between 1-second updates. Consider setting SL further from liquidation price to avoid liquidation occurring before SL triggers.

steps.title: Ensure Version Alignment

steps.title: Import and Render the Leaderboard Widget

steps.title: Add Campaigns Widget (Optional)

commonIssues.issue: Leaderboard widget not rendering.

workflows.name: Tracking Real-Time Campaign Volume and User Data
workflows.description: Get real-time trading volume data for campaigns, quests, and competitions on your Orderly-powered DEX using dedicated campaign endpoints.
prerequisites: Active Orderly-powered DEX with a broker ID
Campaign set up with Orderly team (with campaign_id)

steps.title: Understand Data Freshness Levels
steps.description: Standard volume endpoints like `get-builders-users-volumes` and `get-builders-leaderboard` are updated hourly or daily. For real-time tracking, use dedicated campaign endpoints.
steps.important: Real-time campaign data is updated approximately every 30 seconds during the campaign period.

steps.title: Set Up a Dedicated Campaign
steps.description: Contact the Orderly team to set up a dedicated trading campaign with a `campaign_id`. This enables real-time volume tracking for the campaign duration.
steps.important: Campaign data is archived after the campaign ends. Starting from Campaign 75, the archiving window is 6 months.

steps.title: Query Campaign Rankings
steps.description: Use the campaign ranking endpoint to rank users by volume or PnL in real-time.
steps.code:
// Rank users by volume or PnL:
GET /v1/public/campaign/ranking?campaign_id={id}&broker_id={broker_id}&sort_by=volume&size=50&page=1

steps.title: Get Per-User Campaign Info
steps.description: Retrieve detailed per-user campaign information including volume, PnL, and progress.
steps.code:
// Detailed per-user info:
GET /v1/public/campaign/user?campaign_id={id}&address={wallet_address}

steps.title: Verify Campaign Criteria
steps.description: Check if a user has met specific campaign criteria (e.g., volume threshold, number of trades).
steps.code:
// Verify user criteria:
GET /v1/public/campaign/verification?campaign_id={id}&address={wallet_address}

steps.title: Map Trading Addresses to Wallet Addresses
steps.description: The address shown on the Orderly leaderboard is the internal trading account address, not the user's actual wallet address. Request address mapping from the Orderly team before distributing rewards.
steps.important: The Orderly technical team can map trading addresses to actual wallet addresses (e.g., Abstract Global Wallet) for campaign reward distribution.

steps.title: Alternative: Run Your Own Indexer
steps.description: For full control, builders can run their own indexer using the open-source `orderly-dashboard` repository, which indexes Orderly Layer 2 data with a sync delay of seconds to minutes.
steps.code:
// Open-source indexer:
// https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/orderly-dashboard

commonIssues.issue: Campaign data no longer accessible after campaign ends.
commonIssues.solution: Campaign data is archived after the campaign ends (6 months for campaigns after ID 75). Export all needed data before the archiving deadline.

commonIssues.issue: Leaderboard shows internal trading addresses instead of wallet addresses.
commonIssues.solution: Request address mapping from the Orderly technical team before distributing rewards. The leaderboard shows internal Orderly account addresses, not user wallet addresses.

commonIssues.issue: Volume data not updating in real-time.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the dedicated campaign endpoints (get-campaign-ranking, get-campaign-user-info) rather than the standard volume endpoints which update hourly/daily.

workflows.name: Enabling Privy and Abstract Global Wallet Authentication
workflows.description: Integrate Privy wallet authentication and Abstract Global Wallet (AGW) into your Orderly-powered DEX for seamless user onboarding.
prerequisites: Privy account and App ID from https://dashboard.privy.io
Orderly SDK with wallet connector packages

steps.title: Install Privy Wallet Connector Package
steps.description: Import `WalletConnectorPrivyProvider` from the separate package `@orderly.network/wallet-connector-privy` (not from `@orderly.network/wallet-connector`).
steps.code: npm install @orderly.network/wallet-connector-privy

steps.title: Wrap App with Privy Provider
steps.description: Wrap your app with the Privy provider and pass your Privy configuration.
steps.code:
// Reference implementation:
// https://github.com/OrderlyNetworkDexCreator/dex-creator-template/blob/main/app/components/orderlyProvider/privyConnector.tsx

import { WalletConnectorPrivyProvider } from "@orderly.network/wallet-connector-privy";

<WalletConnectorPrivyProvider
  privyAppId="YOUR_PRIVY_APP_ID"
>
  <OrderlyAppProvider
    brokerId="your_broker_id"
    brokerName="Your Broker"
    networkId="mainnet"
  >
    {children}
  </OrderlyAppProvider>
</WalletConnectorPrivyProvider>
steps.important: The Orderly team does not automatically upgrade the Privy dependency to the latest version to avoid breaking changes. If you need a newer Privy SDK feature, use the Privy SDK directly alongside the standard Orderly Wallet Connector.

steps.title: Configure Abstract Global Wallet (AGW)
steps.description: For AGW integration, set up Privy at https://dashboard.privy.io and provide the Privy App ID to the Orderly SDK. In the DEX creator, enable Abstract wallet support and configure chain selection to Abstract only.
steps.important: AGW integration requires Privy as the underlying authentication provider.

steps.title: Prioritize Abstract Wallet in Login UI
steps.description: To prioritize Abstract wallet in the login UI, go to Privy settings: User Authentication > Advanced > Prioritise Options Displayed, and select Web3 wallets.

steps.description: If using a multisig wallet (e.g., Gnosis Safe) to collect broker fees, you cannot directly sign in to Orderly because multisig wallets cannot sign the messages required for generating Orderly credentials. Instead, delegate an EOA (Externally Owned Account) wallet to act as the signer on behalf of the multisig.
steps.important: The EOA can be replaced later using the same delegation process. The EOA only has signing authority — funds are always credited to the multisig account.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base fee that varies by Builder Tier (e.g., 2.5 bps for Public tier, 2 bps for Platinum, 1 bp for Diamond). Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection and Withdraw Revenue
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account. Log in to the DEX UI with the admin wallet used to create the DEX. The revenue generated will appear as a trading balance that can be withdrawn directly through the DEX frontend.
steps.code:
GET /v1/holding
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id
steps.important: Revenue withdrawal is done through the DEX frontend itself, not through the Orderly One dashboard.

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.

commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Multisig wallet cannot sign Orderly credentials.
commonIssues.solution: Use the delegate signer feature to assign an EOA wallet to sign on behalf of the multisig. Register the delegation at the broker registration portal.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: Users confused about position settlement after delisting.
commonIssues.solution: Communicate clearly that the index price is fixed at the average price of the last hour before delisting. All open positions are settled at this price.

commonIssues.issue: Token still showing in UI after delisting.
commonIssues.solution: Update your frontend configuration to remove the delisted token. For SDK builders, ensure your symbol list is synced with Orderly's current listings.

workflows.name: Understanding and Managing Account Transfers, Sub-Accounts, and Liquidations
workflows.description: Handle account operations including device transfers, sub-account fund management, partial vs full liquidations, and key management best practices.

steps.title: Transfer Orderly Account to a New Device
steps.description: Transfer account credentials via QR code or export. The Orderly key is bound to the device where it was created — generating a new key on a new device creates a separate key, not a migration.
steps.important: If using biometric authentication, the key is tied to the original device's biometric profile. You must export/transfer credentials rather than regenerate them.

steps.title: Manage Sub-Account Fund Transfers
steps.description: Only the main account can make deposits and withdrawals. Sub-accounts only support internal fund transfers between the main account and the sub-account.
steps.important: Funds deposited always go to the main account first, and withdrawals also originate from the main account. Sub-accounts and main accounts share the same credentials, so there is no way to differentiate them outside of Orderly for direct on-chain deposits/withdrawals.

steps.title: Understand Partial vs Full Liquidation
steps.description: Partial liquidation occurs when the margin ratio falls below a threshold but is not critically low — only a portion of the position is liquidated. Full liquidation closes the entire position when the margin ratio is critically low, total notional value falls below minimum, or margin ratio equals the target ratio.
steps.important: The outcome depends on the liquidator, the position's notional value, and the symbol. Isolated margin mode (in development) will allow users to separate risk across positions.

steps.title: Configure Isolated Margin Mode
steps.description: Isolated margin mode (SDK v2.11.0+) allows users to allocate specific collateral to individual positions. Users can hold positions in both cross and isolated margin modes simultaneously.
steps.important: When maxing out an isolated margin market order, the SDK reserves a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula to prevent 'margin will be insufficient' rejections.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot deposit directly to a sub-account.
commonIssues.solution: This is by design. All deposits go to the main account first. Use internal fund transfers to move funds from the main account to sub-accounts.

commonIssues.issue: Orderly key lost when switching devices.
commonIssues.solution: Export/transfer credentials before switching devices. Generating a new key on a new device creates a separate key and does not migrate the existing one.

commonIssues.issue: Position liquidated unexpectedly.
commonIssues.solution: Check if partial liquidation thresholds were breached. For isolated margin positions, ensure sufficient collateral is allocated to the specific position.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration

steps.title: Provide Broker Details to Orderly Team
steps.description: Submit your Broker ID (cannot be changed later), Broker Name, Default Taker Fee, Default Maker Fee, and Tier to the Orderly team for initial setup.
steps.important: The Broker ID is permanent once created. Choose it carefully. The fee collection wallet and admin wallet must currently be the same address.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet on Testnet (for Staging)
steps.description: Connect your wallet to a supported testnet (e.g., Ethereum Sepolia) and complete registration via the broker registration UI. The Orderly team must configure the wallet as an admin via a multisig process.
steps.code:
// Testnet broker registration:
https://orderlynetwork.github.io/broker-registration/
steps.important: If you need a separate admin wallet on mainnet for staging (distinct from production), a second broker ID must be set up.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates.

steps.title: Update Default Broker Fee via CLI (Alternative)
steps.description: Use the Python CLI tool to update the default broker fee. Default fees update immediately, but remove any existing fee overrides first.
steps.code:
python3 app/main.py update-broker-default-fee <maker_fee> <taker_fee>

# Example:
python3 app/main.py update-broker-default-fee 0.0000 0.0003
steps.important: There is an asynchronous delay of approximately 20–30 minutes before updated fee rates propagate to users who haven't traded recently. Running a volume-based rate script periodically can help: python3 app/main.py update-user-rate-base-volume

steps.title: Configure Custom Fee Tiers (Optional)
steps.description: Set fee tiers based on trading volume or staked ORDER via the Builder Staking Programme for more granular fee control.
steps.code:
// Builder Staking Programme docs:
https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/user-flows/builder-staking-programme
steps.important: Fee tiers can be set based on trading volume or staked ORDER tokens.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection and Withdraw
steps.description: Broker fees are credited to the configured admin (fee) wallet. View and withdraw by logging into the broker's DEX UI with the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: Updated fees not reflecting for users after 30 minutes.
commonIssues.solution: This is expected behavior due to asynchronous propagation. Run the volume-based rate script (python3 app/main.py update-user-rate-base-volume) periodically to accelerate updates for inactive users.

steps.title: Monitor Maintenance via Announcement API
steps.description: Consume the Orderly announcement API to display maintenance warnings on your custom frontend. Orderly also pushes updates to a dedicated Telegram channel for builders.
steps.important: There is a user-level option to automatically close all positions during maintenance. Builders should surface maintenance warnings prominently.

steps.title: Detect Public Liquidation Events
steps.description: Use the public REST endpoint to get all positions currently under liquidation across all accounts.
steps.important: The public endpoint does not include an accountId field. It shows all liquidations but cannot be filtered by specific user.

steps.title: Query Specific User's Liquidation History
steps.description: Use the authenticated private endpoint to get liquidation records for a specific user's own account.
steps.code:
GET /v1/private/liquidated_positions_of_account
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id

// Docs:
https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-evm/evm-api/restful-api/private/get-liquidated-positions-of-account
steps.important: This requires authentication, so you cannot query arbitrary accounts. Orderly does not provide public per-account liquidation data via API.

steps.title: Check Liquidation History via Dashboard
steps.description: Use the Orderly Dashboard to check a user's liquidation history, trade history, and other account details.
steps.code:
// Dashboard URL:
https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/?broker_id=<your_broker_id>
steps.important: For settled liquidations not available via API, you may need to read data directly on-chain or use the Orderly dashboard query service.

steps.title: Understand Maintenance Margin Ratio (MMR) Triggers
steps.description: Orderly uses a cross-margin system. The MMR defines the minimum balance required relative to position notional value. If unrealized losses reduce the account balance below the MMR threshold, the position is liquidated.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot query another user's liquidation history.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly does not provide public per-account liquidation data via API. Use the public endpoint for all liquidations (without account IDs) or the private endpoint for the authenticated user only.

commonIssues.issue: Settled liquidation data not available via API.
commonIssues.solution: For settled liquidations, read data directly on-chain or use the Orderly dashboard query service at https://orderly-dashboard-query-service.orderly.network/events.

workflows.name: Troubleshooting SDK TypeScript and Dependency Conflicts
workflows.description: Resolve common TypeScript compilation errors and dependency conflicts when building with Orderly SDK v2, including ethers v5/v6 conflicts and hook usage issues.

steps.title: Resolve ethers v5/v6 Type Conflicts
steps.description: The error 'Type BytesLike is not assignable to type string' in abi-coder.ts is caused by multiple ethers versions. Orderly SDK v2 depends on ethers v6.
steps.code:
# Delete node_modules and lock file, then regenerate:
rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json
npm install

# If using yarn, force ethers v6 via resolutions:
# package.json:
"resolutions": {
  "ethers": "^6.0.0"
}
steps.important: Check that ./node_modules/@orderly.network/core/node_modules/ethers resolves to v6.

steps.title: Debug useCollateral and useOrderEntry Hooks
steps.description: If useCollateral shows holdings but useOrderEntry returns maxQty = 0, the issue is typically with order type or form validation, not the collateral balance.
steps.important: It is strongly recommended to deploy the reference Orderly UI alongside your integration for debugging purposes to compare behavior.

steps.title: Set Leverage Programmatically with useSymbolLeverage
steps.description: Use the useSymbolLeverage hook to set leverage for a symbol. The leverageLevers array from useCollateral is for UI display only.
steps.important: The leverageLevers array (e.g., [1, 25, 50, 75, 100]) returned by useCollateral is for UI display only and can be ignored when setting leverage programmatically.

steps.title: Enable Isolated Margin Mode
steps.description: Isolated margin mode must be manually enabled by the Orderly team for each broker ID. Contact the Orderly team with your broker ID to request activation.
steps.important: It is recommended to first enable and test isolated margin in the staging environment, as the feature may be in beta.

commonIssues.issue: Type 'BytesLike' is not assignable to type 'string' in abi-coder.ts.
commonIssues.solution: Delete node_modules and lock file, then regenerate. If your project uses ethers v5, use yarn resolutions to force ethers v6 or isolate the dependency.

commonIssues.issue: maxQty is 0 despite having collateral balance.
commonIssues.solution: Check order parameters (type, side, symbol) in useOrderEntry. Deploy the reference Orderly UI for comparison debugging.

commonIssues.issue: Isolated margin mode not available.
commonIssues.solution: Contact the Orderly team to enable isolated margin for your broker ID. Test in staging first.

workflows.name: Joining Trading Competitions via API

steps.title: Verify Trading is Enabled
steps.description: Ensure the user's account has trading enabled (AccountStatusEnum.EnableTrading) before attempting to join a competition.
steps.important: Users must have trading enabled before they can join a competition.

steps.title: Call the Competition Join Endpoint
steps.description: Make a POST request to the competition join endpoint with standard orderly-* authentication headers. No request body is needed.
steps.code:
POST /v1/client/competition/join
Headers:
  orderly-timestamp: <timestamp>
  orderly-account-id: <account_id>
  orderly-key: <api_key>
  orderly-signature: <signature>

// No request body required
steps.important: The system automatically tracks all trades from the DEX, but users must call this endpoint to appear on the leaderboard.

steps.title: Verify Leaderboard Appearance
steps.description: After joining, verify that the user appears on the competition leaderboard by querying the campaign ranking endpoint.
steps.code: GET /v1/public/campaign/ranking?campaign_id={id}&broker_id={broker_id}&sort_by=volume&size={pageSize}&page={page}

commonIssues.issue: User cannot join competition despite having an account.
commonIssues.solution: Verify that the user's account status is AccountStatusEnum.EnableTrading. Accounts without trading enabled cannot join competitions.

commonIssues.issue: User joined but not appearing on leaderboard.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the POST /v1/client/competition/join call was successful. The system tracks trades automatically, but the join endpoint must be called explicitly.

workflows.name: Implementing Copy Trading on Orderly
workflows.description: Build a copy trading system on your Orderly-powered DEX using subaccounts, internal transfers, and the order enum feature for custom fee structures.
prerequisites: Active broker ID with API access
Backend infrastructure for managing lead trader signals
Understanding of Orderly subaccount and internal transfer APIs

steps.title: Design Copy Trading Architecture
steps.description: Plan your copy trading system. Orderly does not natively provide real-time trade signals or order details of other users. Common approaches include: (1) Lead traders set up read-only API keys, (2) Monitor order placement via frontend API requests, (3) Listen to trade notifications.
steps.important: Copy trading typically tracks position changes rather than individual order details. Position history is available on-chain.

steps.title: Set Up Subaccounts for Fund Isolation
steps.description: Use subaccounts to isolate copy trading funds from users' main accounts.
steps.important: Subaccounts allow you to separate copy trading capital and manage risk independently.

steps.title: Implement Lead Trader Signal Capture
steps.description: Set up a mechanism to capture lead trader orders. Options include having lead traders provide read-only API keys or monitoring their order placement through your frontend.
steps.important: Order information is private on Orderly. You cannot access other users' order details without their explicit API key sharing.

steps.title: Configure Custom Fees with Order Enum
steps.description: Use the order enum feature to apply custom additional fees per order, useful for copy trading fee structures where copiers pay a premium.
steps.important: Order enum is particularly useful for copy trading or automated trading strategies where extra fees need to be charged.

steps.title: Execute Copy Trades via API
steps.description: When a lead trader's signal is captured, programmatically place matching orders for all copiers using the Orderly API.
steps.important: Consider slippage and timing differences when copying trades across multiple accounts.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot access lead trader's order details in real-time.
commonIssues.solution: Have lead traders set up read-only API keys for your copy trading system, or monitor order placement through frontend API requests.

commonIssues.issue: Copy trades experience significant slippage.
commonIssues.solution: Implement batch order execution and consider using limit orders instead of market orders to reduce slippage for copiers.

commonIssues.issue: Users interfere with copy trading bot orders.
commonIssues.solution: Use subaccounts to isolate copy trading funds. Communicate clearly to users that they should not manually trade on subaccounts managed by the copy trading system.

workflows.name: Implementing Grid Trading with Isolated Funds
workflows.description: Build a grid trading bot on Orderly using subaccounts for fund isolation and internal transfers to separate grid strategy capital from user main accounts.
prerequisites: Active broker ID with API access
Understanding of Orderly subaccount and internal transfer APIs

steps.title: Create Subaccounts for Grid Strategies
steps.description: Use subaccounts to create isolated execution spaces for each grid trading strategy instance.
steps.important: Grid trading requires isolated execution spaces to prevent strategy orders from interfering with users' manual trades.

steps.title: Transfer Funds to Grid Subaccount
steps.description: Move the allocated grid trading capital from the user's main Orderly account to the dedicated subaccount using internal transfers.
steps.code:
POST /v1/internal-transfer
Body: {
  "from_account": "main_account_id",
  "to_account": "grid_subaccount_id",
  "token": "USDC",
  "amount": "1000"
}
steps.important: Internal transfers between Orderly accounts are instant and do not incur gas fees.

steps.title: Execute Grid Orders via API
steps.description: Place and manage grid orders programmatically using the Orderly API on the subaccount.
steps.important: Monitor grid order status and adjust the grid as market conditions change.

steps.title: Handle User Frontend Intervention
steps.description: Be aware that if users access the API directly, they may interfere with grid strategy orders. Currently, there is no built-in mechanism to prevent this.
steps.important: A disclaimer is the only interim solution. Hidden sub-account functionality may be needed for full grid trading support in the future.

commonIssues.issue: Users manually modify or cancel grid bot orders.
commonIssues.solution: Currently, there is no built-in mechanism to prevent user frontend intervention on grid bot orders. Use disclaimers and consider implementing hidden sub-account functionality.

commonIssues.issue: Grid orders fail due to insufficient margin in subaccount.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure sufficient funds are transferred to the subaccount before placing grid orders. Monitor margin requirements as positions accumulate.

commonIssues.issue: Internal transfer fails between accounts.
commonIssues.solution: Verify that both the source and destination accounts exist and that the transfer amount does not exceed available balance.

workflows.name: Setting Up and Staking ORDER for Builder Tier Upgrades
workflows.description: Stake ORDER tokens to upgrade your broker tier in the Builder Staking Programme, unlocking lower taker fees, negative maker fees, and additional benefits.

steps.title: Understand the Tier System
steps.description: Review the Builder Tier System. Tiers are based on 30-day average trading volume OR ORDER tokens staked. Higher tiers offer reduced fees and additional benefits.
steps.important:
Tiers:
- Public: Default, 2.5 bps taker fee
- Silver/Gold: Reduced fees at higher thresholds
- Platinum: 2 bps taker fee (≥ $1B 30d volume OR 2M ORDER staked)
- Diamond: 1 bps taker fee (≥ $10B 30d volume OR 7M ORDER staked)
Maker fees remain at 0 bps (or negative at Silver+).

steps.title: Stake ORDER Tokens
steps.description: If using Orderly One, stake directly from the dashboard's graduation page using the DEX creation wallet. Alternatively, use any wallet for staking and provide the staking address to Orderly support for manual configuration.
steps.important: The staking address can be changed, but the Orderly One admin wallet address cannot be changed.

steps.title: Verify Tier Upgrade
steps.description: After staking, verify that your broker tier has been upgraded by checking your fee rates or contacting Orderly support.
steps.important: Tier upgrades based on staking are processed after the staking transaction is confirmed.

steps.title: Understand Unstaking Rules
steps.description: Be aware of the unstaking and conversion periods before committing ORDER tokens.
steps.important: Unstaking ORDER requires a 7-day waiting period. esORDER requires a 90-day conversion period to ORDER with no yield during conversion.

steps.title: Leverage Negative Maker Fees (Silver+ Tiers)
steps.description: At Silver tier and above, negative maker fees are applied. These settle immediately on each execution for traders. Builder maker and taker revenue are batched and settled together once per day.
steps.code:
// More details:
https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/trading-basics/trading-fees#builder-staking-programme
steps.important: As of May 2026, maker fee rebates are live: maker fees can be set to negative values (-0.5bps to 0), meaning Orderly subsidizes makers.

commonIssues.issue: Tier not upgrading after staking ORDER.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the staking address is correctly associated with your broker ID. If using a non-Orderly One wallet, contact Orderly support to manually configure the association.

commonIssues.issue: Need to unstake ORDER urgently.
commonIssues.solution: Unstaking requires a 7-day waiting period. Plan staking commitments accordingly.

commonIssues.issue: esORDER conversion taking too long.
commonIssues.solution: esORDER requires a 90-day conversion period to ORDER with no yield during conversion. This is by design and cannot be expedited.

workflows.name: Managing RWA Perpetual Markets on Orderly
workflows.description: Understand and manage Real World Asset (RWA) perpetual trading on Orderly, including weekend trading mechanics, price bands, and fee structures.

steps.title: Understand RWA Market Types
steps.description: Orderly supports RWA perpetuals including US stocks (NVDA, TSLA, GOOGL, etc.), commodities (gold, silver via CME), and forex pairs (JPY/USD, EUR/USD). These use USDC collateral with no actual token or on-chain settlement.
steps.important: RWA perps are purely perpetual contracts — there is no actual token settlement. Liquidity for commodities comes from CME via market makers.

steps.title: Handle Weekend and Off-Hour Trading
steps.description: RWA markets use price bands during weekends and off-hours when traditional markets are closed. Orderly applies mark price ±1% bands to protect against manipulation during thin liquidity periods.
steps.important: Trading can continue during CME closures (weekends) with MM-provided quotes and static index prices. When markets reopen, bands are removed and price discovery normalizes.

steps.title: Understand RWA Fee Structure
steps.description: RWA taker fees are tier-based and aligned with crypto pair fees (1-3 bps depending on your builder tier).
steps.important: RWA pair fees are now aligned with crypto pair fees. Your builder tier determines the exact rate.

steps.title: Monitor Oracle Sources
steps.description: Orderly uses multiple oracles for RWA pricing: Finage, Tradermade, Pragma, Pyth, Stork, and Chainlink.
steps.important: Multiple oracle sources ensure robust pricing even during off-hours.

steps.title: Communicate Weekend Risks to Users
steps.description: Inform users that liquidity can be thin during weekends, which may result in wider spreads and the ±1% price band limiting price movement.
steps.important: Users should be aware that weekend RWA trading carries additional spread and liquidity risks.

commonIssues.issue: RWA prices seem stuck during weekends.
commonIssues.solution: This is expected behavior. Orderly applies ±1% price bands during off-hours to protect against manipulation. Prices normalize when traditional markets reopen.

commonIssues.issue: Wide spreads on RWA pairs during weekends.
commonIssues.solution: Liquidity is naturally thinner during weekends when CME and traditional markets are closed. Market makers provide quotes but spreads may be wider.

commonIssues.issue: Users confused about RWA settlement.
commonIssues.solution: Clearly communicate that RWA perps use USDC collateral and are purely perpetual contracts — there is no actual stock, commodity, or forex token settlement.

workflows.description: Programmatically register users for Orderly trading competitions and integrate reward claiming directly into your DEX frontend.
prerequisites: Active broker ID with API access
Users with Orderly accounts under your broker ID
Backend capable of signing API requests

steps.title: Register Users for Competitions
steps.description: Use the competition join endpoint to register users programmatically. Since the broker holds private keys for managed accounts, registration can be signed and submitted from the operator backend.
steps.important: The leaderboard uses a hybrid volatility-adjusted scoring mechanism (based on modified ROI) considering both PnL and ROI. Daily points are recalculated hourly based on UTC 00:00 account balance.

steps.title: Check User Reward Status
steps.description: Query the competition prizes endpoint to check a user's rank, points, prize amount, and claim status.
steps.important: The claim window is configurable per season. Check claim_expires_at to inform users of deadlines.

steps.title: Initiate Reward Claims
steps.description: Use the claim endpoint to initiate reward distribution for eligible users.
steps.important: Rewards are credited directly to the user's Orderly perpetual account — no external wallet transaction required.

steps.title: Build Frontend Claiming UI
steps.description: Create a competition dashboard in your DEX frontend that shows user rankings, points, and a claim button for eligible rewards.
steps.important: Display the claim_expires_at deadline prominently to encourage timely claiming.

commonIssues.issue: Competition join API call fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure all orderly-* headers (timestamp, account-id, key, signature) are correctly generated and that the user has an active Orderly account.

commonIssues.issue: User reward shows as 'expired'.
commonIssues.solution: The claim window has passed. Each season has a configurable claim_expires_at deadline. Communicate deadlines clearly to users.

commonIssues.issue: Points calculation seems inconsistent.
commonIssues.solution: Points use a hybrid volatility-adjusted scoring mechanism based on modified ROI, not just raw PnL. Daily points are recalculated hourly.

steps.important: The Orderly team will align with market makers accordingly based on your requirements.

steps.title: Monitor Liquidity Improvements
steps.description: After the liquidity team has coordinated with market makers, monitor the pair's spread, depth, and slippage metrics to verify improvements.
steps.important: Continue to provide volume data and feedback to the liquidity team for ongoing optimization.

commonIssues.issue: Liquidity improvement request not prioritized.
commonIssues.solution: Provide concrete volume projections and demonstrated growth. Liquidity improvements are prioritized for pairs with clear volume potential.

commonIssues.issue: Spreads remain wide after liquidity request.
commonIssues.solution: Work with the Orderly team to refine targets. Some pairs may have inherent liquidity constraints based on the underlying asset.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, set up default trading fees, and manage fee revenue.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions

steps.title: Provide Broker Details to Orderly Team
steps.description: Submit your desired Broker ID, Broker Name, Default Taker Fee, and Default Maker Fee to the Orderly team to create your broker ID.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base fee of 2.5 bps (0.025%) taker and 0% maker. Anything charged above the base fee is retained by the broker. For example, setting a 0.06% taker fee means the broker earns 0.035% (0.06% - 0.025%).

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature on mainnet. Different wallets can be used for mainnet and testnet. The chain you register on does not need to match your deployment chain.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.025% (2.5 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates. The fee rate cannot be changed via the API endpoint /v1/broker/fee_rate/default without proper authentication.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account. Check the balance by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet, clicking 'Enable trading' to sign the transaction, or using the private Get Current Holding endpoint.

steps.title: View Broker Metrics on Dune
steps.description: Filter and view broker-specific metrics on the Dune dashboard using your broker ID.

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause. Contact the Orderly team in the main group if you need to negotiate custom base fee rates.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised or needs to be changed.
commonIssues.solution: Register the new wallet address as an Orderly account at the broker registration portal, then request the wallet change from the Orderly team providing the new wallet address and broker ID. Changing the master wallet causes no downtime and does not affect fee data or historical records.

commonIssues.issue: Fees appear as zero despite trading activity.
commonIssues.solution: Contact the Orderly tech support team with your admin wallet address to investigate missing fee credits. Ensure you have clicked 'Enable trading' to sign the transaction when checking balances.

workflows.name: Adding Custom Chains to Orderly SDK
workflows.description: Add support for new chains like Story, Solana, Monad Testnet, or Sei to your Orderly-powered DEX using the chainFilter prop in OrderlyAppProvider.
prerequisites: Chain ID of the target network
Broker ID registered on the target chain (if applicable)

steps.title: Import Chain Types
steps.description: Import the necessary chain types from @orderly.network/types for built-in chains.
steps.code: import { Arbitrum, Optimism } from "@orderly.network/types";

steps.title: Configure chainFilter Prop for Mainnet Chains
steps.description: Use the chainFilter prop on OrderlyAppProvider to specify which mainnet chains to enable, including custom chains by their ID.
steps.code:
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  brokerName="Your Broker"
  networkId="mainnet"
  chainFilter={{
    mainnet: [
      Arbitrum,
      Optimism,
      { id: 90009090 }, // Solana
      { id: 1514 },     // Story Protocol
    ],
  }}
>
  {children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
steps.important: Chain IDs can be found at chainlist.org. For Solana, use ID 90009090. For Story Protocol, use ID 1514.

steps.title: Add Testnet Chains with Full Configuration
steps.description: To add testnet chains like Monad Testnet, use the testnet key in chainFilter with full chain configuration including RPC URL and currency details.
steps.important: Your broker_id must be registered on testnet as well. For mainnet-only deployments, pass {testnet: []} to disable testnet chains.

steps.title: Set a Default Chain Programmatically
steps.description: Use the useStorageChain and useAppContext hooks to programmatically set the default chain for users.
steps.important: The OrderlyAppProvider does not have a networkConfig property for setting the default chain. If you only want to support a single chain, use chainFilter to exclude all other chains.

steps.title: Handle Network Switching
steps.description: The networkId cannot change during runtime. Use a page refresh or separate domain when switching between testnet and mainnet.
steps.important: For Solana support, ensure you are using SDK v2.0.0+ (Hooks SDK) and have applied the Solana Multi-DVN security upgrade (v2.12.3+).

commonIssues.issue: Chain does not appear in the chain selector.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the chain ID is correct and that the chainFilter prop is properly structured. For testnets, ensure showTestnet is not set to false in overrides.

commonIssues.issue: Solana deposits/withdrawals fail.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you have upgraded to SDK v2.12.3+ for the mandatory Solana Multi-DVN security upgrade.

commonIssues.issue: Default chain not applying.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the useStorageChain and useAppContext hooks correctly. The OrderlyAppProvider does not support a networkConfig property for default chain selection.

Admin wallet or any registered user wallet for API auth

steps.title: Fetch Daily Trading Volumes via API
steps.description: Use the public daily volume API endpoint to retrieve user trading volumes by epoch for campaigns or quests.
steps.important: The Orderly team has indicated plans to create a fully public endpoint (no auth required) and a dedicated campaign ranking API.

steps.title: Query Campaign Rankings
steps.description: Use the campaign ranking API to get sorted leaderboard data for trading competitions.
steps.code: GET https://api-evm.orderly.org/v1/public/campaign/ranking?campaign_id={id}&broker_id={broker_id}&sort_by=volume&size=100&page=1

steps.title: Check User Liquidation and Position History via Dashboard
steps.description: Construct a URL with the user's wallet address and broker ID to view their complete trading history including deposits, trades, partial liquidations, and position closures.

steps.title: Retrieve Historical Volume Data via Kline API
steps.description: For historical volume aggregation over time, use the Kline (candlestick) REST endpoint since paginated historical volume endpoints are not available.

steps.title: Fetch Liquidation History
steps.description: Retrieve liquidation history via the public REST API endpoint.

steps.title: Derive Orderly Account ID from Wallet Address
steps.description: The Orderly account ID is calculated by hashing the wallet address + broker ID. Use this to find users who traded with your broker ID.

commonIssues.issue: Volume API returns empty data.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the API authentication is using a wallet registered under your broker ID. The endpoint filters data based on the authenticated broker.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot find a specific user's trading history.

commonIssues.issue: Need bulk historical volume data.

workflows.name: Understanding Orderly Margin, Leverage, and Position Mechanics
workflows.description: Understand how cross margin, isolated margin, leverage, and position tracking work on Orderly to build accurate trading UIs and handle user queries.
prerequisites: Understanding of perpetual futures trading concepts

steps.title: Understand Cross Margin vs Isolated Margin
steps.description: Orderly supports both cross margin (account-level) and isolated margin (position-level, SDK v2.11.0+). Cross margin shares collateral across all positions, while isolated margin dedicates specific collateral to individual positions.
steps.important: Isolated margin mode is supported starting from SDK v2.11.0 and is rolled out gradually across all Orderly DEXs. SDK v2.12.0 adds UI labels on TradingView chart position lines displaying cross/isolated margin mode labels along with leverage.

steps.title: Handle Account-Level Leverage
steps.description: Leverage on Orderly is account-level (cross margin), not per-order. The configured max account leverage is a cap that prevents creating positions with excessive leverage.
steps.important: Opening a position does not deduct USDC from the displayed balance in cross margin mode. The system tracks margin usage via the margin ratio.

steps.title: Display Available Trading Capacity
steps.description: To show users their available trading capacity, display free collateral and estimated leverage based on input parameters. The Hooks SDK provides hooks that calculate these values automatically.

steps.title: Determine Long vs Short from Position API
steps.description: Check the quantity field in the position response to determine position direction.

steps.title: Handle Isolated Margin Max Order Bug Fix
steps.description: SDK v3.1.0 fixes an issue where maxing out an isolated margin market order at 100% was incorrectly rejected. The SDK now reserves a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula.
steps.important: Ensure you are on SDK v3.1.0+ to avoid false rejections when users max out isolated margin positions.

steps.title: Understand Price Tick Rules
steps.description: Order prices must satisfy the tick rule: (price - quote_min) % quote_tick == 0. The price must be evenly divisible by the quote_tick.

commonIssues.issue: USDC balance does not decrease when opening a position.
commonIssues.solution: This is expected behavior with cross margin. Opening a position does not deduct USDC from the displayed balance. Instead, the system tracks margin usage via the margin ratio. Display free collateral to show available capacity.

commonIssues.issue: Isolated margin market order at 100% is rejected.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.0+ which fixes this issue by reserving a taker fee buffer matching the backend frozen-margin formula.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot cancel individual TP or SL from a Position_TP_SL trigger order.
commonIssues.solution: You cannot cancel an individual child order (TP or SL) from a Position_TP_SL trigger. You must cancel the entire parent order and recreate it with only the desired child order(s).

commonIssues.issue: Order price rejected by tick rule.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the order price satisfies (price - quote_min) % quote_tick == 0. The price must be evenly divisible by the quote_tick value for that symbol.

workflows.name: Integrating Custom Wallet Providers and Custodial Solutions
workflows.description: Integrate custom wallet providers like Privy or Turnkey, or implement centralized custodial wallet solutions for deposits and withdrawals without requiring users to hold gas tokens.
prerequisites: Orderly React SDK or Core SDK installed
Custom wallet provider that supports EIP-712 message signing

steps.title: Verify EIP-712 Signing Support
steps.description: Ensure your wallet provider supports signing EIP-712 messages, which is required for Orderly authentication and order signing.
steps.important: If the wallet provider supports signing EIP-712 messages, it can work with Orderly.

steps.title: Implement Custom Wallet Connection Provider
steps.description: Follow the Orderly documentation to implement a custom wallet connection provider for solutions like Privy or Turnkey.

steps.title: Implement Custodial Deposit Flow
steps.description: For centralized (offchain/custodial) wallets, create an EOA address for the user, sign EIP-712 to register and create Orderly keys, then deposit from the master wallet.
steps.important: This avoids needing to fund each user EOA with gas tokens for multiple transactions.

steps.title: Implement Custodial Withdrawal Flow
steps.description: For withdrawals from custodial accounts, have the user's EOA sign the withdrawal message with the receiver set to the master wallet.
steps.important: This approach avoids needing to fund each user EOA with gas tokens for withdrawal transactions.

commonIssues.issue: Custom wallet provider fails to sign Orderly messages.
commonIssues.solution: Verify that the wallet provider fully supports EIP-712 message signing. Some wallet abstraction solutions may not implement this standard correctly.

commonIssues.issue: Custodial deposits fail to credit user accounts.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the EIP-712 registration was completed successfully and that the depositTo function is called with the correct user Orderly account ID derived from their EOA address and broker ID.

commonIssues.issue: Users need gas tokens for transactions.
commonIssues.solution: Use the custodial deposit/withdrawal flow where the master wallet handles all on-chain transactions, eliminating the need for individual user EOAs to hold gas tokens.

workflows.description: Customize the Orderly trading interface beyond basic CSS changes, including building custom components with the Hooks SDK and handling platform-specific input formatting.
prerequisites: Orderly React SDK or Hooks SDK installed

steps.title: Apply Minor CSS Customizations
steps.description: For minor customizations like changing colors or hiding elements, modify the CSS via theme.css to override the original design.
steps.code:
/* Override colors, spacing, and other CSS properties */
/* in your theme.css file */

steps.title: Build Custom Components with Hooks SDK
steps.description: For significant UI changes (rearranging components, adding new input fields, rebuilding the order entry form), build from scratch using the React Hooks SDK.

steps.title: Build Custom Order Entry Component
steps.description: Use the useOrderEntryScript hook from @orderly.network/ui-order-entry to build a fully custom order entry component.

steps.title: Handle iOS Decimal Input Formatting
steps.description: On iOS, the decimal separator (dot or comma) on the numeric keyboard is determined by the device's region/language settings. Handle both formats in your input components.
steps.code:
<input inputmode="decimal" pattern="[0-9]*[.,]?[0-9]*">

// In JavaScript, convert commas to dots before parsing:
value = value.replace(',', '.');
steps.important: You cannot force a specific decimal separator on the native iOS numeric keyboard. Always handle both dot and comma separators.

steps.title: Consider Orderly DEX Portal for No-Code Customization
steps.description: The Orderly DEX portal provides a no-code/low-code way to customize your DEX while maintaining SDK updates automatically.
steps.code:
// Orderly DEX Portal:
// https://dex.orderly.network/

commonIssues.issue: iOS numeric keyboard shows comma but app expects dot.
commonIssues.solution: Use inputmode='decimal' with pattern='[0-9]*[.,]?[0-9]*' and convert commas to dots in JavaScript before parsing: value = value.replace(',', '.').

commonIssues.issue: Pre-built SDK components are too limiting for custom designs.
commonIssues.solution: Switch to the Hooks SDK for full flexibility. Use hooks like useOrderEntryScript to build custom components while leveraging Orderly's business logic.

commonIssues.issue: Custom components break after SDK updates.
commonIssues.solution: When building custom components with the Hooks SDK, rely on stable hook interfaces rather than internal implementation details. Consider the Orderly DEX portal for automatic update compatibility.

workflows.name: Calculating and Querying Broker Fees from Indexer Database
workflows.description: Calculate broker fees, differentiate trade types, and query executed trades using the Orderly dashboard indexer database and Builder Leaderboard API.
prerequisites: Access to Orderly dashboard indexer database
Broker ID configured in the analyzer

steps.title: Understand Fee Data Limitations in Indexer
steps.description: The Orderly dashboard indexer database does not index whether a trade is maker or taker, and this information is not published to the blockchain.
steps.important: The side field in the partitioned_executed_trades table indicates trade direction (true = sell/short, false = buy/long), NOT maker/taker status.

steps.title: Use Builder Leaderboard API for Fee Calculation
steps.description: To calculate fees with maker/taker differentiation, use the Builder Leaderboard API endpoint which returns total_fee and broker_fee per user per day.
steps.important: Broker fees are aggregated and distributed daily, not per individual trade.

steps.title: Query Executed Trades by Transaction ID
steps.description: Join partitioned_executed_trades with serial_batches on block_number and transaction_index to query trades by transaction_id.
steps.important: Do not use log_index for joining as it differs between the two tables. Use block_number and transaction_index.

steps.title: Run the Dashboard Analyzer
steps.description: Use the orderly-dashboard-analyzer to process indexed blockchain data into a queryable database for your broker.
steps.code:
orderly-dashboard-analyzer --config-path <CONFIG_PATH> -s <START_BLOCK> -e <END_BLOCK>

// Config example (config.json):
{
  "indexer_address": "http://<IP>:8018",
  "start_block": 25200000,
  "start_block_timestamp": 1743484800,
  "pull_interval": 2,
  "batch_block_num": 500,
  "server_port": 8019,
  "get_broker_url": "https://api-evm.orderly.org/v1/public/broker/name"
}
steps.important: The broker_id must be pre-filled in the broker_info table (with broker_id and broker_hash) before running the analyzer. If data is missing, delete the analyzer database and re-run from the desired start block.

steps.title: Filter Trades by Broker Using User Info
steps.description: The user_info table contains account_id, wallet address, and broker_id for registered users. Join with user_perp_summary to filter trades by broker.
steps.code:
// Join user_info with user_perp_summary to filter by broker_id
// user_info contains: account_id, wallet_address, broker_id

commonIssues.issue: Cannot determine if a trade was maker or taker from the indexer.
commonIssues.solution: The indexer does not track maker/taker status. Use the Builder Leaderboard API which provides total_fee and broker_fee breakdowns per user per day.

commonIssues.issue: Analyzer shows missing data for certain blocks.
commonIssues.solution: Delete the analyzer database and re-run from the desired start block. The analyzer only processes blocks after the last indexed block, so it won't re-process already indexed data.

commonIssues.issue: Join on log_index returns incorrect results.
commonIssues.solution: Do not use log_index to join partitioned_executed_trades with serial_batches as they differ between tables. Use block_number and transaction_index instead.

commonIssues.issue: Analyzer data lags behind the indexer.
commonIssues.solution: The analyzer may have processing delays relative to the indexer due to asynchronous execution. Allow time for the analyzer to catch up.
