workflows.name: Understanding the Builder Tier System and Staking Program
workflows.description: Understand how the Orderly Builder Tier System categorizes brokers and how the Builder Staking Program provides fee reductions based on trading volume or $ORDER staked.
prerequisites: Understanding of current trading volume metrics

steps.title: Review Tier Classifications
steps.description: The Builder Tier System categorizes brokers into tiers with fee reductions based on 30-day average trading volume or $ORDER staked.
steps.important: Tiers: Public (default, 2.5 bps taker fee), Silver (reduced fees), Gold (further reduced), Platinum (2 bps taker fee), Diamond (1 bps taker fee). Maker fees remain at 0 bps across all tiers.

steps.title: Check Tier Requirements
steps.description: Review the volume and staking thresholds for each tier to determine upgrade eligibility.

steps.title: Upgrade via Trading Volume
steps.description: Increase your 30-day average trading volume to qualify for higher tiers automatically.
steps.important: Volume is calculated as a 30-day rolling average across all trading activity under your broker ID.

steps.title: Upgrade via $ORDER Staking
steps.description: Stake $ORDER tokens to qualify for higher tiers without meeting volume requirements.

steps.title: Access Tier Benefits
steps.description: Higher tiers provide benefits including marketing support, listing campaigns, and fee reductions.
steps.important: New brokers default to the Public tier. Brokers can upgrade by increasing trading volume or staking ORDER tokens.

commonIssues.issue: Not sure which tier my broker qualifies for.
commonIssues.solution: Check your 30-day average trading volume on the Dune dashboard or admin portal. Compare against tier thresholds: Platinum requires ≥$1B volume or 2M ORDER staked; Diamond requires ≥$10B volume or 7M ORDER staked.

commonIssues.issue: Staking transaction fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you have approved the ORDER token for the proxy contract and that you are attaching sufficient LayerZero fee (quote the fee via quoteStakeOrder and multiply by 1.1 for safety margin).

commonIssues.issue: Tier upgrade not reflected in fees.
commonIssues.solution: Tier upgrades based on volume use a 30-day rolling average, so changes may take time to reflect. Contact Orderly support if staking-based upgrades are not applied.

relatedWorkflows: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration

workflows.name: Handling Cross-Chain Address Mapping and Withdrawal Fees
workflows.description: Understand how Orderly handles address mapping between EVM and Solana chains, and manage withdrawal fees across different networks.
prerequisites: Active Orderly-powered DEX with multi-chain support
Understanding of EVM and Solana address formats

steps.title: Understand EVM-Solana Address Mapping
steps.description: For deposits and withdrawals, Orderly saves the original Solana user address as bytes32 in the ledger. For staking and claiming rewards, the Solana address is converted into an EVM address.
steps.important: The Solana address is converted by keccak256 hashing and truncating to 20 bytes, with the mapping saved when the user first claims a reward. EVM and Solana users are included in the same Merkle tree using EVM addresses.

steps.title: Handle Address Collision Risk
steps.description: The collision risk of truncating to 20 bytes is considered acceptable since EVM addresses themselves are derived from a bytes32 hash (e.g., via CREATE2 or EOA generation).
steps.important: No special handling is required for address collisions in normal operation.

steps.title: Check Withdrawal Fees Per Chain
steps.description: Withdrawal fees are charged to cover gas fees incurred by Orderly when processing withdrawals. Fees differ per chain.

steps.title: Handle Minimum Withdrawal Amounts
steps.description: Some chains have minimum withdrawal amounts due to high transaction fees. For example, ETH withdrawals require amounts larger than 10 USDC equivalent.
steps.important: Upgrade to SDK version 2.7.4 or later to get improved withdrawal error messaging that clearly communicates minimum thresholds instead of generic 'Amount error' messages.

steps.title: Understand Cross-Chain Order Routing
steps.description: All orders placed on an integrated platform are automatically routed to Orderly's orderbook. Post-trade transactions are recorded on Orderly Chain via LayerZero cross-chain messaging.
steps.important: Multi-chain support is handled automatically by the SDK. Builders do not need to implement cross-chain messaging themselves.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal shows 'Amount error' without descriptive message.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK version 2.7.4 or later. Earlier versions show a generic 'Amount error' toast when the withdrawal amount is below the minimum threshold. The updated SDK provides clear error messaging.

commonIssues.issue: Solana user cannot claim staking rewards.
commonIssues.solution: The Solana address must be mapped to an EVM address first. This mapping is saved when the user first claims a reward. Ensure the user has initiated at least one claim to establish the mapping.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal fees seem too high.
commonIssues.solution: Withdrawal fees cover actual gas costs on each chain and vary by network. Check the Get Supported Collateral Info API for current fee rates per chain.

workflows.name: Managing Community Vote to Retain Token Governance
workflows.description: Handle the Community Vote to Retain governance process for tokens at risk of delisting, including SDK support for governance communication.
prerequisites: SDK v2.8.11 or later for governance UI support

steps.title: Monitor Vote to Retain Announcements
steps.description: When tokens are identified for potential delisting due to sustained low metrics, a 'Vote to Retain' governance process is initiated.
steps.important: The voting period typically lasts 5 days.

steps.title: Understand Voting Thresholds
steps.description: To save a token from delisting, more than 3% (or 5% in some cases) of total staked $ORDER must vote 'AGAINST Delisting'.
steps.important: Only staked $ORDER tokens have voting power. Brokers should encourage their communities to stake $ORDER and participate.

steps.title: Enable Governance UI Support
steps.description: Ensure your SDK supports the 'Community Vote' announcement message type for proper governance communication in the UI.
steps.code:
// SDK v2.8.11+ supports the 'Community Vote' announcement message type
"@orderly.network/react": "^2.8.11"
steps.important: Without SDK v2.8.11+, governance announcements may not display properly in your DEX interface.

steps.title: Inform and Mobilize Community
steps.description: Notify your community about active votes and encourage participation using their staked $ORDER tokens.
steps.important: Brokers are encouraged to actively inform their communities and encourage participation to retain valuable trading pairs.

steps.title: Handle Vote Outcome
steps.description: If the vote fails to retain the token (insufficient AGAINST votes), prepare for delisting by following the token delisting settlement process.
steps.important: If delisted, the index price is fixed at the average price of the last hour before delisting. All open positions are settled at this fixed price.

commonIssues.issue: Community Vote announcement not showing in DEX UI.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v2.8.11 or later which supports the 'Community Vote' announcement message type for proper governance communication.

commonIssues.issue: Users don't know how to vote.
commonIssues.solution: Direct users to stake $ORDER tokens and participate in governance through the Orderly platform. Only staked $ORDER has voting power.

commonIssues.issue: Token delisted despite community effort.
commonIssues.solution: Follow the delisting settlement process: inform users that the index price is fixed at the average price of the last hour before delisting, and all open positions will be settled at this price.

workflows.description: Use the Orderly testnet faucet to credit USDC to your Orderly account for testing deposits and trading on Arbitrum Sepolia.

steps.title: Register on Testnet

steps.title: Request USDC from Faucet

commonIssues.solution: The testnet faucet credits USDC directly to your Orderly account balance, not your wallet address. Check your Orderly trading account balance instead of your wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Faucet request fails.

commonIssues.issue: Need to migrate between SDK options.
commonIssues.solution: The Core SDK underlies both Components and Hooks SDKs, so business logic remains consistent. Plan migration by replacing UI components while keeping API integration intact.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, set up default trading fees, and enable testnet access.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions

steps.title: Request Broker ID Setup
steps.description: Provide the following information to the Orderly team: Broker ID, Broker Name, Default Taker Fee, Default Maker Fee, Default RWA Taker Fee, Default RWA Maker Fee, and Tier. The broker ID will be set up on both testnet and mainnet.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. The base taker fee can be reduced by staking ORDER tokens or hitting volume thresholds.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The wallet address and Orderly Account ID must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates. Brokers cannot charge a performance fee on realized PnL; revenue comes from the maker/taker fee split only.

steps.title: Configure Post-Graduation Settings (Self-Hosted)
steps.description: For self-hosted deployments, set the broker ID in your environment configuration.
steps.important: Fee rates (maker/taker) can be adjusted later in the admin console. You can also configure referral thresholds and fee splits there.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account in USDC. Check the balance by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet or using the private Get Current Holding endpoint.
steps.code:
GET /v1/holding
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: Discrepancy between dashboard revenue figures and actual USDC balance.
commonIssues.solution: Contact Orderly support to investigate. Broker fees are automatically credited daily in USDC.

workflows.name: Tracking Broker Volume, Fees, and User Analytics
workflows.description: Fetch trading volume, daily stats, per-user fee breakdowns, and liquidation data for your broker using REST APIs, WebSocket streams, and dashboards.

Orderly API authentication configured (orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id headers)

steps.title: Fetch Overall Broker Volume
steps.description: Use the public endpoint for builder volume to get aggregate trading statistics.

steps.title: Get Daily Volume and Fee Breakdown
steps.description: Use the private leaderboard endpoint for a daily breakdown of volume and fees, including per-user broker_fee data.

steps.title: Track Per-User Volume and Fees
steps.description: Use the Get Builders Users Volumes endpoint to track fees paid per user for analytics or points campaigns.

steps.title: Retrieve Referral Rebate Data
steps.description: Referral rebates are calculated separately from broker fees. Use the referee rebate summary endpoint to get rebate details.

steps.title: Get Real-Time Volume via WebSocket
steps.description: For finer-than-daily granularity, subscribe to the private WebSocket execution report stream and aggregate trade volumes on your side.
steps.important: Orderly does not offer an hourly broker volume REST endpoint or webhooks. Real-time aggregation via WebSocket is the recommended approach for sub-daily granularity.

steps.title: Retrieve Broker-Wide Liquidation Data
steps.description: Use the admin liquidations endpoint to get all liquidations under your broker without iterating per-user.

steps.title: Compute Liquidated Volume
steps.description: Use the cost_position_transfer field from the liquidations response to calculate total leveraged position notional.
steps.important: The position_notional field represents the total for the entire liquidation event, not per individual row.

steps.title: Use Dune Dashboard for Analytics
steps.description: Access the Orderly Dune dashboard for additional analytics and visualizations.
steps.code:
// Dune Dashboard:
https://dune.com/orderly_network/orderly-dashboard

steps.title: Detect Abusive Trading Behavior
steps.description: Use the admin orders API to get granular order data for detecting patterns like wash trading.

commonIssues.issue: broker_fee values seem higher than expected.
commonIssues.solution: The broker_fee value reflects fees before referral rebates are deducted. Check the referral rebate summary endpoint to see the net amount after rebates.

commonIssues.issue: No historical fee rate data available for users.
commonIssues.solution: There is no API to retrieve historical snapshots of user fee rates. Use GET /v1/client/fee_rate to check current rates only.

commonIssues.issue: WebSocket stream not receiving execution reports.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure proper authentication for the private WebSocket stream. Check the authentication documentation and verify your account_id is correct.

steps.description: Withdrawals to addresses other than the connected wallet are disabled by default for security. Contact Orderly support to enable this feature.

commonIssues.issue: Fee rate update returns unauthorized error.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal to custom address fails.
commonIssues.solution: Withdrawals to addresses other than the connected wallet must be explicitly enabled by the Orderly team. Contact support to request enablement for your broker or specific whitelisted accounts.

commonIssues.issue: Programmatic withdrawal request fails.

workflows.name: Building Advanced Trading Features with SDK Hooks
workflows.description: Implement advanced trading features including TP/SL bracket orders, position history retrieval, funding fee calculation, and market filtering using Orderly SDK hooks and APIs.

steps.title: Create TP/SL (Bracket) Orders
steps.description: Use the setValues function from useOrderEntry to set take-profit and stop-loss trigger prices along with base order parameters.
steps.important: TP/SL orders trigger when the mark price hits the target price, not the last traded price. In high volatility or low liquidity, the position may settle at a price different from the trigger price.

steps.title: Retrieve User Position History
steps.description: Use the usePositionHistoryScript hook to access full position history including PnL, status, and position IDs.

steps.title: Calculate Total Funding Paid on a Position
steps.description: There is no single field for cumulative funding. Aggregate the funding fee history using the REST API.
steps.important: You must aggregate the funding fee history manually. There is no single field that returns cumulative funding on a position.

steps.title: Filter Markets in the Market Selector
steps.description: Pass a dataAdapter function to OrderlyAppProvider to filter which symbols appear in the Market Selector.
steps.important: Markets disabled in Orderly One settings are NOT automatically filtered in custom SDK integrations. You must implement filtering manually via the data adapter.

steps.title: Understand 24h Price Change Calculation
steps.description: The 24h price change is based on the last traded price, not the mark price.
steps.important: The 24h price change uses last traded price, not mark price. There is no API for historical mark price K-line data.

steps.title: Calculate IMR-Based Leverage Limits
steps.description: Display position-size-dependent leverage limits rather than a single maximum leverage figure, as margin requirements scale with position notional size.
steps.important: Frontends should display position-size-dependent leverage limits rather than a single maximum leverage figure. The effective leverage limit for a given position size should be calculated as 1 / IMR.

steps.title: Check User's Orderly Key Status
steps.description: Verify if a user's Orderly Key is valid and active.

commonIssues.issue: TP/SL order triggers at unexpected price.
commonIssues.solution: TP/SL orders trigger based on mark price, not last traded price. In high volatility or low liquidity, the execution price may differ from the trigger price.

commonIssues.issue: Position history shows incomplete data.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure enableSortingStorage is set to true and that the user is properly authenticated. The hook returns all symbols when symbol is set to undefined.

commonIssues.issue: Filtered markets still appear in the selector.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the dataAdapter function is correctly passed to OrderlyAppProvider. Markets disabled in Orderly One are not auto-filtered in custom SDK builds.

commonIssues.issue: Leverage displayed does not match expected maximum.
commonIssues.solution: Maximum leverage decreases as position notional size increases beyond the Small_Notional_Limit threshold. Calculate effective leverage as 1 / IMR for the specific position size.

workflows.name: Implementing Gasless Deposits and Internal Transfers
workflows.description: Build one-click or gasless deposit flows using master wallet approaches, smart contract depositTo functions, and internal transfer features.
prerequisites: Smart contract development capability (for gasless flows)
Understanding of Orderly Vault contract architecture

steps.title: Master Wallet Approach for Gasless Deposits
steps.description: Use a master wallet to transfer funds directly to the user's Orderly account off-chain, bypassing the standard deposit workflow.
steps.important: The master wallet transfers funds directly to the user's Orderly account off-chain. This approach requires careful security considerations for the master wallet.

steps.title: Use depositTo for Third-Party Deposits
steps.description: The depositTo function in the vault smart contract allows depositing on behalf of another user, unlike deposit which only deposits to the caller's own account.
steps.important: Cross-chain deposits require msg.value to cover LayerZero fees, which cannot be easily sponsored via standard gas sponsorship.

steps.title: Build Smart Contract Wrapper for Gas Sponsorship
steps.description: For cross-chain gasless deposits, create a smart contract wrapper that maintains a balance of native gas tokens to handle msg.value on behalf of users.
steps.important: Standard gas sponsorship cannot cover msg.value for LayerZero cross-chain fees. A wrapper contract with pre-funded native gas tokens is needed.

steps.title: Implement Internal Transfers for Rewards
steps.description: Use the internal transfer feature to send USDC/USDT to specific user accounts for rewards or giveaways.
steps.important: Internal transfers may need to be enabled by the Orderly team for your broker. Contact support to request enablement.

steps.title: Handle Smart Contract Account (SCA) Deposits
steps.description: When using a Smart Contract Account instead of an EOA signer, the EOA must still be used for Orderly account creation and signing. The SCA calls approval and deposit functions on the Orderly Vault.
steps.important: For SCA withdrawals, ensure the destination address is the SCA. Withdrawing to an address different from the signer requires the broker to be whitelisted by the Orderly team.

commonIssues.issue: Cross-chain gasless deposit fails due to LayerZero fees.
commonIssues.solution: Standard gas sponsorship cannot cover msg.value for LayerZero fees. Implement a smart contract wrapper that maintains a balance of native gas tokens to handle msg.value on behalf of users.

commonIssues.issue: Internal transfer option not available in UI.
commonIssues.solution: Internal transfers may need to be enabled by the Orderly team for your broker. Contact support to request enablement, or use the internal transfer API directly.

commonIssues.issue: SCA deposit fails with approval error.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the SCA properly calls the approval function on the token contract before calling deposit on the Orderly Vault. Reference useDeposit.ts in the hooks package for the correct flow.

workflows.name: Indexing On-Chain Data and Retrieving Token Assets
workflows.description: Self-index Orderly on-chain data for liquidation events, retrieve token icons, and build custom withdrawal pages using indexed data APIs.

steps.title: Set Up Self-Hosted Indexer
steps.description: Use Orderly's open-source indexer to index on-chain data for liquidation events and other activities.
steps.important: Liquidation events can be decoded from OperatorManager eventUpload calldata using V2 schema with bizType=17 on mainnet.

steps.title: Use Public Indexed Data APIs
steps.description: Alternatively, use the public indexed data APIs instead of self-hosting an indexer.

steps.title: Retrieve Token Icons and Logos
steps.description: Token logos are hosted on Orderly's OSS with a predictable URL pattern. Derive the logo name from the symbol.

steps.title: Build Custom Withdrawal Page
steps.description: For users who deposited under a different or demo broker ID, build a custom withdrawal page using the registration check API and dashboard query service.

commonIssues.issue: Liquidation events not decoding correctly.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using V2 schema with bizType=17 for mainnet liquidation events from the OperatorManager eventUpload calldata.

commonIssues.issue: Token logo returns 404.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the symbol name derivation: remove PERP_ prefix and _USDC suffix. Some tokens may have different naming conventions. Check the available symbols endpoint for the correct base asset name.

commonIssues.issue: User cannot find their account for withdrawal.
commonIssues.solution: Direct users to https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/ to view all their accounts across different broker IDs.

workflows.name: Configuring DEX Domain and Preventing Browser Fraud Warnings
workflows.description: Set up custom domain configuration on Orderly One and configure DNS records to prevent browsers from flagging your DEX as fraudulent.

steps.title: Configure DEX Domain and Card Info
steps.description: Set up your custom domain and card information in Orderly One to ensure proper link generation and user experience.
steps.code:
// Configure at:
https://dex.orderly.network/dex/card
steps.important: This is critical if you self-host your DEX on a custom domain. Without proper configuration, Orderly One may display the default domain, leading to broken links and poor user experience.

steps.title: Set Up SPF DNS Record
steps.description: Add an SPF TXT record to your domain to help establish domain authentication.

steps.title: Set Up DMARC DNS Record
steps.description: Add a DMARC TXT record to further strengthen domain authentication and prevent browser fraud warnings.

steps.title: Verify Configuration
steps.description: After DNS propagation (may take up to 48 hours), verify that your DEX is no longer flagged by browsers like Brave.
steps.important: DNS changes may take time to propagate. Test across multiple browsers after configuration.

commonIssues.issue: DEX still flagged as fraudulent after DNS setup.
commonIssues.solution: DNS propagation can take up to 48 hours. Also ensure both SPF and DMARC records are correctly configured. Some browsers may cache fraud warnings — try clearing browser cache or testing in incognito mode.

commonIssues.issue: Broken links when sharing DEX URL.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the domain and card info are properly configured at https://dex.orderly.network/dex/card. Without this, Orderly One may generate links using the default domain.

workflows.name: Customizing PnL Card and Understanding PnL Settlement
workflows.description: Configure PnL (profit and loss) card/poster settings including text layout and font, and understand how PnL settlement works on Orderly.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK integrated or Orderly One DEX

steps.title: Configure PnL Card Settings
steps.description: PnL card settings can be configured in the app/utils/config.tsx file of your SDK project.
steps.important: The PnL card allows customization of text layout, font, and visual appearance for shareable profit/loss posters.

steps.title: Understand PnL Settlement Mechanics
steps.description: PnL settlement is for on-chain settlement. Before settlement, actual funds in the on-chain vault are not affected to cover realized gain/loss.
steps.important: The settlement process transfers one trader's losses to another trader's gains at the vault level. A trader can only withdraw funds after settling unrealized PnL.

steps.title: Understand Referral Revenue Share Calculation
steps.description: Referral revenue share is calculated on the broker's portion of the fee, not the total trading fee.
steps.important: Brokers cannot charge a performance fee on realized PnL. Revenue comes from the maker/taker fee split only.

commonIssues.issue: PnL card customization not taking effect.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the configuration is in the correct file (app/utils/config.tsx) and reference the sample configuration gist for proper syntax.

commonIssues.issue: Users unable to withdraw after profitable trades.
commonIssues.solution: Traders can only withdraw funds after unrealized PnL is settled on-chain. This is by design for the on-chain settlement mechanism.

commonIssues.issue: Referral commission seems lower than expected.
commonIssues.solution: Referral revenue share is calculated on the broker fee only (after deducting the Orderly base fee), not the total trading fee. Verify the fee breakdown.

workflows.name: Enabling Isolated Margin Mode
workflows.description: Enable Isolated Margin Mode for your DEX, which must be activated at the broker level by the Orderly team and requires specific SDK versions.

steps.title: Request Isolated Margin Enablement
steps.description: Contact the Orderly team to request Isolated Margin Mode enablement for your broker ID. This goes through production environment testing.
steps.important: Isolated Margin Mode must be enabled by the Orderly team at the broker level. It must be enabled separately for testnet and mainnet.

steps.title: Upgrade SDK
steps.description: Ensure your SDK is at version 2.11.0 or higher, which is required for Isolated Margin Mode support.

steps.title: Wait for Activation
steps.description: After the Orderly team enables the feature, there may be a ~20 minute delay before it becomes active.
steps.important: Plan for the activation delay when scheduling the feature rollout.

steps.title: Handle Permissionless Markets
steps.description: Permissionless listing markets may be configured as 'isolated only'. Ensure your frontend correctly defaults to isolated margin mode for these markets.
steps.important: Permissionlessly listed markets are Isolated-only to limit risk exposure. They do not support cross margin.

commonIssues.issue: Isolated Margin option not appearing after enablement.
commonIssues.solution: Wait ~20 minutes after the Orderly team confirms enablement. Ensure SDK is v2.11.0+ and that the feature was enabled for the correct environment (testnet vs mainnet).

commonIssues.issue: Cross margin still available on permissionless markets.
commonIssues.solution: Permissionless markets should default to isolated margin only. Check that your frontend correctly handles the _arthur suffix and forces isolated margin mode.

workflows.name: Choosing and Implementing an Integration Approach
workflows.description: Select from five integration options ranging from no-code to full API integration, each with different time-to-market and customizability tradeoffs.
prerequisites: Clear requirements for customizability vs time-to-market
Broker ID (or plan to obtain one)

steps.title: Evaluate No-Code Solution (Orderly One)
steps.description: For fastest time-to-market, use Orderly One to define branding, appearance, and fees with no coding required.
steps.important: Best for teams that want a production-ready DEX with minimal development effort.

steps.title: Evaluate Components SDK
steps.description: Use pre-built React components with theming support for appearance customization while maintaining rapid development.
steps.important: Best for teams that want React components with custom theming but don't need fully custom UI.

steps.title: Evaluate Hooks SDK
steps.description: Use React hooks library for building fully custom frontend components while leveraging Orderly's trading logic.
steps.important: Best for teams that want full UI control while using Orderly's battle-tested hooks for trading logic.

steps.title: Evaluate Core SDK
steps.description: Use the minimal wrapper for Orderly API and EIP-712 signing, usable with any UI library (not limited to React).
steps.important: Best for non-React frameworks or teams that want minimal abstraction over the Orderly API.

steps.title: Evaluate Direct API Integration
steps.description: Build everything yourself using the REST/WebSocket API directly, with full control over every aspect.
steps.important: Best for teams with specific technical requirements or non-JavaScript stacks. Requires the most development effort but offers maximum flexibility.

commonIssues.issue: Unsure which integration approach to choose.
commonIssues.solution: Start with Orderly One for fastest launch, then migrate to Components SDK or Hooks SDK as customization needs grow. You can migrate from custom SDK to Orderly One or vice versa.

commonIssues.issue: Core SDK documentation is incomplete.
commonIssues.solution: Refer to the Hooks SDK and Components SDK source code for implementation patterns. Contact Orderly support for specific Core SDK questions.

workflows.name: Generating and Managing Orderly API Keys
workflows.description: Generate ed25519 keypairs for API authentication, register them with Orderly, and manage key lifecycle including expiration and deletion.
prerequisites: Active Orderly account (wallet registered with a broker ID)

steps.title: Understand API Authentication Model
steps.description: Orderly uses ed25519 keypairs for API authentication. When a user creates an account and enables trading (both requiring a Web3 wallet signature), an ed25519 keypair is generated locally and the public key is registered with Orderly. All subsequent API calls use this keypair — no wallet signature needed per call.
steps.code:
// Documentation:
https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/evm-api/api-authentication
steps.important: A user may create multiple keypairs for the same account. Every user needs their own API key per account. A broker cannot use a single API key for all users.

steps.title: Generate ed25519 Keypair Locally
steps.description: Generate an ed25519 keypair on the client side. The private key is never exposed to Orderly or any server.
steps.important: Base URL is api.orderly.org (api-evm.orderly.org is deprecated but still works).

steps.title: Register Public Key with Orderly
steps.description: Register the public key via the public endpoint or through the DEX UI portfolio/API key page.
steps.important: You can set an expiration time when creating the key. On the DEX UI, expiration time cannot be set at the moment, but there is a delete button available.

steps.title: Generate Broker Admin API Key
steps.description: For broker admin operations, generate an admin API key. Only the broker admin can generate these keys.
steps.important: For Solana wallets, prefix the Orderly public and private keys with 'ed25519:' (e.g., ed25519:4oQzRVURCNxu...).

commonIssues.issue: API calls return authentication errors.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the signing message format is exactly {timestamp}{method}{path}{body}, the signature is base64url-encoded, and the timestamp is in milliseconds.

commonIssues.issue: Need to revoke a compromised API key.
commonIssues.solution: Use DELETE /v1/client/orderly-key to remove the key, or use the delete button in the DEX UI portfolio page.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawals fail even with valid API key.
commonIssues.solution: Withdrawals always require a wallet signature from the user, regardless of API key authentication. This is a security requirement.

relatedWorkflows: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration

workflows.description: Programmatically retrieve multi-level referral data, per-trader PnL/volume stats, aggregated volume, and market maker metrics for your broker.

Active broker ID with trading activity

steps.title: Pull Multi-Level Referral Data
steps.description: Use the admin endpoint to retrieve referral data for all traders under your broker ID.
steps.important: Base URL is api.orderly.org. Authentication requires an admin API key with ed25519 message signing.

steps.title: Get Per-Trader Leaderboard Stats
steps.description: Retrieve daily PnL and trading volume data for traders under your broker for leaderboard purposes.
steps.important: For indexed settlement chain data and dashboards, see https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/ and its API at https://orderly-dashboard-query-service.orderly.network/swagger-ui/#/

steps.title: Get Aggregated Volume Data
steps.description: Retrieve aggregated volume data for all users under your broker.

steps.title: Check Market Maker Reward Metrics
steps.description: Monitor Q_final (est_score) and market maker reward metrics in real time.

steps.title: Track DEX Volume via DEX Board
steps.description: Use the DEX board to monitor your platform's trading volume.

commonIssues.issue: Admin API returns authentication errors.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using an admin API key (not a regular user key) and that the signing message format is correct: {timestamp}{method}{path}{body}.

commonIssues.issue: Win rate data is missing from leaderboard.
commonIssues.solution: Win rate is not provided as a pre-calculated field. You must calculate it yourself by tracking profitable trades versus total trades from trade history.

workflows.name: Resolving Withdrawal and Margin Errors
workflows.description: Diagnose and resolve the 'Withdrawal Pre Margin Check Failed' error (error code 20) and handle unsettled PnL that blocks withdrawals.
prerequisites: Active Orderly trading account with open positions or pending orders
API access or DEX UI access

steps.title: Identify the Error
steps.description: Error code 20 ('Withdrawal Pre Margin Check Failed') means withdrawing the specified amount would leave the account undercollateralized given current open positions and orders.
steps.important: This is a safety mechanism to prevent accounts from becoming insolvent.

steps.title: Free Up Margin
steps.description: Close or reduce open positions and/or cancel pending orders to free up margin for withdrawal.

steps.title: Check for Unsettled PnL
steps.description: After closing positions, PnL may remain 'unsettled' in the free collateral calculation, still blocking withdrawals.

steps.title: Settle PnL
steps.description: Call the settle PnL endpoint to finalize unrealized PnL from closed positions.
steps.code:
POST /v1/settle_pnl

// After settling, retry the withdrawal.

steps.title: Retry Withdrawal
steps.description: After freeing margin and settling PnL, retry the withdrawal request.
steps.important: If the error persists, verify that sufficient free collateral exists by checking the account summary endpoint.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal still fails after closing all positions.
commonIssues.solution: Check for unsettled PnL via GET /v1/private/get-all-positions-info and call POST /v1/settle_pnl before retrying.

commonIssues.issue: Pending orders are blocking withdrawal.
commonIssues.solution: Cancel all pending orders to free up reserved margin. Open orders lock margin even if they haven't been filled.

commonIssues.issue: Collateral value fluctuation affecting available margin.
commonIssues.solution: When depositing volatile assets (e.g., SOL) as collateral, the account's USDC-denominated value fluctuates with market price. Free collateral uses the collateral's weight factor (e.g., SOL weight = 0.8). To avoid fluctuations, deposit stablecoins like USDC instead.

workflows.name: Implementing Custom Fee Tiers for Users
workflows.description: Deploy volume-based fee tiers and token-holder rebates for your DEX users using the open-source broker fee admin tool.
prerequisites: VPS or server for hosting the fee admin script (e.g., Hetzner)

steps.title: Deploy the Fee Admin Script
steps.description: Clone and deploy the open-source broker fee admin tool via Docker.
steps.important: Volume-based and token-holder rebates are not yet natively implemented in Orderly One and require this self-hosted backend.

steps.title: Configure Volume-Based Fee Tiers
steps.description: Define fee tier buckets in broker.yaml with volume thresholds and corresponding fee rates.
steps.code:
# broker.yaml example:
statistical_days: 30  # 30-day average volume lookback

fee_tiers:
  - min_volume: 0
    maker_fee: 0.0002
    taker_fee: 0.0005
  - min_volume: 1000000
    maker_fee: 0.0001
    taker_fee: 0.0004
  - min_volume: 5000000
    maker_fee: 0
    taker_fee: 0.0003
steps.important: The system auto-updates user fees daily based on the configured lookback period.

steps.title: Add Token-Holder Rebates (Optional)
steps.description: Extend the script to fetch on-chain token balances and apply discount rules for token holders.
steps.important: The tool uses the same API call to set per-user special rates that override default tiers.

steps.title: Configure Swap Fees (If Applicable)
steps.description: Configure swap fees in the Orderly One dashboard for the Deposit Zap-in feature.
steps.important: The configured swap fee is added on top of existing liquidity provider fees. Swap functionality currently supports EVM chains; cross-chain swap is a planned feature.

commonIssues.issue: Fee tiers not updating for users.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the Docker container is running and the cron job for daily updates is properly configured. Check that statistical_days is set correctly in broker.yaml.

commonIssues.issue: Per-user special rates not overriding default tiers.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the API call to set per-user rates is using the correct admin authentication and the rate format matches Orderly's expected decimal format.

commonIssues.issue: Swap fees too high causing user complaints.
commonIssues.solution: A fee under 0.2% is generally recommended to remain competitive. The maximum allowed is 1% (100 bps).

workflows.name: Resolving SWR Dependency Conflicts in Next.js
workflows.description: Fix SWR version conflicts and React Server Component issues when using the Orderly Hooks SDK with Next.js.
prerequisites: Next.js project with Orderly Hooks SDK

steps.title: Identify the Conflict
steps.description: SWR version conflicts can cause errors like 'export default (reexported as useSWR) was not found in swr'.
steps.important: This typically occurs when different Orderly packages depend on different SWR versions.

steps.title: Install Specific Package Versions
steps.description: Install compatible versions of the Orderly packages to resolve SWR conflicts.
steps.code: npm install @orderly.network/react@internal @orderly.network/hooks @orderly.network/core
steps.important: Using @internal tag for the react package may resolve version mismatch issues.

steps.title: Add 'use client' Directive
steps.description: In Next.js React Server Components environments, add the 'use client' directive at the top of modules where SWR is imported.
steps.important: SWR hooks must run in client components, not server components.

steps.title: Prepare Minimal Reproduction (If Issues Persist)
steps.description: If issues persist after trying the above steps, prepare a minimal reproduction repo for the DevRel team.
steps.important: Share the reproduction repo with the Orderly DevRel team for further investigation.

commonIssues.issue: Error: 'export default (reexported as useSWR) was not found in swr'.
commonIssues.solution: Install specific compatible versions: npm install @orderly.network/react@internal @orderly.network/hooks @orderly.network/core

commonIssues.issue: Hooks not working in Next.js App Router.
commonIssues.solution: Add 'use client' directive at the top of any module that imports SWR or Orderly hooks. These cannot run in React Server Components.

commonIssues.issue: Version conflicts persist after reinstalling.
commonIssues.solution: Delete node_modules and package-lock.json, then reinstall. If issues persist, prepare a minimal reproduction repo for the DevRel team.

workflows.name: Understanding Cross-Chain Deposits, Trading, and Withdrawals
workflows.description: Understand how Orderly handles omnichain operations including deposits to chain-specific vaults, off-chain trading, and cross-chain withdrawals via LayerZero.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of Orderly's omnichain architecture

steps.title: Understand Deposit Flow
steps.description: Users deposit into asset manager vaults on their native chain (e.g., Solana vault for Solana users, OP vault for Optimism users).
steps.important: Each chain has its own vault contract. Deposits are chain-specific.

steps.title: Understand Trading Flow
steps.description: Trading happens off-chain via a centralized matching engine with one-click trading — no per-trade signatures required.
steps.important: After initial account setup and trading enablement (which require wallet signatures), all trades are executed using the ed25519 API key without additional wallet signatures.

steps.title: Understand Cross-Chain Rebalancing
steps.description: Orderly rebalances funds between chain vaults using LayerZero. Withdrawals are typically instantaneous because vaults are pre-funded.
steps.important: Cross-margin is used across all positions. The overall margin is calculated globally regardless of which chain the deposit came from.

steps.title: Handle Collateral Value Fluctuations
steps.description: When depositing volatile assets (e.g., SOL), the account's USDC-denominated value fluctuates with the asset's market price.
steps.important: To avoid balance fluctuations from collateral price changes, deposit stablecoins like USDC instead of volatile assets.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal takes longer than expected.
commonIssues.solution: If the destination chain vault needs rebalancing, withdrawal may take ~1-2 minutes. Users can alternatively withdraw from another chain with available liquidity for instant processing.

commonIssues.issue: Account balance fluctuates without trading.
commonIssues.solution: This occurs when volatile assets (e.g., SOL) are used as collateral. The USDC-denominated value changes with market price. Use stablecoins to avoid this.

commonIssues.issue: Isolated margin vs cross margin confusion.
commonIssues.solution: Isolated margin (SDK v2.11.0+) allocates specific margin to individual positions. Cross margin shares margin across all positions. SDK v3.1.0 fixed an issue where maxing out isolated margin market orders at 100% would be rejected — the SDK now reserves a taker fee buffer.

workflows.name: Configuring EIP-712 Signing for Orderly Account Registration
workflows.description: Set up EIP-712 domain separator configuration and implement typed data signing for Orderly account registration and API authentication on EVM chains, including native mobile implementations.
prerequisites: EVM wallet integration (web or native mobile)
Understanding of EIP-712 typed data signing
For native apps: web3j (Android) or web3swift (iOS) library

steps.title: Configure the Off-Chain EIP-712 Domain
steps.description: Use hardcoded values for the off-chain domain separator regardless of the connected chain. The verifyingContract is a placeholder — no real smart contract verifies it.
steps.important: The name is always 'Orderly' and the verifyingContract is always the hardcoded placeholder address.

steps.title: Configure the On-Chain EIP-712 Domain
steps.description: For on-chain operations, use the Ledger contract address on Orderly L2 as the verifyingContract.
steps.code:
// Refer to supported chains documentation for contract addresses:
// https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-evm/addresses
steps.important: The on-chain domain uses actual deployed contract addresses, unlike the off-chain placeholder.

steps.title: Implement EIP-712 Signing in Native Android (Kotlin)
steps.description: Use the web3j library for EIP-712 signing in native Android applications.
steps.important: Do not manually hash data before passing to the signing function. Ensure proper ABI encoding and Keccak256 hashing (not standard SHA-3).

steps.title: Implement EIP-712 Signing in Native iOS (Swift)
steps.description: Use the web3swift library for EIP-712 signing in native iOS applications.
steps.important: The signing must happen client-side; never transmit the private key to a backend server.

steps.title: Consider Alternative Approaches for Mobile
steps.description: If native EIP-712 implementation is not feasible, consider alternatives for mobile wallet integration.
steps.important: For Solana Seeker or similar devices, ensure compatibility with the Seed Vault native wallet and consider adding WalletConnect support.

commonIssues.issue: EIP-712 signature verification fails on Orderly backend.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using Keccak256 hashing (not standard SHA-3) and that the domain separator matches exactly. The chainId must match the user's connected chain.

commonIssues.issue: Native mobile app cannot sign Orderly transactions.
commonIssues.solution: Verify that the signing happens client-side and that the private key is never transmitted. If native implementation is too complex, use an embedded WebView or WalletConnect bridge.

commonIssues.issue: Signature format mismatch between web and native implementations.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure both implementations produce the same signature format (r, s, v components). Test with known test vectors from the Orderly examples repository.

commonIssues.solution: Ensure the time range does not exceed 30 days. The account_id is derived from the user's wallet address — verify it is correct.

commonIssues.issue: Open interest values don't match broker UI.
commonIssues.solution: The API returns open interest in base token units. Broker UIs typically display in USD. Multiply by the index price to convert.

workflows.name: Requesting Higher API Rate Limits for Copy-Trading and Bot Backends
workflows.description: Request elevated API rate limits from Orderly for backend systems that fan out orders to many sub-accounts, such as copy-trading platforms and AI trading agents.
prerequisites: Defined target request rate and endpoint list

steps.title: Identify Rate-Limited Endpoints
steps.description: Determine which specific endpoints are hitting rate limits in your backend system.
steps.important: Per-endpoint rate limits for GET requests cannot be modified on the backend. For high-frequency data needs, use WebSocket subscriptions instead.

steps.title: Prepare Request Information
steps.description: Gather the required information to submit to the Orderly team for rate limit elevation.

steps.title: Submit Rate Limit Request to Orderly Team
steps.description: Contact the Orderly team with your prepared information. They will whitelist your IP to lift gateway-level limits.
steps.important: The Orderly team can whitelist specific IPs to bypass gateway-level rate limits for POST endpoints.

steps.title: Use WebSocket for High-Frequency Data
steps.description: For real-time market data needs, switch from REST API polling to WebSocket subscriptions.
steps.important: There is no restriction limiting WebSocket to 10 connections per IP. WebSocket is the recommended approach for high-frequency data.

steps.title: Track AI Agent Volume with order_tag
steps.description: Use the order_tag parameter when placing orders to track volume generated specifically by your bots or AI agents.
steps.important: Currently, the order_tag must be a valid referral code belonging to the same broker ID. Orderly is introducing order_tag enums for more flexible tagging.

commonIssues.issue: GET endpoint rate limits still apply after IP whitelisting.
commonIssues.solution: IP whitelisting only lifts gateway-level limits for POST endpoints. GET endpoint rate limits cannot be modified. Switch to WebSocket subscriptions for high-frequency data retrieval.

commonIssues.issue: WebSocket connection drops frequently.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your WebSocket client properly handles ping/pong frames and implements reconnection logic. Verify the URL is composed correctly per documentation.

commonIssues.issue: Public WebSocket does not respond to ping/pong.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the WebSocket URL is correctly formatted. Even public streams may require an account-id parameter for DDoS prevention.

workflows.name: Setting Up Delegate Signers for Smart Contract Deposits and Withdrawals
workflows.description: Configure delegate signers to allow smart contracts to execute deposits and withdrawals on behalf of users without requiring direct user signatures for each transaction.
prerequisites: Smart contract deployed for deposit/withdrawal management

steps.title: Register Delegate Signer via Broker Portal
steps.description: Establish the delegate signer link between your smart contract and the user's Orderly account through the broker registration UI.
steps.important: The delegate signer link must be established before the smart contract can interact with Orderly's deposit and withdrawal flows.

steps.title: Implement Smart Contract Deposit Flow
steps.description: Once the delegate signer is linked, the smart contract can execute deposits on behalf of users by sending on-chain deposit transactions to Orderly smart contracts.
steps.important: Deposits are not performed via REST API but by sending on-chain deposit transactions to Orderly smart contracts on the source chain.

steps.title: Implement Smart Contract Withdrawal Flow
steps.description: The smart contract can also execute withdrawals on behalf of users using the delegate signer authorization.
steps.important: Withdrawals require EIP-712 wallet signing. The delegate signer feature allows the smart contract to handle this without requiring the user to sign each transaction directly.

steps.title: Test on Testnet
steps.description: Test the full deposit and withdrawal flow on testnet before deploying to production.
steps.important: For Solana testnet, admin wallet registration via the standard UI is not yet supported. Use your own trading UI with the broker ID configured.

commonIssues.issue: Smart contract deposit transactions fail.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the delegate signer link is properly established in the broker registration portal. Ensure the smart contract address matches exactly.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal transactions revert on-chain.
commonIssues.solution: Check that the EIP-712 signature is correctly generated by the smart contract. Ensure the delegate signer authorization is active and not expired.

workflows.name: Understanding Orderly Fee Structure and Builder Staking Program
workflows.description: Understand Orderly's fee structure for perpetual trading, including maker/taker fees, funding rates, RWA market fees, and how to reduce base fees through the Builder Staking Program.

steps.title: Understand Base Fee Structure
steps.description: Orderly charges a base 3bps (0.03%) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Brokers can add any fee on top, which they keep.
steps.important: Every trade that results from order matching incurs either a maker or taker fee. Maker fee applies when adding liquidity (limit orders). Taker fee applies when removing liquidity (market orders or matching limit orders).

steps.title: Understand Funding Rate Fees
steps.description: In addition to trading fees, funding rate fees are charged continuously while positions remain open.
steps.important: When the funding rate is negative, short positions pay long positions (and vice versa). Funding fees are deducted continuously as long as the position remains open.

steps.title: Reduce Base Taker Fee via Builder Staking Program
steps.description: Brokers can reduce the base taker fee by staking ORDER tokens or achieving volume thresholds through tier levels.
steps.important: Fee configuration is managed by the Orderly team during broker ID setup and can later be adjusted by the broker via the admin wallet.

steps.title: Configure RWA Market Fees
steps.description: For RWA perpetual markets (e.g., stock perps), the base fee follows the builder fee program tiers. Builders charge their own fees on top.
steps.important: Orderly has indicated flexibility on RWA fees, allowing builders to set their own fees on top of base fees going forward.

steps.title: View Accumulated Revenue
steps.description: Monitor your broker's accumulated trading volume and revenue through the admin dashboard and public API.
steps.important: Accumulated revenue is collected in your Orderly account and must be withdrawn to your admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Confusion about total fee charged to users.
commonIssues.solution: Total user fee = Orderly base fee + Builder fee on top. The builder keeps everything above the base fee. Check your tier level to know your base fee.

commonIssues.issue: Funding rate charges seem unexpected.
commonIssues.solution: Funding rates are separate from trading fees and are charged continuously. Check the funding rate for each market before opening positions.

commonIssues.issue: Revenue not appearing in admin wallet.
commonIssues.solution: Revenue is collected in the Orderly account, not directly in the wallet. You must withdraw accumulated revenue from the Orderly account to your admin wallet.

workflows.name: Setting Up and Managing Market Maker Accounts
workflows.description: Create and configure Market Maker (MM) accounts on Orderly with specialized fee structures and rate limits for professional market-making operations.
prerequisites: EVM wallet address for the MM account
Ability to maintain maker volume ratio above 75%

steps.title: Submit MM Account Information
steps.description: Navigate to the dedicated MM account creation portal and provide the required information.
steps.important: MM accounts can ONLY be created from dmm.orderly.network. They cannot be created through the standard registration flow.

steps.title: Wait for Orderly Team Configuration
steps.description: Once the account information is provided, the Orderly team will configure the account with specialized fee rates and rate limits.
steps.important: The Orderly team sets the account fee to taker +2.5bps / maker -1.5bps and the rate limit to 50 calls/sec.

steps.title: Maintain Maker Volume Ratio
steps.description: To maintain the preferential MM fee structure, ensure that the maker volume ratio stays above 75% of total trading volume.
steps.important: If the maker volume ratio drops below 75%, the account may lose its MM fee benefits.

steps.title: Configure Trading Infrastructure
steps.description: Set up your trading bots and infrastructure to use the registered IP address and wallet for all MM trading activity.
steps.important: Only the registered IP address should be used for trading to maintain compliance with the MM account configuration.

commonIssues.issue: MM fee rates not applied to trades.
commonIssues.solution: Verify that the Orderly team has completed the account configuration. Ensure you are trading from the registered wallet address and IP.

commonIssues.issue: Rate limit exceeded during high-frequency trading.
commonIssues.solution: MM accounts are configured with a 50 calls/sec rate limit. If you need higher limits, contact the Orderly team to discuss your requirements.

commonIssues.issue: MM fee benefits lost.
commonIssues.solution: Check your maker volume ratio. It must remain above 75% to maintain the preferential fee structure. Adjust your strategy if the ratio has dropped.

workflows.name: Handling USDC Decimal Precision on BNB Chain
workflows.description: Correctly handle USDC decimal precision differences between on-chain (18 decimals) and Orderly (6 decimals) when processing deposits and withdrawals on BNB Chain.

steps.title: Understand the Decimal Mismatch
steps.description: USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain, but Orderly only supports 6 decimals for deposits and withdrawals. This mismatch can cause precision errors if not handled correctly.
steps.important: Always use 6 decimals when interacting with Orderly's API for USDC on BNB Chain, regardless of the on-chain representation.

steps.title: Query Token Decimals from Public API
steps.description: Before processing any on-chain transaction, always refer to the decimals field in the chain_details from the Public Token API.
steps.important: Never hardcode decimal values. Always fetch them dynamically from the API to avoid precision mismatches.

steps.title: Convert Decimals in Deposit Flow
steps.description: When processing deposits, convert from the on-chain decimal representation (18 for USDC on BNB Chain) to Orderly's expected 6 decimals.

steps.title: Convert Decimals in Withdrawal Flow
steps.description: When processing withdrawals, convert from Orderly's 6 decimals back to the on-chain 18 decimals for BNB Chain.

steps.title: Exclude BNB Chain If Not Supported
steps.description: If you prefer not to support BNB Chain and don't want to upgrade to SDK v2.3.0 (required for BNB Chain support), use the chainFilter configuration to explicitly exclude it.
steps.code:
<OrderlyAppProvider
  chainFilter={{
    mainnet: [
      Arbitrum,
      Optimism,
      Base,
      // BNB Chain excluded by omission
    ],
  }}
>
  {children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>

commonIssues.issue: Deposit amounts are off by a factor of 10^12.
commonIssues.solution: You are likely using the on-chain 18-decimal representation directly with Orderly's 6-decimal system. Always convert using the decimal difference.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal amounts are incorrect on BNB Chain.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are converting from Orderly's 6 decimals to the on-chain 18 decimals before broadcasting the withdrawal transaction.

commonIssues.issue: Hardcoded decimals break when new chains are added.
commonIssues.solution: Always fetch decimal values dynamically from the Public Token API's chain_details rather than hardcoding them.

workflows.name: Broker Offboarding and Wind-Down Process
workflows.description: Properly wind down or offboard a broker from Orderly Network, including disabling deposits, directing users to the offboarding portal, and managing open positions.
prerequisites: Decision to wind down broker operations

steps.title: Contact Orderly to Disable Deposits
steps.description: Request that Orderly disable deposits for your specific broker ID. This prevents new funds from entering the system while allowing existing positions to be managed.
steps.important: Orderly can disable deposits for a specific broker, but cannot stop trading for a single broker or force-close positions.

steps.title: Wind Down Frontend
steps.description: Shut down or modify your frontend application to prevent new trading activity while guiding users to the official offboarding portal.
steps.important: The broker must wind down their frontend and direct users to Orderly's official offboarding portal.

steps.title: Direct Users to Offboarding Portal
steps.description: Provide users with the link to Orderly's official offboarding portal where they can still manage positions and withdraw funds.
steps.code:

steps.title: Display Vault Information to Users

steps.important: OmniVault is accessible via Binance Web3 Wallet, DeBank, and Gate. Liquidations on Orderly flow to this vault first, providing additional PnL.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, graduate your DEX, and set up default trading fees.

EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions

steps.title: Request Broker ID Setup
steps.description: Contact the Orderly team to create a broker ID. Provide: Broker ID (no spaces), Broker Name, Default Taker Fee, and Default Maker Fee. Setup typically takes 1-2 days due to approval and multisig collection for enacted chains.
steps.important: Orderly charges a 0.03% taker fee and no maker fee; anything above that is retained by the broker. Fees can be changed later via the admin wallet.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig wallets are supported on EVM for security.

steps.title: Graduate Your DEX
steps.description: After your broker ID is set up, proceed to the graduation page to register your admin wallet and start earning fees.
steps.important: Fees are only collected from the time the admin wallet is registered forward (not retroactively).

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account. Check the balance by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet or using the private Get Current Holding endpoint.
steps.code:
GET /v1/holding
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: Broker ID setup taking longer than expected.
commonIssues.solution: Broker ID setup typically takes 1-2 days because it requires approval and multisig collection for the enacted chains. Contact the Orderly team if it exceeds this timeframe.

prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.9.0 or later (or latest Orderly One version)
Access to Admin Tool or Orderly One dashboard

steps.title: Upgrade SDK
steps.description: Ensure your DEX is running SDK version 2.9.0 or later. For Orderly One DEXs, ensure you are on the latest version available on the platform.
steps.important: As of SDK v2.12.4, users can bind a referral code to their existing account at any time post-registration, rather than being required to provide a code during registration.

steps.title: Activate the Referral Program
steps.description: Enable or upgrade the referral program via the Admin Tool or through the Orderly One dashboard.
steps.code:
// Admin Portal:
https://admin.orderly.network/login
steps.important: The multilevel program supports up to 15 levels of referrals. Level 1 affiliates are users who claim a referral code directly from the DEX's rewards page.

steps.title: Configure Referral Code Parameters
steps.description: When creating a referral code, configure the rebate rates. All values are expressed as absolute decimals (e.g., 0.5 means 50% of fees).
steps.important: Referral rebates are settled in USDC regardless of the collateral asset used, and are sent to users once per day. Orderly's base fee is excluded from the referral fee split — only the broker's own fee portion is shared.

steps.title: Integrate Affiliate Page
steps.description: The Orderly SDK includes a built-in affiliate page component. Users claim referral codes directly from the DEX's rewards/affiliate page rather than receiving shared codes.
steps.important: Existing single-level referral codes remain functional. New codes are generated through the multilevel system.

steps.title: Use order_tag for Per-Order Referral Tracking
steps.description: Attach a referral code at the order level using the `order_tag` field in the create order API. This overrides any account-level referral binding.
steps.code:
POST /v1/order
Body: {
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "order_type": "MARKET",
  "order_quantity": "0.01",
  "side": "BUY",
  "order_tag": "BBBB" // Overrides account-level referral code
}

commonIssues.issue: Cannot register referral code for a KOL/affiliate.
commonIssues.solution: The KOL/affiliate must first connect their wallet and sign in to create an Orderly account. Attempting to register a ref code before the user has signed in will result in an 'address is not registered' error.

commonIssues.issue: Rebates not appearing for users.
commonIssues.solution: Rebates are settled once per day in USDC. Ensure the referral code is correctly bound to the user's account and that the rebate rates are properly configured.

commonIssues.issue: Confusion about which fees are shared in referrals.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly's base fee (0.03% taker) is excluded from the referral fee split. Only the broker's own fee portion above the base fee is shared with referral participants.

workflows.name: Running an Orderly Network L2 RPC Node
workflows.description: Set up and operate an Orderly Network L2 RPC node built on the OP Stack with Celestia for data availability (Alt-DA), using op-reth and Conduit's external node infrastructure.
prerequisites: Server with sufficient storage and compute resources
GCP project for snapshot access (requester-pays bucket)
Understanding of OP Stack node architecture

steps.title: Clone the External Node Repository
steps.description: Use Conduit's external node repository which contains the compatible versions and flags for running an Orderly L2 node.
steps.important: Orderly Network migrated from op-geth to op-reth (completed by June 2026). Node operators must use op-reth, not op-geth.

steps.title: Configure Celestia Alt-DA Parameters
steps.description: Set up the Celestia namespace and Alt-DA configuration in your node setup. The op-alt-da service is required.
steps.important: The op-node must be vanilla (not Celestia's fork). The Celestia op-alt-da component is still required after the op-reth migration.

steps.title: Download a Snapshot
steps.description: Syncing from genesis is not recommended due to complexity around the Alt-DA migration block height. Use a snapshot instead from the requester-pays Google Cloud Storage bucket.
steps.important: There are no free public snapshots available. You need to configure a GCP project following the Conduit guide. Genesis sync requires running the Celestia fork first and then switching to vanilla op-node around the Alt-DA migration block height.

steps.title: Start the Node
steps.description: Launch the node using docker-compose with the Celestia configuration. The node uses op-reth, op-node (vanilla), and op-alt-da service.
steps.important: Syncing is supported via consensus-layer (CL) peers using snapshots rather than from genesis.

steps.title: Monitor Node Health
steps.description: Verify the node is syncing correctly and serving RPC requests. Monitor logs for any Alt-DA or Celestia-related errors.
steps.important: Ensure the L1 beacon URL is configured for fallback to Ethereum blobs in case Celestia data availability is temporarily unavailable.

commonIssues.issue: Node fails to sync from genesis.
commonIssues.solution: Do not sync from genesis. Use a snapshot from the GCS bucket instead. Genesis sync involves significant complexity around the Alt-DA migration block height.

commonIssues.issue: op-geth errors after migration.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly Network has migrated from op-geth to op-reth. Ensure you are using op-reth as documented in the Conduit external node repository.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot access snapshot bucket.
commonIssues.solution: The snapshot bucket is requester-pays. You must configure a GCP project and enable billing to access the snapshots. Follow the Conduit guide for setup.

commonIssues.issue: Celestia data availability errors.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the Celestia namespace is correctly configured (0000000000000000000000000000000000000000000584cb53884b3945) and the op-alt-da service is running. Configure an L1 beacon URL as fallback.

workflows.name: Retrieving Broker User Trading Data via API

steps.title: Fetch Per-Trade Transaction Details
steps.description: Use the Orderly dashboard query service indexing endpoint to retrieve per-trade details (date, volume, PnL, traded asset, user) for specific users.
steps.important: The account_id field is derived as hash(wallet_address, broker_id). Filtering is only available per specific user (account_id). There is currently no API to aggregate trades by broker, user, and market simultaneously.

steps.title: Fetch Aggregated Volume for Leaderboards
steps.description: Use the Builder's Leaderboard API endpoint to retrieve aggregated volume for specific or all users over a given time period, useful for points or rewards systems.
steps.important: Orderly does not expose individual user order data (including addresses and order values) to brokers via WebSocket or other public streams for privacy reasons.

steps.title: Fetch Full Broker ID List
steps.description: Use the public REST API to retrieve the full list of broker IDs for populating broker selectors or integration purposes.
steps.code: GET https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/evm-api/restful-api/public/get-builder-list

commonIssues.issue: Cannot aggregate trades by broker, user, and market simultaneously.
commonIssues.solution: This is a current API limitation. The events_v2 endpoint only supports filtering per specific user (account_id). Use the Builder's Leaderboard API for aggregated volume data instead.

commonIssues.issue: account_id derivation is incorrect.
commonIssues.solution: The account_id must be derived as hash(wallet_address, broker_id). Ensure you are using the correct hashing method and that the broker_id matches exactly.

commonIssues.issue: Need individual user order data via WebSocket.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly does not expose individual user order data to brokers via WebSocket for privacy reasons. Use the dashboard query service or Builder's Leaderboard API instead.

workflows.name: Setting Up Orderly Webhooks for Order Notifications
workflows.description: Configure webhook endpoints to receive real-time order status change notifications (NEW, FILLED, PARTIAL_FILLED, CANCELLED, REJECTED) from Orderly with HMAC SHA-256 authentication.
prerequisites: Ability to verify HMAC SHA-256 signatures

steps.title: Request Webhook Setup
steps.description: Contact the Orderly team to configure a webhook endpoint for your broker_id. Orderly will generate a keypair and provide you with the public key for verification.
steps.important: Orderly sends POST requests to a single webhook endpoint whenever an order associated with your broker_id reaches a final state (FILLED, CANCELLED, REJECTED).

steps.title: Implement Webhook Handler
steps.description: Create an endpoint that receives POST requests with full order details and verifies the HMAC SHA-256 signature using the public key provided by Orderly.
steps.important: If your endpoint returns a status code outside 200–299, Orderly will retry the delivery.

steps.title: Use REST API as Golden Source
steps.description: While webhooks provide real-time notifications, always use the REST API as the golden source for order state recovery and reconciliation.
steps.important: Webhooks are supplementary — implement REST API polling as a fallback for critical order state tracking.

steps.title: Supplement with WebSocket Streams
steps.description: For frontend applications, use the WebSocket executionreport stream to listen for order status updates in real time.

commonIssues.issue: Webhook deliveries are being retried.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your endpoint returns a 2xx status code within the timeout period. Check server logs for processing errors that may cause non-2xx responses.

commonIssues.issue: HMAC signature verification fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using the correct public key provided by Orderly and that the signature verification follows the HMAC SHA-256 standard exactly.

commonIssues.issue: Missed webhook notifications.
commonIssues.solution: Always use the REST API as the golden source for order state. Implement periodic reconciliation via REST API to catch any missed webhook deliveries.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, set up default trading fees, and graduate your DEX to start earning revenue.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions
1,000 USDC or 750 $ORDER for DEX graduation (if using Orderly One)

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. You only need to register on one chain — there is no need to register separately on Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, etc. You can use different wallets for mainnet and testnet.
steps.important: The admin wallet is used to: (1) set fee rates, (2) receive broker fee distributions, and (3) log into the broker admin panel. Many brokers use a multisig on mainnet via the delegate signer feature. The admin wallet can be changed later.

steps.title: Graduate Your DEX (Orderly One)
steps.description: If using Orderly One, pay the graduation fee to start earning revenue from transaction fees. Before graduation, the DEX is functional but does not generate revenue.
steps.important: The admin account and payout address must be the same wallet — they cannot be separated on the backend.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your delegate signer address credentials (key/secret). Ensure the API key was generated using the admin (multisig) wallet address.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees via the API or admin portal. Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee for standard assets, and 5 bps taker / 0 bps maker for RWA assets. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker.
steps.important: Testnet and mainnet fee configurations are separate. Builders at Silver tier and above may qualify for negative maker fees (rebates). RWA pair fees are now aligned with crypto pair fees as of 2026.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection and Distribution
steps.description: Broker fee revenue is automatically distributed to the admin wallet's account assets. It is not shown in the broker admin panel (which displays referral data). Query fee distribution history via the REST API.
steps.important: Builder revenue is batched and settled once per day. This flow is not yet integrated into the SDK, so use the API directly.

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet. Use the delegate signer address credentials (key/secret).

commonIssues.issue: Automated broker ID graduation fails on Orderly One.
commonIssues.solution: Contact the Orderly DevRel team with the transaction hash, the wallet address used on Orderly One, and the desired broker ID. Verify that the selected chain matches the chain of the token sent in the transaction. The team can manually register the broker ID and name on the backend.

commonIssues.issue: 'Visit DEX' link points to a dummy domain and cannot be changed from UI.
commonIssues.solution: The 'Visit DEX' link set during graduation via Orderly One cannot be modified from the UI. Contact the Orderly DevRel team to manually update the link to the correct production domain on the backend.

steps.title: Stake $ORDER Tokens

steps.important: Staking provides an alternative path to higher tiers without needing to achieve the volume thresholds.

steps.title: Verify Tier Upgrade

steps.important: As a Diamond-tier broker, you can offer taker fees as low as 1.5 bps, making your DEX more attractive to active traders.

steps.title: Configure Competitive Fee Rates
