commonIssues.issue: Tier not upgrading despite meeting volume requirements.
commonIssues.solution: Tiers are based on 30-day average trading volume. Ensure the volume is sustained over the full period. Contact Orderly support if the tier does not update automatically.

commonIssues.issue: Unsure which tier to target.
commonIssues.solution: For competitive fee offerings, target Diamond tier (1 bps base taker) or Platinum tier (2 bps base taker). Silver tier is the minimum for negative maker fee eligibility.

workflows.name: Creating Bracket Orders with Take Profit and Stop Loss
workflows.description: Create bracket orders with nested Take Profit and Stop Loss child orders using the Orderly REST API for automated position management.
prerequisites: Orderly API key with trading permissions
Understanding of algo order types and nested order structures
Active Orderly account with sufficient margin

steps.title: Understand Bracket Order Structure
steps.description: Bracket orders use `algo_type: 'BRACKET'` on the parent order with nested `child_orders` arrays. Stop orders do not support TP/SL directly — only Limit/Market parent orders do.
steps.important: The TP/SL side must be opposite to the position side. Set `reduce_only: true` on all child orders.

steps.title: Construct the Bracket Order Payload
steps.description: Build the JSON payload with the parent order and nested TP/SL child orders using the Create Algo Order endpoint.
steps.important: The `trigger_price_type` can be set at the child_orders level to specify whether the trigger uses mark price, index price, or last traded price.

steps.title: Submit and Verify the Order
steps.description: Send the bracket order to the Create Algo Order endpoint and verify it was placed correctly by checking the response and querying active algo orders.
steps.code:
// Verify active algo orders:
GET /v1/algo/orders?symbol=PERP_ETH_USDC&algo_type=BRACKET
steps.important: For a BUY parent order, TP/SL child orders must have side 'SELL'. For a SELL parent order, they must have side 'BUY'.

commonIssues.issue: Child orders rejected with validation error.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure `reduce_only: true` is set on all child orders and that the TP/SL side is opposite to the parent order side.

commonIssues.issue: Trying to add TP/SL to a Stop order.
commonIssues.solution: Stop orders do not support TP/SL directly. Only Limit or Market parent orders can have bracket child orders.

commonIssues.issue: Trigger price not activating as expected.
commonIssues.solution: Check the `trigger_price_type` setting. By default, it may use mark price. Ensure the trigger price value is realistic relative to the current market price.

commonIssues.issue: REST API returns stale data.

commonIssues.issue: WebSocket connection drops frequently.

workflows.name: Handling USDC Decimal Precision on BNB Chain
workflows.description: Manage the decimal precision mismatch for USDC on BNB Chain, where on-chain USDC uses 18 decimals but Orderly only supports 6 decimals for deposits and withdrawals.
prerequisites: Integration with Orderly Public Token API

steps.title: Query Token Decimals from Public Token API
steps.description: Before processing any on-chain transaction, always refer to the `decimals` field in the `chain_details` returned by the Public Token API.
steps.important: USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain, but Orderly only supports 6 decimals for deposits and withdrawals. Always use the API-returned decimals value.

steps.title: Adjust Amount Calculations
steps.description: When constructing on-chain transactions for USDC on BNB Chain, use 18 decimal precision. When interacting with Orderly APIs, use 6 decimal precision.
steps.important: Failing to handle the precision mismatch will result in incorrect deposit/withdrawal amounts — potentially off by a factor of 10^12.

steps.title: Implement Dynamic Decimal Handling
steps.description: Build your integration to dynamically read and apply the correct decimal precision from the API rather than hardcoding values.
steps.important: This approach ensures your integration remains correct even if decimal configurations change for other tokens or chains in the future.

commonIssues.issue: Deposit amounts are wildly incorrect on BNB Chain.
commonIssues.solution: You are likely using 6 decimals for on-chain transactions when BNB Chain USDC requires 18 decimals. Always read the `decimals` field from the Public Token API's `chain_details`.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal amounts appear too small on BNB Chain.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are converting from Orderly's 6-decimal representation to BNB Chain's 18-decimal representation when constructing the withdrawal transaction.

workflows.name: Customizing Orderly SDK UI — Chain Filters, Testnet, and Localization
workflows.description: Customize the Orderly SDK user interface by filtering chains, hiding testnet options, adding new chains, and fixing localization bugs.
prerequisites: Chain IDs for target networks (from chainlist.org)

steps.title: Hide Testnet and Filter Mainnet Chains
steps.description: Use the `chainFilter` prop on `OrderlyAppProvider` with an empty `testnet` array to hide testnet chains and specify which mainnet chains to show.
steps.code:
<OrderlyAppProvider
  chainFilter={{
    mainnet: [Arbitrum],
    testnet: [],
  }}
>
  {props.children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
steps.important: There is no built-in default chain setting. To default to a specific chain like Base, prompt the user's wallet provider to switch chains on connection.

steps.title: Add New Chains (e.g., Story, Solana)
steps.description: Include custom chain IDs in the chainFilter to add support for new networks.
steps.important: Look up chain IDs at chainlist.org. If using the Components SDK, new supported chains may appear automatically.

steps.title: Configure Testnet-Only Mode
steps.description: To support only testnet networks (e.g., Monad testnet) and exclude mainnet, set the testnet array with chain info and leave mainnet empty.
steps.code:
<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="orderly"
  brokerName="Orderly"
  networkId="mainnet"
  chainFilter={{
    testnet: [{
      id: 10143,
      chainInfo: {
        name: "Monad Testnet",
        public_rpc_url: "https://testnet-rpc.monad.xyz",
        chainId: 10143,
        currency_symbol: "MON",
        explorer_base_url: "",
        vault_address: "",
      },
    }],
    mainnet: []
  }}
>
  {props.children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>
steps.important: Use `chainFilter` to explicitly exclude chains you don't want (e.g., BNB Chain) if you prefer not to upgrade to a version that includes them.

steps.title: Fix English (en) Localization Bug
steps.description: There is a known bug where changing the English locale JSON file does not update default text in the UI. Fix it by removing a specific code block.
steps.important: Other languages work correctly. Only the English (en) locale is affected by this bug.

commonIssues.issue: Arb Sepolia still appears after hiding testnet.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are using a compatible SDK version. Some versions like 2.0.0 introduced config changes that may affect chain filtering behavior.

commonIssues.issue: English locale changes not reflected in UI.
commonIssues.solution: Delete the `if (lang === LocaleEnum.en)` block in `app/components/orderlyProvider/index.tsx` as described in the localization fix step.

commonIssues.issue: New chain not appearing in selector.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the chain ID is correct at chainlist.org and that the chainFilter prop is properly structured with the correct nesting.

workflows.name: Understanding Orderly Withdrawal Security and Mechanisms
workflows.description: Understand how Orderly handles withdrawals, the security mechanisms in place, and what brokers can implement for additional security layers.

steps.title: Understand Withdrawal Verification
steps.description: All withdrawals are verified against a private key signature — there is no way to forge a withdrawal without the user's private key. Orderly API keys (access keys) do not have withdrawal permissions.
steps.important: This means even if an API key is compromised, an attacker cannot initiate withdrawals. Only the user's private key can authorize fund movements.

steps.title: Configure Withdrawal Receiver Addresses
steps.description: Withdrawals can be sent to any specified receiver address via the API. The user controls the destination address through their signed withdrawal request.
steps.important: Orderly does not restrict withdrawal destinations at the protocol level.

steps.title: Implement Broker-Level Security (Optional)
steps.description: While Orderly does not currently support time-locked withdrawals or IP-based restrictions at the protocol level, brokers can implement their own security layers.
steps.important: These security measures are implemented at the broker/frontend level, not at the Orderly protocol level.

commonIssues.issue: Users requesting time-locked withdrawals.
commonIssues.solution: Orderly does not support time-locked withdrawals at the protocol level. Implement this at the broker level using smart contracts or custom withdrawal approval workflows.

commonIssues.issue: Users requesting IP-based withdrawal restrictions.
commonIssues.solution: Implement IP restrictions on your broker's servers or frontend. Orderly does not enforce IP-based restrictions on withdrawal requests at the protocol level.

prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation (1,000 USDC or 25% discount with $ORDER) or approved BD partnership
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions

steps.title: Obtain a Custom Broker ID
steps.description: Graduate your DEX via Orderly One by paying the 1,000 USDC fee (or 25% discount if paid with $ORDER), or contact the Orderly BD team for a free partnership setup. Before graduation, DEXs use the shared 'Demo' broker ID.
steps.important: Partnership setup may take 3-4 days including multisig signing. The Orderly team handles the initial backend configuration.

steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done separately on both mainnet and testnet.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature. Many brokers use a multisig on mainnet.

steps.important: Testnet and mainnet are separate environments. You must register an account under your broker ID on each network separately.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees via the admin portal UI or by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. As of 2026, maker fee rebates range from -0.5bps to 0, meaning brokers can pay users to provide liquidity.

steps.title: Configure Volume-Based Fee Tiers
steps.description: Use the Python fee admin script to set per-user fee tiers based on trading volume. Configure tiers in a YAML file and run the script periodically (e.g., via cron job).
steps.code:
# YAML configuration example:
rate:
  fee_tier:
  - maker_fee: 0.03%
    taker_fee: 0.07%
    tier: '1'
    volume_max: 500000
    volume_min: 0

# Python script:
# https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/orderly-evm-broker-fee-admin
steps.important: This script updates per-user fee tiers based on their trading volume — it does NOT change the default/static fee displayed on the UI. It must be run periodically to keep user tiers updated.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection and Claim Rebates
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account. Check the balance by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet or using the private Get Current Holding endpoint.
steps.important: To claim rebates, log in to your own UI or the broker registration UI with the admin wallet and withdraw. A dedicated fee breakdown API for builders is not yet available.

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet. Admin credentials (Orderly Key/Secret) are not the wallet private key — generate them from the broker registration page or Portfolio > API Keys.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: Volume-based fee tiers not updating for users.
commonIssues.solution: The Python fee admin script must be run periodically (e.g., via cron job). It does not run automatically. Ensure the YAML configuration is correct and the script completes successfully.

steps.title: Review Builder Tier Classifications
steps.description: The Tier System categorizes builders into Public, Silver, Gold, Platinum, and Diamond tiers based on 30-day average trading volume or ORDER staked.
steps.important: Higher tiers also enable co-marketing support and listing campaigns. RWA pair fees are also tier-based as of late 2025.

steps.title: Stake ORDER Tokens
steps.description: Stake ORDER tokens to qualify for higher builder tiers and reduced base fees.
steps.code:
// Staking portal:
https://app.orderly.network/staking
steps.important: Staking is an alternative to meeting volume thresholds. For example, staking 2M ORDER qualifies for Platinum tier (2 bps) without needing $1B in 30-day volume.

steps.title: Leverage Maker Fee Rebates
steps.description: As of 2026, Orderly offers negative maker fees (maker fee rebates) ranging from -0.5bps to 0. Brokers can keep the rebate as revenue or pass it to users as incentives.
steps.code:
// Maker fee rebate details:
// https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/trade-on-orderly/trading-basics/trading-fees#builder-staking-programme
steps.important: Brokers have full flexibility to either keep the rebate as their own revenue or pass it to users as incentives to boost volume.

steps.title: Monitor Tier Status
steps.description: Track your 30-day volume and staking amounts to maintain or improve your tier classification.
steps.important: Tier benefits include marketing support, listing campaigns, and fee reductions. Losing tier status will increase your base taker fee.

commonIssues.issue: Tier classification not updating after staking.
commonIssues.solution: Tier updates may take time to process. Ensure your staking wallet address was correctly provided during broker ID registration. Contact Orderly support if the tier does not update.

commonIssues.issue: Unclear how maker fee rebates are distributed.
commonIssues.solution: Maker fee rebates (-0.5bps to 0) are credited to the broker. The broker decides whether to retain them or pass them to users. Configure this through your fee structure.

steps.important: Referral splits apply only to the broker's portion of fees, not Orderly's base fee.

commonIssues.issue: FeeTierModule not displaying correct tiers.

workflows.name: Tracking TVL and On-Chain Activity
workflows.description: Calculate Total Value Locked (TVL) and track deposits/withdrawals on Orderly contracts for analytics and monitoring.
prerequisites: Access to blockchain indexer (Dune, custom indexer, etc.)
Knowledge of Orderly contract addresses on target chains

steps.title: Index Deposit Events
steps.description: Track deposit events from Orderly contracts. The user wallet address is found in `args.userAddress` for both deposit event types.
steps.important: Both deposit event types use args.userAddress for the user's wallet address.

steps.title: Index Withdrawal Events
steps.description: Track withdrawal events. Note that the user wallet address is in `args.receiver` (NOT `args.sender`), and the fee is already deducted from the amount field.
steps.important: A common mistake is using args.sender instead of args.receiver for withdrawal tracking. The receiver is the actual user.

steps.title: Calculate TVL
steps.description: Compute TVL as the sum of all deposits minus the sum of all withdrawals.
steps.important: Ensure consistent decimal handling across chains. For example, USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain but Orderly only supports 6 decimals for deposits/withdrawals.

steps.title: Handle Decimal Precision Differences
steps.description: Always refer to the `decimals` field in the `chain_details` returned by the Public Token API before processing on-chain transactions.
steps.important: Mismatched decimal precision is a common source of errors in TVL calculations and on-chain transaction processing.

commonIssues.issue: TVL calculation is significantly off.
commonIssues.solution: Check decimal precision handling across chains. USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain but Orderly uses 6. Always reference the Public Token API's chain_details.decimals field.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawal tracking shows wrong user addresses.
commonIssues.solution: Use args.receiver (not args.sender) for the AccountWithdraw event. The sender may be the contract, while the receiver is the actual user.

steps.description: Add a delegate signer to register a smart contract as a user on Orderly. This allows the contract to sign and execute trades.
steps.code:
// Documentation:
https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/user-flows/delegate-signer
steps.important: Alternatively, an EOA wallet can be used for trading instead of the delegate signer feature, though fully automated on-chain execution is not possible either way.

steps.title: Configure Trading Parameters for Hedging
steps.description: When setting up hedging strategies, carefully consider the funding rate to avoid unnecessary costs.
steps.important: Funding rate direction determines whether hedging is cost-effective. Shorting when funding is negative means you pay funding fees instead of receiving them.

steps.title: Implement Trade Execution Logic
steps.description: Build the smart contract logic to execute trades on Orderly using the delegate signer authentication.
steps.important: Fully automated on-chain execution is not possible — the delegate signer or EOA must interact with Orderly's off-chain matching engine via API.

commonIssues.issue: Smart contract cannot sign Orderly API requests.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the delegate signer is properly registered and that the contract implements the required EIP-712 signing interface. Refer to the delegate signer documentation for implementation details.

commonIssues.issue: Hedging costs are higher than expected.
commonIssues.solution: Check the funding rate direction before executing hedge trades. If the pool is net long and you're shorting, only proceed when the funding rate is positive to avoid paying extra fees.

steps.title: Prompt User to Create Read-Only API Key
steps.description: The user must create a read-only Orderly API key for authentication. The user signs a message with their wallet to establish the connection between the third-party platform and Orderly.
steps.code:
// API authentication docs:
https://orderly.network/docs/build-on-omnichain/evm-api/api-authentication

workflows.description: Deploy ORDER or custom tokens cross-chain using LayerZero's Omnichain Fungible Token (OFT) standard.

steps.title: Reference Orderly OFT Implementation
steps.description: Use Orderly's public OFT token repository as a reference for your cross-chain token deployment.
steps.code:
// Reference repository:
https://github.com/OrderlyNetwork/oft-token
steps.important: Orderly increased the token transfer type from uint64 to uint256 and uses 18 decimals. The default LZ devtool contracts are non-upgradeable.

steps.title: Configure Token Parameters
steps.description: Set up your OFT token with the correct decimal configuration and transfer type settings.
steps.important: For Solana (SPL tokens supporting only u64), local decimals must be set to 10, resulting in an 8-decimal loss when bridging from EVM to Solana.

steps.title: Deploy Across Target Chains
steps.description: Deploy the OFT token contract on each target chain and configure LayerZero endpoints for cross-chain communication.
steps.important: Stargate may have example interfaces for OFT-based token sends that can serve as additional reference.

commonIssues.issue: Decimal precision loss when bridging to Solana.
commonIssues.solution: This is expected behavior. Solana SPL tokens support only u64, so local decimals must be set to 10, resulting in an 8-decimal loss when bridging from EVM (18 decimals) to Solana.

commonIssues.issue: Cross-chain transfers failing.
commonIssues.solution: Verify LayerZero endpoint configuration on all deployed chains. Ensure gas is provided for cross-chain message delivery. Check LayerZero explorer for message status.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, and set up default trading fees.
prerequisites: Broker ID requested from Orderly team (text with no spaces, e.g., 'pump_space')
Broker Name and desired default maker/taker fees
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions

steps.title: Request Broker ID from Orderly Team
steps.description: Provide the Orderly team with a Broker ID (text with no spaces), a Broker Name, and desired default maker/taker fees. The broker ID is required to go live with a perp DEX built on Orderly's infrastructure.
steps.important: The broker ID must be approved and created by the Orderly team before proceeding with registration.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments. The connected chain does not matter for registration.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Testnet and mainnet can use different addresses. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly (takes one to two days), log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account. Check the balance by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet or using the private Get Current Holding endpoint. There is no direct API to check which address is the admin — only keys from the admin account can access broker-admin authenticated APIs.
steps.code:
GET /v1/holding
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id

steps.title: Update Admin Fee Wallet Address (If Needed)
steps.description: To update the fee wallet address later, provide the new address to the Orderly team. The new wallet must first be registered on your DEX under your broker ID before the team can update it manually.
steps.important: Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet. This process takes one to two days after registration.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot determine which wallet is the admin.
commonIssues.solution: There is no direct API to check which address is the admin. Only keys from the admin account can access broker-admin authenticated APIs. To confirm fee collection, check that the Orderly account balance (not the wallet balance) of the admin account increases daily as fees accrue.

workflows.name: Enabling Deposit Zap-in (Auto-Swap Deposits)
workflows.description: Enable the Deposit Zap-in feature that allows users to deposit any token into their Orderly perpetual account, with the token automatically swapped to a supported collateral asset during the deposit process.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.10.1 or later installed

steps.title: Verify SDK Version
steps.description: Ensure your application is using Orderly SDK v2.10.1 or later, which introduced the Deposit Zap-in feature.
steps.code:
// Check your package.json
"@orderly.network/react": "^2.10.1"

steps.title: Enable Swap Deposit Prop
steps.description: Add the `enableSwapDeposit` prop to your `<OrderlyAppProvider>` component to activate the feature.
steps.code:
import { OrderlyAppProvider } from "@orderly.network/react";

<OrderlyAppProvider
  brokerId="your_broker_id"
  brokerName="Your Broker"
  networkId="mainnet"
  enableSwapDeposit
>
  {children}
</OrderlyAppProvider>

steps.title: Configure Dynamic Chain Support (Optional)
steps.description: Zap-In Deposit supports dynamic chain configuration via API, allowing users to deposit from chains that may not be statically configured in your app.
steps.important: The deposited token is automatically swapped to a supported collateral asset (e.g., USDC) during the deposit process.

commonIssues.issue: Deposit Zap-in option does not appear in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the `enableSwapDeposit` prop is correctly set on the OrderlyAppProvider and that you are using SDK v2.10.1 or later.

commonIssues.issue: Swap fails for certain tokens.
commonIssues.solution: Not all tokens may have sufficient liquidity for the auto-swap. Ensure the token has a valid trading pair on the supported DEX aggregators used by the Zap-in feature.

workflows.name: Configuring the Multilevel Referral Program
workflows.description: Enable and configure the Orderly DEX Multilevel Referral Program to scale growth and incentivize communities through multi-tier referral rewards, including referral code URL parameters and post-registration binding.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.9.0 or later (v2.12.4+ recommended for post-registration binding)
Access to Admin Tool or Orderly One dashboard

steps.title: Upgrade SDK
steps.description: Ensure your DEX is running SDK version 2.9.0 or later. For Orderly One DEXs, ensure you are on the latest version available on the platform.
steps.important: As of SDK v2.12.4, users can bind a referral code to their existing account at any time post-registration, rather than being required to provide a code during registration.

steps.title: Activate the Referral Program
steps.description: Enable or upgrade the referral program via the Admin Tool or through the Orderly One dashboard.
steps.code:
// Admin Portal:
https://admin.orderly.network/login

steps.title: Configure Referral Code Parameters
steps.description: When creating a referral code, configure the rebate rates. All values are expressed as absolute decimals (e.g., 0.5 means 50% of fees).
steps.important: Referral rebates are settled in USDC regardless of the collateral asset used, and are sent to users once per day.

steps.title: Set Up Referral Code URL Parameters
steps.description: Append a referral code parameter to any URL on your Orderly-powered DEX to pre-fill the referral code during user registration. The SDK handles registration automatically when a user accesses the platform via a referral link, though the user must sign a message.
steps.important: This works on any page that uses the Orderly referral provider — the frontend sends the code to bind it to the user's account. The referral code must be a valid, active code configured in the admin portal. Referral links can be obtained from the Rewards page of the DEX.

steps.title: Use order_tag for Per-Order Referral Tracking
steps.description: Attach a referral code at the order level using the `order_tag` field in the create order API. This overrides any account-level referral binding.
steps.code:
POST /v1/order
Body: {
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "order_type": "MARKET",
  "order_quantity": "0.01",
  "side": "BUY",
  "order_tag": "BBBB" // Overrides account-level referral code
}

steps.title: Build Custom Affiliate/Referral Tracking
steps.description: Referral and affiliate programs must be developed by each DEX independently; Orderly provides the underlying APIs. Brokers can also act as referrers for a third-party broker, in which case the third-party broker generates the referral code.
steps.important: For tracking traffic and volume from specific affiliate links, brokers need to build their own affiliate/referral tracking system on top of Orderly's APIs.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot register referral code for a KOL/affiliate.
commonIssues.solution: The KOL/affiliate must first connect their wallet and sign in to create an Orderly account. Attempting to register a ref code before the user has signed in will result in an 'address is not registered' error.

commonIssues.issue: Rebates not appearing for users.
commonIssues.solution: Rebates are settled once per day in USDC. Ensure the referral code is correctly bound to the user's account and that the rebate rates are properly configured.

commonIssues.issue: Referral code not binding when user visits referral URL.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the referral code is valid and active in the admin portal. The user must sign a message for the binding to complete. The code must be in the format ?ref={REFERRAL_CODE} appended to any page using the Orderly referral provider.

workflows.name: Upgrading to Solana Multi-DVN Security Model
workflows.description: Mandatory security upgrade for all DEXes integrated with Solana, migrating from a single LayerZero DVN to a 3-of-3 consensus model using three independent DVNs.

steps.title: Upgrade SDK to v2.12.3+
steps.description: Update your Orderly SDK to version 2.12.3 or later. This version facilitates the migration to the new multi-verifier framework for the Solana Vault contract.
steps.important: This is a critical security upgrade following a LayerZero exploit. DEXs that do not upgrade may experience failures with Solana deposits and withdrawals.

steps.title: Verify Solana Wallet Connection Fixes
steps.description: SDK v2.12.3 also includes Google OAuth login support within Telegram Mini Apps and fixes for Solana wallet connection issues. SDK v2.11.2 fixes a bug where Privy Wallet generated duplicate Solana addresses.
steps.important: Ensure all Solana wallet connection flows are tested after the upgrade.

steps.title: Verify Solana Deposit/Withdrawal Functionality
steps.description: After upgrading, test Solana deposits and withdrawals on testnet to ensure smooth operations under the new 3-of-3 consensus model.
steps.important: The upgrade eliminates a single point of dependency by using three independent Decentralized Verifier Networks (DVNs).

steps.title: Deploy to Production
steps.description: Once verified on testnet, deploy the updated SDK to your production environment.
steps.important: All builders supporting Solana must upgrade to ensure continued operation.

commonIssues.issue: Solana deposits or withdrawals fail after upgrade.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure all SDK packages are updated to v2.12.3 or later. Check that no conflicting older versions remain in your dependency tree.

commonIssues.issue: Cross-chain messages stuck in verification.

workflows.name: Debugging Orderly API Requests and Resolving SDK Errors
workflows.description: Troubleshoot Orderly API request payloads, resolve common SDK errors, and handle module resolution issues during upgrades.
prerequisites: Access to a partner DEX for comparison (e.g., WooFi)

steps.title: Compare API Payloads with Partner DEX
steps.description: Open a partner DEX (e.g., WooFi) that uses Orderly, perform the same operation (deposit, withdrawal, trade), and inspect the network request in the browser's developer console. Compare the payload structure, parameter types (string vs. number), and values against your own request to identify discrepancies.
steps.important: This is the recommended debugging approach for identifying API request issues.

steps.title: Resolve 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading get)' Error
steps.description: This error typically occurs when mixing SDK v1 and v2 components in the same project. Use SDK v2 exclusively and follow the official templates.
steps.important: Never mix SDK v1 and v2 components in the same project.

steps.title: Resolve Module Resolution Errors in Create React App
steps.description: When upgrading the SDK in a CRA-based project, you may encounter strict ESM module resolution errors (e.g., related to node-stdlib-browser/cjs/proxy/process or @binance/w3w-utils). Modify your Craco configuration to handle polyfills and module resolution properly.
steps.important: Ensure you are using node-polyfill-webpack-plugin and configure Craco's webpack settings to resolve fully specified ESM paths.

steps.title: Handle USDC Decimals on BNB Chain
steps.description: USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain, but Orderly only supports 6 decimals for deposits and withdrawals. Always refer to the decimals field in the chain_details returned by the Public Token API before processing on-chain transactions.
steps.important: SDK v2.3.0 or higher is required for BNB Chain integration. If you prefer not to upgrade, use chainFilter to explicitly exclude BNB Chain from your configuration.

commonIssues.issue: 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading get)' error in TradingPage.
commonIssues.solution: This occurs when mixing SDK v1 and v2 components. Use SDK v2 exclusively and follow the official Next.js template. Configure a custom wallet connection provider for your existing wallet setup.

commonIssues.issue: 'Can't resolve process' or similar ESM module errors after SDK upgrade in CRA.
commonIssues.solution: Install node-polyfill-webpack-plugin and configure Craco's webpack settings to handle polyfills and resolve fully specified ESM paths.

commonIssues.issue: Deposit/withdrawal precision mismatch on BNB Chain.
commonIssues.solution: USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain but Orderly supports only 6. Always check the decimals field in chain_details from the Public Token API. Use SDK v2.3.0+ or exclude BNB Chain via chainFilter.

commonIssues.issue: API request returns unexpected error.
commonIssues.solution: Compare your request payload with the same operation on a partner DEX like WooFi using browser developer tools. Check parameter types (string vs. number) and values.

workflows.name: Understanding the Orderly Key Authentication Flow
workflows.description: Understand and implement the Orderly key (ed25519) registration and authentication flow for API integrations.

steps.title: Generate ed25519 Key Pair Client-Side
steps.description: The Orderly key is an ed25519 private key generated client-side and registered with the backend, functioning similarly to a JWT for sessions. The Orderly key (public key) and Orderly secret (private key) are generated together.
steps.important: Key generation and storage happens on the client side (localStorage). The key is passed into the signing function provided by write functions.

steps.title: Sign EIP-712 Message for Registration
steps.description: The setup/authentication flow requires the user to sign an EIP-712 message before trading. This binds the ed25519 key to the user's wallet address.
steps.important: The user must sign the EIP-712 message to complete key registration.

steps.title: Execute Sequential Action Params
steps.description: The action params returned from setup are executed sequentially — the second action is only called after the first fetch completes.
steps.important: Ensure your implementation handles the sequential nature of action params correctly to avoid race conditions.

steps.title: Authenticate API Requests
steps.description: Use the generated Orderly key pair to sign and authenticate API requests with the required headers.
steps.important: The timestamp must be current UTC time in milliseconds for the signature to be valid.

commonIssues.issue: Authentication fails with invalid signature.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the timestamp is current UTC time in milliseconds and that the ed25519 key pair was correctly generated and registered.

commonIssues.issue: Key not persisting across sessions.
commonIssues.solution: The Orderly key is stored in localStorage. Ensure your application does not clear localStorage unexpectedly and that the key registration flow completes successfully.

commonIssues.issue: Sequential action params failing.
commonIssues.solution: The second action is only called after the first fetch completes. Ensure your implementation properly awaits each action before proceeding to the next.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration

steps.title: Provide Broker Details to Orderly Team
steps.description: Submit your Broker ID, Broker Name, Default Taker Fee Rate, and Default Maker Fee Rate to the Orderly team for initial setup.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Any amount above the base fee is retained by the broker.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig and smart contract wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Once an admin wallet is registered, the broker can adjust base fees themselves via the REST API. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account. Check the balance by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet or using the private Get Current Holding endpoint.

Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

workflows.name: Configuring the Multilevel Referral Program
workflows.description: Enable and configure the Orderly DEX Multilevel Referral Program to scale growth and incentivize communities through multi-tier referral rewards, including commission splits and per-order tracking.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.9.0 or later (or latest Orderly One version)
Access to Admin Tool or Orderly One dashboard

steps.title: Upgrade SDK
steps.description: Ensure your DEX is running SDK version 2.9.0 or later. For Orderly One DEXs, ensure you are on the latest version available on the platform.
steps.important: As of SDK v2.12.4, users can bind a referral code to their existing account at any time post-registration, rather than being required to provide a code during registration.

steps.title: Activate the Referral Program
steps.description: Enable or upgrade the referral program via the Admin Tool or through the Orderly One dashboard.

steps.title: Create Referral Codes Programmatically
steps.description: Create referral codes via the broker backend using the private REST API endpoint. Each broker must create codes through their own admin setup.
steps.important: Referral codes are created by the broker via their backend. This is not something Orderly can do on behalf of integrators.

steps.title: Configure Multi-Level Commission Splits
steps.description: When assigning a commission rate to an L1 affiliate (e.g., 80%), that affiliate can freely split their allocation with downstream referees. The L1 affiliate controls the distribution.
steps.important: The referrer and referee share the broker's net fee (gross fee minus Orderly's base fee). Rebates are credited on a daily basis in USDC.

steps.title: Use order_tag for Per-Order Referral Tracking
steps.description: Attach a referral code at the order level using the `order_tag` field in the create order API. This overrides any account-level referral binding and allows third-party integrations to attribute trades.
steps.code:
POST /v1/order
Body: {
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "order_type": "MARKET",
  "order_quantity": "0.01",
  "side": "BUY",
  "order_tag": "BBBB" // Overrides account-level referral code
}
steps.important: The order_tag is set per-order by the integrator and does not need to be pre-created by Orderly. It functions similarly to a referral code.

steps.title: Retrieve Referral Information for Display
steps.description: Use the private REST API to retrieve referral details including fee share configuration for building custom invite/signup pages.

steps.title: Retrieve All Referral Users
steps.description: Use the admin endpoint to get all referees including those without referral codes. The private endpoint only returns referees who have created their own codes.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot register referral code for a KOL/affiliate.
commonIssues.solution: The KOL/affiliate must first connect their wallet and sign in to create an Orderly account. Attempting to register a ref code before the user has signed in will result in an 'address is not registered' error.

commonIssues.issue: Rebates not appearing for users.
commonIssues.solution: Rebates are settled once per day in USDC. Ensure the referral code is correctly bound to the user's account and that the rebate rates are properly configured.

commonIssues.issue: Referral list missing users without codes.
commonIssues.solution: Use GET /v1/admin/referee/list for all referees. The private endpoint GET /v1/referral/multi_level/referee_list only returns referees who have created their own referral codes.

workflows.name: Capturing Builder Revenue and Understanding Fee Mechanics
workflows.description: Understand how builders capture revenue on Orderly through broker fee layers, maker fee rebates, order_tag attribution, and the Builder Staking Programme.
prerequisites: Active broker ID registered with Orderly

steps.title: Route Orders Through Your Broker ID
steps.description: To capture revenue, builders must set up their own Orderly broker and route all orders through their broker ID. Routing trades through another broker's ID will not allow fee capture.
steps.important: Orderly does not currently support per-order builder codes like some other DEXs. API/SDK integration allows backend-only order routing without requiring a frontend.

steps.title: Add Custom Fee Layer
steps.description: Builders can add their own fee layer (e.g., a taker spread markup) on top of Orderly's base fees within their own system.
steps.important: Any amount above Orderly's base fee is retained by the broker.

steps.title: Leverage Maker Fee Rebates via Builder Staking
steps.description: Stake $ORDER tokens to access negative maker fees ranging from -0.5 bps to 0 bps (Silver tier and above). Negative maker fees settle immediately on each execution for traders.
steps.important: Builder maker and taker revenue are batched and settled once per day. Builders can keep the rebate as revenue or pass it to users as trading incentives.

steps.title: Use order_tag for Volume Attribution
steps.description: Set the order_tag field to any string value when placing orders to attribute trades and receive a share of broker fees. This allows third-party integrations (e.g., trading terminals) to track volume.
steps.important: The order_tag overrides the user's default referral code when present and does not need to be pre-created by Orderly.

steps.title: Check Volume Attributed to Broker or Referral Code
steps.description: Use the private REST API to retrieve volume data attributed to your broker or specific referral codes.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot capture fees when routing through another broker's ID.
commonIssues.solution: You must route all orders through your own broker ID. Routing through another broker's ID (e.g., Aegis) will not allow fee capture.

commonIssues.issue: Maker rebates not appearing.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your DEX is at Silver tier or above in the Builder Staking Programme. Negative maker fees settle immediately per execution, but builder revenue is batched daily.

commonIssues.issue: Understanding fee split between broker, referrer, and trader.
commonIssues.solution: The referrer and referee share the broker's net fee. Example: 4 bps taker fee with 3 bps Orderly base = 1 bps broker fee. With 50/50 referral split: broker gets 0.5 bps, referrer gets 0.5 bps, trader gets no discount.

steps.title: Implement Delegate Signer for Smart Wallets
steps.description: If each user has their own smart wallet (smart contract), use the delegate signer functionality for registration, Orderly key creation, withdrawals, and other operations.
steps.important: Smart contract wallets cannot sign messages the same way as EOAs. The delegate signer pattern allows an EOA to sign on behalf of the smart contract wallet.

steps.title: Register Smart Wallet via Delegate Signer
steps.description: During the registration process, provide both the smart wallet address and the delegate signer (EOA) address that will sign transactions on behalf of the smart wallet.

steps.important: Coin98 requires the 'Override Metamask' setting to be enabled for proper integration.

commonIssues.issue: Smart wallet registration fails.

workflows.description: Understand the Excalibur Club high-volume trader rebate program and the Orderly trading rewards mechanism with staking multipliers.

steps.title: Understand Excalibur Club Eligibility
steps.description: The Excalibur Club provides a 0.5 bps rebate to brokers on all trading volume generated by users whose trailing 30-day trading volume exceeds 250 million USDC.
steps.important: Eligibility is evaluated daily. Note: this program may not continue post-TGE.

steps.title: Monitor High-Volume Traders
steps.description: Track user trading volumes to identify users approaching or exceeding the 250M USDC trailing 30-day threshold for Excalibur Club benefits.
steps.code:
// Use the builder users volumes endpoint:
GET /v1/builder/users/volumes

steps.title: Understand Trading Rewards Mechanism
steps.description: Trading rewards are distributed from a pool (e.g., 1M ORDER per epoch) proportionally based on a DEX's share of total Orderly volume. Users earn based on staked esORDER and trading volume with a dynamic multiplier.
steps.code:
// Trading rewards documentation:
// https://orderly.network/docs/introduction/tokenomics/trading-rewards/trading-rewards-mechanism
steps.important: Historically, rewards equated to approximately 1.5–2 bps equivalent. The exact multiplier formula depends on staked amount, individual trading volume, and total platform volume.

steps.title: Leverage Builder Staking Programme
steps.description: Stake $ORDER tokens to access lower base fee tiers (Silver, Diamond) and negative maker fees. Staking currently provides APY paid in USDC.
steps.important: Until volume-based tier qualification is available, tiers are determined purely by staking amount.

commonIssues.issue: Excalibur Club rebate not appearing.
commonIssues.solution: Verify the user's trailing 30-day volume exceeds 250M USDC. Eligibility is evaluated daily. Note that this program may not continue post-TGE.

commonIssues.issue: Trading rewards lower than expected.
commonIssues.solution: The multiplier is dynamic and depends on staked esORDER amount, individual trading volume relative to total platform volume. Check the mechanism documentation for the current formula.

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, set up default trading fees, and withdraw accumulated broker revenue.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions

steps.title: Register Broker ID with Orderly Team
steps.description: Provide the following to the Orderly team: Broker ID, Broker Name, Default Taker Fee, Default Maker Fee, Broker Tier, and Staking Wallet. Use broker ID 'demo' for development/testing while waiting for approval.
steps.important: Broker ID approval requires multi-signature authorization and may take a few days. Fee rates can be adjusted later via the admin console.

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee. The Maker Fee ranges from -0.5bps to 0 (Orderly subsidizes makers). Brokers can retain the maker rebate as revenue or pass it to users. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection and Withdraw Revenue
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account. Withdraw via your DEX frontend (log in with admin wallet) or the broker registration tool.
steps.important: Withdrawal amounts may be less than expected due to network gas fees. On Ethereum mainnet, gas fees can be significant. On Arbitrum or Base, the withdrawal fee is a flat $1. Use the DEX UI to preview fees before withdrawing, or switch to a cheaper network.

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet shows as 'unregistered' when trying to access fees.
commonIssues.solution: Verify you are using the correct admin wallet address associated with your broker. If using a multisig, ensure the delegate signer is properly configured.

commonIssues.issue: Withdrawn amount is less than expected.
commonIssues.solution: The difference is due to network withdrawal (gas) fees. Switch to a cheaper network like Arbitrum or Base (flat $1 fee) to reduce costs. The admin portal UI does not display current withdrawal fees per network.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

workflows.name: Managing Isolated Margin Positions via API
workflows.description: Set leverage, retrieve liquidation prices, and adjust margin for isolated margin positions using the Orderly REST API.
prerequisites: Orderly API credentials (API key and secret)
Active Orderly account with no open positions or pending orders on target symbol (for margin mode switching)
Understanding of isolated vs cross margin behavior

steps.title: Verify Current Margin Mode
steps.description: Check the current margin mode for a symbol before attempting to change it. You can only switch margin mode when there are no open positions or pending orders.
steps.code:
GET /v1/client/margin_modes
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id

steps.title: Set Leverage for Isolated Margin
steps.description: Use the singular `/v1/client/leverage` endpoint (NOT the plural `/v1/client/leverages`) to set leverage for a specific symbol in Isolated Margin mode.
steps.code:
POST /v1/client/leverage
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id
Body: {
  "symbol": "PERP_BTC_USDC",
  "leverage": 3,
  "margin_mode": "ISOLATED"
}
steps.important: The plural `/v1/client/leverages` endpoint updates ALL symbols atomically and uses Cross margin behavior. Always use the singular endpoint for isolated margin per-symbol configuration.

steps.title: Get Estimated Liquidation Price
steps.description: Retrieve the estimated liquidation price for isolated positions using the isolated positions endpoint.

steps.title: Add Margin to Existing Isolated Position
steps.description: Increase or decrease collateral for an existing isolated position without changing the position size.
steps.code:
POST /api/v1/adjust_isolated_margin
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id
Body: {
  "subaccountId": "12345",
  "symbol": "PERP_BTC_USDC",
  "amount": 100,
  "type": "ADD"
}
steps.important: Set `type` to `"ADD"` for increasing margin or `"REDUCE"` for decreasing margin. This does not change the position size.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot switch margin mode for a symbol.
commonIssues.solution: You can only switch margin mode when you have no open positions or pending orders on that symbol. Close all positions and cancel pending orders first, then verify via GET /v1/client/margin_modes.

commonIssues.issue: Leverage change affects all symbols instead of just one.
commonIssues.solution: You are likely using the plural `/v1/client/leverages` endpoint which updates all symbols atomically with Cross margin behavior. Use the singular `/v1/client/leverage` endpoint for per-symbol isolated margin configuration.

commonIssues.issue: Position quantity smaller than filled order amount.
commonIssues.solution: This typically indicates a partial liquidation occurred. Check the user's position history for liquidation events. Liquidations trigger when the maintenance margin ratio (MMR) is breached. Provide the wallet address to Orderly tech support or check: https://orderly-dashboard.orderly.network/address/{ADDRESS}?broker_id={BROKER_ID}

// DefiLlama adapter source:

commonIssues.solution: This is expected. DefiLlama only tracks on-chain Vault smart contract balances. Orderly's official TVL also includes Ceffu (off-exchange settlement) balances which cannot be tracked on-chain.

workflows.name: Troubleshooting Common SDK and Integration Issues
workflows.description: Resolve frequent builder issues including Solana adapter bundling errors, PnL settlement failures, watchlist persistence, wallet compatibility, and SSL certificate problems.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK integrated in your project
Access to browser developer tools for debugging
Basic understanding of your build system (webpack/vite)

steps.title: Fix Solana Adapter Bundling for EVM-Only Projects
steps.description: The @orderly.network/hooks package hardcodes the Solana adapter as a dependency, forcing EVM-only integrators to bundle 242+ Solana packages causing OOM builds.
steps.important: This is a known high-impact builder experience issue. Monitor SDK release notes for the fix making Solana adapters optional.

steps.title: Debug PnL Settlement Failures
steps.description: When a user cannot settle PnL, verify the wallet is actually signing the settle_pnl request and that it reaches Orderly's servers.
steps.important: If the request never hits Orderly's servers, the issue is on the client side (e.g., signing failure). Provide the user's wallet address to Orderly tech support for further debugging.

steps.title: Fix Watchlist/Favorites Not Persisting
steps.description: Implement a custom ConfigStore to properly persist watchlists and favorites in local storage.
steps.important: The default ConfigStore does not separate watchlists by network. Implement custom logic using networkId if your app serves both mainnet and testnet from the same URL.

steps.title: Fix Binance Wallet Chain-Switching Errors
steps.description: Integrate the Binance Blocknative connector to resolve chain-switching issues with Binance Wallet connected via WalletConnect.

steps.title: Fix SSL Certificate Errors After Domain Changes
steps.description: When changing from a root domain to a subdomain (or vice versa), SSL certificates need to be re-provisioned.
steps.important: SSL certificates are provisioned automatically when you configure your custom domain through Orderly One and set correct DNS records. Propagation may take time. Root-to-subdomain changes require a new certificate unless using a wildcard certificate.

steps.title: Fix 'transactRemote is not exported' Error
steps.description: This error occurs due to version incompatibility with @solana-mobile/wallet-adapter-mobile after upgrading to SDK v2.1.1.

steps.title: Handle USDC Decimal Precision on BNB Chain
steps.description: USDC on BNB Chain uses 18 decimals on-chain, but Orderly only supports 6 decimals for deposits and withdrawals.
steps.important: Precision mismatches will cause deposit/withdrawal failures. Always refer to the API response rather than assuming decimal precision.

commonIssues.issue: Build fails with out-of-memory (OOM) errors.
commonIssues.solution: This is likely caused by the Solana adapter bundling issue. Configure tree-shaking to exclude Solana modules or pin to an earlier SDK version.

commonIssues.issue: Limit orders and positions not showing on TradingView chart.
commonIssues.solution: This functionality requires the paid version of TradingView. Some features may be available in the free version but are not implemented in the Orderly TradingPage component for the free tier.

commonIssues.issue: Mobile tabs (Trading, Portfolio, Markets) not appearing.
commonIssues.solution: Mobile tab navigation requires explicit configuration in your app config. Refer to: https://github.com/OrderlyNetworkDexCreator/dex-creator-template/blob/main/app/utils/config.tsx#L231-L233 and ensure you are using a recent SDK version.

commonIssues.issue: Affiliate dashboard pages not rendering correctly.

steps.important: All Orderly components and hooks use the connection provider context, ensuring compatibility with custom wallet providers.

workflows.name: Handling System Maintenance and Pending Orders
workflows.description: Manage Orderly system maintenance windows, configure automatic cancellation of pending orders, and track cross-chain withdrawal delays.
prerequisites: Access to Orderly System Updates Telegram channel

steps.title: Monitor Maintenance Announcements
steps.description: Join the Orderly System Updates Telegram channel for maintenance notifications. Maintenance windows are typically ~2 hours and occur roughly monthly.
steps.code:
// Join the notification channel:
https://t.me/+VnpoOvYpJXA2ZTc1
steps.important: Announce maintenance schedules to your users in advance. During maintenance, there is no trading activity.

steps.title: Configure Auto-Cancel for Pending Orders
steps.description: By default, pending orders are NOT automatically cancelled during maintenance. Users or brokers must explicitly enable this via the maintenance config API.
steps.important: Without this configuration, pending orders will remain in the order book and may execute when trading resumes after maintenance.

steps.title: Track Delayed Cross-Chain Withdrawals
steps.description: If a user's cross-chain withdrawal hasn't arrived, search for the transaction on the Orderly dashboard and track it via LayerZero.
steps.important: Cross-chain withdrawals may experience delays during security upgrades or LayerZero DVN migrations.

steps.title: Revoke Compromised or Unused API Keys
steps.description: Remove Orderly Keys (API keys) using the Remove Orderly Key endpoint when they are no longer needed or if compromised.
steps.important: Regularly audit and revoke unused API keys as a security best practice.

commonIssues.issue: Users complain about pending orders executing after maintenance.
commonIssues.solution: Inform users to enable auto-cancel via the maintenance config API, or implement this as a default setting in your DEX. Communicate clearly that pending orders remain active by default.

commonIssues.issue: Cross-chain withdrawal stuck for extended period.
commonIssues.solution: Track the transaction on LayerZero scan. Delays can occur during DVN migrations or security upgrades. If the transaction shows as completed on LayerZero but funds haven't arrived, contact Orderly support.

workflows.name: Choosing and Implementing an SDK Integration Path
workflows.description: Select the appropriate Orderly SDK integration option based on your customization needs and time-to-market requirements, from no-code to fully custom implementations.
prerequisites: Defined DEX requirements and customization needs
Development team with React/TypeScript experience (for SDK options)
Understanding of API integration patterns (for no-SDK option)

steps.title: Evaluate Integration Options
steps.description: Orderly offers four integration paths with varying levels of customization and time-to-market.
steps.important: Choose Components SDK for fastest time-to-market, Hooks SDK for custom UI with Orderly logic, Core SDK for non-React frameworks, or No SDK for full control.

steps.title: Set Up Trailing Stop Orders (SDK v2.6.3+)
steps.description: If using SDK v2.6.3 or later, Trailing Stop orders are available. They activate at a trigger price, track price extremes, and execute on retrace.
steps.code:
// Upgrade to SDK v2.6.3+ to enable Trailing Stop orders
"@orderly.network/react": "^2.6.3"
steps.important: Trailing Stop orders activate at a trigger price, track price extremes, and execute on retrace. Ensure your SDK version supports this order type.

steps.title: Configure Custom Asset Categories (SDK v2.12.0+)
steps.description: As of SDK v2.12.0, builders can configure custom asset categories for their UI (e.g., separating Crypto and RWA markets).
steps.important: Custom asset categories help users navigate markets more effectively, especially for DEXs offering diverse asset types.

steps.title: Leverage SDK v3 Plugin System
steps.description: SDK v3 introduces a Frontend Plugin System and Module Marketplace for extending the trading interface without forking the SDK.
steps.important: The plugin system enables builders to develop, share, and install custom modules without forking the SDK.

commonIssues.issue: Unsure which SDK option to choose.
commonIssues.solution: Start with the Components SDK for fastest deployment. Migrate to Hooks SDK if you need custom UI. Use Core SDK for non-React frameworks. Choose No SDK only if you need full control over every aspect.

commonIssues.issue: Core SDK documentation is incomplete.
commonIssues.solution: The Core SDK (@orderly.network/core) is not yet fully documented. Refer to the REST/WebSocket API documentation and EIP-712 signing examples for guidance.

workflows.name: Understanding Orderly Vault and Subaccount Architecture
workflows.description: Understand how Orderly's vault model handles fund custody and trading, and how subaccounts relate to the main account for independent trading states.
prerequisites: Understanding of on-chain vs off-chain settlement

steps.title: Understand the Vault Model
steps.description: Orderly vaults are on-chain asset management tools. Funds are deposited on Orderly, then mirrored to a custodial account (Ceffu) for trading on Binance.
steps.important: Strategy providers run their strategies on Binance using the mirrored funds. This architecture provides deep liquidity while maintaining on-chain custody.

steps.title: Understand Subaccount Architecture
steps.description: Subaccounts are derived from and share the same main wallet address. Each subaccount has its own independent trading state.
steps.important: Subaccounts are treated as independent trading accounts. The main account has control over all its subaccounts, enabling portfolio separation and risk management.

steps.title: Use Subaccounts for Risk Management
steps.description: Leverage subaccounts to separate trading strategies, isolate risk, or manage different portfolios under a single wallet address.
steps.important: Each subaccount maintains its own margin and liquidation state, preventing cross-contamination of risk between strategies.

commonIssues.issue: Confusion about where funds are actually held.
commonIssues.solution: Funds are deposited on-chain in Orderly Vault smart contracts, then mirrored to Ceffu for trading execution on Binance. The on-chain vault maintains custody while Ceffu enables off-exchange settlement.

commonIssues.issue: Subaccount balances not reflecting correctly.
commonIssues.solution: Each subaccount has independent balances. Ensure you are querying the correct subaccount. The main account can view and control all subaccounts.

relatedWorkflows: Setting Up Permissionless Vaults
Managing Isolated Margin Positions via API

workflows.name: Setting Up Broker Admin Wallet and Fee Configuration
workflows.description: Complete process to register a broker ID, configure the admin wallet for fee collection, set up default trading fees, and manage Futures Fee Collector accounts for broker fee rebates.
prerequisites: Broker ID created via Orderly One graduation or approved setup
EVM or Solana wallet for admin functions

steps.title: Register Admin Wallet
steps.description: Register the wallet you want to use as the admin wallet under your broker ID. This must be done on both mainnet and testnet if you need capabilities in both environments.
steps.important: The wallet address must be shared with Orderly support to be enabled as the admin account in the backend. Multisig wallets are supported via the delegate signer feature.

steps.title: Access Admin Portal
steps.description: Once the admin wallet is set up by Orderly, log in to the admin portal using your admin credentials.

steps.title: Configure Default Fees
steps.description: Update default builder/broker fees by calling the private 'Update Default Builder Fee' endpoint or using the admin portal UI. Requests must be signed using Orderly API authentication.
steps.important: Orderly charges a base 0.03% (3 bps) taker fee and 0% maker fee. Anything above the base fee is retained by the broker. Base taker fees can be reduced by staking ORDER tokens: 100k ORDER reduces to 2.75bps, 250k ORDER reduces to 2.5bps. Alternatively, maintaining a rolling average daily volume of 3M qualifies for 2.5bps taker by default. Testnet and mainnet require separate fee updates.

steps.title: Configure Futures Fee Collector Account
steps.description: When migrating to a new Futures Fee Collector account, generate the new account via the broker registration portal using the delegate signer flow, then pre-fund it before the system maintenance cutoff.
steps.important: CRITICAL: Pre-fund the new fee collector account before the switch. The new account only collects fees generated after the switch, but the first broker rebate occurs the following morning based on the previous day's total fees. Without pre-funding, the rebate will fail due to insufficient balance.

steps.title: Verify Fee Collection
steps.description: Broker fees are credited daily to the admin wallet's Orderly account. Check the balance by logging into your DEX with the admin wallet or using the private Get Current Holding endpoint.
steps.code:
GET /v1/holding
Headers: orderly-key, orderly-signature, orderly-timestamp, orderly-account-id

commonIssues.issue: Saving fee configuration fails in the UI.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure you are logged in with the correct broker admin account. A mismatch between the logged-in wallet and the actual broker admin account is a common cause.

commonIssues.issue: Admin portal login fails.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the wallet has been registered as an Orderly account under your broker ID and that Orderly support has enabled it as the admin wallet.

commonIssues.issue: Admin wallet is compromised.
commonIssues.solution: Immediately stop using all devices containing the private key and contact Orderly support to change the admin wallet. Revenue settlement history remains with the old account to preserve data integrity.

commonIssues.issue: Broker rebate fails after migrating to new Futures Fee Collector account.
commonIssues.solution: The new account was likely not pre-funded before the switch. Deposit sufficient USDC into the new fee collector account immediately. The first rebate is calculated on the previous day's total fees, so the new account needs funds to cover it.

workflows.name: Configuring the Multilevel Referral Program
workflows.description: Enable and configure the Orderly DEX Multilevel Referral Program to scale growth and incentivize communities through multi-tier referral rewards, including API-based code creation and post-registration binding.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.9.0 or later (v2.12.4+ recommended for post-registration binding)
Access to Admin Tool or Orderly One dashboard

steps.title: Upgrade SDK
steps.description: Ensure your DEX is running SDK version 2.9.0 or later. For Orderly One DEXs, ensure you are on the latest version available on the platform.
steps.important: As of SDK v2.12.4, users can bind a referral code to their existing account at any time post-registration, rather than being required to provide a code during registration.

steps.title: Activate the Referral Program
steps.description: Enable or upgrade the referral program via the Admin Tool or through the Orderly One dashboard.
steps.code:
// Admin Portal:
https://admin.orderly.network/login

steps.title: Create Referral Codes via Admin Panel or API
steps.description: Create referral codes using the admin wallet via the admin panel or programmatically via the REST API. The admin wallet is the only wallet authorized to create codes.
steps.important: When creating a code, specify the taker rebate for both referee and referrer. All values are expressed as absolute decimals (e.g., 0.5 means 50% of fees). Only accounts bound to a referral code are eligible for rebates and can create their own referral codes.

steps.title: Understand Multi-Level Fee Chain
steps.description: The referral system works in a multi-level chain where fees cascade through referrers.
steps.important: Referral rebates are settled in USDC regardless of the collateral asset used, and are sent to users once per day.

steps.title: Implement Frontend Referral Dashboard
steps.description: Use the Components SDK referral components to display a referral dashboard for your users.
steps.important: As of SDK v2.12.4, users can also bind a referral code to their existing account at any time after registration.

steps.title: Use order_tag for Per-Order Referral Tracking
steps.description: Attach a referral code at the order level using the `order_tag` field in the create order API. This overrides any account-level referral binding.
steps.code:
POST /v1/order
Body: {
  "symbol": "PERP_ETH_USDC",
  "order_type": "MARKET",
  "order_quantity": "0.01",
  "side": "BUY",
  "order_tag": "BBBB" // Overrides account-level referral code
}

commonIssues.issue: Cannot register referral code for a KOL/affiliate.
commonIssues.solution: The KOL/affiliate must first connect their wallet and sign in to create an Orderly account. Attempting to register a ref code before the user has signed in will result in an 'address is not registered' error.

commonIssues.issue: Rebates not appearing for users.
commonIssues.solution: Rebates are settled once per day in USDC. Ensure the referral code is correctly bound to the user's account and that the rebate rates are properly configured (not 0%).

commonIssues.issue: API claim_code endpoint returns errors.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure the account is already bound to an upstream referral code and that the fee split percentages are properly configured (not 0%). Verify all required headers are present.

workflows.name: Handling Permissionless Token Listings
workflows.description: Manage permissionless token listings on your Orderly-powered DEX, including syncing frontend configurations, supporting new markets automatically, and listing Real World Assets (RWAs) with custom oracles.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK v2.12.0 or later (v3.0.3+ recommended for mobile fixes)
Price oracle and market maker for RWA listings

steps.title: Upgrade SDK for Permissionless Support
steps.description: Ensure your SDK is at least v2.12.0 for full UI rendering and trading support of permissionlessly listed symbols. SDK v3.0.3+ fixes display issues on mobile (e.g., empty Interval, Funding Cap/Floor values).

steps.title: Sync Frontend Configuration
steps.description: When new permissionless markets are announced, update your frontend configuration to support the new symbols. Monitor Orderly announcements for new listings.
steps.important: Permissionless listings allow builders to list any asset not currently on Orderly. As the market owner, the builder earns 100% of liquidation fees plus 50% of Orderly's base fee on that market.

steps.title: List Real World Assets (RWAs)
steps.description: List any RWA using Orderly's Permissionless Listings feature by connecting a suitable price oracle and having a market maker or MM bot to support the market.
steps.important: Builders can list any RWA (FX pairs, US stocks, commodities, interest rates) by providing their own oracle price feed and market maker support.

steps.title: Handle Chart Data for New Markets
steps.description: SDK v3.1.3 optimizes K-line history loading so the chart stops requesting unavailable historical data before a market's listing time, reducing unnecessary requests and improving page stability.
steps.important: Permissionlessly listed markets are Isolated-only to limit risk exposure.

steps.title: Notify Users of New Markets
steps.description: Inform your users about newly available permissionless markets and any specific trading rules (e.g., isolated margin only).

commonIssues.issue: Permissionless symbols show empty values in funding rate modal on mobile.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.0.3 or later, which fixes the display of Interval, Funding Cap/Floor, and Estimated Funding Fee values.

commonIssues.issue: Chart requests fail for newly listed markets.
commonIssues.solution: Upgrade to SDK v3.1.3+ which optimizes K-line history loading to stop requesting unavailable historical data before a market's listing time.

commonIssues.issue: Cannot use Cross Margin on permissionless markets.
commonIssues.solution: This is by design. Permissionlessly listed markets only support Isolated Margin to limit risk exposure.

commonIssues.issue: RWA market prices drift from reference price.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure your market maker or MM bot is actively providing liquidity and that your oracle price feed is reliable and frequently updated.

workflows.name: Integrating Privy Wallet with Custom UI
workflows.description: Integrate Privy wallet authentication with Orderly SDK using a custom UI (without Orderly's prebuilt React components), ensuring proper wallet recognition and account state management.
prerequisites: Orderly SDK with wallet-connector-privy package installed

steps.title: Wrap Application with Providers
steps.description: Wrap your custom UI with WalletConnectorPrivyProvider and OrderlyAppProvider, configuring Privy, Wagmi, and Solana settings.
steps.code:
<WalletConnectorPrivyProvider
  network={networkId === 'mainnet' ? Network.mainnet : Network.testnet}
  privyConfig={{ appid: privyAppId, config: { loginMethods: ['email'] } }}
  wagmiConfig={{ connectors: getEvmConnectors() }}
  solanaConfig={getSolanaConfig(networkId)}
>
  <OrderlyAppProvider brokerId='...' brokerName='...' networkId={networkId}>
    <YourCustomUI />
  </OrderlyAppProvider>
</WalletConnectorPrivyProvider>

steps.title: Implement Connect Button with useWalletConnector
steps.description: Use the useWalletConnector hook to connect via Privy. You MUST use this hook — do not call Privy's login/OAuth hooks directly.

steps.title: Read Account State
steps.description: After connecting, read wallet and account state from the appropriate hooks.
steps.important: Orderly recognizes the account ONLY when the wallet connects through useWalletConnector().connect(...) with WalletConnectType.PRIVY. Calling Privy's login hooks directly will not register the wallet with Orderly.

commonIssues.issue: Wallet connects in Privy but Orderly does not recognize the account.
commonIssues.solution: You must use useWalletConnector().connect({ walletType: WalletConnectType.PRIVY }) instead of calling Privy's login/OAuth hooks directly. Orderly only recognizes accounts connected through its own hook.

commonIssues.issue: Account state shows as disconnected after Privy login.
commonIssues.solution: Ensure both WalletConnectorPrivyProvider and OrderlyAppProvider wrap your component tree in the correct order, and that you are reading state from useAccount() after the connect() call resolves.
